It is located in the compartment under the windscreen and can be replaced by removing the special access flap. The filter is fitted on both the manual version and the automatic version of the climate control system.

INTRODUCTION The vehicle is equipped with a system that cleans and washes the front and rear windscreens. The vehicle may be fitted as an option with a pressurised liquid washing system for the front headlamps. WINDSCREEN WASH/WIPE The windscreen wash/wipe assembly cleans and washes the windscreen. There is an electronic device for the management of this function that identifies the presence of drops of water on the windscreen (rain sensor). The innovative features of the windscreen washer assembly are essentially: - the smart wash operating strategy applied for the windscreen wiper. - the presence of the rain sensor. The windscreen wiper mechanism was developed to optimise the sweep area and allow the brushes to operate under the correct conditions (wiping angle, pressure on the windscreen) at all times. Due to the electronic control system and according to the position of the right steering wheel stalk switch, the system manages operation of the direct current wiper motor by means of two windings, i.e. at two rotating speeds. The rain sensor allows automatic assembly operation under weather conditions that would require the user to intervene repeatedly and continuously. The smart washing strategy assured by the electronic control system allows the residual traces of washer fluid that are normally apparent at the end of the washing cycle on a conventional winscreen wash/wipe system to be removed. the smart washing function follows the logic described below: by pulling the lever towards the steering wheel (unstable position) the jet of fluid and the screen washing is activated. By keeping the lever pulled for more than half a second it is possible to automatic activate the screen washer jet and the actual windscreen wiper in a single movement. The operation of the windscreen wiper ends four strokes after the lever is released. WINDSCREEN/REARSCREEN WASHER ELECTRIC PUMP The electric windscreen washer pump is activated through the right steering column switch unit lever. By moving the right steering column switch unit lever towards the driver (unstable position) the two-way pump receives an electrical power supply and is capable of supplying the front jets; conversely by pulling the lever towards the dashboard the pump is rotated in the opposite direction and the fluid comes out towards the rearscreen washer pipe and the rear jets are supplied. REAR WINDSCREEN WASH/WIPE (REARSCREEN) This device has the task of cleaning the rear windscreen very well. It has a single motor with a 12V supply which operates at voltages of between 9 and 16V with a bimetallic type overload cut out. The wiping function is carried out by a single wiping element consisting of a plastic arm with internal linkage. The jet is fastened to the upper edge of the tailgate. REARSCREEN WIPER FUNCTION The electronic module controls the intermittent operation of the rearscreen wiper motor in a similar way to the one described for the windscreen wiper. The activation of the rearscreen wiper is synchronous with that of the windscreen wiper, but a frequency that is half that of the windscreen wiper (for every two impulses of the windscreen wiper, one is sent to the rearscreen wiper). Automatic function The system, in addition to the manual activation described previously, is activated automatically via the Body Computer which sends information to the steering column switch unit electronic module. When, with the windscreen wiper activated either in manual or automatic operating mode (rain sensor), reverse gear is engaged, the dashboard control unit receives the signal from the reversing switch and sends it to the body computer which sends it to the steering column switch unit electronic module which controls the rearscreen wiper motor. HEADLAMP WASHER The headlamp washer system is designed to clean the surfaces of the front light clusters and keep them clean. The headlamp washer system consists of: - a specific electric pump on the windscreen washer fluid reservoir; - two devices with spray nozzles which are bolted to the bumper; - three connecting pipes between the pump and the devices inside the bumper; OPERATING CYCLE The function is activated when the following conditions arise: - ignition key inserted and turned to ON position; - dipped headlamps on; - headlamp washer control active on stalk. The control is activated by a windscreen washer control on the stalk unit that identifes the windscreen washing action. The Body Computer downloads the windscreen washer control activation time and increases a counter. Because the nozzles are controlled by pump delivery pressure, they operate at the same frequency as the pump. RIGHT STEERING COLUMN SWITCH UNIT LEVER This includes the front and rear wiper controls. All the controls are activated by operating either the stalk or the wheel control on the actual lever. A button on the end of the stalk switch also controls trip computer functions. For further details, See descriptions 5560 INSTRUMENTS A - Windscreen wiper control; A1 - Windscreen wiper intermittence adjustment/Rain sensor sensitivity; B - Winscreen wiper control; C - Rear wiper control; D - Rear washer control; E - Trip computer control button. Windscreen wiper control This is operated by moving the lever in the same plane as the steering wheel. The control can be operated to 5 different positions: Pos. 1= Single sweep (UNSTABLE): ANTICLOCKWISE DIRECTION; Pos. 2= No circuit activated (STABILE): POS. REST; Pos. 3= Intermittent / Automatic(STABLE): CLOCKWISE DIRECTION; Pos. 4= Continuous 1st SPEED (STABLE): CLOCKWISE DIRECTION; Pos. 5= Continuous 2nd SPEED (STABLE): CLOCKWISE DIRECTION. ADJUSTMENT OF WINDSCREEN WIPER INTERMITTENCE/RAIN SENSOR SENSITIVITY The control is located at the end of the stalk and operated by turning a wheel control clockwise to 4 stable positions corresponding to 4 different rain sensor settings with increasing sensitivity: ELECTRONIC MODULE (BUILT INTO STALK UNIT) This control unit controls the operation of the electric motors, front and rear wipers and washer functions. In particular, it controls the operation of: - Windscreen wiper: sweep rate; - Rearscreen wiper: sweep rate and control during reversing; - Windscreen washer function, with smart washing; - Rearscreen washer function, with smart washing; - Rain sensor. Rear wiper control The control is located on the stalk and operated by turning a wheel control. The control offers 2 stable positions and is moved clockwise: - Pos. 1 = No circuit operated; - Pos. 2 = Rear wiper operated. REAR WASHER CONTROL This is operated by pushing the stalk towards the facia. The operation is UNSTABLE, i.e. the stalk returns to rest position when released. The control simultaneously operates the rear wiper in smart washing mode. RAIN SENSOR The rain/dusk sensor, located on the windscreen glass by the electrchromic interior rear view mirror, is operated by the steering column switch unit electronic control unit. Location The rain sensor, described below, is located under the interior rear view mirror. A - Rain / dusk sensor B - Interior rear view mirror SYSTEM COMPOSITION The device works on an infrared wave length: based on the principle of refraction of a light beam through the glass, it allows the automatic adjustment of the number of windscreen wiper strokes proportional to the intensity of the rain. Through the variation of the infrared rays the device is capable of measuring the dimensions, number and quantity of drops of rain present on the glass; as the refraction mode varies, the sensor reacts producing electrical impuses which are processed and sent via the serial network. The windscreen wiper control unit (incorporated in the steering column switch unit) operates the windscreen wiper according to the speed set by the rain sensor. The sensor communicates with the steering column switch unit and the body computer by means of an A-BUS serial interface. The rain sensor consists of two sets of four infrared ray leds arranged in a ring and a receiving element located in the centre of the leds. The sensor, integrated with the dusk sensor function and housed in the rear view mirror unit, is kept in contact with the windscreen by a spring that acts on a protective cover located behind the actual mirror. The LED and receiver, embedded in a polymer, are connected to the windscreen wiper control unit by means of a wire with a connector. In this way, the sensor can be removed easily after removing the cover and disconnecting the connector. The device is activated by moving the steering column switch unit from the stop or first speed positions to the intermittent/automatic position. At this point the windscreen wiper completes a confirmation stroke informing the user that it has moved on to automatic operation. The dynamic interference (raindrop) detection sensitivity is adjusted by means of a wheel on the lever to four levels. Each time the sensitivity is altered, the windscreen carries out a confirmation stroke. If the lever remains in the auto position and the panel is switched off, at the next key ON the automatic function is not activated. In this case, to return to automatic mode, simply move the wiper lever to any position or turn the sensitivity setting ring on the actual lever. This happens both if there is a fault in the system and in normal operating conditions. Operation When the right lever is moved to intermittent/automatic position A1, the rain sensor is activated. The frequency of the windscreen wiper strokes is automatically adjusted depending on the amount of water on the windscreen. the frequency varies continuously from nil (no stroke - windscreen dry) to wiping at the second continuous speed (heavy rain) The activation of the rain sensor involves a windscreen wiper arm stroke as feedback to confirm that it has been switched on. If the panel is off (key-off), the RAIN SENSOR places the windscreen wiper system in stand-by when the stalk is left in AUTOMATIC position. Next time the ignition key is turned on, no wipe cycle is performed even if rain is present. To restore AUTOMATIC system operation, only of the following manoeuvres may be performed on the steering wheel stalk unit wiper stalk: - the stalk may be moved from AUTOMATIC position to any other position and return to AUTOMATIC position; - sensitivity may be adjusted by turning the WHEEL (increased or decreased). When RAIN SENSOR operation is reset by means of one of the above manoeuvres, the wiper moves through one beat even if the glass is dry to notify the uwer that it has been reactivated. If the stalk unit does not receive a signal from the Rain Sensor (due to breaks in the wiring or Sensor malfunctions), the windscreen wiper should operate in accordance with the intermittent mode cycle described with the right stalk in intermittent/automatic position. Recovery function If the operation of the rain sensor is found to be incorrect, the recovery function is implemented and the operation of the windscreen wiper is managed as if it were in manual mode. The electronic module establishes that the rain sensor is not working correctly if, for a period of 3 secs., it does not receive significant information from the sensor or if it receives a failure status from the A-BUS network. The sensor also communicates the fault message to the Body Computer. The Body Computer controls the activation of the fault signalling at the instrument panel. If the fault is intermittent and the recovery situation is implemented, the fault signalling at the NQS disappears, but the automatic mode operation is not restored. To activate it again, move the wiper lever in the steering column switch unit into any position and then return it to the Auto position, or turn the sensor sensitivity wheel. DUSK SENSOR Operation The side lights and the dipped headlamps can be automatically activated using the dusk sensor if the AUTO function in the steering column switch unit is set. The dusk sensor is an infra red device which operates at different sensitivity levels: when the dusk sensor is activated a message is shown on the instrument panel display indicating the sensitivity setting (from 1 to 3): this setting can be adjusted using the "Mode +" and "Mode -" buttons. At the key on, the dusk sensor communicates the information relating to the outside brightness to the Body Computer via the A-BUS serial network, sending it periodically once a second. When the user activates the dusk sensor, the Body Computer acquires the AUTO command and transmits it to the instrument panel which activates the message to select the sensor sensitivity setting, restoring the last value selected previously. The variation in the sensor sensitivity level can also be made after the activation both with the vehicle driving or stationary by searching for the item relating to the sensor sensitivity within the instrument panel menu. The Body Computer uses the message transmitted by the dusk sensor to activate/deactivate the side lights and dipped headlamps. The side lights and the dipped headlamps are switched on simultaneously, whilst the side lights are switched off 10 seconds after the dipped headlamps are turned off. Recovery function In the presence of the following faults: - failure signal by the sensor; - Body Computer no longer receives information from the dusk sensor via the A-BUS line. The Body Computer implements the following strategies: - If the steering column switch unit is in the AUTO position and the side lights are off: it supplies the failure signal to the instrument panel and simultaneously switches on the side lights and the dipped headlamps. - If the steering column switch unit is in the AUTO position and the side lights are on: it supplies the failure signal to the instrument panel and switches on the side lights and the dipped headlamps. - If the steering column switch unit is not in the AUTO position: it supplies the failure signal to the instrument panel and does not implement any recovery action for the dusk sensor.

ELECTRICAL AND ELECTRONIC SYSTEM General specifications In conventional electrical systems, functions are activated with the aid of dedicated point-to-point lines The increase in the number of electrical/electronic devices on board cars has given rise to heavier and more complex connections. This is partly due to the complexity of the functions implemented in the burgeoning number of electronic units - which also need to exchange data continually: all this makes new electrical systems more difficult to install and increases the complexity of fault diagnosis. Many problems have been overcome and new electrical systems have been optimised compared to conventional systems by using a network form of connection. This provides a more effective means of managing communication on the board the car and of transferring data between the various subsystems. Information is distributed via serial pathways (buses) that may take the form of: individual wires, twisted wire pairs or even optical fibres. Let us now take a look at the move from traditional systems to those known as multiplexing systems. Conventional solution The four control units illustrated below require a number (N) of wires for each input/output data item in order to perform their function. This multiplied the amount of cable required to the point that systems are made more complex (design and manufacture) and more voluminous (weight, bulk, cost). Some 40 kg of wiring looms are required that stretch for more than 2 km - and this figure could double every 10 years because even now a car could be equipped wiht 20 to 40 electronic control units (ECUs). 1 - Climate control management node 2 - Engine management node 3 - Engine temperature sensor (for engine management node) 4 - Instrument panel node 5 - Engine temperature sensor (for instrument panel warning light) 6 - Engine cooling fan 7 - Engine temperature bulb The first step towards reducing the volume and complexity of wiring looms was to group several electronic functions in a single unit, therefore: LESS COMPONENTS = LESS WIRES. Examples of integation The multifunction control unit manages the: central locking, electric windows, courtesy light timer, heated rear windscreen and heated, external rear view mirrors timer. 1 - Multifunction control unit 2 - Central locking 3 - Electric windows control unit 4 - Centre courtesy light 5 - Rear courtesy light 6 - Heated rear windscreen / Heated door mirrors The itegration of the electrical/electronic functions in a single unit has made it possible to improve: - the management of current consumption; - the operation of the consumers because they are managed by a single control unit; - the search for faults by means of autodiagnosis of the control unit. This first stage made it possible to reduce the number of electronic units but not to reduce the volume of the cable looms to a sufficient extent. Multiplexing solution This solution makes it possible to reduce the volume of the cable looms and to considerably improve the transmission of information between various electronic units. These transmissions takes place via a BUS channel comprising 2 cables (the main one already used for the telephone, radio, television network, etc.). A - B - C: NODES (CONTROL UNITS) D: MASTER CONTROL UNIT OR BODY COMPUTER A1 - A2, B1 - B2, C1 - C2: COMMUNICATION BUS In addition to reducing and simplfying the wiring and improving communication between electronic units, the multiplexing solution also makes it possible to reduce the number of sensors (INFORMATION SHARING). A - Conventional solution B - Multiplexing solution 1 - Climate control management node 2 - Engine management node 3 - Engine temperature sensor (for engine management node) 4 - Instrument panel node 5 - Engine temperature sensor (for instrument panel warning light) 6 - Engine cooling fan 7 - Engine temperature bulb 8 - Instrument panel node 9 - Climate control management node 10 - Engine temperature information 11 - Body Computer Node 12 - Engine management node 13 - Engine temperature sensor (for engine management node) In general terms, in order to transmit data via a multiplexing system we need to define the following: - (A) THE TRANSMISSION CHANNEL (electric wires, fibre optics, radio waves, etc.); - (B) THE TYPE OF SIGNAL (voltage, current, light, etc.); - (C) THE COMMUNICATION PROTOCOL (all the rules that allow management of analogue or digital transmission type, code type, address, transmission order, error detection etc.). On this model the transmission channel (A) comprises a pair of electrical wires and is known as BUS. The type of signal (B) is VOLTAGE and the communication protocol (C) is the CAN (Controller Area Network) developed by BOSCH. Mini F.L.Ore.N.C.E. SYSTEM STRUCTURE General specifications The Mini F.L.Ore.N.C.E. structure for this model manages some of the vehicle's electrical equipment, controlling the bodywork functions directly (control of access, visibility, on board information, comfort, etc.). To improve the system, the structure follows the regional topological approach: each control unit (electronic or electromechanical) is located in a centre of gravity position in relation to the functions managed. This allows the power and signal distribution system to be minimised. This is also made possible through extensive use of serial communication networks that allow us to overcome problems of space-saving, reliability, weight and cost. The structure consists of three CAN communication networks which connect nodes belonging to the three different areas (vehicle dynamic control, on board information and bodywork functions) and a certain number of complementary serial lines. Power is distributed via the junction units and/or fuse boxes connected to control elements (relays and static actuators) to ensure maximum electrical protection and minimum complexity of the wiring. All wiring looms have been made modular by changing the way functions are distributed inside the connectors and replacing welds with short-circuiting joints. The structure of the wiring has been designed to simplify the fitting through the reduction in the number of sections, the reduction in lengths and the elimination of critical crossovers and has also been designed to encourage the production of all cable looms in a modular manner (through the composition of subassemblies) with the aim of producing the most simple in line sequencing of the wiring on the Fiat Auto production lines. The possibility of using the most up to date automatic wiring construction equipment has also been taken into account. The system (e.g.: door wiring, dashboard wiring) can potentially be adapted for automatic wiring production systems. The architecture developed is compatible with various user interface solutions (control arrangement, information allocation and display method). The electrical protection (fuses) and the relays are grouped together in the power distribution junction units located in the engine compartment and the dashboard. These junction units also act as connections for the various wiring and electrical distribution. Modular system Wiring To allow the construction for subassemblies (electrical functions) and to facilitate the possible automatic production, all welding (splice) and couplings with minted terminals has been avoided; even if this restricts the advantages of automatic production, soldering or minting can be used for coupligns that do not interconnect different assemblies. To produce a minimum number of wiring families, each circuit has a section coupling that should maintain the same position inside the coupling, irrespective of the trim level; the position and the type of the coupling on the vehicle should also not depend on the trim level (high or low). Components To safeguard the modular nature of the wiring the inlets/outlets for each junction unit should not differ according to the trim level/engine type, the position of the connector or the cable/terminal/connector interface. B-can connection The B-CAN (low speed) network comprises 2 electrical wires (sec. 0.35 mm²), one White/Pink shown in the wiring diagram as the CAN-A cable and one Black/Pink one shown in the wiring diagram as the CAN-B cable. The information is transmitted via this pair of wires on 2 voltage levels (V), one High and one Low associated with the CAN-A and the CAN-B cables, respectively; the mathematical difference between these two levels produces two associated voltage values at two logic levels 0 or 1. The latter constitute the elementay information unit known as a BIT (binary figure) and, suitably combined, make up the information to be transmitted. V Can A - V Can B = 3.6 - 1.4 = + 2.2 V (bit 0) V Can A - V Can B = 0.2 -4.8 = -4.6 V (bit 1) B-can connection diagram The principle diagram for the B-CAN for the full optional version of this model is illustrated below. The transmission of information is similar to that of the B-CAN; in this case the High voltage level is associated with the CAN-H cable, whilst the Low voltage level is associated with the CAN-L cable. For the C-CAN too, it is the mathematical difference between these two voltage levels that gives rise to the two logic levels 0 and 1, but with one difference illustrated in the diagram: The network interface cannot communicate via the C-CAN network if one of the following situations arises: - Interruption of one of the two CAN cables (H and L); - Short circuit between the two CAN cables (H and L); - Short circuit of the CAN-H cable or CAN-L cable to +Vbatt.; - Short circuit of the CAN-H cable or CAN-L cable to earth. Priority in case of transmission conflict for several nodes The system protocol allows the mini F.L.Ore.N.C.E. to handle superimposition problems when several nodes need to emit a frame simultaneously. The node that transmits the lower priority message immediately interrupts its transmission and makes way for the node that is transmitting a higher priority message. In practice, the high priority message is sent to the network without any interruption or delay. The higher priority frame gains the right to be transmitted on the BUS. A dominant level (0) always takes precedence over a recessive level (1). The communication on the A-BUS line takes place via the exchange of data packages between the different control units. Each control unit connected to the A-BUS line has its own electronic address; when a control unit has to send a command/information to another control unit it mus always include the address of the destination control unit in the data package. The transmission always takes place from a transmitter control unit to a receiver control unit (one-way). When the reception of data is over, the receiving control unit should send the result to the transmitter control unit thereby ending the exchange of the data package. Unlike CAN NETWORKS, on the A-BUS line the transmission priorities are assigned to each control unit and not to the information being transmitted, therefore the order in which the control units have access to the line if there is a transmission conflict is decided at design level. LOGISTIC MODE The low consumption mode (Logistic Mode) should be activated when vehicles are in storage during the stage between the end of the production line until delivery to the final customer. This system, managed by software inside the Body Computer, is used to reduce current absorption due to accidental or deliberate activation of unnecessary loads. This function makes it possible to save battery energy which is useful when the vehicle is parked, possibly for long periods, in forecourts before being sold. The activation of the Logistic Mode should guarantee the possibility of starting up the vehicle and driving it without adverse effects in terms of safety even if there is a slight lowering of on board comfort standards and certain functions. The function should be disabled in the workshop before the vehicle is handed over to the Customer. All versions of the CROMA, diesel and petrol, are involved. The following functions are involved in the activation of the Logistic Mode: - Central locking - Remote control functions - Electric windows movements - Radio - Navigator - Current socket/cigar lighter - Clock - Climate control (manual / automatic) - Additional heater - Sun roof - Sun roof - Heated seats - Switching on of courtesy lights - Switching on of boot/bonnet lights - Switching on of puddle lights - Switching on of fog lights/rear fog lamps - Switching on of main beam headlamps Deactivation of the logistic mode The low consumption supply mode should be activated in the factory straight after the dynamic/functional tests. The procedure should be carried out 100% on engine types that have this function using special equipment (control unit diagnostic device) and only if there are no serious type errors present. The deactivation procedure is as follows: - Connect the terminal with the diagnostic device to the vehicle EOBD socket and turn the key in the ignition device (TEG Reader) ON. - Check that the battery recharging warning light is flashing (this warning light flashing means that the Logistic Mode low consumption mode is activated). - Deactivate the low consumption supply mode by carrying out the fault diagnosis of the Body Computer node using the Examiner. - The Body Computer node will receive the Logistic Mode deactivation command from the diagnostic equipment and, in addition to exiting the low consumption conditions reactivating full operation, it will send the Standard Power command to the CANS (B-CAN, C-CAN). - All the control units involved, on receiving the CAN message, will restore their full operation and send a confirmation message to the Body Computer node. - Delete the error memory in all control units with a diagnostic function. - Turn the key in the ignition OFF and then ON. - Check that the battery recharging warning light is on constantly. REPLACING AND INITIALIZING NETWORK NODES Some of the CAN nodes are programmed with default settings which the customer will discover on acquiring the vehicle. The nodes storing this information are the: - Body Computer; - Instrument Panel; - Climate control system control unit. - Steering Lock Node; - Driver's Door Node; - Passenger door node. If the Body Computer is being replaced, an "identical copy" of the Body Computer must be obtained from the Parts Dept as a V.O.R. order supplying the vehicle chassis number: this copy will contain all the default settings entered when the vehicle was new which are stored in the Parts Dept. database for the vehicle chassis number. If the Body Computer, Instrument Panel, Climate Control System Control Unit, Steering Lock Node, Driver's Door Node, Passenger Door Node is being replaced, the Parts Dept. will send a pristine component. once fitted; the initial default data must be transferred to it by carrying out the "PROXI ALIGNMENT" procedure using the Examiner. If other nodes are being replaced, no initialization operation is required. However, always check that the system has not picked up errors during the removing-refitting operations, etc. using the Examiner. The PROXI alignment procedure using the Examiner does not have to be carried out for the initialization of the luggage compartment node. Battery disconnection If the battery is disconnected, the Body Computer, the Instrument Panel, the Climate Control System Control Unit and the Steering Lock Node all preserve the information received and do not have to be initialized again when the battery is reconnected, whilst the other nodes lose some or all of the information stored in their memory.

BODY COMPUTER NODE Specifications The Body Computer Node (NBC) is an electronic component connected to the vehicle serial networks which manages the basic functions of the Mini F.L.Ore.N.C.E structure (interior/exterior lighting, immobilizer, fault diagnosis, heated rear windscreen, door locking, alarm, fuel level) and houses the gateway between the B-CAN and the C-CAN. The NBC also carries out interconnection functions between the dashboard, front and rear wiring and is connected to the Dashboard Control Unit (CPL) by means of a connector at the front. There is also a fixed EOBD connector at the front capable of carrying out the fault diagnosis via the K line for the Engine Management Node and the systems not connected to the B-CAN line (e.g. the air bag) and via the B-CAN line for the nodes connected to it. There is a possible assembly programme for the latter. General functions of the body computer node To sum up, the NBC carries out the following functions: - Receives and transmits information on the B-CAN (e.g.: diagnosis, warning lights, controls, data); - Receives and transmits information on the C-CAN; - Houses the gateway for communication between the C-CAN and B-CAN; - Is connected to the dashboard, front and rear wiring; - Allows interface for fault diagnosis (EOBD); - Low consumption supply mode management (Logistic Mode); - Is connected to the CPL to take supplies/signals and operate relays. The following functions are included: - management of the courtesy lights with a timer and dimmer function; - management of the on/off outputs at the relays: headlamp washer pump, main beam headlamps, fog lights, dipped headlamps, rear windscreen and services, - on/off management of left/right direction indicators and hazard warning lights; - on/off output management directly at loads and light check function: front and rear side lights (left and right), front, rear and side direction indicators (left and right), number plate lights (left and right), brake lights (left and right), rear fog lamps (left and right); - management of the on/off outputs at the loads: hazard warning LED, etc.; - acquisition and repetition of vehicle speed signal; - management of the driver for the ideogram lights; - management of the driver for SBMT (switching off loads with ignition OFF); - recovery serial line (W) management to engine management control unit (immobilizer); management of serial line (A-BUS) to rain/dusk sensor, steering column switch unit, volumetric alarm control unit and tyre pressure control unit; - entire system master: management of slave nodes in its direct jurisdiction and monitoring by other master nodes, monitoring and management of protocol errors, timer control; - entire system fault diagnosis: collection of diagnostic information, management of fault diagnosis through EXAMINER.; - acquisition of on/off signals: control of dipped headlamps, control of main beam headlamps, control of boot lock opening, control of boot lock locking, handbrake control, hazard warning lights control, left and right rear fog lamps control, fog lights relay control, left direction indicators control, right direction indicators control, parking lights control, side lights control, city control, steering column switch unit auto control, headlamp washer control, FIS control, boot button, bonnet button, front brake pad wear, brake fluid level, reverse gear engaged; - acquisition of analogue signals: fuel level, alternator voltage (D+), battery voltage; - recognition of brake lights fuse status, centre courtesy light control, left and right spot lights control, brake lights controls, acquisition of signals for lock sensors from doors; - preparation for possible inclusion of new electric functions. 5520A IGNITION SWITCH T.e.g. module “transmitter for entry and go” The TEG is part of the Smart-Key system which comprises the following components: - T.E.G. (Transmitter for Entry and Go) electronic key; - TEG-Reader for radiofrequency receiver and electronic key; - Steering Lock Node NBS. The Smart-Key system carries out the following functions on the vehicle: - vehicle access through remote control radiofrequency recognition; - vehicle ignition/starting through immobilizer system; - power supply distribution (+15, INT/A, 15/54, +50) through Steering Lock Node (NBS); - mechanical steering lock/release; - mechanical emergency back-up key. 1 - Steering Lock Node (NBS) 2 - T.E.G. Reader Node (NTR) 3 - T.E.G. 4 - Back up insert The Smart-Key system is far more secure that all previous protection systems with immobilizers, etc. because the control and security codes are memorized is 4 separate areas of the CAN: the Body Computer, engine management control unit, steering lock node and TEG-Reader. Operation Inserting the teg in the teg reader The TEG can be turned to 3 different positions inside the TEG Reader: two stable (OFF and ON) and one unstable (START). The position recognition conditions take place by means of the change in status of the four switches TEG_IN, TEG_MAR, TEG_Crank1 and TEG_Crank2. SW1, Teg IN SW2, Teg MAR SW3, Teg CRANK1 SW4, Teg UNLOCK SW5, Teg CRANK2 M, Engine The TEG can only be inserted in the reader in the OFF position and this causes the change in status of the TEG_IN switch with the consequent wake up of the CAN and the sending, via the NBS B-CAN, of the Power ON request (+15) to the Body Computer. If the TEG is recognized, the steering is released and the NBS sends the TEG Reader the signal to release the mechanical mechanism preveting the rotation of the TEG in the reader. The activation of the release changes the status of the TEG_lock switch. This switching causes a break in the power supply for the locking/unlocking motor. If whilst turning the TEG from the OFF position to the ON position the speed of the manoeuvre causes sticking, the manoeuvre can be completed without having to return the TEG to the OFF position. If the TEG change in status information (from Locked to UnLocked) does not arrive within 400 ms or the key remains in the Locked condition, the customer will be advised via the instrument panel and should proceed with unlocking it using the emergency procedure described later on. If the TEG is not recognized, the NBS will not release the steering and will send a warning message to the Instrument Panel Node (NQS). Therefore, the reader can only be turned to the ON position if a valid TEG is inserted in order to provide the +15 and activate the vehicle starting stage in the START position. Key on Inserting a TEG in the TEG Reader produces the unlocking of the steering by the NBS and, if all the safety conditions are met, the consequent request of the activation of the +15. The NBS asks the NBC for permission to give the +15 and, after checking the Immobilizer code via the NTR, it releases the steering and sends the go ahead to the Power ON. When the go ahead from the NBC is received by the NBS, the request to unlock the rotation of the TEG in the reader is made and, once a feed back signal is sent to confirm that the NTR has unlocked it , the TEG is free to be turned to the ON and START positions. If the Immo is not recognized, the NBS does not receive the go ahead from the NBC and the steering is not released. This is also signalled at the NQS. Once the TEG is turned to the ON position the TEG_ON switch changes status and the NBS activates the +15/54, INT and INT/A loads. On versions with automatic transmission if, in the +15 state, the NBS detects, via the CAN, that the gear lever is in a position other than P (PARK), the NBS itself will lock the TEG in the reader by means of a special signal. The locking of the steering by the steering lock node takes place when the TEG is extracted from the TEG Reader. If the battery is disconnected the Steering Lock Node remains in the condition (unlocked or locked) that it is in: therefore for all workshop operations or repairs that require turning the steering with the battery disconnected, the TEG must be left inside the reader, a key on carried out (turn it to the ON position) and then turn it OFF (key off) when the battery is disconnected: the steering will thereby remain unlocked and free to turn. Lighting The lighting of the ring nut is managed directly by the TEG Reader and follows the B-CAN status, in particular: - at the key on: the ring nut is always lit up; - at the key off: the ring nut is lit up as long as the B-CAN is activated. Once it goes to sleep the LEDs that light up the ring nut are also switched off. Deactivation of +15 on, switching off of engine and extraction of teg In the Key On status (from Key Off or return to this state after starting), when the TEG is turned to the OFF position, the NBS deactivates the load +15/54, INT and INT/A and activates the unlocking of the TEG in the TEG Reader. If, at the time of the deactivation, the speed of the vehicle is more than 4 km/h, then the NBS does not command the locking of the steering when the TEG is extracted. In this case the user is advised through the following signal at the NQS: "The steering will not be locked". If the vehicle is equipped with automatic transmission, the TEG does not turn to the OFF position at the Key Off, but stops in an intermediate position where the key cannot be extracted. For this restriction to be removed, the gear lever must be in position P (Park). Activation of starting The engine is started by rotating the TEG to the unstable START position and by pressing the clutch pedal or the brake pedal (recovery function) for versions with a manual gearbox or the brake pedal only for versions with automatic transmission. When the starting command is recognized, before activating the starter motor the NBS checks the following conditions: - clutch/brake pedal pressed within 200 ms (timeout) of the activation of the +15 - validation of +15 signal (present at the B-CAN as well) - starting enablement by the NBC (IMMOBILIZER check) The starter motor is driven (+50) until the clutch/brake pedal is released or for a maximum of 10 seconds. (or the key is released). On versions with automatic transmission, the additional condition of the gear lever being in P (PARK) must be observed. During the starting stage, the NBS disables the INT/A power supply and the relative loads. If starting takes place correctly, the NBS, evaluating the engine rpm signal, commands the mechanical locking of the TEG in the TEG Reader. If the starting is not successful, the NBS cuts off the power supply to the motor (+50) and enables the INT/A. The TEG must be returned to the OFF position and the cranking procedures repeated in order to repeat the starting operation. Failed STARTING: if starting fails it is no longer possible to "push start" the engine by activating the starter motor with a gear engaged (the clutch/brake should be pressed to enable starting and disconnect the transmission). If the vehicle is towed after the Battery Run Down condition, this is preceeded by the classic "bridge between batteries" in order to guarantee the recognition of the key and the consequent release of the steering. System signals The Smart Key system controls several warning lights and/or sends message signals to the instrument panel for the following functions: - vehicle access and/or alarm - steering lock/release - vehicle starting and switching off - electric steering lock failure - failed TEG recognition - steering not locked signal - TEG reader failure signal - TEG in reader signal when driver's door is opened at Key-Off - signalling of insertion of the TEG in the TEG Reader Components Remote control The remote control system is made up of a radiofrequency transmitter, incorporated in the TEG, which sends the variable code to the receiver. the frequency varies according to the country it is sold in: (e.g. Europe 433.92 MHz) The user can carry out the following actions using the TEG: - central locking - unlocking of the doors/boot; - opening - closing the windows; - switching on the courtesy light; - switching on-off of the alarm (if present). The transmitter has a range of about 20 m. Receiver The radiofrequency receiver is built into the TEG-Reader module. the frequency varies according to the country it is sold in. It memorizes up to eight transmitters and allows the remote control operations mentioned above. 1 – TEG Reader 2 - Slit for emergency unlocking The receiver has the following functions: - receiving and decoding the signals coming from the transmitter. - managing the transmitter programming. - managing the command for opening and closing of the doors. - to carry out self-diagnosis. The receiver can memorize up to eight remote control codes. Teg with three buttons 1 - door locking 2 - door unlocking 3 - boot release 4 - back up key The TEG is an electronic device which, used in place of a traditional key, produces: - access to the vehicle by carrying out all the normal operations by remote control: - starting of the vehicle: if introduced and turned inside the special reader, it deactivates the electric steering lock and provides the enablement for starting in accordance with the logics described previously. The remote control section has a 433.92 MHz transmitter with 3 control buttons for the vehicle access functions and a special retractable plastic insert that can be extracted manually. The TEG homologation is in accordance with Dir. 95/56 CE and conforms with the requirements of European insurance companies and their associated technical centres. Mechanical emergency key (back up) In emergencies, the TEG is used like a regular mechanical key in order to carry out manoeuvres on the mechanical back-up pawls (door opening-closing, air bag activation-deactivation, etc.). The mechanical key is a special insert that can be extracted manually from the TEG. Extraction in an emergency The TEG can be released in any circumstances, even with the vehicle moving, through the mechanical emergency insert. In effect, if there is a fault that prevents the rotation of the TEG and it returns to the OFF position, the slot can be mechanically unlocked by following the procedure described below. - extract the back up key from the TEG; - insert the emergency key in the slot and push it right in. This manoeuvre will manually activate the unlocking of the retaining motor and the rotation of the TEG will be released. The NBS will detect that this operation has been carried out and will send a signal to the instrument panel to indicate that the steering is not locked. it is not permissible to extract the TEG from the TEG Reader by force as this would result in the hook that retains the key in the reader being broken. If the TEG is extracted in an emergency, the steering will NOT be locked. Similarly, if the TEG is extracted with the speed of the vehicle above 4 Km/h, the steering will NOT be locked. Fiat code system The TEG also manages the operation of the Immobilizer system known as the FIAT CODE: The system is based on the transmission and reception of a radiofrequency signal with a rolling code. Each transmission produces a rolling code managed by a mathematic algorithm. The tramsmission message is memorized in the receiver in a non volatile memory (EEPROM) in such a way that information is not lost even if the batteries are replaced. For some time now, in addition to motors with series or series/parallel windings, motors have been developed with ceramic manget ferrite type permanent magnet energizing. Circular magnet with magnetically preorientated crystals The rough components are directed into the desired shape by pressing and extrusion. Lastly, after a thorough baking procedure, the material turns into the magnets that have a black ceramic structure. The magnetizing treatment takes place during the manufacturing process. The magnets have a circular sector and thereby replace the polar part and the winding. 1 - Radial orientation 2 - Parallel orientation Stator-inductor The positioning of the magnets cannot be done through strong compression or by means of riveting because the magnets are reasonably fragile: they are secured by flexible means, clipw which, in some cases, are stuck to the casing. The casing assembly can be compared with a simple mechanical component without wires to be fitted using two special bolts; it has 6 magnetic poles. 1 - Permanent N-S magnets Rotor-armature (with epicyclic reduction unit) The rotor-armature is illustrated in the diagram below. 1 - Shaft 2 - Ring gear/crown wheel 3 - Satellite/planet gears 4 - Pinion/sun gear 5 - Armature 6 - Commutator/switch Rotor-armature (with epicyclic reduction unit) Given that the magnetic field is produced by permanent magnets, the energizing is the same in all motor operating conditions; in addition, as there are no energizing windings, there is no energizing current or ohmic resistance: the total resistance only depends on the armature circuit. The rotation speed is only influenced by the current that passes through the blades and reaches the rotor depending on the voltage. Since the motor is equipped with permanent magnets, i.e. with fixed polarity, the direction of rotation depends on how the current is sent to the blades. When rotating the rotor transmits motion to the three satellite gears fitted on special supports that transmit their drive torque to the ring gear or crown wheel in one piece with the output shaft where the pinion is located and the engine flywheel is rotated. 5530A ALTERNATOR AND COMPONENTS Composition The alternator is a rotary machine that transforms mechanical energy into electrical energy. 1 - Rotor electromagnetic circuit 2 - Fitting rods 3 - Rectifier side support 4 - Negative heat dissipation plate 5 - Positive heat dissipation plate 6 - Zener type power press-fit diode 7 - Commutator 8 - Regulation unit 9 - Heat shield cover 10 - Rectifier side bearing 11 - Rectifier side inner fan 12 - Stator electronic circuit 13 - Control side support 14 - Control side inner fan 15 - Control side bearing As with all electrical machines, it is made up of two basic parts: inductor (rotor) and stator. The rotor for an alternator with internal ventilation is illustrated in the diagram below. Rotor The rotor consists of a cylindrical magnetic core, concentric to the driveshaft, with a toroidal coil winding and two opposing magnetic impellers which are magnetized by the winding located in the actual core. The impellers have six talon shaped poles each with reciprocal interpolation producing six alternate North poles and six South poles. There is therefore a single rotor winding which produces the e.m.f. for all the partial magnetic circuits. Stator The following diagram shows the stator. 1 - Star connection stator 2 - Triangle connection stator The stator consists of a ring shape pack joined by two or more axial seams electrically welded on the outer part. It is normally equipped with thirty six grooves which contain a three-phase winding made from copper wire insulated with vinyl acetate and connected, as necessary, in a star or triangle formation. Rectifier bridge The rectifier bridge is illustrated in the diagram. 1 - Zener type power diode 2 - Dissipation plate 3 - Alternator B + terminal Specifications of the bridge The bridge consists of: - Zener press-fit diodes. - Diodes fitted in the dissipator plates electrically welded to the connection terminals. - Sheared dissipator plates. - Large dimension dissipators. - Phase insulation until the connection with the bridge via a rubber cable duct. - Limitation of excess tension in the case of "+ battery" load disconnection guaranteed by zener diodes. 1 - Normal diode 2 - Zener diode Zener diodes The feature of both diodes, if polarized directly, is to pass the current from the anode to the cathode (V+ I+): then a zener diode behaves like a normal silicon diode. If inversely polarized, the current does not initially pass from the cathode to the anode up to value VZ. Beyond value VZ the normal diode is destroyed, the zener diode, on the other hand, continues to operate normally because its resistance in these conditions decreases sharply. Zener diodes are therefore voltage stabilizer diodes. Voltages of between 4.7 and 24 Volts are used in cars. It is one of the most important components in the regulation unit. It is often used for protection against polarity inversion or as protection against excess voltage. Specifications of internal ventilation alternators The main feature of this type of alternator, with a 115 mm stator diameter, is having dual internal ventilation with the vanes at an angle to guarantee the maximum flow of air and limit noise at the same time. For the same power output alternators with internal ventilation are smaller and lighter than types with external ventilation thereby satisfying current application requirements (there is always less space in engine compartments). In addition to this, in terms of quality, reliability and durability, these alternators meet higher standards than the best competition currently on the market. In depth studies and research have made it possible to introduce measures in production to reduce noise limits produced by various components (fluidynamics, magnetics, mechanics). In these conditions the energizing circuit (rotor) is enabled to earth by the regulator electronics. With the alternator rotating through the effect of the variation of the rpm and the magnetic field, a three-phase alternating voltage is produced in the electrical circuit (stator) which rectified by the diode bridge can exit terminal B+. When the upper fixed calibration level (13.7 - 14.2 V) is reached it charges the battery and supplies the system. The Body Computer checks the efficiency of the alternator recharging system by detecting two parameters: the voltage signal coming from terminal D+ of the actual alternator and the engine rpm signal received on the CAN from the engine management control unit. At the key-on as long as the voltage is below around 5.5 V, the Body Computer signals the insufficient recharging state; when the voltage exceeds 5.5 V, the warning light goes out; if, on the other hand, with the engine moving (speed above 700 rpm), the voltage decreases below the level of 4.5 V, then the warning light comes on constantly accompanied by the display of a message. 5530B BATTERY AND LEADS Specifications The main specifications of the batteries used on new models are the active material support plates produced thanks to the calcium lead production technology that has replaced the older antimony lead one. Control system The battery is fitted with an indicator for checking the charge which a water gauge that makes it possible to monitor the quality of the electrolyte level and the state of charge of the battery; this also allows the customer to make an initial check on the efficiency of the battery. This device comprises a transparent plexiglas cylinder: one end contains a gauge fastened to the cover of the battery; at the other end there is a drip tray, made from an acid-resistant material, drilled to allow contact between the battery electrolyte and a green coloured ball, housed in the drip tray, that can slide along a plane tilted towards the centre of the cylinder. The lights are activated by operating the light flasher stalk within 2 minutes of switching the engine off: each time the lever is operated, the period for which the lights are on is increased by 30 seconds to a maximum of 210 seconds. The function is excluded if the ignition is turned ON or if the flasher lever is operated for more than two seconds. Dipped beams The vehicle is equipped with two dipped beams in the headlamps. When the ring nut on the left steering column switch unit lever is turned twice, the dipped headlamps circuit is enabled. The switching on of the dipped headlamps is managed by the Body Computer: the dipped headlamps control function is activated through the enablement signals with the key inserted and turned to the ON position and the specific command from the steering column switch unit. With the dipped headlamps on, the simultaneous presence of the main beam and fog lights commands disables the dipped headlamps. The subsequent deactivation of one of these two commands, with the dipped headlamps control still on, means that the dipped headlamps will be turned back on again. Main beams The vehicle is equipped with two main beams in the headlamps. When the function is activated the warning light in the instrument panel comes on. A special relay managed by the Body Computer controls the activation of the fog lights; the function can be activated in certain conditions, namely: key in ON position enablement, control signal coming from the special switch and side lights on. If the side lights are switched off, the fog lights are also turned off; switching the side lights on later on does not involve the activation of the fog lights which will be restored when the appropriate button is pressed again. Rear foglamps The vehicle is equipped with two very bright rear fog lights located in the rear light clusters (moving part). Like for the fog lights, the function is activated by the special button located in the panel to the left of the steering wheel; when the lights are on the warning light in the instrument panel comes on. A special relay managed by the Body Computer controls the activation of the rear fog lamps; the function can be activated in certain conditions, namely: key in ON position enablement, control signal coming from the special switch and dipped headlamps or fog lights on. If the dipped headlamps or fog lights are switched off, then the rear fog lamps are also turned off; switching the dipped headlamps or the fog lights on later on does not involve the activation of the rear fog lamps which will be restored when the appropriate button is pressed again. If the key is switched off (OFF position) and then switched back to the ON position, the button must be activated again to turn on the rear fog lamps. Lights check This function makes it possible check the lighting system for the entire vehicle, in particular: - side lights and no. plate lights - direction indicators - brake lights - rear fog lamps The following is checked for each of the circuits: - circuit open or bulb missing - short-circuit to earth (bulb s.c. or wiring s.c. to earth) - short circuit to battery voltage (wiring short circuited to Vbatt.) When one of the situations described above is ascertained, the Body Computer makes the failure status available to the CAN: the "exterior lighting fault" warning light lights up on the instrument panel and the information is simultaneously shown on the display. In addition, the continuity of the protective fuse for the switch on the brake pedal is checked for the brake lights If there is a failure with one of the bulbs for the rear side lights, with the side lights on, the brake light on the same side comes on dimly to simulate the brightness of the side light. The system also detects any fault in the dusk sensor switching on the general failure warning light in the instrument panel if necessary and, at the same time, the information is shown on the display. In the direction indicators failure condition, the lights failure warning light in the instrument panel is lit up and the flashing frequency for the corresponding visual warning and the acoustic warning is increased; the flashing frequency of the exterior direction indicators and the LED in the hazard warning lights button, on the other hand, remains unchanged. A button, situated in the panel to the left of the steering wheel, controls the function, allowing the adjustment of the headlamps in four positions from 0 to 3. When the dipped headlamps are switched off, the movement is inhibited and the current position of the headlamp parabolas is maintained; when the dipped headlamps are switched on again, the headlamp alignment symbol will come on in the display with the number of the last position memorized. 1 - Alignment position indicator The headlamp alignment correcter function is managed directly by the Instrument Panel Node; if there is a fault in the system the headlamps assume a configuration that avoids oncoming vehicles from being dazzled. GAS DISCHARGE HEADLAMPS Introduction The lighting devices occupy a fundamental position amongst the vehicle's active safety systems. The need to improve the performance of current systems based on halogen bulbs in terms of the light flow emitted and the spectral distibution and life of the bulb has led to the development of gas discharge headlamps technology and the devices that allows its operation on the vehicle. There are basically three types of advantage from the development of this technology: - the increased light efficiency allows a reduction in the absorption of electrical energy; - the bulb lasts, on average, twice as long as a halogen bulb. The technology of gas discharge headlamps has led to the development of a series of devices that include: - xenon bulbs; - optics (reflective surface of the headlamp); - control electronics, comprising the igniter and the ballast; - automatic light beam alignment correction. Light cluster assembly Every light cluster includes the components necessray for the operation of the discharge bulb (bulb, igniter, control unit, dipped headlamp alignment control motor): the traditional components are also present (side lights, direction indicators). Section of headlamp by gas discharge bulb. 1 - Gas discharge bulb/igniter 2 - Ballast control unit The lamp contains the following bulbs: - W5W Blue Vision Long Life bulb (side lights function) - PY21W Silver bulb (front direction indicators function) - H1 55W bulb (main beam headlamps function) - D1S (OSRAM) bulb 35W (dipped/main beam headlamps function) The vehicle is equipped with a control unit for switching on and checking each headlamp, one right and one left, which are activated when the dipped headlamps function is requested controlled by the steering column switch unit turning the ring nut two positions. The CPS (left headlamp control unit) and CPD (right headlamp control unit) control units switch the gas discharge bulbs on and off at the times defined by the software and in accordance with international legislation. The CPS is the master control unit, whilst the CPD performs the slave role. The CPS acquires the command for the dipped headlamps, the vehicle speed VSO and the signals from the potentiometers located on the wheel axles. Depending on the inputs, the CPS directly controls the switching on of the left front headlamp (dipped headlamps) and similarly the CPD via the serial line. As a result, the CPD manages its own headlamp. The potentiometers on the wheel axles are used by the CPS for managing the headlamp alignment for both headlamps (directly for the left one and via the CPD for the right one). If there is a fault, the CPS positions the headlamps so that oncoming vehicles are not dazzled. The CPS carries out the fault diagnosis for the sub-system (CPS + CPD and the potentiometers on the axles) and memorizes the faults. The view of the connector and the pin out is illustrated below. Pin Function 1 Dipped headlight 3 Main beam headlight 4 Side light 5 Direction indicator 9 INT power supply 10 Speedometer signal (for left headlamp only) 11 Diagnostic line K 12 Master/Slave serial line 13 Electronic earth 14 Bulb earth Xenon bulb Xenon bulbs consist of a bulb containing two electrodes spaced a few millimetres apart and filled with low pressure xenon gas. The emission of light is produced by an arc between the two electrodes which is maintained during the operation of the bulb; this process is similar to what takes place in neon lights. Unlike the latter however, in automotive applications, it is unthinkable to have to wait for a few minutes before the process stabilizes, therefore the light cluster has an electronic control device (control unit) that allows operation, as far as the warming up times are concerned, comparable to traditional headlamps. View of D1S (OSRAM) 35W gas discharge bulb Pilot electronics Each bulb is controlled by pilot electronics comprising two devices: the ballast control unit and the igniter. The ballast has the function of converting the low voltage direct current coming from the battery into a medium tension alternating current and of controlling the operation of the sub-system in closed loop. For this purpose the ballast control unit is capable of controlling the voltage-current during the switching on stage in an excellent manner and it is capable of providing the bulb with the power required for operating when it is warmed up. The igniter is controlled by the ballast and is capable of producing the high tension (max 25 KV) required for te arc between the electrodes. The ballast for the left headlamp performs the MASTER function: it is the one that receives the signals from the sensors, processes them and transmits them to the ballast for the right SLAVE headlamp. OPERATION The operation of a xenon bulb is divided into four stages. Ignition During this stage the ballast produces a voltage capable of causing the engagement of a suitable device located in the igniter. A step-up transformer circuit transfers the suitably amplified excess voltage to the bulb thereby causing a discharge between the electrodes. Take-over (arc maintenance) During this stage (lasting several seconds) the bulb receives the excess power supply necessary for producing the rapid evaporation of the metallic halides contained in the bulb in order to guarantee that the operating brightness is reached quickly. In these conditions the bulb produces a light flash that is twice the intensity of normal for a period of about 100 microseconds. Warm up For a period of about two minutes, the ballast regulates the light intensity determining the physical state of the bulb from its impedance properties (closed loop control). Steady state The light beam is controlled continuously in closed loop in the steady state. 1 - Power supply (12V) 2 - High tension generator 3 - Square wave generator 4 - CPU 5 - Step-up transformer circuit A - Ballast B - Igniter C - Bulb On the new version the bulb forms one piece with the igniter. Main beam management The xenon bulbs have a dual function: dipped headlamp and stable main beam headlamp. The switching of the two functions takes place by means of an actuator located in the lower part of the elliptical module. The "flasher" function, on the other hand, allows the additional main beam headlamp bulbs only to come on. The Body Computer controls the power supply for the additional main beam headlamps and the electronics inside the headlamps (dipped/main beam headlamps xenon bulb switching motor) sending an earth signal to the engine compartment junction unit which energizes the specific relay for the function. Activation of the high beams in flashing mode is managed directly by the engine compartment control unit by means of two signals sent to the supplementary halogen bulbs (55W) built into the headlamps. These bulbs are active in fixed mode, but the high beam control (via xenon bulbs) renders them secondary. Automatic headlamp alignment correcter As a result of the brightness of the bulb light beam, the vehicle must be equipped with an automatic headlamp alignment correcter to prevent the driver's of oncoming vehicles being dazzled. The device intervenes in certain conditions: - static type, due to the distribution of the load; - dynamic type, due to acceleration and deceleration. The automatic correcter also guarantees improved driving comfort because the area lit is kept stable and your eyes do not have to constantly adapt to the variations in the lighting. This automatic device is managed by a stepping actuator and two load sensors connected to the front and rear suspension, on the left hand side. The correction in this case is carried out through the signal for the load sensors which periodically supply the vehicle alignment conditions. When the key is in the ON position, the control unit is activated and completely resets the headlamps to the exact distance calculated depending on the vehicle load which consists of lowering it and then repositioning it exactly. The adjustment does not take place immediately, but is filtered over a period of time to prevent undesired corrections (e.g. pothole or unmade roads). This correction is also made with the lights off, so that the moment the light beam is switched on it is already correctly positioned. The sensors are fastened to the bodyshell, whilst a lever positioned on them follows the movement of the suspension; they receives a power supply from the headlamp control unit and provide a linear output signal proportional to the position of the suspension in relation to the bodyshell. A - Part fastened to the bodyshell B - Part fastened to the suspension linkage a - Lever angle V - Sensor output signal voltage An adjustment actuator inside the light cluster produces the movement of the headlamp parabola, transforming rotary motion into linear motion. 1 - Stepping adjustment motor Self-diagnosis The electronics that manage the system have an autodiagnostic function that continuously checks operation. The control unit carries out continuous self-diagnosis of system operation. More specifically: - it detects and stores faults - it recognises the various components and the fault type The faults memorized in the control unit can be analyzed using the Examiner or other diagnostic equipment. Recovery The management logic for the autodiagnostic function also has a recovery function which, if errors are detected, automatically lowers the light beam so that it is not dazzling under any circumstances and guarantees sufficient lighting for driving safely until a Service Centre can be reached. Zeroing If one of the system components is replaced (headlamp, sensor, etc.) a self-learning procedure must be carried out, connecting to the diagnostic equipment, which makes it possible to autoamtically reset the system which should recognize the the position of the headlamp correctly aligned in position 0 from where the various adjustments can be set. Light beam manual adjustment In order to carry out the adjustment of the light beam manually, the two ring nus on the light cluster can be used: the ring nut on the outside of the unit is designed for the horizontal adjustment, the middle one for the vertical adjustment. The vertical adjustment takes place both by using the specific ring nut and also by turning the horizontal adjustment ring nut, thereby allowing the angular correction of the light beam. 1 - Vertical adjustment ring nut 2 - Horizontal/angular adjustment ring nut

Operation Display at key on The information in the standard display is: - date (on the 14 character alphanumerical line) - clock - milometer - headlamp alignment corrector information - outside temperature - ice symbol (in the case of ice danger) - automatic transmission readings (where present) With the ignition in the OFF position and the front doors closed, the display shows the clock and should not be lit up. The moment one of the front doors is opened in the key off position, the display will show: - clock - milometer Set-up menu display Access to the menu screen The buttons for the set-up are present in the controls, pressing "MODE" activates the ambient menu. The + and - buttons are used for navigating inside the menu. The menu set-up functions can be selected using the "MODE" / "+" / "-" buttons which should only be activated with the vehicle stationary with the exception of the following functions: "SPEED LIMIT EXCEEDED" (selecting activation/deactivation of speed limit and selecting speed limit level). Not all the functions can be activated during the fault message display cycles The operation should be the sequential type as described below. "MODE" buttons With 1 brief press: - if the vehicle speed is less than 4 km/h: activation of the "complete" set-up menu and shown on the display; - if the vehicle speed is above the 4km/h parameter: activation of the "reduced" set-up menu; - confirmation of the selected function; - confirmation of the setting/modification and return to the main menu screen (same option). With 1 long press and not on the release of the button: - memorizing of the modifications confirmed with the short press and return to the standard screen (or the screen activated before the "MODE" button was pressed briefly). "+" / "-" keys - Selection of functions present in the set-up menu. - Setting/adjustment of functions present in the set-up menu; The setting of the functions (e.g. clock adjustment) takes place in increasingly shorter steps depending on the time the button is kept pressed. Timeout If no operation is carried out for a period of 60 seconds, the standard screen is restored (or the screen activated before the "MODE" button was pressed). The following functions can be displayed whilst the vehicle is being driven by pressing the "MODE" button: - Introductory words for opening the menu - Selecting speed limit activation/deactivation - Selecting speed limit level - Dusk sensor sensitivity level adjustment - Menu exit The following functions can be displayed whilst the vehicle is stationary by pressing the "MODE" button: - Introductory words for opening the menu - Selecting speed limit level - Selecting speed limit activation/deactivation - Dusk sensor sensitivity level adjustment - TRIP B activation / deactivation. -- Clock adjustment - Hour mode (12h / 24h) - Date adjustment - Activation/deactivation of boot release together with unlocking of all the doors - Activation/deactivation of unlocking of front door only - Activation/deactivation of automatic locking of doors + boot above 20 km/h - Setting unit of measurement for distances - Setting unit of measurement for fuel consumption - Language setting - Volume of buzzer for alarms/failures/warnings - Button pressing buzzer volume (roger beep) - Reactivation of buzzer for SBR signalling - Service interval display (km/miles/days) - Menu exit Lighting dimmer The driver can adjustment the brightness inside the passenger compartment (lighting for graphics/gauges/control panel display and climate control) by pressing the "MODE +" and "MODE -" buttons. The lighting brightness cannot however be reduced to zero. The effect of the adjustment of the brightness (after pressing the buttons) is immediately visible. The dimming value is transmitted by the NQS via the CAN to allow the brightness value to be sent to the other Nodes. If the side lights are deactivated, the display is 100% lit up and the brightness cannot be adjusted (dimmed). The adjustment is only possible with the exterior lights on. The warning lights are not subject to adjustment/dimming (brightness always 100%). If the brightness is adjusted the first line of the display shows the message "Lighting" and the brightness adjustment symbols come on/go off. This screen remains for 5 seconds after the lst command is given after which the previous screen is displayed. The lighting for the display during the screens relating to the signalling of faults/information (with the exception of the ICE DANGER cycle) is not subject to adjustment/diming and the brightness always remains constant at 100% in daytime conditions (side lights deactivated). The display lighting during screens relating to other signals is, on the other hand, subject to adjustment/dimming. The "MODE +" and "MODE -" buttons remain activated to regulate the brightness of the control panel and the other vehicle components. However the message "Lighting" is not shown on the first line of the display and the brightness adjustment symbols come on/go off. Ice danger warning signal To warn the driver of the possible presence of ice on the road, if the outside temperature remains below 3 degrees C, the temperature reading flashes and the "snow" symbol and the "Ice danger" message are displayed in place of the clock . At the end of the warning cycle: - the message disappears and the screen prior to the event reappears; - the temperature reading stops flashing; - the "snow symbol" remains in the special area of the display (as long as T is below 6 °C). This display only takes one after the outside temperature is recognized to be T < 3°C and is only repeated if the temperature reaches the value T > 6°C and then returns again to T < 3°C. If the outside temperature at the key-on is T < 3° C, then the display shows the entire diagnostic cycle at the key-on (check in progress, etc. ad defined previuosly) and later on it initiates the "warning cycle" described above. Dusk sensor The dusk sensor sensitivity is adjusted by means of the special item in the setup menu. This adjustment is only possible with the vehicle stationary. It is possible, during the display, to adjust the setting of the dusk sensor from (1 to 3) shown in the control panel display using the "MODE +" and "MODE -" buttons. Once the setting is adjusted, it is memorized in the control panel and transmited on the CAN. The last setting memorized is displayed when the dedicated item is selected. The set-up menu item that allows the adjustment of the sensitivity levels is also present when the dusk sensor is present but not activated. This item should only appear if the dusk sensor is not present. Clock display The reading in hh:mm should always remain present at the key on and at the key off. The clock adjustment is an item in the set-up menu. It is also possible to select the hh:mm information from the set-up menu in 24h mode (0 - 23 h) or in 12h mode (1 - 12) without the indications AM and PM. Outside temperature reading The outside temperature reading should be guaranteed in standard screen conditions. At the key on, until the NQS receives the first frame with the outside temperature information, the part of the display dedicted to this information will show nothing; if, as a result of problems with the signal, the outside temperature information continues not to be present in the network for longer than the standard recovery time, some dashes with the unit of measurement set will be displayed in place of the temperature, e.g.: (---°C). Planned maintenance When the planned maintenance (so-called service) is close to the next interval, this is displayed automatically at the key on (after the initial check procedure), the spanner symbol and the "service" message followed by the number of kilometres or miles (depending on the unit of measurement set using the set-up menu (see chapter on "Functions that can be selected/activated using the "MODE"/"+"/"-") buttons until the next service. The display of the programmed maintenance information can also be shown if the user requests by selecting a special item in the setup menu. In this case the display is possible, irrespective of the intervals. There are 9 services in the Planned Maintenance Programme as follows: 1st service 2nd service 3rd service 4°, 5°, 6°, 7°, 8° 9th service After: - 30,000 km (or 18,000 mi) After:- 30,000 km (or 18.000 mi) from 1st service After:- 30,000 km (or 18.000 mi) from 2nd service After: ……………. After:- 30,000 km (or 18.000 mi) from 8th service The starting information for the "mileage" is 30,000 km (or 18,000 mi) and is set by the supplier of the instrument panel. The starting figure of 30,000 km is then suitably converted into miles by the control panel, in order to guarantee that the levels are recognized, corresponding to the signals in the display (as defined in the next paragraph). Counter reset by the service network At each service interval, the Service personnel should: - reset the "km" (or miles) counter to the starting vlue (30,000 km/18,000 mi) using the diagnostic equipment. It should be possible to read/rewrite the data using the diagnostic equipment. - memorize that the Planned Maintenance (service) has taken place.
