It should be possible to read/rewrite the data using the diagnostic equipment. The number of the service should decrease at each Reset-Info-Service beginning with the starting figure = 9 (decreasing from 9 to 0). If the instrument panel is being replaced, the Service personnel should: - reset the km/mi in the milometer. - read the number of services carried out and enter them into the new panel. - read the km/mi counters until the next service and enter them into the new panel. - read the last service date and rewrite it in the new control panel. If the battery is disconnected the data memorized in the control panel will be preserved. The only settings that need resetting are the date and the time. Follow me home function The following are shown on the control panel display: - the "follow me home" function activated message. - The total seconds set using the steering column switch unit which should not decrease during the display. - After the steering column switch unit has been pressed 7 times (210 seconds) it cannot increase further. The display of the screen for the FOLLOW ME HOME function remains for 20 seconds starting from the last time the steering column switch unit is pressed unless the function is deactivated during the display using the left steering column switch unit lever. This also takes place after the steering column switch unit is pressed for the seventh time. Rev counter This indicates the engine rpm with the help of a stepping motor. The control electronics and the operation is achieved by means of a microprocessor which guarantees the precision of the signal in the gauge. Odometer When starting, the milometer display shows the total or trip mileage in km memorized at the previous key off. The tripmeter is reset by keeping the TRIP button in the steering column switch unit pressed for more than 2 secs.; the total mileage can also be zeroed only once within the first 200 km. In the case of a new instrument the mileage reading is preceeded by and "H", after the first 200 km the letter "H" disappears automatically. Fuel level gauge The reading is the analogue type produced by a stepping motor, the control electronics and operation is achieved using a microprocessor. The fuel level is measured by a sensor in the tank which informs the Body Computer by means of an interface (microprocessor) transforming it into a percentage value. The system guarantees that there are no fluctuations/errors in the readings for the fuel gauge. The reading for the fuel reserve is siganlled by both the warning light and an acoustic signal through a buzzer inside the panel. Engine coolant temperature gauge The reading is the analogue type produced by a stepping motor, the control electronics and operation is achieved through a microprocessor, the red sector in the gaug signals the max. temperature correspondingn to the danger zone. TRIP COMPUTER General specifications The TRIP computer is a specific function that makes it possible to show various information in the control panel display relating to the operating state of the vehicle. These scales are summarized in the table below. Scales Units of measurement Decimal metric system Position Imperial Distance travelled km mi Instantaneous fuel consumption and average fuel consumption km/l l/100km mpg Range km mi Average speed km/h mph Trip time hh:mm hh:mm The control panel receives the following information to compute these scales (input): Control panel input Received from Instant distance, with % increase included NBC Fuel level (as a percentage of a full tank) NBC Capacity of fuel tank, in litres (memorized in NQS, calibration parameter entered during EOL programming) Memorized in the NQS Real instatnt speed (without increase) NBC Instantaneous fuel consumption (litres/hour) NCM Trip time counted Clock inside NQS The unit of measurement for the consumption can be set by the user (km/l or l/100km or mpg) All information appears individually in the display Whenever the battery is connected, all the TRIP values are reset. Measurement unit setting via the menu is maintained at all times. The counting/updating of the TRIP scales only takes place with the engine running. Zeroing by manual reset of one of the TRIP data items automatically resets all the others (apart from RANGE and INSTANTANEOUS FUEL CONSUMPTION). After this, the count for each data item proceeds independently of the rest. Resetting the General TRIP also resets TRIP B. TRIP B is reset independently. The resetting takes place by pressing the button for longer than 2 secs. (and not when the button is released). The automatic zeroing takes place when: - the distance travelled data item reaches the mileage limit of 9999.9 (km or mil); - when the trip time reaches the counter limit of 99.59; - every time the battery is reconnected General TRIP Range Distance travelled Average fuel consumption Instant fuel consumption Average speed Trip time TRIP B Distance travelled - B Average consumption - B Average speed - B Journey time - B The display cycle can be interrupted in two ways: - removing the cause of the malfunction that produced the problem; - the driver pressing the "MODE" button. In this case the screen prior to the fault will be reproposed but the signal should be kept activted through the warning light in the panel which should remain on until the cause of the malfunction that produced the fault is solved. The message corresponding to the TRIP function activated should be shown on the display (in other words in addition to "B" for selecting Trip B). It should be possible to exclude the display for TRIP B from the set-up menu. The control panel should always process the data for Trip B and then transmit it via the CAN even when the display in the actual panel is excluded using the set-up menu. Recovery If information is missing (no relevant CAN signals) some of the TRIP data will display the message "not available". If the speed sensor is faulty, all the TRIP counters display dashes "----" together with the data characteristics (with units of measurement) for each item (km or mi for range , km/h or mph for average speed etc.). If the fuel level sensor is faulty, dashes only "----" will be displayed for the Range, together with descriptions (with the relevant units of measurement) for each item. If the instant fuel consumption signal is not validated, dashes "-----" will be displayed for the Range, Average consumption, Instantaneous consumption together with descriptions (with the relevant unit of measurement) for each item. If the malfunction disappears, the counting of the various items continues in their different ways and the values downloaded prior to the mission are not reset and the mission is not restarted. Range The range indicates the estimated distance (in km or miles) that the car could travel with the fuel currently in the tank, assuming the mission is continued applying the same driving style (same fuel consumption conditions). The range is calculated using the following information: - received from the NBC; - instantaneous mileage; - fuel level (as a percentage of a full tank); - received from the NCM; instantaneous fuel consumption (in litres/hour); - fuel tank capacity, in litres (calibration parameter entered during the EOL programming - supplier). when the range is calculated for versions with DPR (Diesel Particulate Filter) a different value is used for the calculation parameters. Distance travelled The distance travelled by the vehicle from the start of the mission is indicated, i.e. from when the user carried out a rest by pressing the dedicated button. The reading is consistent with the display on the total mileage recorder. Each time the battery is reconnected and at the beginning of each new mission (reset), the display shows "0:0", after which the calculated value is displayed. At each key on, the value stored at the previous key off is displayed. When the maximum possible distance is reached, the mileage display should be automatically zeroed and, at the same time, there is a total TRIP reset with the exception of the Range and Instantaneous Consumption items. The calculation of the Distance Travelled is activated at the key on. The distance reading should be displayed and sent on the CAN with: - range between 0 and 9999.9 km (or mi) - resolution of 0.1 km (or miles) - update of display: every 0.1 km (or miles) Average fuel consumption Average fuel consumption measn the ratio between distance travelled since the start of the mission and number of litres consumed since the start of the mission. The control panel downloads the fuel consumption signal via the CAN and processes it to divide it by the distance travelled since the start of the mission. The calculation is only carried out with the engine running (300 rpm). At the start of a new mission, due to the battery being reconnected, the average consumption figure is initialized at the "predefined average standard consumption" value personalized for the vehicle/engine type. At the start of a new mission due, on the other hand, to a reset (by the user by pressing the dedicated button or a reset of one of the TRIP parameters) the Average Consumption value is initialized at the "average consumption value calculated during the previous mission". A weighting to be attributed to the above initial value to avoid excessive fluctuations in the reading shown during the first few minutes of the mission. The information displayed tends to represent the actual mission consumption condition within 3 minutes and the effect of the standard data becomes nil within 3 minutes. The value displayed is equal to "----" for a distance travelled by the vehicle from the start of the mission equal to the parameter 500 m, after which the value calculated will be displayed. At each key on, the value stored at the previous key off is displayed. The displayed average consumption is equal to"----", whenever: - The user resets the counter by pressing the dedicated button. - One of the TRIP parameters is reset. The value is displayed and sent on the CAN with: - resolution of 0.1 km/l (or mpg) - calculation precision: < 0.1 km/l (or mpg) - display updated every 10 s ± 0.1s - max value shown equal to 50 km/litre - 2 l/100km -99.9 mpg - min value shown equal to 4 km/litre - 25 l/100km - 2mpg Instantaneous fuel consumption The Instantaneous Fuel Consumption refers to the value of litres of fuel consumed per unit of distance travelled by the vehicle during the mission. The value displayed makes the user aware of the differences in fuel consumption connected with the style of driving without varying excessively and/or with inconsistent values. The Instantaneous Fuel Consumption is calculated using the following information: - received from the NBC; - instantaneous mileage - received from the NCM; instantaneous fuel consumption (in litres/hour) Average speed The average speed is calculated from the beginning of the mission, as a ratio between distance travelled and trip time. The calculation is only carried out with the engine running (300 rpm). Each time the battery is connected and at the start of each new mission (reset) the display will show "----" for a distance travelled by the vehicle from the start of the mission equal to the parameter 500 m after which the value calculated will be displayed. At each key on, the value stored at the previous key off is displayed. The displayed average speed is equal to"----", whenever: - The user resets the counter by pressing the dedicated button. - One of the TRIP parameters is reset. The value is displayed and sent on the CAN with: - resolution of 0.1 km/h (or miles) - calculation precision: < 0.1 km/h - display updated every 10 s ± 0.1s (10 s ± 0.1 s ). Journey time The trip time shows the time elapsed from the start of the mission, i.e. since the user reset the counter by pressing the dedicated button or an automatic reset occurred Each time the battery is reconnected and at the beginning of each new mission (reset), the display shows "0:00", after which the calculated value is displayed. At each key on, the value stored at the previous key off is displayed. If the vehicle is parked with the engine off (key off), the accumulated trip counter stops but does not reset to zero. The count resumes as soon as the vehicle sets off again (next key on - engine running). The counting of the Journey Time is activated at the key on with the engine running (parameter 300 rpm). Starting at the key on, the Journey Time is indicated in hh:mm and is sent on the CAN with: - range between 0:00 and 99:59 - resolution equal to 1 min. - display updated every minute - data update every second - the two dots between hh and mm flash during normal operation (frequency 1 Hz. – D.C. 50%) When the maximum possible value is reached (99.59), the journey time display should be automatically zeroed and, at the same time, there is a total TRIP reset with the exception of the Range and Instantaneous Consumption items. Buzzer specifications The buzzer function is produced by a piezoelectric acoustic signal. On versions with auto. trans. the buzzer is also responsible for the signals coming from the CAN as well as the specific signals for the Automatic Transmission. The function is also activated with the key off. Buzzer function access priority Since the buzzer function on the automatic transmission version is shared between the requirements of the panel and the requirements of the automatic transmission control unit, access priority is given to the Automatic Transmission Node function. This Node notifies the Panel of the decision/desire to activate the buzzer; the signal is the low active type and is managed directly by the microprocesssor. If the Automatic Transmission Node activation signal is present , the buzzer is activated by the electronic structure inside the Panel. In the case of a short circuit to earth for the pin involved, the stage is protected by there will be an increase in the stand by current. DPF SYSTEM On vehicles equipped with this system (DPF) certain operating conditions may occur on diesel engines that will have the following impact on the customer: 1) Particle Filter blocked: the GENERAL FAILURE warning light is activated and/or the display of a specific message in the Control Panel display (QdB) combined with an acoustic signal 2)Engine oil in poor condition: the minimum engine oil pressure warning light flashes with a specific message in the Control Panel display. Warnings to the customer If the Particle Filter is blocked, the following message is displayed: "Pollution control filter blocked, see manual" plus an acoustic signal If the oil is in poor condition, the minimum oil pressure warning light will flash and the display will show the following message: "Change the engine oil". The warning light must be reset at each oil change. For further details See descriptions 1080B EXHAUST EMISSION CONTROL SYSTEM

OPERATION Systems for the control of petrol and diesel engines offer Cruise Control as a function, i.e. a system that automatically maintains a cruising speed set by the driver. The Cruise Control system control is integrated in the steering column switch unit which controls the direction indicators and the front/rear windscreen wiper. The location of the Cruise Control system control is illustrated in the diagram. 1 - Cruise Control stalk 2 - Lighting/turn signal stalk 3 - Horn / radio controls connector (Steering Wheel Node) 4 - Air Bag connectors 5 - Front/rear wiper control stalk 6 - Clock spring The third lever for the steering column switch unit incorporates the Cruise Control system controls, namely: - the ring nut switch for activating/deactivating the system; - the lever with the vehicle speed increase/decrease memorizing function; - the Resume button that calls up a saved speed. 1 - Resume button recalls a stored speed; 2 - Lever with the vehicle speed increase/decrease memorizing function; 3 - Ring nut switch (ON: Cruise attivated; OFF: Cruise deactivated). Pin Out (six way connector) Pin Function 1 Resume control positive signal 2 Ignition-operated power supply 3 N.C. 4 Cruise control on positive signal 5 Deceleration (-) control positive signal 6 Acceleration (+) control positive signal The electronic system is managed by the engine management control unit. It automatically maintains the cruising speed set by the user through the direct management of the engine. Memorizing the speed selected To activate the operation of the Cruise Control: - operate the ring nut switch to the ON position; - let the vehicle reach the desired speed; it should be remembered that the Cruise Control can only be activated for speeds above 40 km/h. It is advisable to engage it in fourth gear or higher where the road conditions allow the speed set to be maintained safely. - push the steering column switch unit lever upwards to increase the speed, the lever returns automatically (unstable). - release the accelerator pedal and let the system work directly; - the warning light in the instrument panel should come on constantly with the signal coming from the engine management control unit, via the CAN, indicating the Cruise Control operating status. The warning light going out indicates that the system is deactivated. Variation in the speed memorized If you wish to alter the vehicle speed memorized it is necessary to: (A) Speed increase: - push the lever upwards: this produces an acceleration ramp at a constant, programmable gradient; - when the lever is released (automatic return), the system keeps the new speed reached by the vehicle memorized. (B) Speed decrease: - push the lever downwards: having achieved the reduction in the vehicle speed in relation to the speed set previously using the Cruise Control, release the lever and the system will maintain the new vehicle speed. The Cruise Control system can operate throughout the permitted engine rpm range and can manage cars with manual or automatic/sequential gearboxes. System adjustment does not cut in under the following circumstances: - with a manual gearbox, in neutral, reverse, 1st speed; - with an automatic/sequential transmission, with the lever in position P, N, R and 1st speed. Resume button function This function makes it possible, by pressing the button, to return the vehicle to the last speed value memorized if the Cruise Control has been switched off in certain circumstances (for example, by operating the clutch or braking). Deactivation of the cruise control (A) The Cruise Control is deactivated by the user by: - operating the ring nut switch to the OFF position; - switching the engine off; - operating the clutch pedal or brake pedal (in such cases, the last speed achieved is stored and can be recalled by pressing the Resume button); - placing the automatic/sequential gear lever in position N, P, R (in such cases, the last speed achieved is stored and can be recalled by pressing the Resume button); - vehicle speed below the minimum permitted (about 40 km/h) or above the maximum permitted; for versions with a manual gearbox, if the lever is operated without using the clutch, consistency between the engine rpm and the vehicle speed starts to fail; in all cases, pressing the Resume button allows the system to be reactivated. Activating the accelerator with the Cruise Control activated: by pressing the accelerator (for example to overtake) the Cruise Control system allows a momentary increase in the speed of the vehicle being momentarily deactivated, but as soon as the accelerator pedal is no longer pressed, the system reactivates the speed setting memorized. The recognition of the gear engaged is carried out by comparing the vehicle speed with the engine speed with the clutch engaged. (B) The Cruise Control is automatically deactivated if: - accidental or incorrect operation of the buttons on the lever takes place; - the acceleration is above the calibrated limit (e.g. steep descent); - the deceleration is above a calibrated limit (e.g. the gear selector lever is operated without using the clutch); - there is a fault in the system; - the ABS or ESP intervene. The system turns off automatically when the signals used by the Cruise Control software are incorrect because they are due to component defects: - vehicle speed sensor; - accelerator pedal potentiometer; - brake switch plausibility; - clutch switch plausibility; - Cruise control switch plausibility and Resume key; - Cruise switch plausibility and speed increase or decrease lever positions. The Cruise Control system is also deactivated if errors occur in components that impair engine operation, namely: - engine management control unit; - engine rpm sensor; - electronic throttle body sensors/actuators (for petrol engines); - engine load meter (for petrol engines), - ignition coils (for petrol engines), - injectors; - high pressure system components (for diesel engines). A serious malfunction of the engine management system of the Cruise Control system that requires the Cruise Control system to become "blocked" (i.e. disabled until the vehicle is switched off) is defined as a "fault". A "problem" is an irregular situation (due to a malfunction or incorrect command by the user such as, for example, the simultaneous accidental activation of the Resume and (+) (-) buttons that causes the Cruise Control system to be deactivated but does not require it to be locked. In the case of both faults and problems an error code that can be read using the diagnostic equipment is memorized, but these Cruise Control errors do not cause the engine failure warning light or the Cruise Control warning light to come on.

INTRODUCTION The vehicle is equipped with an electronic control system that governs the acivation of specific containment devices in the event of frontal or side impact. The frontal protection system includes the dual stage driver and passenger front Air Bags, the driver's keen Air Bag, front seat belts with pretensioners and a load limiter fitted onthe buckle with a belt fastened sensor, rear seat belts with pretensioners and a load limiter on the reel, two additional impact sensors and a manual passenger Air Bag disabling switch (OPT). The side protection system comprises two Air Bags housed in the side members under the roof, two Side Bags on the front seats and two side impact sensor; two Side Bags for the rear seats are available as an optional extra with the disabling switch fitted on the right rear parcel shelf mounting bracket. The vehicle is also equipped with a passenger presence sensor - SBR - fitted on the seat. The presence of the SBR sensor on the passenger seat makes it possible to prevent unnecessary signalling at the instrument panel if the seat belt is not fastened. All versions are equipped with 7 Air Bags fitted as standard (dual stage activation front, driver's knee bag, side on the front seats and window bags) and two available on request (side on the rear seats) making a total of 9 units. The front protection system features new SMART AIR BAG activation software that automatically adapts activation parameters according to impact severity and whether or not the seat belts are worn. Driver and passenger front airbags feature two-stage activation: when the impact is of medium severity the electronic control unit only activates the first Air Bag intervention stage avoiding the emission of unnecessary energy for the protection of the occupant. Conversely, in the case of very severe impact, the control unit activates both stages to absorb most of the kinetic energy from the occupant's body before it strikes the steering wheel or dashboard. In this case the driver's knee protection Air Bag is also activated. Two additional ECS “Early Crash Sensor” near the front light clusters also help the electronic control unit to operate more quickly than a conventional system so that the airbag activation stage is completed before the occupant's body begins to move towards the steering wheel or dashboard. In addition, these senors detect underbody stresses or impacts for which the activation of the Air Bags is not necessary as there is no risk to the occupants. The air bag system components are designed to work on a specific vehicle. They therefore CANNOT be tampered with, adapted or installed on other types of vehicle. The car must be handed over to the customer with the passenger airbag deactivation switch in the ON position and control panel warning lights off. For safety reasons, NO continuity checks can be carried out on the wiring. The electrical connection beween the Air Bag system components is achived through dedicated wiring featuring a yellow outer casing, incorporated in the dashboard cable loom as far s the front devices are concerned and in the seat cable loom as far as the Side Bags and the front pretensioners are concernerd and in the rear cable loom as far as the lateral devices and the rear pretensioners are concerned. The control unit is connected to the system via two connectors, one for the dashboard lead and the other for the rear lead. The control unit is connected to the vehicle CAN, through which it exchanges information with other nodes, turns on warning lights in the instrument panel and performs diagnostic operations. Because the control unit is a node in the CAN , the airbag system has the following possibilities: - connection to the standard diagnostic socket via the CAN and not the dedicated K line; - connection to the instrument panel for the operation of the warning lights; - connection to the panel to satisfy the EuroNCAP protocol which involves a series of warnings if the seat belts are not fastened; - connection to the Body Computer for potential end of line customisation (Proxi) with a consequent reduction in the number of spare parts. The front airbag module on the passenger side may be deactivated voluntarily by means of a special key-operated switch on the side of the facia (OPT). GRAVE DANGER! The front airbag module MUST be deactivated if a child seat is fitted to the front passenger seat. If the vehicle does not have a passenger Air Bag disabling switch (OPT device) it is ABSOLUTELY prohibited to put a child seat on the front seat. Front passenger side airbag module deactivation does not disable the sidebag modules. This means that any children carried in the car are protected against side impact. COMPOSITION The system consists of the following devices: - an electronic control unit; - two (driver and passenger) front air bags with dual stage activation, - an Air Bag protecting the driver's knees; - two frontal impact detection sensors ECS (Early Crash Sensor); - passenger air bag manual disabling switch (OPT); - passenger presence sensor on the seat (SBR); - two front electronic pretensioners on the seat belt buckles; - two Side Bags on the front seats; - two window bag modules for the side protection of occupants; - two side impact sensors in the side pillars; - two Side Bags on the rear seats; - rear air bags manual disabling switch; - two rear side electronic pretensiners on the reel. The following indications show the system is working properly: - signalling warning light in the instrument panel; - passenger air bag disabled warning light in the instrument panel; - rear side air bags disabled warning light in the instrument panel; - connection via B-CAN with the diagnostic socket included in the Body Computer for checking the operation using the EXAMINER. 1 - Electronic control unit. 2 - Front passenger Air Bag disabling switch 3 - Rear sidebag deactivation switch 4 - Passenger side airbag module 5 - Driver's airbag module 6 - Driver's knee airbag module 7 - Passenger sidebag module 8 - Driver's sidebag module 9 - Passenger side impact sensor 10 - Driver's side impact sensor 11 - Passenger window bag module 12 - Driver's window bag module 13 - Passenger side pretensioner 14 - Driver's side pretensioner 15 - Rear pretensioners 16 - Driver's front impact sensor 17 - Passenger front impact sensor 18 - Passenger presence sensor (SBR) 19 - Left rear Side Bag module 20 - Right rear Side Bag module 21 - Air Bag system fault indication warning light 22 - Passenger side front airbag deactivation warning light 23 - Seat belt not fastened warning light 24 - Rear Air Bag deactivation warning light ELECTRONIC CONTROL UNIT 1 - Electronic control unit. 2 - Indication showing direction of motion The control unit is the central processing unit for the occupant protection system: it is firmly secured to the floor of the vehicle by the centre tunnel. It manages all the containment system detection and activation devices by processing signals from the various sensors distributed throughout the vehicle and internal sensors. The control unit should always be fitted with the arrow (2), stamped on the adhesive plate, facing the direction of travel of the vehicle. Always check that there are no foreign bodies between the control unit and the bodyshell and tighten the fixing bolts to the recommended torque. Composition The control unit contains an electronic deceleration sensor tht enables safety device activation. This sensor consists of two-directional accelerometers that are part of the ECS front sensor and power the operation of the side sensors. Operation Frontal impact When the impact is of medium severity the electronic control unit only activates the first Air Bag intervention stage avoiding the emission of unnecessary energy for the protection of the occupant. Conversely, in the case of very severe impact, the control unit activates both stages to absorb most of the kinetic energy from the occupant's body before it strikes the steering wheel or dashboard. For very serious impacts the driver's knee Air Bag module intervenes to afford greater protection. In addition, two supplementary ECS sensors also allow the airbags and pretensiners to be activated earlier than a conventional system so that the airbag activation stage is completed before the occupant's body begins to move toward the steering wheel or dashboard. Side impact Similarly, when side impact occurs, the control unit is able to recognise direction and intensity and thus activate the two front and rear Side Bags and the two Window Bags on the side affected by the impact. To provide total cover against side impacts, two satellite sensors located in the centre pillars are used. When a side impact takes place, the satellite sensors detect the impact signal directly along the transverse axis of the vehicle and send it to the Node. When processed by the control unit microprocessor, this signal reveals the severity of the side impact and is thus able to decide whether to operate the sidebags on the affected side, only if the control unit safety sensor enables the activation. The side Air Bags (Window Bags and Side Bags) are activated simultaneously and independently of the front safety devices. After each activation of one of the controlled systems (pretensioners, front airbags, sidebags), the control unit stores the activation in its permanent memory and controls activation of the fault warning light on the instrument panel. Before it is replaced, the control unit guarantees activation of individual devices within the following limits: - 3 impacts with activation of front seat belt pretensioners alone; -3 impacts in total with side bag activation (right or left); - 1 impact with activation of the pretensioners and front airbags; - any combination of the above cases up to the maximum number. If one of the limits described is not reached, it will be possible to reuse the control unit after carrying out the RESET procedure using the EXAMINER once system operating conditions have been restored. The final activation, corresponding to the maximum number for the limits indicated above, will prevent further reset procedures. More specifically: - it detects and stores faults; - it diagnoses connnections to system components and any type of fault that has occurred; - it indicates the source of these faults by turning on an instrument panel warning light. Faults stored in the control unit may be deleted only after the fault has been repaired by means of the EXAMINER device. If a fault is detected in the passenger airbag disablement switch (where fitted), the control unit treats is as though it is off for safety reasons. Module operation is therefore inhibited and the instrument panel warning light is turned on. DRIVER'S AIR BAG MODULE The following figure shows an assembly view 1 - Cover 2 - Bag 3 - Containment case 4 - Gas generator connectors Specifications The driver side air bag is a passive safety device. It takes the form of a bag that inflates automatically in the case of frontal impact to interpose itself between the driver's body and front passenger compartment structures. The airbag module is installed in the middle of the steering wheel. The module cover also acts as a horn control. Composition The module comprises: - a plastic cover that tears at preset points when activated to allow the bag to expand correctly. - a 60 litre bag, made out of nylon thread woven to minimse skin abrasions in the case of contact and folded in such a way as to ensure that inflation is gradual and not directed toward the driver; - two pyrotechnic type gas generators; - a containment case. Operation Bag inflation is determined by a gas generator that offers two intervention stages that can be activated separately according to impact severity. Each gas generator is activated by two electrical resistances that burn propellent inside the generator to allow the bag to expand. Bag inflation opens the flap on the dashboard along predefined cut lines. When fully inflated, the bag is in an optimal position to protect the occupant. Bag deflation is immediate, due to the hole present in the lower part of the bag. This hole also softens contact between passenger and bag to avoid the risk of abrasions. PASSENGER AIR BAG MODULE 1 - Cover 2 - Bag 3 - Gas generator connectors Specifications The passenger airbag module is a passive safety device that protects the front passenger in the event of front impact by means of a bag that interposes itself between the occupant and the vehicle dashboard. Composition The module comprises: - a metal containment mount; - a paper bag protection that opens along predefined tear marks in the event of activation to allow the bag to emerge; - a 100 litre bag in nylon, a fabric that minimises skin abrasions in the event of contact. The bag is folded so that it does not inflate directly towards the occupant. - two pyrotechnic type gas generators; - mounting brackets on the crossmember; Operation The passenger airbag operates in exactly the same way as the driver's side airbag. Bag inflation opens the flap on the dashboard along predefined cut lines. When fully inflated, the bag is in an optimal position to protect the occupant. The braids inside the airbag unfold in such a way as to allow inflation to the maximum specified dimensions to prevent collateral damaging effects on passengers. Inflation is immediate due to the presence of 2 vent holes in the end of the bag. KNEE AIR BAG MODULE (DRIVER'S SIDE) 1 - Gas generator 2 - Bag 3 - Cover Specifications An Air Bag module has also been fitted in the lower part of the dashboard, under the steering wheel. This module, in addition to protecting the lower limbs, increases protection for the driver, particularly by preventing them from sliding forward, which is a possible cause of injury, particularly to the chest. Composition The knee bag module consists of a metal container that houses the gas generator and a nylon bag. The container is secured to a mounting plate and a safety plate that secures it rigidly to the lower part of the dashboard. Operation The gas generator is electrically activated by means of a signal from the electronic control module. Following this signal, a pyrotechnic activation is triggered that causes the gas in the generator to expand. The expanding gases emerge through openings to inflate the bag. When the bag is inflated, the bag is in an optimum position to perform its role of protecting the driver. Bag deflation is immediate due to the presence of vent holes in the end of the bag. SIDE BAG MODULE The following figure shows an assembly view 1 - Seat trim 2 - Side bag module 3 - Power lead Specifications The front seats contain two side bag modules installed beneath the trim to increase the protection offered by the body in the event of side impact. This device ensures the airbag is always in an optimum position in relation to the occupant, regardless of the angle of the seat or the size of the occupant. The side bag protects the chest area and also - together with the door panels - protects critical areas of the body such as the ribs and abdomen. Its position on the seat always ensures maximum efficacy irrespective of seat position, even if the seat occupant is not seated correctly, because bag opening dynamics minimise the risk of body damage due to impact against the body. Do not cover the front seat squab with extra covers. Do not wash the seat squab with water or steam under pressure. Composition The side bag module consists of a metal container that houses the gas generator and a nylon bag with a volume of 11 litres. The module container includes a paper bag protection with preset break points. When the backrest cover is fitted, the exterior of the trim in the area over the bags includes seams designed to yield easily to allow the bag to inflate. The module is connected to the electrical system by means of two leads with yellow sheaths. These are contained, together with the seat earth connection lead, in a protective fabric-lined duct secured to the seat structure. Both leads end in a green connector. The connectors are secured to a mounting that can be extracted on the bottom of the actual seat. Operation The gas generator is electrically activated by means of a signal from the electronic control module. Following this signal, a pyrotechnic activation is set off that causes the gas in the generator to expand. The gases expand and emerge through openings to inflate the bag. Bag inflation causes the weak seams in the backrest trim to yield and allow the bag to emerge. When fully inflated, the bag is in an optimal position to protect the occupant. Bag deflation is immediate due to the presence of two vent holes in the end of the bag. Rear side Air Bags In this case too the Side Bags protect the chest and, together with the door panels, guarantee protection in the critical areas of the body like the ribs and the abdomen. Their installation at the sides of the seat backrest always guarantee maximum protection. The operating principle is the same as for the rear Side Bags. SIDE WINDOW BAG MODULE Assembly view 1 - Connector 2 - Gas generator 3 - Bag retaining bands 4 - Bag 5 - Sealing brace Specifications The window bags are activated together with the sidebags and interpose themselvers between the occupant and the vehicle to prevent the head coming into contact with highly intrusive objects such as glass, pillars etc. Because the window bags extend from the front pillar to the luggage compartment, they protect front and rear passengers. The window bag system offers the best performance due to the broad area covered and their ability to be self-supporting even without a backing. The permeability of the bag guarantees protection even in "long" impact situations such as roll over. Composition The window bag module consists of: - a gas generator secured by mounts to the rear car pillar; - a flexible pipe in permeable cloth secured by a band to the gas generator that diffuses the gas evenly over the entire length of the bag; - a bag of about 29 litres in volume secured to the gas generator together with a flexible pipe. It is made out of permeable nylon and folded inside a containment sleeve. When inflated, the bag is designed to ensure impact energy is correctly absorbed while maintaining the occupant's head at an appropriate distance from the impact area. Once inflation is completed, gas is expelled through the porous fabric. - easy-opening plastic clips that secure the bag to the ceiling rail; - a retaining strap secured to the front pillar that holds the bag in position once inflated; Operation The gas generator is electrically activated by means of a signal from the electronic control module. Following this signal, a pyrotechnic activation is set off that causes the gas in the generator to expand. The expanding gas emerges through special openings and is distributed evenly along the length of the bag through the hose to make the bag inflate. the increase in bag volume causes the fastening container to break, the sleeve seams to yield and the trim to open. Everything is arranged so that the bag emerges correctly downward. The bag is made to inflate correctly by a retaining belt on the front end of the bag. When fully inflated, the bag is in an optimal position to protect the occupants. The bag deflates immediately after being inflated by the gas because the fabric is permeable. CLOCK SPRING 1 - Electrical connectoin for connecting air bag first stage 2 - Electrical connection for connecting air bag second stage 3 - Steering wheel electrical function lead 4 - Steering column switch unit 5 - Clock spring Specifications The clock spring transfers the electrical signal to controls on the steering wheel (horn and other optional radio controls) and connects the airbag module without risk of breakage. The device, composed of two plates, is an integral part of the steering column switch unit. Inside the two plates, the leads connecting the Air Bag module, the steering wheel control unit and, on the basic version, the horn buttons are wound in a coil so that they can follow steering wheel movements. The pin out for the clock spring is illustrated below: Pin Function 1 Negative signal from horn control button 2 N.C. 3 B - CAN B 4 B - CAN A 5 Ignition-operated power supply 6 Earth 7 N.C. 8 N.C. 9 Level 2 airbag (+) 10 Level 2 airbag (-) 11 Level 1 airbag (-) 12 Level 1 airbag (+) Composition The clock spring has three connections on the steering wheel side: two are designed to connect the Air Bag module (first and second stage), one for connecting the electrical functions for the steering wheel (horn or radio controls control unit NVO plus horn, depending on the version). Operation Inside the two plates, the leads connecting the air bag module and the various electrical functions are wound into a spiral with sufficient coils to follow the steering wheel rotations. The upper plate is turned by fasteners on the inside of the retaining ring that fit into the seat on the steering wheel hub. In the working position, the steering wheel presses on the ring to release it from its fasteners and thus allow both plates to turn freely. When the steering wheel is removed, the spring-loaded ring locks rotation between both plates. This function prevents the upper plate, now no longer secured to the steering wheel, from turning freely and unwinding or winding the coil inside the device and possibly causing it to break. The clock spring on the version known as stand alone should never be separated from the steering column switch unit to prevent damaging the rotation and release device. Before fitting the steering wheel in its housing, break the red key for the steering column switch unit that guarantees it. Once the nut tightening the steering wheel is removed, it cannot be reused and should be replaced. FRONT IMPACT SATELLITE SENSORS The location of the ECS front impact sensors is described below Specifications The additional ECS “Early Crash Sensor” located on the ends of the headlamp carrier crossmember helps the electronic control unit to operate more quickly than a conventional system so that the airbag activation stage is completed before the occupant's body begins to move towards the steering wheel or dashboard. In addition, these senors detect underbody stresses or impacts for which the activation of the Air Bags is not necessary as there is no risk to the occupants. SIDE IMPACT SATELLITE SENSORS Location of side impact sensor 1 - Satellite side impact sensors 2 - Link connection Specifications The side protection system consists of the airbags and also an electronic control circuit that ensures the system operates correctly. Two satellite sensors containing an accelerometer are installed inside the side pillars to measure accelerations resulting from side impact. Operation If the acceleration level detected by the relevant sensor causes a given threshold to be exceeded, the information is compared with a measurement obtained by a safety sensor in the air bag system electronic control unit. If the measured values are consistent, the control unit controls activation of the side bags and window bags on the side affected by impact. PASSENGER SIDE AIR BAG DISABLEMENT KEY SWITCH (OPTIONAL) A switch located in the dashboard on the passenger side allows the user to deactivate the passenger air bag so that a child seat can be installed without problems. On the front seats, child seats are positioned facing towards the back of the car. Operation An switch operated by means of the emergency key in the TEG allows enablement (ON) and disablement (OFF) of the air bag module on the passenger side. In this case, the control unit cuts out passenger air bag activation but enables normal operation of the pretensioner (only with seat belt fastened) and the side bags. This happens because if a passenger is present but the switch has been left OFF by accident, the air bag will not activate - only the pretensioner. Deactivation is indicated by a warning light in the instrument panel coming on. Composition 1 - key-operated switch 2 - OFF position: Passenger air bag disabled 3 - ON position: Passenger air bag enabled 4 - Passenger side disablement warning light The unit consists of a case that houses the switch, a key barrel inserted in the case and held in place by a clip and a plate that indicates the positioned assumed by the switch (ON or OFF). Switch faults are indicated by activation of the air bag system fault warning light. During the normal key on diagnostic procedure (4 seconds), the electronic control unit checks switch status. If the status identified is OFF, the module is excluded from possible activation, the corresponding signal is saved and the warning light in instrument panel comes on. If the status identified at the end of the four second diagnostic procedure is ON, the warning light flashes for a further four seconds and then goes off. In the case of switch anomalies or faults, the system reacts as follows: - passenger side module is not activated - air bag system fault warning light comes on - passenger side air bag module disablement warning light comes on - deactivation status is saved. The switch is not operated with the ignition key ON (e.g. using the second key). In this case, the electronic control unit saves an error, indicates it by turning on the air bag system fault warning light and deactivates the module. REAR AIR BAGS DISABLEMENT KEY SWITCH A switch operated by means of the emergency key in the TEG allows enablement (ON) and disablement (OFF) of the rear Side Bag modules. In this case the control unit excludes the activation of the Side Bags, but not the pretensioners (only with the seat belt not fastened). This is because if the passengers are not present but the switch has been incorrectly left OFF, the Side Bags doe not intervene but only the other side devices intervene (window bags, front side bags). Deactivation is indicated by a warning light in the instrument panel coming on. Composition 1 - Casing 2 - Connector 3 - Key barrel 4 - Plate 5 - Rear side bags disabled warning light FRONT SEAT BELT PRETENSIONERS The seat belt pretensioners are pyrotechnic devices incorporated in the buckle which attaches to the belt. In the case of a frontal impact, the pretensioner intervenes recovering the inevitable lengthening of the actual belt due to the action of the weight of the body which is kept as close as possible to the seat. If the belt remains close to the body, it can absorb the kinetic energy produced during the impact very gradually. Operation Having detected an impact, the control unit activates the ignition circuit which supplies the gas generator (1) in a similar way to the Air Bag module. The pressure of the gas, created by the combustion of the propellant inside the generator (1) is applied ot the surface of the piston (2) and produces a force that is exerted on the latter in the cylinder (3). There is a steel cable (4) fitted on the piston (2) whose end is connected to the seat belt mounting. The movement of the piston (2) drives the buckle downwards shortening the actual belt by a few centimetres recovering the lengthening and any slack. After activation the pretensioner stops working and cannot, under any circumstances, be repaired. The activation is signalled by the special Air Bag warning light in the instrument panel. The pretensioner intervention levels are lower than those for Air Bags which means that impacts in which only the pretensioner intervenes can take place. Seat belt fastened sensors for front seats When seat belts are not worn and therefore there is a considerable risk of serious injury even for slight impacts compared with when the occupant is wearing a seat belt, the special seat belt fastened sensors in the front belt buckles, in addition to activating the alarm warning light in the panel and the buzzer, allow the control unit to adapt the activation of the Air Bags and prevent the activation of the pretensioners (which, as the saet belts are not fastened, would only create an additional cost in the repair of the vehicle). REAR SEAT BELT PRETENSIONERS 1 - Gas generator 2 - Electrical connector 3 - Belt 4 - Reel Specifications The pretensioners are pyrotechnic devices that are activated electrically by means of a signal from the electronic control unit. They are built into the rear seat belt reel. Activation of the seat belt pretensioners is controlled by the same strategy as the air bags. The pretensioners are designed to take up slack in the seat belt to ensure it holds the occupant against the backrest from the first moments of impact, thus reducing movement inside the passenger compartment. The belts are also equipped with load limters that decrease the force transmitted by the belts to the chest. Operation When the car decelerates to a sufficient extent, as measured by system acceleromters, the electronic sensor in the electronic control unit sends a signal to trigger the gas generator pyrotechnic charges. The combustion of the propellant creates a chemical reaction producing inert gases whose pressure generates a force that pushes a piston upwards, changing the rotary movement of the reel to the opposite direction of the belt unwinding, rewinding it by a few centimetres. AIRBAG SYSTEM WARNING LIGHTS 1 - Air Bag system fault warning light 2 - Passenger side disablement warning light 3 - Seat belt not fastened warning light 4 - Rear side bags disabled warning light Air Bag system fault warning light With the TEG inserted and turned ON, the Air Bag system fault warning light (red) comes on for about four seconds (initial self-diagnosis stage) and then goes off. If the control unit detects a fault in the warning light, it saves the corresponding fault code. If no system faults are detected at key on and no fault conditions are present in the fault memory, the warning light goes off after four seconds of self-diagnosis. Otherwise it stays on. The warning light stays or comes on durng normal car operation in the following cases: - the control unit detects a fault in the airbag system; - the control unit detects a crash with system activation; - when a fault is detected in the warning light connection circuit. As a consequence of a crash when the pretensioners or sidebags alone are activated, the warning light stays on until system operating conditions are restored (replacement of affected part or control unit repair using an EXAMINER) If the crash causes the front airbag modules to activate, the warning light stays on permanently because the control unit cannot reset (in this case the control unit must be replaced). If internal operating errors occur during the operational lifetime of the control unit that cannot be repaired by means of the EXAMINER, these are indicated by permanent activation of the warning light. Passenger Air Bag disabled warning light With the TEG inserted and turned ON, the amber yellow passenger side air bag disabled warning light comes on for about four seconds (initial self-diagnosis stage) and flashes for the next 4 seconds. If the control unit detects a fault in the warning light, it saves the fault code, turns on the fault warning light and keeps the rear Side Bag modules disabled. System operation is restored by means of an EXAMINER as with the fault warning light. The disabling of the passenger side module MUST only be carried out in key off conditions: otherwise, this operation causes an error to be stored in the control unit. Rear side bags disabled warning light With the TEG inserted and turned ON, the amber yellow rear Side Bags disabled warning light comes on for about four seconds (initial self-diagnosis stage) and flashes for the next 4 seconds. If the control unit detects a fault in the warning light, it saves the fault code, turns on the fault warning light and keeps the rear Side Bag modules disabled. System operation is restored by means of an EXAMINER as with the fault warning light. The disabling of the rear modules MUST only be carried out in key off conditions: otherwise, this operation causes an error to be stored in the control unit. Seat Belt Reminder "FIRST WARNING CYCLE" WARNING LIGHT SIGNAL The "seat belts" warning light signals that the (driver's or passenger side) seat belts are not fastened in accordance with the following strategy: - the warning light comes on in fixed mode, at key-on, if the seat belt has not already been fastened; - the warning light comes on in fixed mode if, with key on, the belt is unfastened (unless the following conditions apply, when the warning light should flash); - the warning light comes on in fixed mode if, with key on, the belt is unfastened (unless the following conditions apply, when the warning light should flash); - the warning light goes out if, the seat belt is fastened at key on. - the warning light should remain off at key off. The signalling via the warning light on constantly can never be excluded. "WARNING CYCLE": WARNING LIGHT AND HORN SIGNAL The warning cycle is activated for 90 seconds if, with the seat belt not fastened and the key inserted (key on status), at least one of the following conditions is verifed: - time elapsed equal to 60 secs and vehicle speed above 10 km/h; - vehicle speed above 25 km/h; - distance travelled more than 500 m; The warning cycle consists of the warning light coming on in flashing mode (frequency of 2 Hz DC 50%) combined with an acoustic signal. Operation during the 90 second cycle - if the seat belts are fastened, the warning cycle is interrupted immediately (the warning light goes out and the buzzer stops) and the system is ready for a new signal cycle; - if one of the three events that caused the activation of the warning cycle no longer exists, the cycle continues until the 90 secs have elapsed; - if a further warning is required, the warning light indicates the new event by interrupting the current warning cycle (the acoustic signal stops and the seat belt reminder warning light changes from a flashing to a fixed light) and activating the new signal. The system then resumes the warning cycle prior to the new, most recent event. If the seat belt is fastened during the new event warning, the warning cycle ceases; - if the key is turned off, the warning cycle stops immediately. Operation after 90 seconds If the seat belt unfastened status persists: - the acoustic signalling is deactivated; - the warning light flashing cycle stops and the warning light remains on in fixed mode. The warning cycle is only carried out once, if the above mentioned conditions occur: then, at the end of the 90 second period, if the seat belt is still not fastened, it is not repeated. New warning signal The warning cycle is only repeated when the seat belt not fastened condition is detected again (transition from seat belt fastened to seat belt not fastened) and one of the three conditions described previously is detected. Method for excluding the warning cycle (warning light flashing/horn) The user can deactivate the warning cycle temporarily by means of the following procedure: Within one minute of key-on, proceed as follows: - do up the driver and passenger side seat belts. To make the procedure easier, the seat belts can be fastened before the key on. - keep the belts fastened (simultaneously) for at least 20 s (with the TEG inserted and turned ON). - unfasten at least one of the seat belts. The warning cycle will be automatically activated again at each new key on operation. The deactivation procedure must be performed using a diagnostic instrument (Examiner) in communication with the control panel. Noone can deactivate the signal issued by the warning light on the dashboard. This is always present (fixed light) if the seat belt is unfastened. Warnings The deactivation / reactivation of the front and side passenger Air Bag protecting the chest (Side Bag) takes place by means of a special switch with a key located on the passenger side of the dashboard. Only operate the switch with the engine off and the ignition key extracted. The switch and key has two positions: - Activated configuration (ON position): warning light in the instrument panel off; babies cannot be transported under any circumstances on the front seat. - Deactivated configuration (OFF position): warning light instrument panel on; babies can be transported on the front seat protected by suitable retention systems. The warning light in the instrument panel remains on constantly until the Air Bags are reactivated. The deactivation / reactivation of the rear side Air Bags protecting the chest, takes place using the special switch and key located in the boot under the rear parcel shelf brackets. Only operate the switch with the engine off and the ignition key extracted. There are two positions for the switch and key: - Activated configuration (ON position): warning light in the instrument panel off; babies cannot be transported under any circumstances on the rear seats. - Deactivated configuration (OFF position): warning light instrument panel on; babies can be transported on the rear seats protected by suitable retention systems. The warning light in the instrument panel remains on constantly until the Air Bags are reactivated. If the Air Bag warning light does not come on when the ignition is turned ON or it remains on whilst driving (together with the message in the display), it is possible that there is a fault in the system. In this case, the Air Bags or the pretensioners may not be activated in the case of an accident or (in a smaller number of cases) they may be activated incorrectly. When the ignition key is turned to the ON position, the passenger Air Bag disabled warning light (with the passenger side and front Air Bag disabled switch in the ON position) comes on firstly in fixed mode and then flashing for a few seconds (in order to remind that the passenger Air Bag will activate in the case of an impact) after which it should go out. When the ignition key is turned to the ON position, the passenger Air Bag disabled warning light (with the rear side Air Bags disabled switch in the ON position) comes on firstly in fixed mode and then flashing for a few seconds (in order to remind that the rear side Air Bags will activate in the case of an impact) after which it should go out.

FIAT CODE SYSTEM The vehicles are equipped with an electronic system known as the FIAT CODE to produce the engine immobilizer function. The FIAT CODE system only allows the engine to be started by means of the NCM after a secret code, memorized previously in the NCM, is received. The second generation Code system is incorporated in the Body Computer Node (NBC). The FIAT CODE consists of 5 essential elements (in addition to the Body Computer which act as a control unit): - CAN line for dialogue between the NBC and the NCM - two-way serial line for recovery (W line); - two TEG devices (electronic key) containing a transponder with a secret code; - an (NTR) aerial that reads the code contained in the TEGs; - the NCM. Operation The FIAT CODE allows the start of the engine management by the NCM by means of a coded dialogue between the NBC and NCM during the stage that precedes start up. After key on - i.e. TEG correctly inserted in the TEG Reader and turned to the ON position - the NCM sends a code request to the NBC, which responds only after it has identified (via its aerial) the presence of a known TEG. If the secret code in the answer is valid, the NCM continues with the regular engine management activities, allowing the engine to be started up. The NCM can only memorize the secret code by means of a particular self-programming procedure described later on. Operation of the FIAT CODE is guaranteed if any of the other NBC functions are not working properly. After recognizing an enabled transponder, the FIAT CODE switches off any alarm system. Interaction between the fiat code and the electronic key (teg) Every TEG contains a transponder with an IDENTIFICATION CODE and a SECRET CODE. As soon as the TEG is inserted, the transponder is energized and sends the identification code to the NTR which, having recognized it as one of the enabled ones, continues with the cryptographic transponder recognition strategy. If the identification code is not recognized, the procedure is aborted and the engine cannot be started. The cryptographic transponder is recognized by means of a challenge-response algorithm with an encrypted code exchange. The code recognition time is less than 160 ms per attempt. The NTR attempts the transponder acquisition for up to 1 second. Communication between the engine control node and the fiat code The dialogue between the NBC and the NCM is activated on the C-CAN in normal operating conditions. Every exchange of information between the NBC and the NCM is guided by the NCM (the NBC never interrogates the NCM but only responds after a request). After KEY-ON, the flow of code exchange operations between the NBC and the NCM depends on the status (blank or memorised) of the engine control unit. If the NCM is blank, the procedure involves sending a fix-code request to the NBC: in this way the NCM learns the secret code and stores it in its memory. This procedure is known as CODE RECORDING (the TEG must always be present in the TEG Reader). If the NCM is not memorized, the procedure involves a double exchange of secret codes between the NCM and the NBC. 1 - Key-On 2 - NCM initialisation 3 - The NCM is memorized 4 - Memorisation successfully completed? 5 - ENABLE ENGINE MANAGEMENT = the software flow continues with engine management 6 - PROHIBIT ENGINE MANAGEMENT = To enable a new procedure (request code = ENQ) it is necessary to remove and resupply the +15 (KEY-OFF and KEY-ON) 7 - Is the secret code valid? 8 - SEE POINT 6 9 - SEE POINT 5 A - CODE VERIFY B - CODE RECORDING Code recording The CODE RECORDING procedure is the memorizing of the fix code in the engine control unit. Only after the NBC has memorized the identification codes, the secret code and the fix code, is the NBC ready to satisfy the request to transmit a code to a pristine NCM. After power on, the engine control unit initialises its software and requests a fix code if it is blank. If the NBC is not blank, it responds by sending the fix code, but only after having recognized an authorized TEG. If the TEG is not authorized (key unrecognized) or there is no TEG inserted, the NBC does not respond. If the FIAT CODE is blank and there is not a transponder in the TEG Reader, a FIX code request is sentf from the NCM to the NBC and the latter does not respond. Code verify This standard procedure is repeated throughout the vehicle lifetime whenever the user inserts the TEG in the Reader and turns it to the ON position (KEY ON): this procedure enables the starting of the engine if the TEG is enabled. The code verify procedure continues even when the user places the TEG in the START position (CRANKING). When the TEG is inserted in the reader (NTR), the NBC recognizes whether the TEG transponder is one of the ones enabled (up to 8 TEGs available). If it is recognized, the steering is released and the TEG is enabled to rotate to the ON and START positions for engine starting. At the same time as the KEY ON, the NCM sends a starting authorization request to the NBC. In response to this request, the NBC only sends a response, encrypted by the Minikrypt, to the engine control unit if the transponder is recognized as enabled. If the NBC receives further verification requests, it only needs to re-read the transponder in the aerial before responding to the NCM if visible signs of tampering are present (see later). If the result of the transponder recognition is negative (incorrect transponder, no readable transponder, etc.), the NBC will send the code (incorrect transponder or missing transponder) to the engine management control unit and the vehicle protection system failure warning light in the instrument panel will come on. If the FIAT CODE is blank and the NCM sends a FIX code request, the FIAT CODE, after having recognized a transponder, will respond by refusing starting authorization. Method of using c-can or recovery line w Communication between the NBC and NCM takes place along the C-CAN line by default: if the C-CAN line is faulty, the recovery strategy is as follows: - the NCM changes to recovery status on the W serial line and requests the code from the NBC: if the outcome is positive, start-up is permitted; - in the event of problems on the W line, the NCM transfers to recovery status by means of the Diagnostic instrument at the end of the retransmission attempts. The recovery strategy is mainly managed by the NCM, which acts as a master unit during communication: the NBC, acting as the slave unit, must always be ready to respond to code requests from the C-CAN network and also from the W serial line. Communication via the c-can network Communication via the Body Computer and the NCM takes place via the following two CAN messages: - IMMO CODE REQUEST (immo code request) - IMMO CODE RESPONSE (immo code response). The IMMO CODE REQUEST is sent by the NCM and received by the NBC. The IMMO CODE RESPONSE is sent by the NBC and received by the NCM. Communication via the w line If the system changes to recovery mode due to a malfunction in the CAN network, information must be exchanged between the NCM and NBC via the W serial line. This code exchange is only carried out for the CODE VERIFY procedure: it is not therefore possible to run a CODE RECORDING procedure via the W line. Information must be exchanged via the serial line in exactly the same way as via the C-CAN network: The NCM control unit is the communication master unit while the NBC control unit responds to requests received by the NCM. Both messages - IMMO CODE REQUEST and IMMO CODE RESPONSE - are carried on the serial line. CHECKING THE W LINE ELECTRICAL CONNECTION Because communication only takes place on the W line in recovery mode, an ERROR status would not not be recognised until the system was used i.e. because the customer would not be able to move the vehicle. A strategy for checking the W serial line has therefore been added so that the line can be diagnosed. About 1 second after the key on a code is sent on the W line to the NBC. If the NBC does not repeat it correctly, the fault will be signalled at the instrument panel for the activation of the passenger compartment protection system failure warning light (CODE) which will flash three times. Protection codes The FIAT CODE function is performed via the exchange of secret codes between system subunits (TEG, NTR, NBC, engine management control unit). - UNIVERSAL CODE: this is the code that an unprogrammed NBC sends to the NCM when it detects the presence of a transponder in the TEG. The vehicle protection warning light comes on at a frequency of 1.6 Hz and duty cycle of 50%. The warning light flashes to indicate that the system is properly connected but the vehicle is not protected by a code. - IMMO CODE: This is the basic code that provides the secret code and the fix code. An automatically generated immo code is allocated to each vehicle. The IMMO CODE is used to generate all the other secret codes used by the FIAT CODE function. - SECRET CODE: This code is resident in the transponder. It is stored in the transponders contained in the TEG when the transponders are programmed and in the NBC when the keys are programmed at the end of line. - FIX CODE: This is stored in the NBC during end of line programming. - ELECTRONIC CODE (PIN): This is obtained from the fix code and printed on the CODE CARD, which is given to the vehicle owner. It takes the form of a 5-figure decimal code (0 is not permitted). It is used to access the NBC memory in protected mode in order to reprogram or program new remote control units (TEGs) and/or perform specific diagnostic functions. - IDENTIFIER: This is resident in the transponder and different for each transponder. It is stored in the FIAT CODE during the programming procedure. The NBC manages a table of enabled identifiers and another table of disabled identifiers. Fiat code function in the nbc/ntr The FIAT CODE is a function of the NBC/NTR. The main FIAT CODE functions are: - to place the alarm in a deactivated state after recognizing an enabled TEG (NBC); - to energize the aerial to read the TEG transponder (NTR); - to send the random code to the transponder (NTR); - to receive the encrypted code transmitted by the TEG (NTR); - to store the secret code (NBC/NTR); - to manage a list of up to a maximum of 8 enabled identification codes (NTR); - to manage a list of 4 permanently disabled identifiers (NTR); - to manage the C-CAN line towards the engine control unit (NBC); - to control activation of the warning light on the panel via communication with the NQS (NBC); - to carry out autodiagnosis (NBC/NTR). Aerial The aerial is located in the TEG Reader from where it is also managed. Since the aerial needs to be as close as possible to the transponder (on account of electro-magnetic immunity, the limited range of the transponder and small dimensions) it is fastened to the front part of the TEG-Reader. Transponder (in the teg) A cryptographic transponder is located inside the TEG. Operation At the time of the +15, the transponder is energised by the aerial and responds by emitting a rolling, encrypted secret code. If the code is recognized as valid, the NBC sends the engine control unit, on request, a coded signal allowing the engine to be started. Up to 8 electronic keys (TEGs) can be stored in the NBC. The TEGs are supplied already memorised by the production plant. All the codes are also stored in a database managed by Parts. When the new vehicle is delivered to the customer, the service network does not need to carry out any memorisation procedure. If the TEGs are lost or extra TEGs are required, order from Parts in accordance with the procedures described below and in the REPAIR PROCEDURES section. Op. 5580E ANTI-THEFT DEVICE Specifications The transponder in the TEG has the information required for a coded dialogue with the TEG Reader encoded in its memory. The identification code differs from transponder to transponder to guarantee that no two transponders have the same identification code even if there is a request for a duplicate in the Network. Programming the teg The memorisation procedure is divided into two stages in sequence: - the transponder in the TEG is stored in the NTR; - The NBC manages memorisation of the fix code in the engine control unit. This second stage is implemented automatically when the first is completed successfully after key on. The transponders are sent to the TEG manufacturer programmed with the identifier (different for each transponder). The manufacturer generates an immo code, computes the relevant codes (secret code, fix code) and programmes the secret code and the programming date in the transponders. Once programmed, it prints a bar code on a disposable label that contains the immo code, the TEG identifiers, the programming date, the emergency key mechanical code (door opening). The secret code contained in the TEGs is used the encrypted algorhithm for recognition of the TEG. Programming a new body computer If the Body Computer is replaced, the NBC must be programmed with the secret code and fix code of the vehicle on which it will be installed. The database is accessed using the chassis number to obtain the vehicle immo code. This is used to supply the secret code and fix code, which are programmed in the NBC. Once the NBC has been installed in the vehicle, the TEG identifiers are stored (see reprogramming). An NBC programming operation can only be performed with a blank NBC by the FIAT parts dept. Reprogramming the teg TEG reprogramming involves storing the TEGs enabled upon vehicle start-up in the NTR. New TEGs to be programmed and TEGs already programmed will be entered in the NTR so that they can be recognised by the TEG Reader, which stores those presented during the procedure in the enabled identifier table and transfers those not presented from the table to the disabled identifier table. Disabled teg table If an enabled TEG is no longer available (lost, stolen or no longer operational), its operation must be disabled during the subsequent programming procedure (necessary to memorise a new replacement TEG for example). The TEG Reader manages a table in the EEPROM that can contain data on 4 disabled TEGs: the identifiers of enabled TEGs not presented during the reprogramming procedure are transferred to this table. If the disabled TEG table is full, any new TEG will replace the first entered in the table. This table also allows the traceability of TEGs used on the vehicle. Reprogramming procedure The minimum time required for KEY-ON during the memorisation procedure is 1 second. The TEG reprogramming procedure is performed/guided by the Diagnostic/Inspection Instrument: this procedure is activated by means of access protected by the vehicle PIN. Once the procedure is activated, the flow is as follows: - the Diagnostic instrument commands the NTR to initialise the TEG learning procedure; - the operator inserts the first TEG and asks the TEG Reader to learn it: the NTR reads the transponder following key-on, checks whether the secret code is correct and, if so, leans the TEG identifier; - the operator repeats the second operation for all the TEGs. Once all the TEGs have been learnt, the Diagnostic instrument commands the NTR to store them permanently in its EEPROM via the following procedure: - the NTR compares the learnt identifiers with those currently in its memory. - data on TEGs stored in the EEPROM but not presented during learning are moved to the disabled TEG table. - data on learnt TEGs are stored in the enabled TEG table only if they are not already present in the disabled TEG table. - it is possible to program up to 8 enabled TEGs. Deleting a lost teg from the memory The procedure is similar to that described in the previous paragraph. All the TEGs owned must be presented. Those not presented will be deleted, i.e. transferred to the disabled identifier table. At any time it is possible to delete a lost TEG from the memory using the Diagnostic/Inspection Instrument. The identifier of this TEG is transferred to the disabled identifier table and will no longer be recognised. Code card This card shows: - The emergency code (electronic code) that allows the Service Network to program electronic keys (TEGs) and remote controls using an EXAMINER. - The emergency key mechanical code identifies the mechanical profile of the key and must be specified on the order to receive the key already cut. 1 - Electronic code 2 - Mechanical code OPERATION The electronic emergency code is also used for system diagnosis and for other operations using Examiner or other diagnostic instruments. Many of these operations (e.g. TEG Memorisation) can be carried out only once this code has been entered. Before any operation, it is therefore necessary to ask the Customer for their Code Card. The Code Card must not be left in the vehicle in case it is stolen. Code warning light (vehicle protection) The Code warning light (vehicle protection) is located in the instrument panel and is controlled by a message from the NBC on the B-CAN.
