Fault diagnosis The allows self-diagnosis to be carried out for system components. The NTR is capable of identifying and memorizing the presence of the following malfunctions in its EEPROM: Transponder: - defective or missing transponder or secret code incorrect - deleted/disabled - unknown/not memorized Transponder aerial: - electrical connection defective (circuit open, short circuit to earth or to battery) Active diagnosis By means of commands sent from the Diagnostic instrument, it is possible: To ask whether the NBC type is: - blank (whenever a TEG is inserted) - programmed at end of line (whenever a TEG is inserted) - spare part (whenever a TEG is inserted) blank/programmed NCM link with NCM OK / KO - Request the number of TEGs programmed. - Read one TEG at once and find out for each TEG: Valid transponder - whether the TEG is memorised - its position in the table - whether the secret code is valid the TEG ID - Request the number and identifier of the last TEG used - Request a reading of all enabled TEGs - Request the number of TEGs enabled and the number of TEGs disabled - Perform manual memorisation of TEGs by means of successive acquisitions and the condition of the transponder must be verified at each acquisition It is also possible detect the presence of a transponder in the aerial and whether it is valid or not. - Request current system status identified by: Last TEG used and enabled and recognised the NBC has received a code request from the engine control unit the NCM is blank the FIAT CODE is blank the NBC is enabled to send the Minikrypt key the identifier of the last TEG used is present in the enabled TEG table the identifier of the last TEG used is present in the disabled TEG table The FIAT CODE has identified a tampering attempt at the +15 supply - Control activation/deactivation of the CODE warning light at the NQS Programming the electronic keys / electronic key (teg) The electronic key is programmed at end of line together with the FIAT CODE. During the vehicle's lifetime, it is possible to make the Electronic Key Reader (NTR) learn new keys, e.g. if ELECTRONIC KEYS (TEGs) are added or deleted. Upon each new programming procedure, all the Electronic Keys not presented during the above procedure (for the removal of lost keys) are cleared from the memory. All available Electronic Keys (TEGs) must be programed upon each programming. Those not presented will be deleted from the memory and it will not be possible to program them. Procedure for storing an electronic key (teg) The ELECTRONIC KEY (TEG) storage procedure is managed by the Diagnostic instrument (Examiner) and can be activated only by entering the ELECTRONIC CODE (see CODE CARD). The procedure consists of learning the ELECTRONIC KEY (TEG) codes and involves secret codes being received by the TEG Reader and then stored. During the procedure, the codes are stored permanently in the TEG Reader EEPROM memory. Once the procedure is activated, the flow is as follows: - the Diagnostic instrument commands the Electronic Key Reader (NTR) to initialise the ELECTRONIC KEY (TEG) learning procedure and confirms this to the operator; - the operator enters the first ELECTRONIC KEY (TEG) to be stored; - the Electronic Key Reader (NTR) receives the secret code and the ID of the ELECTRONIC KEY (TEG) and learns it; - the Diagnostic instrument confirms that learning has taken place; - the previous stages are repeated for each ELECTRONIC KEY (TEG) that must be learned, up to a maximum of 8; - once the ELECTRONIC KEYS (TEGs) have been learned, the operator asks the Diagnostic instrument to store them: - the diagnostic equipment commands the Electronic Key Reader (NTR) to store the ELECTRONIC KEYS (TEGs) learnt. Only the ELECTRONIC KEYS (TEGs) learnt during the procedure will be stored in the EEPROM (therefore all the ELECTRONIC KEYS (TEGs) not presented will not be stored). The production plant transfers all the necessary data into this data base together at the time of vehicle production. ALARM SYSTEM Specifications The vehicle protection system on the CROMA makes it possible to combine excellent protection against break in attempts and suitable comfort for the customer, providing a high specification and trim level, starting with central locking and extending to the computerized vehicle entry/starting system. The central locking has, fitted as standard, dead locks and protection functions (independent driver's door unlocking, independent boot release, automatic locking of the doors at speed) and comfort features (electronic key window closing) that can be customized by the user through a menu in the instrument panel. The system can be operated up to 20 m away from the vehicle using the remote control electronic key (TEG) (with 3 buttons and a back up mechanical insert that can be extracted). The alarm system includes perimeter protection, volumetric protection and anti-lifting protection. The door has an LED to signal that it is closed. The system consists of: ANTI-THEFT ALARM CONTROL UNIT (CSA) The CSA is an electronic component connected to the A-bus serial line and to the front wiring which manages the acoustic alarm functions. VOLUMETRIC ALARM CONTROL UNIT (CAV) The CAV is an electronic component supplied with the front courtesy light, connected to the A-bus serial line and to the rear wiring which incorporates the volumetric and anti-tilt sensors and the exclusion buttons. 1 - Volumetric sensors exclusion button 2 - Anti-tilt sensor exclusion button REMOTE CONTROL KEY This is a key with electronic remote control that makes it possible to control the central locking and the vehicle alarm at a distance. It contains a secret code that identifies it and allows recognition. 1 - Boot release button 2 - Button for unlocking doors / switching off alarm 3 - Button for locking doors / switching on alarm DETERRENT LED There is a red LED at the side of the safety knob in the driver's door panel. With the alarm system switched on, the LEDs in the front door panels flash red (deterrent function). 1 - Deterrent LED INSTRUMENT PANEL WITH DISPLAY The display in the instrument panel is used to show the customer warning messages. Operation System operation is co-ordinated by the NBC, which sends/receives commands from external modules via the A-Bus serial line. For further details, See descriptions 5505 INSTRUMENT/GAUGE ELECTRICAL CIRCUITS There are eight different possible states for the alarm system: - DEACTIVATED; - REST; - ON; - SURVEILLANCE; - ALARM; - OFF; - PROGRAMMING; - FAULT DIAGNOSIS; Each of these statuses is described in the following paragraphs. Deactivation The deactivation state is the state in which the alarm system finds itself each time the key is recognized. This operation effectively turns off the alarm except for signalling. When the alarm system is deactivated it does not respond to the commands from the receiver. It is possible to move from the deactivated state to the rest state by turning the key to key-off. Rest Rest status is the basic alarm system status. It is possible to change from rest status to the diagnostic state: when a session is activated - Fault diagnosis: using the diagnostic equipment connected to the NBC. - Surveillance: when the vehicle is protected by issuing an on command and passing through the on stage. - Deactivated: when an enabled key is recognized. In the rest condition, the NBC continues to acquire the +15 status to stop the system changing to surveillance mode and above all to prevent alarm activation. This information distinguishes two fundamental rest modes: vehicle operating (+15 present) or left (+15 absent), which is a prelude to surveillance mode. The on command changes the alarm from rest to surveillance model This operation is always inhibited in the presence of a +15 signal. Switching on The alarm system is switched on the moment the doors are locked which takes place by pressing the button in the remote control transmitter button signalled by the direction indicators coming on (managed in the same way as for the remote control system) and by a beep at the same time as the direction indicators come on: both signals are activated/deactivated for every planned operating mode (blinker engagement/disengagement and beep engagment/disengagement parameters). When the command is received, the NBC activates the alarm activation procedure as described within 100 ms: - siganlling of switching on in progress. - plausibility of door (2 or 4), bonnet and boot switch status is also checked (perimeter protection): If one of the entrances if found not to be closed, this entrance is excluded from surveillance. - sensor status check; if the siren is OK "siren already on" or "siren does not respond" the blinkers flash twice. Diagnostic information display The presence of problems when switching on is signalled by a warning beep: - problem type indicated by means of the deterrent warning light - flashing of volumetric sensors that are faulty at 8 Hz for 2.5 secs., warning light on constantly for 10 seconds if one or more of the following problems are detected: siren faulty anti-tilt sensor faulty Automatic activation Automatic activation allows the alarm system to switch from rest to surveillance mode in automatic, timed manner. The automatic activation mode is as follows. from KEY-OFF: - KEY OFF is detected - the self-activation counter begins counting - the counter reaches the "SELF-ACTIVATION TIME" value set in the EPPROM - the NBC checks whether a valid transponder is present - if there is a valid transponder, the automatic activation takes place irrespective of the door status. - if there is no valid transponder, the automatic activation takes place irrespective of the door status. For the mode described above, during the automatic activation cycle, the system continuously checks that there is no +15 until the time out is reached or the alarm system is activated. If the +15 signal is present with the transponder/CID valid and recognized, the procedure should be interrupted. Surveillance During the surveillance stage, the NBC is activated for reading the commands passing along the serial line: if a command read/received by the NBC implies an action, this action should be set in moitino immediately. During the surveillance stage, the NBC carries out a check onthe +15 signal. The NBC downloads information on the presence of a +15 signal: if it detects the presence of the +15 signal for longer than 100 ms, understood as a permanent state and not debounce, without a previous deactivation command, the NBC interprets this manoeuvre as a theft attempt and controls the changeover to alarm status. Perimeter surveillance The NBC monitors the status of the six inputs from the four doors, bonnet and boot: if one of these changes status for more than 500ms, the NBC recognizes an intrusion attempt. Exclusion of external modules due to low battery voltage. If the battery voltage is below 8.5 V ± 5% (a figure that can be programmed in the EEPROM) for longer than 30 mins, the NBC deactivates external modules (volumetric sensors, tilt sensor, external input modules) in order to safeguard the life of the battery and to be able to start up the engine later on. Protection against false alarms due to BC reset During the surveillance stage, external interference or a theft attempt could cause the NBC to reset and re-initialise its functions. In this case, the NBC checks whether the alarm was on before the reset so it can re-activate the external modules, except from those excluded at the last activation. In the case of a reset no visual/acoustic signal should be made. Alarm activation During the surveillance stage, the alarm may be activated by the perimeter protection and also by external modules (ultrasound, anti-tilt, etc.) or the siren (due to the wires being cut). When one of the alarm activation signals is received, the NBC immediately changes to alarm status and triggers the cycle specified for the type of alarm received. Boot opening/closing management The boot opening command is accepted in the following states: Deactivation, Rest, Surveillance and Alarm. Any request is ignored during the Switching on and Switching off states. The system, whether in Surveillance or in Alarm, on receipt of boot opening command, disables the volumetric/anti-tilt external modules that control the alarm system input modules and switches them off, disables the boot entry perimeter protection (the door and bonnet entries remain activated) and implements the blinker signalling. The disabling of the perimeter protection is intrinsice in the NBC which simply does not take into account the possible switching of the boot switch. If within 1 second of the command recognition (by the remote control) the boot switch does not change status (from boot closed to boot open), the system switches the volumetric, anti-tilt and perimeter protection functions back on again. In particular, if the alarm is on, the blinkers are only activated if the entry is under surveillance (boot switch operating at the previous switching on) and the alarm system is activated. The timed period of 1 second to detect a change in status of the switch makes it possible to ensure the protection of the vehicle even with the boot entry faulty. If the boot is left open and the boot opening command, at the end of the 1 second time out, has not detected variations in the switch status, the system switches the volumetric/anti-tilt protection on again. The visual signal should indicate that the opening has taken place using the remote control/passive entry. The modules are switched back on when the lid closed signal is received. Alarm If one of the sensors involved in the surveillance identifies an irregular situation (attempted or actual intrusion, interference and/or theft of the vehicle), the alarm sytem moves to ALARM status. Alarm status is characterised by the activation of optical/acoustic signals consisting of activation of the siren and indicators. The signalling comprises a succession of alarm cycles, understood as the stage during which the visual/acoustic signalling is activated. The signals are activated by sending information to the various alarm system sub-modules: this information also contains the cause of the alarm trigger so that each module can produce a signal that is consistent with the operating modes for the various countries. Memorizing the cause of the alarm The system is required, for diagnostic purposes, to keep track of the alarm causes recognized by the NBC. The NBC memorizes the last 10 alarm causes, associating the cause and alarm system state at the time the system was switched on with each of the causes. The following alarm causes can be memorised: - driver's door - passenger door - left rear door - right rear door - ultrasound sensor - anti-tilt sensor (if fitted) - cutting of siren cables - boot - bonnet - +15 - cutting of +30 cable - siren intrusion with incorrect DSIR command - intrusion of external modules with DUS or DAINC command - incorrect heart-beat For each alarm cause, the system status is memorised, described by: - driver's door open - passenger door open - left rear door open - right rear door open - bonnet open - boot open - alarm system activated by self-activation - alarm system switched on by owner - ultrasound sensor defective - anti-tilt sensor defective (if fitted) - siren defective - serial line not operational Switching off Deactivation may occur in surveillance mode or in alarm mode. It is carried out by the remote control which commands the NBC to switch off the alarm system the moment the doors are unlocked. The deactivation takes place by means of the information which switches off the alarm system modules and controls the activation of the visual/acoustic signals for the switching off stage. This information should be sent within 100 ms of receiving the deactivation command: the command is accepted even with the +15 signal present. On switching off the NBC interrupts the perimeter protection and, if present, all the counter-measures activated. The alarm system can also be switched off in passive mode by: - inserting an enabled key in the ignition switch and turning it to the +15 position: the alarm system, on recognizing the +15, verifies the presence of an enabled key and, if the answer is positive, switches the alarm off. if the user enters the passenger compartment with the alarm system activated, the moment the +15 signal is given, the alarm system will switch off. After deactivating and at the first key on, the control unit runs the signals for the volumetric, anti-tilt, perimeter, +15 and +30, sending the information to the function that manages the deterrent LED. The messages signalling break in attempts are shown in the panel. END OF LINE PROGRAMMING System configuration It is possible to program the configuration of the alarm system installed on the vehicle at the end of line by defining the presence/absence of the following modules: - siren - ultrasound module - tilt module This information can be read, but not modified, by the diagnostic equipment which will adapt its diagnostic procedures depending on the configuration present. The configuration is transferred to the Body Computer by means of the vehicle Customisation procedure (PROXI). The programming allows the NBC to memorize the operating mode thereby allowing the system to be configured in accordance with the country to which it is being exported in line with the laws in force there. The system is in the rest state during the programming stage. Function fault diagnosis No diagnostic checks are required for the perimeter protection switches. The NC diagnoses the operation of the serial line for connection to the siren and external modules, checking for short circuits to earth, to the battery and for the presence of open circuits. A diagnostic check is carried out on the serial line when communication is activated, typically upon activation of the alarm system. The fault diagnosis of the external modules is carried out by the functions that manage them and that provide nformation on the module status. The diagnostic information obtained at the time of activation is stored in the EEPROM to ensure the system can be serviced. Active diagnostics During a diagnostic session, the NBC can be requested to carry out a diagnostic check on the A-Bus serial line which can have the following possible outcomes: OK, short circuit to earth, short circuit to battery. It is also possible to read the alarm cause table stored in the NBC. Recovery If an external module (ultrasound, tilt) is recognized as not functioning, it is excluded for the entire surveillance cycle. The next time the system is switched on, the diagnostic check is carried out again on the modules which should be reactivated if they are recognized as working.

Parking sensors system The "Parking Assistance" system supplies the driver with information on distance when approaching obstacles behind the vehicle thereby providing help with parking manoeuvres and identifying obstacles that are outside the field of vision. The information of the presence/distance of an obstacle is transmitted to the driver by means of acoustic warnings whose frequency depends on the distance of the obstacle. COMPOSITION The parking assistance system comprises the following components: 1 - Electronic control unit (NSP); 2- Ultrasound sensors; 3 - Trailer connection; 4 - Connection to CAN (Body Computer); 5 - Connection to CAN (Instrument Panel); The buzzer on this version in inside the instrument panel. Parking sensor node (nsp) The NSP is an electronic component incorporated in the CAN that provides the driver with assistance during manoeuvres with reverse gear engaged by recognizing any dangerous obstacles. The electronic control unit carries out the following functions: - Activating the sensors - Processing the signals received by the sensors - Checking the operation of the sensors - Activating the buzzer in the instrument panel - Managing the fault diagnosis and test functions The electronic control unit has a device that protects against voltage fluctuations and short circuits. Pin out The control unit and pin out is illustrated in the diagram below 1 - Electronic control unit. A - CONNECTOR A B - CONNECTOR B CONNECTOR A (16-way) Pin Function 1 Ignition-operated power supply 5 Negative deactivation signal if tow hook is fitted 7 B-CAN A 8 Earth 14 B - CAN B CONNECTOR B (12-way) Pin Function 1 Sensor earth 2 Right rear inner sensor signal 3 Left rear inner sensor signal 4 Right rear outer sensor signal 5 Left rear outer sensor signal 6 Sensor positive Sensors The sensors are incorporated in the rear bumper using special adaptors (covers). The sensors use ultrasound technology and act as intelligent transmitters/receivers with triangulation technology: allowing improved detection in critical situations or in the presence of small obstacles. The impulses emitted are reflected by any obstacles; the transducer receives an echo which is converted into a digital signal and sent to the electronic control unit. The system covers the middle and side area of the rear of the vehicle. In the case of an obstacle in the middle area, it is detected at distances of less than 150 cm for the entire width of the vehicle. In the case of an obstacle in the side area, it is detected at distances of less than 0.6 m. Operation The sensor is an ultrasound transducer which acts as an intelligent transmitter and receiver of ultrasound impulse packages. Both the frequency and the voltage of the impulses are produced in the transducer. The impulses emitted are reflected by any obstacles; the transducer therefore receives an echo which is amplified and converted into a digital signal, sent to the electronic control unit via the same line used for the transmission request. Each sensor can also be operated as a receiver only, in order to be able to take a triangular measurement between two sensors. This technique allows better detection of small obstacles and in situations featuring critical reflection. The sensors all have the same electrical and mechanical properties; the maximum detection distance for each sensor can be adjusted using software according to the location of the actual sensor. Sensor pin out Pin Function 1 Sensor power supply 2 Sensor signal 3 Earth OPERATION The operation is illustrated in diagrammatic form. Measuring distance of obstacles The electronic control unit controls the sensors which convert the control unit electrical signals into ultrasound signals at a rhythm which varies between 3 and 10 measuring processes per second. The signal, reflected by any obstacles, is received by the sensor and amplified by it, converted into a digital signal and sent, in this format, to the electronic control unit. The control unit compares the signal transmitted with the one rececived and, using suitable algorhythms, calculates the time elapsed between the issue of the signal and the reception of the echo. This information is translated into distance and the driver is notified by means of acoustic signals. Reflections from the ground are ignored unless they have the characteristcs of an obstacle. Self-diagnosis The control unit carries out an autodiagnostic test when it is switched on. The sensors are diagnosed each time they are activated. Recovery strategies The sensors and the wiring are subject to continuous fault diagnosis during the operation of the system. A fault in only one sensor inhibits the operation of the entire system. Activation and deactivation of the system When the control unit is switched on (vehicle key-on and reverse gear engaged) an autodiagnostic test and a test on all the peripheral functions are carried out. The system is ready to use in under 0.5 seconds. The measurement of the distance only takes place when the system is activated. The system is activated when the following two conditions are verified: - Key-ON - Reverse gear engaged When the system is activated the buzzer in the instrument panel sounds intermittently as a warning that the system is activated. If obstacles are present, it signals the distance of the obstacle by means of impulses whose frequency increases as the vehicle gets closer to the obstacle. If there is a problem with the system then a warning signal is emitted. Obstacle distance signal The sound from the buzzer warns the driver that the vehicle is approaching an obstacle. The sound lasts for 75 ms, whilst the pause between the sounds is directly proportional to the distance of the obstacle: impulses in quick succession indicate the presence of an obstacle that is very close. A continuous sound indicates that the obstacle is less than 30 cm away. The sound cycle remains constant if the distance measured by the centre sensors remains unchanged, whilst if this situation occurs for the side sensors, the signal is interrupted after 3 seconds (to prevent signals in the case of manoeuvres alongside walls). If there is a trailer then there is no signalling of rear obstacles. Error signalling Any faults/errors are signalled by means of the instrument panel and acoustically. The acoustic signal stops after 3 seconds. The occurrence of errors/faults whilst the system is activated is signalled immediately.

System activation The CONNECT system may be activated in two different modes: - Automatic activation with the key inserted and turned to the ON position - Manual activation by means of ON button -- Emergency manual activation by means of SOS button Automatic activation When the ignition key is turned to ON position, the CONNECT system turns on automatically to make all the functions described in this chapter active or enabled. Manual activation With the ignition key in OFF position, the CONNECT system comes on when the ON button is pressed to make the following modes available: - MAIN - AUDIO - NAV - TEL - SOS and SERVICE (Targasys) In this mode, the SETUP and TRIP modules can be activated but it is not possible to validate any parameter change, language change or measurement unit change or any other type of adjustment envisaged by the CONNECT system. These limitations are normal when the system is activated by means of the ON button. When the vehicle is not running (key extracted or OFF position), the data transmission devices inside the vehicle are not operational. When ignition key is turned ON, the system begins to work. System deactivation The CONNECT system may be activated in two different modes: - deactivation independent of the ignition key; - deactivation dependent on the ignition key. To choose the deactivation mode, see the Power OFF submenu in the SEPUP menu. Deactivation independent of the ignition key When this mode is active, the CONNECT system may be turned off by pressing the ON button. The display shows the message DEACTIVATION PROCEDURE IN PROGRESS, WAIT A FEW MOMENTS. With the ignition key extracted or in the OFF position, the system deactivates with a delay of 20 minutes if a system destination has been set or if a phone conversation is in progress. Deactivation dependent on the ignition key When this mode is active, the CONNECT system may be turned off by turning the ignition key to the OFF position. Possible system states Possible Connect statuses from the viewpoint of power supply and operation in general are as follows: off state, normal state, stand-by state. Operation still depends on the "system configuration". The configuration of the system memorizes which functions the user has selected as active. The functions are: tuner, CD, CD Changer, telephone, service call and video (dark on/off). - off state: all Connect functions are disabled and the various hardware modules are not supplied with power. - normal state: in the normal state, the Connect system is fully active and all system functions are managed in accordance with the system configuration. Internal modules are operational, as are the internal communication lines. - stand-by state: in this status, the Connect system is active but looks exactly as though it were OFF to the user. In any case the only internal module that is fully operational is the network communcation. PLANNED ACTIONS Switching on The user can switch the system on (change from off state to normal state) by pressing the ON/OFF button or the SOS button irrespective of the key status. If the key is inserted with the system OFF, the Connect continues with the anti-theft procedure (exchange of codes with the body computer node) to then reach the normal state (obviously typical functions will be available if, and only if, the authentication has been successful, otherwise the system will go on stand-by). Deactivation The user can switch the system off using different methods that depend on the status of the actual system (see table below). Normal state If the key is removed and neither a telephone call or a call to the call centre is in progress, the system switches off (or moves to the OFF state; obviously after the system configuration and the backup data is saved). If a phone call or a service call is in progress, there will be a timed delay (20 minutes operation without the key or without any intervention by the user on the buttons on the front panel or the steering wheel) before the Connect is switched off. If the system is in the normal state with the key off, it may switch off for the following reasons: - automatically if the time out described above elapses, - through the intervention of the user pressing the on/off button (unless a service call is in progress). Move to stand-by It is possible to move from the normal state to stand-by (an operation that will look to the user like the system has been switched off but which in reality leaves the Connect activated) when the user presses the on/off button whilst the key is activated. It is possible to exit this state and return to the normal state still using the on/off button or the service call button. ROLLING FUNCTIONS The CONNECT states are summarized in the table below. In this case it is necessary to enter the master code manually to allow authentication with the body computer and operation. Languages available The following languages are available for both strings of displayed text (menus) and navigation voice messages: - French - English - German - Italian - Spanish - Dutch - Portuguese The change of voice command language requires a special CD to be inserted (setup CD). Navigation management and location Dead-reckoning The navigation module receives data concerning the advance and change in direction from the vehicle sensors. This data is accumulated and processed by a specific algorhithm which, also taking into consideration the current position obtained by the GPS satellites, and comparing them with map CDs, makes it possible to caculate the estimated positon of the vehicle (location of the vehicle). Navigation The navigation module is capable of carrying out the following functions. Interface functions with other modules: - Acquisition of RDS-TMC traffic information from tuner module: the module receives traffic information from the tuner module via RDS-TMC messages in the geographical areas where they are available. In any case the information referred to is only the textual type (useful message for the driver); - Route guidance: route guidance involves all the activities of extracting, managing and processing the information required for guiding the user to the destination they have set. The information that is useful for the driver is basically: - calculating route between current position and destination; - recalculating the route in case of deviation from the current route; - calculating an alternative route; - identifying a service centre along the route; - calculating the distance to the destination; - identifying junctions along the route; - identifying manoeuvres at junctions along the route (and graphic and voice instructions for the user); - calculating the distance to the next junction where the user has to make a turn. Digital mapping The map database, contained in a specific CD ROM, is made available to all the system functions. Reduced database management with no CD-ROM (listening to a music CD) It is possible to listen to an audio CD in the CD player during the navigation process. simply following the procedure described. The map CD should be inserted in the CD player for the entire duration of the entering the destination and route calculation activities. At the end of this processing, the CD ROM can be removed using the eject button and at this point the system: 1. suggests loading the route calculated in the memory 2. if the answer is yes, eject the map CD. The audio CD can now be inserted to start listening. In these conditions only some of the map information is available (town names and road names) and it is only relevant to some sections of the route. In any case the reduced data base in the Connect memory makes it possible to deviate from the route with automatic recalculation without the need to reinsert the CD-ROM (however, the effectiveness of this recalculation is extremely dependent on the length of the original route). When the route data in the memory is not sufficient to continue the navigation process, there is a request to reinsert the map CD. If the system is switched off during navigation without a CD ROM, the next time it is switched back on, the map CD must be inserted to access the navigation functions. Complete data base management If a map CD-ROM is present for the entire mission, the navigation function uses the entire data base available (map list, points of interest, etc.). FUNCTIONS SEEN BY THE USER Map display If the navigation function is activated the user can select the map representation of the area with the following features on the display: - possible scales (from 1:10·000 up to 1:20·000·000); - possibility of north up or heading up or bird view depending on the scale of the map set; - representation of specific areas (parks, water, etc.); - names of towns; - POI symbols (Points of Interest, categories: restaurants, hotels, service stations, car parks). Information from Connect Car location information: - name of road and area; - the name of the road being driven along and the area appear constantly in a special window. Traffic information The user is provided with the following traffic information starting with the RDS-TMC information described previously. - symbol on map: the system can be configured to display the symbols on the map corresponding to any traffic jams (some types of event are already displayed). - Explanatory text: an explanatory text with each event. The types of event can be accessed from the menu, having selected the type, a list of all corresponding events is accessed. - Route guidance: pre-recorded voice messages with a female voice. - Junction zoom function: the system can be configured to show the junction, just before a manouevre, greatly enlarged with explicit instructions on the route to take. - Junction drawings with pictograms: the navigation screen permanently displays simplified pictograms for the next two manouevres to be made off the map. Specific configurations for navigation function There are three possible options for calculating the route: - quickest - shortest - motorway yes/no Atlas function: this function makes it possible to use digital maps like a normal road map. Assistance services The following functions can be activated manually by means of a special (SOS) button which allows an automatic call to be sent to the service centre: - medical consultation (subscription service); - roadside assistance (subscription service); - private number; - emergency 112 Operating procedure 1. SOS button pressed 2. Assistance Services screen on the Connect display with Medical Consulation function highlighted. 3. The user can set the system so that, within 25 seconds of pressing the SOS button, the default setting is not altered (by intervening on the front buttons), the call to the service provider for medical consulation will be sent automatically. 4. The user can select roadside assistance (in this case the call will be made to the roadside assistance service provider) or exit the assistance screen (cancelling the call). 5. If the user does not subscribe to the service provider, the only functions that can be activated are the emergency 112 call and a call to a private number or consulation of the settings menu. Infomobility – connect button There is also the possibility, by subscribing to a special service, of taking advantage of a series of external driving aid services (e.g. traffic information, directions on the location of businesses, etc.). Pressing the Connect button activates the display of a menu that makes it possible to select/display Infomobility messages that may have been memorized previously. If the services are activated, by selecting the Connect item it is possible to request information, via a telephone link, from the TargaSys Service Provider. The service centre operator will call the user back. The response may be provided during the phone conversation or it will be completed by sending specific SMS text messages containing the information. Information received by SMS (if containing geographical co-ordinates and a phone number) can be stored in the memory and used directly by the user - via the Connect - to set up a phone call and/or start the navigation to the destination. Phone module The phone module allows normal phone activity, text messages, support for Service Calls to the Provider (described in the relevant chapter) and Internet access by means of WAP (Wireless Access Protocol). The following functions are available to the user: Phone functions The phone module is used to: - accept an incoming phone call; - refuse an incoming call; - forward a phone call. SIM Data Base access functions It is possible to work on an inserted SIM as follows: - read the list of phone numbers saved on the SIM card; - enter a phone number on the SIM; - delete a phone number from the SIM; - copy the contents of a SIM phoneboook to the Connect phonebook and viceversa. Last number functions The module is able to store the last 10 numbers called to help the user with repeat calls. SMS message functions The module manages text messages for the user and also from the service provider. It is therefore possibile: - to display received messages that have not yet been read (full list or selected message); - to display received messages that have been read or saved (full list or selected message); - save a received message; - delete a message (recently received or already saved); - send a message to a particular number entered by the user; - set up the Service Provider number for text messages. Phone module status display function Information on the following is shown on the screen: - intensity of the phone signal received by the aerial; - network operator's name; - presence of text messages received but not yet read; - presence of any call divert. Configuration functions - "call divert": it is possible to divert incoming calls to another phone number; - network operator management: the module manages both the selection of the network operator (manual or automatic search) and the use of a list of preferred operators; - security: use of PIN, PUK and PIN code change. WAP Access to a WAP site requires data to be loaded into the memory: the screen shows the text, links and selection input options. The functions that allow the activation of possible card action are also displayed (max 6, usually in English). For example, the following functions may be shown: next, help, back. Procedure for general use Before the phone module can be used, the user must enter a PIN security code whenever the Connect system is turned on after being turned off (unless "exclude PIN request" has been set under Settings). Unless the SIM card is inserted or the PIN code is entered, the system can be used only for emergency calls (112 in Italy) and not normal user calls or for the service call function. If an incorrect PIN is entered three times, the module is bound to request the PUK code to release the block. Voice recognition Voice recognition module with speaker dependent functions (phonebook, navigation address book, radio station memory) and speaker independent functions for radio, CD, CDC, phone and navigation system. The speaker dependent function allows a sample voice command (prerecorded by the user) to be associated with a phone number in the phonebook and/or a destination present in the destination list (personal). SPECIFICATIONS The front doors have been designed with a structure and panels that feature no sharp corners thereby keeping the risk of possible injury to the occupants to a minimum. The locks and control linkage are protected against break ins by a shield that prevents access to the mechanisms from the outside. The safety closure from the inside of the vehicle is activated by a special button on the centre tunnel at the height of the trim on the gearbox. The side panel features the armrest, directly in the panel and an oddments pocket in the lower part. The layout of the functional elements of the panel has been designed to allow the correct interaction with the body of the occupant in the case of a side impact. They are smooth and soft at the top, whilst the projection of the armrest is rendered harmless by the fact that it collapses at a load level well below that which would risk injury to the organs in the abdomen. The door also features a carrier which, in addition to carrying out a support function for the electric window motor, the guides and the various cables, is integrated with the actual door with a structural function. The door also contains: - opening/closing handle; - exterior side mirror - side rubbing strips (Opt only) The panel also includes: - two speakers, one housed in the door mirror trim; - LED signalling locking of locks, dead lock function and deterrance (driver's side only); - puddle light; - oddments pocket; - door interior opening lever; - electric controls for windows and exclusion button for rear windows (driver's side only); - controls for adjusting door mirrors (driver's side only); The sliding window is made from heat-proof, tempered glass and is moved by a guided cable type window opening device. The seal on the upper profile of the door, by the glass, and the glass scraper trims guarantee an excellent aerodyanmic seal.
