For checks relating to the control unit pin out, See descriptions 5505A MULTI-FUNCTION COMPONENTS Passenger door electric window control The electric windows control on the passenger door is described below. Operation The driver's door control panel sends the signalsfor the electric window function for the actual door to the NPP control unit which manages and carries out the function described later on. For checks relating to the control unit pin out, See descriptions 5505A MULTI-FUNCTION COMPONENTS Front electric windows The electric window controls for both the front doors and the rear doors are managed on the driver's front door. The other doors control their own window opening mechanism directly. After a key off, the front windows can be operated either manually or automatically for a period of 2 minutes. When this timed period elapses the system no longer acquires new commands. The NPG node acquires the electric window commands for both the driver's front door and the passenger door. In addition, it directly controls its own electric window motor and transmits the commands to the NPP via the CAN The NPP node only acquires the commands for the front passenger door and controls its own motor directly. The driver and passenger side door motors are therefore controlled both manually and automatically in accordance with the following strategy: - manual mode refers to the starting and stopping of the window determined manually by the user by pressing the control button for: Ta = activation time > 50 ms and < 300 ms (brief command); when the latter is released, the motor stops; - automatic mode refers to the starting of the window determined manually by the user by pressing the control button for: Ta = activation time > 300 ms (long control). With the node enabled, the electric window should not work when the control buttons are pressed for less than 50 ms. The node should interrupt the operation of the window in the following cases: - when automatic movement is in progress and either the up or down control is pressed; - in the top or bottom end of travel position during either manual movement (in a time of 400ms ± 50ms) or automatic movement (in a time of 300ms +/- 30ms). This is adjusted exclusively through the control for the motor current which is the self-adaptive type. The current self-adaptation means that the control should result in the request to close or open the vehicle windows being successful in conditions that range from a force of 6 - 8 Kg to forces that even reach 16 -18 Kg, in all voltage range (10 -16 V) and temperature (-30°C ÷ 75°C) conditions overcoming non critical conditions. Operating conditions The electric window function should only be activated with the ignitino on (+ 15V) except for the central closing/opening of the windows using the remote control and in the timed period without the key described later on. During the starting stage, any movement of the windows in progress is interrupted and does not continue until the starting is over. The downwards movement of the window during starting does not have to be stopped (but continues until the lower end of travel position) if the NPG and NPP door nodes detect that the movement is due to the intervention of the anti-crush safety system. After a key off, the front windows can be operated either manually or automatically for a period of 2 minutes ± 1sec. managed by the door nodes. . When this period has elapsed, the node no longer acquires new commands, but brings any received before the 2 minute period to a conclusion. If, during the timed period, the door nodes detect the opening of one of the doors, the nodes no longer acquire new commands, but bring any received before the opening of the door to a conclusion. If one of the doors is already open at the key off, the door node brings any commands received before the opening of the door to a conclusion. In the case of commands given simultaneously on the driver's and passenger sides, the passenger window movement logic is as follows: Command from driver's side Command from passenger side Passenger side front window movement Up Up Up Up Down No Movement Down Up Down Down Down Down Central closing/opening of windows activated Central window closing This function makes it possible to completely close the windows in a single operation. The central closing functino using the remote control (signals managed by NBC) is only activated in the following circumstances: - Key - OFF; - Windows initialized; - Anti-crush safety protection activated. The central closing of the windows can only be carried out by means of a specific signal sent from the NBC via the CAN. This command is acquired directly by the NPG and the NPP which implement the movement of the respective windows. Central window opening This function makes it possible to completely open the windows in a single operation. The central opening functino using the remote control (signals managed by NBC) is only activated at the Key-off. The central opening of the windows can only be carried out by means of a specific signal sent from the NBC via the CAN. This command is acquired directly by the NPG and the NPP which implement the movement of the respective windows. The central closing/opening of the windows cannot be activated simultaneously for 4 windows. For this reason the movement follows the logic described below: Left rear electric window Operation delayed by 30 ms in relation to the command Right rear electric window Operation delayed by 60 ms in relation to the command Left front electric window Operation delayed by 90 ms in relation to the command Right front electric window Operation delayed by 120 ms in relation to the command Anti-crush safey function There is an anti-crush safety sensor fitted to the electric window motor which guarantees the reversal of the electric window motor each time an obstacle (e.g. finger, hand, etc.) comes between the window and the actual seal, thereby preventing it from being accidentally crushed. This function confers a high level of safety on the model especially in there are any children on board who activate the windows accidentally. The anti-crush safety function is activated during both manual and automatic operation. There are two "inversion zones" and "non inversion zones" for the anti-crush safety system:ns - the "inversion zone" corresponds to the space between 200 mm from the upper edge and the upper edge itself; - the "non inversion zone" corresponds to the remaining space. If the NPG and NPP detect the presence of an obstacle in the "inversion zone" whilst the window is moving upwards, they should interrupt the upwards movement and reverse it immediately in a total time of < 30ms. The reversal of the window should reach a position corresponding to an opening of at least 200 mm from the upper edge or at least 50 mm higher than the initial starting position of the window. During the entire inversion time the NPG and NPP do not accept any type of rasing or lowering command. If the NPG and NPP detect the presence of an obstacle in the "non inversion zone" they should only interrupt the upwards movement of the window. Override function management If the anti-crush safety function intervenes five consecutive times within a minute, the NPG and NPP should inhibit the automatic closing operation of the window (the opening operation continues to be present automatically) only allowing it in steps of 7 cm ± 1cm with the control button having to be released for the next manoeuvre (degraded window closing mode). In order to restore the correct operation of the system, one of the following operations must be performed: - key off operation followed by a key on; - a downwards movement of the window in question made by the user. Anti-crush safety system initialization procedure If the system has not been initialized, the NPG and NPP respectively: - do not allow the automatic closing of the window (the opening continues to be present automatically), but only in manual mode; - do not allow the central opening/closing. The initialization of the anti-crush safety system is designed for the NPG and NPP to learn the window position parameters along the entire travel. The initialization procedure must be carried out: - the first time at the end of the line at the factory; - after each time the battery is disconnected. To initialize the anti-crush safety system, proceed as follows: - place the window to be initialized in the lower end of travel position (manually or automatically); - raise the window in manual mode until it is in the top end of travel position (without interruptions) using the UP button; - once the upper end of travel position has been reached, continue to operate the UP control for at least 1 sec. After having initialized the system the NPG and NPP will allow both the automatic upwards movement of the window and the central opening/closing. Management of anti-crush safety system failure If the NPG and NPP detect a failure in the anti-crush safety system (for example they do not receive the position signal from the sensors) they must inhibit the upwards movement of the window in automatic mode only allowing it in "degraded mode". If, during the manual or automatic upwards movement of the window, the anti-crush safety system failure condition occurs, the NPG and NPP should stop the window immediately. The NPG and NPP send anti-crush safety system failure signals on the network each time the antipinch protection is missing due, for example, to failures in the system or the windows not being initialized. Safety functions in the case of a malfunction If there is a system malfunction, the door node should activate the following procedures: - If the motor power supply outlet wiring is broken, the control unit de-energizes the relays in a maximum of 500ms in the following two cases: on activation (upwards or downwards) because no current is detected; during the upwards movement, because a current below 0.8 A is detected. - If at the key on (ignition key inserted and turned ON), in the presence of a fault at the control buttons (short circuit of buttons remain pressed), the operation of the control is inhibited until the defect disappears (or the button is released) for a period of > 60 ms. - If the buttons are pressed for longer than 12 seconds, the operation of the motor is inhibited; - If the down button is short circuited or pressed for more than 30 seconds, the command is inhibited to be able to close the window. Puddle lights management When the front doors are opened a negative (earth) signal is sent from the microswitches in the driver's side and passenger side lock geared motor to the Body Computer (NBC) which wakes up the CAN and notifies the driver's door (NPG) and passenger door (NPP) nodes of the door status. These control the switching on of the various bulbs in the lower part of the doors. The function is activated both with the ignition device inserted and turned to ON (key on) or not inserted or turned OFF (key off). Opening one of the doors causes the lights to come on for a maximum period of 3 minutes. When this timed period expires it will only be possible to reactivate the puddle lights after one of the doors has been reopened once again. Closing both doors causes the lights to go out immediately. 7005N FRONT DOOR CENTRAL LOCKING SYSTEM Central locking system Introduction The central locking system manages the door and boot locks in order to protect the passenger compartment against entry by unauthorized persons. The door unlocking/locking management strategy is carried out by the NBC, whilst the NPP NPG and NVB nodes activate the motors for the locks in accordance with the commands transmitted via the CAN from the NBC. The fuel flap is managed directly by the NPG and is therefore connected to the locked/unlocked status of the driver's door. The recognition component for the central locking system is the T.E.G. (Transmitter for Entry and Go). A - Front view B - Rear view The T.E.G. has a special insert that be extracted manually in order to be able to lock/unlock the front and rear doors. For the front doors the locking function is carried out at the mechanical back-up pawl located under the exterior handle, whilst the unlocking function is carried out directly at the lock (side part of the door). For the rear door, on the other hand, the door locking function is carried out at the lock; the unlocking function is not permitted. 1 - Emergency key (back-up) 2 - Key release lever The mechanical insert in the T.E.G. makes it possible to control the locking/unlocking of the doors from outside the passenger compartment using the pawls and locks. The pawls in the driver's and passenger doors make it possible to unlock the door concerned only. The vehicle exterior handles allow access to the passenger compartment from the outside to the door unlocked only. The interior handles, on the other hand, make it possible to leave the passenger compartment, with the dead lock not engaged, with the door either locked or unlocked. The boot can be opened by using the boot handle and the electrical contact. The central locking system includes a dead lock function. This function makes it possible to mechanically disconnect the interior door opening handles and the safety knob, so that it is not possible to open the door from the inside after having broken the glass (greater protection against theft). The instrument panel or, on top of the range versions, the NIT info telematic node, are used for personalizing the operation options (user settings): for example, the unlocking of the driver's door or the boot independently. There are 2 buttons (mono stable buttons) in the control panel on the tunnel (PCT) that allow the central locking and unlocking of all the doors. 1 - LED signalling doors locked (amber yellow) 2 - Door locking button 3 - Door unlocking button There is an amber yellow LED in this control panel on the central locking button. If it is on this signals that all the doors are closed whilst if it is off this indicates that at least one of the doors is unlocked. The red deterrent LEd is located on the driver's door panel. Management of central locking from outside the vehicle Central locking system with radiofrequency remote control The T.E.G. has a radiofrequency remote control function that allows the remote control (minimum range 20 m) of the door locking/unlocking operations or the release of the boot. The T.E.G. has 3 buttons that allow the operation of the central locking system: one button for unlocking the doors, one for locking the doors and one for releasing the boot. Each transmitter contains a secret code that identifies it unequivocably. 1 - Boot release button 2 - Door unlocking button 3 - Door locking button Using the T.E.G. as a radiofrequency remote control it is possible through the instrument panel or, on top of the range versions, through the NIT info telematic node, to personalize the operating options (user settings). The direction indicators and the red LED in the door panel are used to signal that the command has been received and/or to signal that a manoeuvre has not been carried out by the system (the signals are activated according to the market). As stated previously, the transmitter has 3 buttons, each of which has a specific function described in the table below. Button/Function Single press Double press Long press End of long press Locking button (with all the doors closed) - Door locking - Boot locking - Courtesy light switching off - Red LED in door and blinker on - Switching on of alarm (if present) - Switching on of dead-lock function - Red LED in door and blinker flashing - Window closing - Window closing interruption Unlocking button - Driver's door unlocking (*). - Boot release (*). - Switching off of dead-lock function. - Switching on of courtesy lights. - Red LED in door and blinker off. - Switching off of alarm (if present). - Unlocking of all the doors (*). - Window opening. - Window opening interruption. Boot button - Boot release. - Blinker flashing. - - - (*): previous set-up using NQS/NIT. The button pressing modes are as follows: - single press: the control component is pressed once; - double press: the control component is pressed twice within 1 second. The double press takes place if a control component is pressed within 1 second of having been released; - long press: the control component is kept pressed continuously for more than 2 seconds; - end of long press: the long action is interrupted the moment the control component is released. Locking the doors When the locking button is pressed, the locks are locked centrally. The normal door locking signals are supplemented by the flashing of the direction indicators for 1 sec. and the LED in the driver's door panel coming on for 3 secs. followed by the deterrent state, in order to signal that the remote command has been received. If the button is pressed with the vehicle already locked, the manoeuvre and the signalling are still carried out. If one or more of the doors has not been properly shut, the locking command is inhibited and the direction indicators flash at 3 Hz (30% duty-cycle) for 3 seconds: this warns the user to make sure the doors are properly shut. If only the boot is not properly shut, the locking command is carried out and the direction indicators flash at 3 Hz (30% duty-cycle) for 3 seconds followed by the deterrent state: this warns the user to make sure the boot is properly shut. Unlocking the doors When the unlocking button is pressed all the doors are unlocked. The normal door unlocking signals are supplemented by two flashes (0.5 secs.) of the direction indicators and the red LED in the driver's door panel going out to signal that the remote command has been received. If the button is pressed with the vehicle already unlocked, the manoeuvre and the signalling are still carried out. Independent driver's door unlocking If the "independent driver's door unlocking" setting is activated, when the unlocking button is pressed only the driver's door is unlocked whilst all the other doors remain locked preventing access by unauthorized persons: it is then possible to unlock the other doors as well by pressing the unlocking button a second time within 1 second of pressing it the first time. Dead lock function The dead-lock function is engaged using the remote control the moment the doors are locked by pressing the button a second time within 1 second of pressing it the first time. The engagement of the dead-lock is therefore a voluntary action. The normal dead locking signalling is supplemented by two flashes lasting 0.5 seconds of the direction indicators and the red LED in the door panel. It is impossible to get out of the passenger compartment after switching on the dead-lock: the dead-lock function should therefore only be activated after checking that the passenger compartment is empty. Opening boot/tailgate There is a third button on the remote control which, if pressed once, allows the release of the boot: the latter is unlocked and released, being slightly raised. The operation is signalled by the direction indicators flashing twice. When the boot is closed again it returns to the state prior to the opening only signalling the locking if there is a surveillance alarm. Auxiliary functions All the door windows can be closed at the time the doors are closed by keeping the locking button pressed for at least 2 seconds: at this point the windows start to move and continue as long as the button is pressed. In the same way, all the door windows can be opened at the time the doors are unlocked by keeping the unlocking button pressed for at least 2 seconds: at this point the windows start to move and continue as long as the button is pressed. The window raising and lowering functions using the remote control are only activated if the anti-crush safety device is activated. Central locking system from inside the vehicle Buttons for central locking and unlocking of the locks There are 2 buttons (mono stable buttons) in the control panel on the tunnel (PCT) that allow the central locking and unlocking of all the doors. When the locking button is pressed all the locking are locked (including the boot). If one or more of the doors is open, the command is inhibited. Pressing the unlocking button unlocks all the locks. If the doors have been locked using the remote control, pressing the unlocking button does not produce any request and the button is disabled. The button must be re-enabled after an unlocking command coming from the remote control and/or FIS (inertia switch). 1 - LED signalling doors locked (amber yellow) 2 - Door locking button 3 - Door unlocking button The LED in the locking button behaves as follows: Action LED status Locking using interior button - All doors closed: ON - One or more doors open: OFF (the command is not carried out) Door locking at 20 Km/h ON Door unlocking command OFF Unlocking by inertia switch OFF The LED goes out: - when any of the doors is opened; - when the timed period of 2 minutes expires (only in key off conditions); - when any unlocking command is given. The door status signalling LED is independent of the boot status. The LED is operated by the NBC which also manages the timed delay at the key off. The behaviour of the door status LED will always follow the instructions of the last command received. In the key off status, the LED should go out after a period of 2 minutes. Each time the central door locking button is pressed at the key off, the door status LED should always come on (or remain on) for a timed delay of 2 minutes after the button is pressed. If there is a move from a key off status to a key on status, the LED should signal the correct status of the doors. Therefore if all the doors are locked at the key on, it should come on or remain off if at least one of the doors is unlocked. Unlocking the locks from the inside Using any of the door handles from the inside, the lock for the door in question should be unlocked and the door opened. To unlock the locks only, use the central unlocking button on the PCT. If the interior handle of one of the doors is pulled when it is opened, the central unlocking of the locks is always commanded. If the "independent driver's door unlocking" setting is activated, pulling the driver's door handle when it is opened, will unlock the driver's door only whilst the other doors will remain locked. If the vehicle battery does not supply sufficient energy to the central locking electrical system (or the battery is run down or after an accident) it is possible to open the doors mechanically. The following mechanical back-ups exist for this situation: - mechanical connection at the exterior handles with the door unlocked (for emergency access from the outside); - mechanical connection at the interior handles with built-in safety unlocking (for leaving the passenger compartment in an emergency); - mechanical unlocking of the driver's/passenger door lock using the pawl with a mechanical insert (for access from the driver's door with the vehicle locked). The exterior mechanical connections are only activated if the doors are unlocked. If the driver has activated the central locking from the inside and if after an accident it has not been possible to activate the automatic unlocking function for the locks because of the battery, it will not be possible to gain access to the passenger compartment from the outside. Central locking system with emergency insert (back-up) Locking the doors The front and rear door locks can be locked individually using the mechanical back-up in the respective locks by inserting the T.E.G. emergency insert and turning it anti-clockwise until it is in the position illustrated in the diagram. The locking of the front and rear doors is exclusively mechanical by nature. Unlocking the doors The front door locks can be unlocked individually by proceeding as follows: - insert the T.E.G. emergency insert in the pawl (driver's or passenger door); - turn the insert towards the rear of the vehicle (1) until the lock is heard to click; - return the insert to a vertical position (2) and extract it from the pawl; - lift up the handle (3). The unlocking of the front doors is exclusively mechanical by nature. Replacing the t.e.g. battery To replace the T.E.G. battery, proceed as follows: - move the retaining lever (1) sideways and extract the emergency metal insert (2); - extract the battery holder compartment (3) using the emergency metal insert and replace the battery (3) pushing it sideways, taking care not to reverse the polarity; - refit the battery holder compartment (3) and the emergency metal insert (2) inside the T.E.G. if the battery is run down, another 100 activations are still guaranteed (including locking, unlocking and opening the boot). Child safety The vehicle has a mechanism on both rear doors that makes it possible to switch the child locks on/off mechanically. With the child-proof locks on the rear doors cannot be opened from inside the passenger compartment using the interior handles. These doors can only be opened from the outside if the door is unlocked. The child-proof locks on/off status is not signalled. The procedure for switching the child-proof locks on is described below: - insert the T.E.G. emergency insert in the special pawl located on the inside of the door (vertical position A); - turn the key and position it horizontally (B); - extract the key and close the door concerned. A - Device switched on (door can be opened from the inside); B - Device switched off (door locked). The device remains on even if the doors/boot are unlocked electrically using the remote control. Unlocking the doors through the f.i.s. signal The F.I.S. (inertia switch) sensor status is acquired directly from the NBC, therefore the latter controls the unlocking of the doors in accordance with the strategy described previously. The NBC replicates the lock unlocking command, for a second time 1 sec., after the command sent previously. The signal coming from the FIS sensor only causes the boot to be unlocked if the boot is subject to the doors. If the boot is set to "always locked", the signal from the inertia switch will not have any effect. Signalling led There is a high efficiency red LED on the vehicle (which is clearly visible from the outside in all light conditions) located in the driver's door panel. 1 - LED The LED signals the following conditions: - locking of the locks: the LED lights up for 3 seconds. If some of the doors or the boot are not properly shut at the time when the locks are locked, the LED flashes at 3 Hz (30% duty-cycle) for 3 seconds. - switching on of dead-lock function: after the dead lock has been switched on, the LED flashes twice for 0.5 seconds. At the end of this dual flashing, the LED remains on constantly until three seconds have elapsed and then moves on to deterrence signalling. - deterrence: once the door lock signal has been issued, the LED flashes at 0.8 Hz (5% duty-cycle) to indicate that the vehicle is locked (dissuasion function): the flashing ends when the locks are later unlocked. The deterrence signalling is only activated if a door locking command has been successful. Specific functions of the central locking system Logic alignment after mechanical unlocking at key on and key off With the vehicle locked, pulling the interior handle produces the mechanical unlocking of the door involved, local to the individual door (not detected by the system). The NBC having detected the transition of the door from closed to open, alters the logic status transmitted on the network and may or may not command the unlocking of the doors, in particular: - opening via the rear handle: the status of the door involved is aligned; - opening via the driver's handle: according to the vehicle set-up, the unlocking of the doors is commanded; - opening via the passenger handle: the central unlocking is commanded. In the last two cases the boot is also unlocked (if it has not been set in an independent mode). Automatic locking It is possible, using the NQS/NIT set-up menu, to enable or disable the automatic locking of the doors when a pre-set speed is exceeded. If the function is enabled, the NBC compares the vehicle speed with the level of 20 Km/h and requests the locking of the doors when this speed is exceeded. The doors are only locked after all the doors are closed and after the first time the level of 20 Km/h is exceeded. If the doors are locked by this function, the user can unlock the doors using the central unlocking button. If the speed drops below 20 km/h with the doors locked, the doors are not released. If, with the vehicle locked, any one of the doors is opened and then closed (mechanically unlocked), when the speed level is next exceeded, the NBC will request the locking once again. Doors/boot/bonnet open buzzer The NQS acquires the door, boot, bonnet (only if the alarm is fitted) status and vehicle speed signals from the B-CAN. After a key on, if the following conditions are verified: - a door or the boot or the bonnet is open; - the speed > 4 Km/h. The NQS emits a cycle of acoustic signals for a period of 5 seconds and (if the display permits) the relevant message is shown (for example, right front door open). The cycle of acoustic signals is only interrupted if at least one of the following conditions takes place: - all the doors, the boot or the bonnet are closed; - the vehicle speed < 4 Km/h. Inhibition by high number of manoeuvres If 10 locking or unlocking manoeuvres are carried out in 25 seconds, the NBC inhibits the locking and unlocking commands and signals for 30 seconds. As a result, the last manoeuvre before the inhibition can be an unlocking or a locking. 7005R FRONT DOOR MIRRORS Introduction The exterior rear view mirrors on the front doors of the Croma carry out the following functions: - electrical movement; - heating; - folding; - outside temperature management (driver's mirror only). This vehicle can be equipped with two mirror adjustment systems: - without driving position node (NAG); - with driving position node (NAG) on driver's seat. The only difference between the two systems described above is as follows: - in the former case, the door mirrors can only be moved; - in the latter case, the door mirrors can be moved, 3 defined positions can be memorized/recalled and the passenger door mirror is automatically positioned after reverse gear is engaged. The heating of the mirrors is managed using the same logic as the defrosting of the rearscreen on all versions with manual and automatic climate control (MAX-DEF). The folding of the door mirrors, managed by the respective door nodes, is activated using the special button the driver's door control panel. On versions with automatic climate control, there is an NTC sensor on the driver's mirror providing outside temperature information that is useful for different strategies, including: - passenger compartment climate control; - outside temperature display at NQS/NIT. Electrical movement The NPG acquires the mirror selection and movement commands directly from the control panel on the driver's door. At the key off any manually operated movement requests are not implemented. In the case of mirrors that are not indexed, the NPG acquires the movement commands for both the driver's door mirror and the passenger door mirror. The NPG manages the movement of the driver's door mirror directly and transmits the movemement commands for the passenger door mirror via the B-CAN. The NPP receives the commands and manages the passenger door mirror directly. In the case of indexed mirrors, in addition to the functions described for non-indexed mirrors, there are the following additional functions: - placing the mirrors in the positions memorized previously by the NAG. - automatic positioning of the passenger door mirror when reverse gear is engaged. The driving position node (NAG) transmits the position that the two door mirrors should be in, in accordance with the memories set previously, via the B-CAN. When this position is received, the NPG and NPP move the respective mirrors until they are in the required position. This movement should be managed in such a way that the mirror is moved from the start position to the finish position as quickly as possible in a linear movement. If commands arrive simultaneously from the NAG and the joystick, the latter take priority and cancel out the NAG command. If, following a request to position the mirrors from the NAG, the movement of the driver's front seat is interrupted, the positioning of the mirrors is completed. The NPG and the NPP are enabled, for a minute after the key off, to receive and implement any movement requests from the memory. Mirror folding The NPG acquires the folding command for both door mirrors (unstable control from the driver's door control panel). Each time the control is pressed it produces the movement of the mirrors in the opposite direction to where they started from. if the position of the mirror is altered voluntarily/accidentally by hand or the battery has been disconnected, the actual position of the mirror could be different from the status memorized by the door nodes therefore the first time the control button is pressed there may be no effect from the point of view of the user. The folding is always activated for both mirrors uding the key on and lasts for 2 minutes after the key off or until one of the doors is opened. An opening/closing movement of the mirrors initiated during this enablement period will be completed. The NPG does not consider any opening/closing commands during a mirror movement in progress. The NPG and NPP operate the opening/closing movement of the mirrors for a maximum time of 8 secs. as a further safety feature in case the mirror encounters an obstacle when it is moving. If the mirror folding command is activated more than 5 or 6 times in a period of 2 minutes, the door nodes should inhibit operation for 30 seconds. The last manoeuvre accepted is that of opening the mirrors. Outside temperature management The outside temperature information is supplied to the network in degrees Celsius (°C). The calculation of the value to be transmitted (every 500 msec) takes place using a specific algorithm that takes into account the value acquired by the NTC sensor located on the driver's door mirror, suitably filtered. The outside temperature information should be measured with an accuracy of at least 0.5°C and with a tolerance of +/- 5% including the tolerance of the sensor and the acquisition hardware. It is sent, via the CAN, to the nodes involved, such as: - NCL, which uses this signal for the automatic control strategies; - NQS, which, depending on the outside temperature, should warn the driver of a possible "ice danger" by means of a symbol and a specific message in the display. - NIT, for its display.

SPECIFICATIONS Like the front doors, the rear doors have also been designed with a structure and panels that have no sharp corners to reduce the risk of possible to injury to the occupants to a minimum. The locks and control linkage are protected against break ins by a shield that prevents access to the mechanisms from the outside. The safety closure from the inside of the vehicle is activated by a special button on the centre tunnel at the height of the trim on the gearbox. The side panel features the armrest, directly in the panel and an oddments pocket in the lower part. The layout of the functional elements of the panel has been designed to allow the correct interaction with the body of the occupant in the case of a side impact. They are smooth and soft at the top, whilst the projection of the armrest is rendered harmless by the fact that it collapses at a load level well below that which would risk injury to the organs in the abdomen. The door also features a carrier which, in addition to carrying out a support function for the electric window motor, the guides and the various cables, is integrated with the actual door with a structural function. The following are also present: - opening/closing handle; - door interior opening lever; - electric window control (if enabled by the contol panel on the driver's side); - oddments pocket. There are two speakers in the panel, one of which is a tweeter for amplified versions and versions with Connect Nav+ The sliding window is made from heat-proof, tempered glass and is moved by a guided cable type window opening device. The seal on the upper profile of the door, by the glass, and the glass scraper trims guarantee an excellent aerodyanmic seal. COMPOSITION Exploded view of the rear door. 1 - Interior door panel 2 - Carrier 3 - Window opening guide 4 - Bowden cable 5 - Armrest 6 - Window opening seal 7 - Glass 8 - Window control 9 - Check strap 10 - Door opening interior handle 11 - Electric window motor 12 - Lock 13 - Speaker 14 - Tweteer 7010M REAR SIDE DOORS ELECTRIC WINDOWS Rear doors eletric windows control The electric windows control on the rear doors is described below. Operation The left and right rear door control panels send a signal to the electric window function for the respective door to the NPG control unit which acquires the commands and transmits them via the CAN to the boot control unit (NVB) which manages and carries out the function described later on. The movement of the rear windows can also be managed by the driver's door control panel. For checks relating to the control unit pin out, See descriptions 5505A MULTI-FUNCTION COMPONENTS Operation The NPG node acquires the electric window commands (local or from the driver's side) for the left and right rear door and transmits them to the NVB via the CAN. The NVB node acquires the commands and manages its electric window motors directly. The left and right door motors are therefore controlled both manually and automatically in accordance with the following strategy: - manual mode refers to the starting and stopping of the window determined manually by the user by pressing the control button for: Ta = activation time > 50 ms and < 300 ms (brief command); when the latter is released, the motor stops; - automatic mode refers to the starting of the window determined manually by the user by pressing the control button for: Ta = activation time > 300 ms (long control). With the node enabled, the electric window should not work when the control buttons are pressed for less than 50 ms. The node should interrupt the operation of the window in the following cases: - when automatic movement is in progress and either the up or down control is pressed; - in the top or bottom end of travel position during either manual movement (in a time of 400ms ± 50ms) or automatic movement (in a time of 300ms ± 30ms). This is adjusted exclusively through the control for the motor current which is the self-adaptive type. The current self-adaptation means that the control should result in the request to close or open the vehicle windows being successful in conditions that range from a force of 6 - 8 Kg to forces that even reach 16 -18 Kg, in all voltage range (10 -16 V) and temperature (-30°C ÷ 75°C) conditions overcoming non critical conditions. Operating conditions The electric window function should only be activated with the ignitino on (+ 15V) except for the central closing/opening of the windows using the remote control and in the timed period without the key described later on. During the starting stage, any movement of the windows in progress is interrupted and does not continue until the starting is over. The downwards movement of the window during starting does not have to be stopped (but continues until the lower end of travel position) if the boot node NVB detects that the movement is due to the intervention of the anti-crush safety system. After a key off, the rear windows can be operated either manually or automatically for a period of 2 minutes ± 1sec. managed by the NVB. When this period has elapsed, the node no longer acquires new commands, but brings any received before the 2 minute period to a conclusion. If, during the timed period, the NVB detects the opening of one of the doors, the node no longer acquires new commands, but brings any received before the opening of the door to a conclusion. If one of the doors is already open at the key off, the NVB brings any commands received before the opening of the door to a conclusion. If commands leave the driver's front door and the driver's or passenger rear door simultaneously, the the movement logic for the driver's or passenger rear window is as follows: Command from driver's front door Command from left or right rear door Left or right rear window movement Up Up Up Up Down No movement Down Up Down Down Down Down Central window opening/closing activation Like the front doors, the rear door windows can also be opened/closed by remote control, in certain conditions, managed by the NVB. For further details, See descriptions 7005 PASSENGER COMPARTMENT FRONT SIDE DOORS Anti-crush safety function For this function too, the strategy adopted by the system for the rear windows is the same as for the front doors. For further details, See descriptions 7005 PASSENGER COMPARTMENT FRONT SIDE DOORS If the NVB detects the presence of an obstacle in the "inversion zone" whilst the window is moving upwards, it should interrupt the upwards movement and reverse it immediately. The intialization procedure for the anti-crush safety system and the safety functions in the case of a malfunction of the NVB are the same as those described for the NPG and NPP door nodes. 7010N REAR SIDE DOORS CENTRAL LOCKING/CLOSING SYSTEM For the description of the operation of the central locking, See descriptions 7005 PASSENGER COMPARTMENT FRONT SIDE DOORS

SPECIFICATIONS The tailgate is produced by traditional pressing processes: it has an extensive bonded window with black serigraphed edges in the area where it overlaps with the structure. There is a defrosting circuit in the glass. There is an opening, under the window in the centre of the panel, that houses the rearscreen wiper blade. The rearscreen washer jet is housed in the top part of the tailgate. The electric opening handle can be found on the lower part. The FIAT logo is above the handle, and the badge saying CROMA is at the bottom on the left. The (left and right) rear light clusters containing the reversing and rear fog lamps are housed at the sides of the panel. For further details, See descriptions 5540 EXTERIOR LIGHTING The third bake light is located inside the tailgate upper trim moulding. The tailgate has an internal cover with two compartments for access to the lights and two housings for putting your hands in in order to be able to open or close the actual tailgate. The tailgate is opened by: - using the electric handle; - pressing the dedicated button on the T.E.G. remote control (release only); - in emergencies, using a special lever on the lock. The tailgate is kept in position by two gas springs. 7015A TAILGATE ASSEMBLY Composition View of tailgate components 1 - Rearscreen washer jet 2 - Wiper arm 3 - Rear light cluster 4 - FIAT logo 5 - CROMA model badge 6 - Handle 7 - Rearscreen wiper motor 8 - Tailgate lock 9 - Internal cover 10 - Seal 11 - Third brake light 12 - Tailgate hinges 13 - Telescopic struts 14 - Rear tailgate 7015B TAILGATE OPENING/CLOSING DEVICES Boot/tailage unlocking and opening Locking/unlocking the boot The boot is considered as a fifth door to all intents and purposes and it is managed by the NBC which receives the status to be implemented and updates the current boot "locked/unlocked" status. The boot default condition is subject to the central locking system. Using the set-up logic managed by the NQS or, if fitted, the NIT, the "boot always locked" option can be set. As a result of the choice made by the user, the boot may or may not be unlocked together with the doors. For further details, See descriptions 7005 PASSENGER COMPARTMENT FRONT SIDE DOORS When the boot is closed, it is aligned with the status of the vehicle (unlocked if the doors are unlocked, locked if the doors are locked) unless there is a different setting; in the latter case, it is locked when closed again. Therefore if the boot is not subject to the door unlocking, it remains in the locked state. The boot is unlocked by a specific command on the remote control. Closing the boot again Once it has been opened using the electric handle, the boot returns to its previous state when it is closed again. - if the vehicle was unlocked, the boot is unlocked and can be opened againg using the handle (fifth door behaviour); - if the vehicle was locked, the boot is locked, realigning itself with the status of the doors. Independent boot unlocking The behaviour of the boot can be set to 2 operating modes using the instrument panel or the NIT: - boot subject to central locking (default): the boot status reflects door status. With the vehicle locked, the boot is locked, with the vehicle unlocked, the boot is unlocked; - boot independent: the boot is always locked (protecting its contents) and can only be opened using the mechanical key in the boot pawl. Emergency opening of the boot In order to be able to open the tailgate from the inside, if the vehicle battery were run down or if there were a problem with the tailgate electric lock, proceed as follows: - completely lower the rear head restraints; - fold the rear seat cushions over; - fold the backrests over; - to unlock the tailgate mechanically, working from the inside of the luggage compartment, use the release lever shown in the diagram. 1 - Tailgate release lever

SPECIFICATIONS The vehicle has two compartment covers: the bonnet and the fuel filler flap. The bonnet consists of an outer cover assembled on a support frame. Layers of sealant are applied between the covering and the frame which, in addition to limiting vibrations also increase the strength of the assembly. The fuel filler flap is made of plastic which is painted to match to the colour of the bodywork. It is kept closed and unlocked by means of an electrically activated motorized device. In emergencies (e.g. electrical system failure) the flap can be unlocked by pulling a special cord. To access this cord the cover inside the luggage compartment on the right hand side must be removed manually. 7025A BONNET LID The bonnet lid, produced through traditional pressing processes, has a frame which has pre-established collapse lines. this safety feature, together with specific retaining hooks, prevents the cover from penetrating the windscreen in the case of an impact. The cover has a preformed panel on the inside made from a sound absorbing material which is designed to improve the comfort of the occupants by reducing the acoustic emissions towards the passenger compartment and the exterior of the vehicle. To lower aerodynamic noise still further, there are two seals on the front support edge of the windscreen base trim and on the inner rear part of the bonnet. To complete the seal of the air intake compartment, thereby insulating it from the engine compartment, there are preformed mountings, made from a foam material, at the sides of the windscreen base trim, that prevent the access of flows of air coming from the actual engine compartment. Opening and closing the bonnet takes place by means of a single, central lock that incorporates a lever which, if pulled, release the safety hook and a bonnet opening switch that is useful for the alarm function. The lock is opened by means of a bowden cable operated by a lever in the lower side part of the dashboard, by the driver's running board. There is a support rod along the front crossmember that, released from its own securing device and fitted in the housing in the cover, allows the bonnet to remain raised. View of bonnet lid components 1 - Bonnet lid 2 - Bonnet hinges 3 - Retaining hooks 4 - Support rod 5 - Weatherstrip seal on bonnet 6 - Sound insulation lining 7 - Mountings 8 - Weatherstrip seal on bonnet crossmember 9 - Lid lock 10 - Release lever 7025C VARIOUS FLAPS (EXTERIOR) Fuel filler flap View of the fuel filler flap 1 - Fuel filler flap 2 - Retaining slot 3 - Fixing nuts 4 - Locking motor pin The fuel filler flap, made from plastic painted the same colour as the bodywork, is operated from inside the vehicle by means of the central locking. The hinged support for the flap is fastened by means of two nuts accessible from the inside of the compartment. There is a slot in the inner part of the flap for matching the locking pin activated by the special motor. The fuel flap is managed directly by the driver's door node (NPG) and is therefore connected to the locked/unlocked status of the driver's door. The fuel flap is locked/unlocked by the locking/unlocking command from the inner button, the pawl using the emergency key (back up insert) or the remote control (TEG). In emergencies a cord is used that is accessible from the right side of the luggage compartment which mechanically releases the fuel flap retaining motor. 1 - Emergency cord 2 - Retaining motor

INTRODUCTION The CROMA is also available in a version with a sun roof with a special extensively glazed area known as "Skydome outersliding" consisting of two electrically operated glass panels, the rear one fixed and the other moving. The roof has two sun blinds that slide independently towards the rear of the vehicle. Whilst driving it is therefore possible, from time to time, to have a different relationship with the surrounding environment. The Fiat CROMA can transform itself from a closed vehicle into a car with a glass roof or a vehicle with a sun roof. When you want the passenger compartment to be bright, it is possible to have the glazed part closed and the blind underneath open. If, on the other hand, you prefer driving under the open skies, it takes just seven seconds to completely open the front glass panel and the blind and you can enjoy a real "window to the world". COMPOSITION The diagram illustrates the sun roof components. 1 - Frame 2 - Wiring 3 - Deflector 4 - Rear blind 5 - Front blind 6 - Blind motor 7 - Connecting rod 8 - Rear moulding 9 - Front moulding 10 - Front glass 11 - Front roof 12 - Rear glass 13 - Rear roof 14 - Centre crossmember 15 - Rear crossmember 16 - Drive cable 17 - Mechanical guide 18 - Rear blind guide 19 - Side seals 20 - Rear blind support 21 - Centre seal 22 - Side seal 23 - Wind seal 24 - Glass seal 25 - Mechanical pipes 26 - Blind pipes 27 - Inclination pin 28 - Roof motor with C.T.A. 29 - Mechanisms The sunroof unit is built with an all-in-one structure: the glazed surface extends in direction Y from the right channel to the left. In direction X is extends to cover some 80% of the roof surface. Two non transparent fixed front and rear panels have the function of guaranteeing the aesthetic continuity with the windscreen and the tailgate. The glazed surface is divided into two panels, the rear one is fixed in heat-proof glass like the front sliding panel activated by a switch that can be adjusted by means of a five position selector. A sealing strip to protect against infiltration around the edges of the sliding section opening is in contact with the front sliding panel profile. The sun roof and electric front blind selectors are located on the front courtesy light cover and, by means of a control unit, control the operation of the electric motor, located on the rear of the roof. The movement for both takes place by means of the motor pinion that drives two flexible racks (bowden). The front and rear blinds used to protect against sunlight are sliding roller blinds. They slide along guides supported by teflon slide pads with rubber bearings between pad and guide. The front sun blind is electrically operated, the rear one is made from polyester and can only be operated manually. The latter has a handle in the front part for the grip which contains an attachment tooth for when the blind is open. The electronic control units are incorporated in the electric motor casing. There are two, one for the moving glass (master) and one for the blind (slave). The main sun roof sub-assemblies are: - Single SMC frame. - A system of right and left mechanisms, inserted in the aluminium guides, for moving the front glass panel, operated by the electric motor by means of a metal spiral cable. - 2 aluminium front guides for the sliding function: for the front pulley, the metal spiral cable and the front blind. - 2 aluminium rear guides for the sliding function for the pulley and the rear blind. - Electrically operated polyester front blind controlled by means of a rocker switch. On opening it wraps around the centre part of the roof allow complete visibility towards the outside of the car. - Manually operated polyester rear blind with a spring roller system which allows 2 positions, open or closed; on opening it wraps around the rear part of the roof allowing complete visibility towards the outside of the vehicle. - 2 glass panels 5 mm thick with a brightness transmission of TL > 13% and an energy transmission TE < 10%. - Front and rear roof panel painted in shiny black with serigraphy fitted on the sun roof kit. - Aluminium deflector with retractable plastic corners to avoid the effects produced by aerodynamic turbulence (buffeting and passenger comfort) in all driving conditions. - Plastic side moulding - Motor activating front glass panel with control unit for anti-crush safety function. - Motor activating front blind with control unit (with annti-crush safety function). FUNCTIONAL SPECIFICATIONS The assembly has no water drains so this function is carried out by the rain gutters on the roof. The positioning of the assembly on the bodyshell is guaranteed by references on the sun roof frame and by drillings in the bodyshell. The bonding to the bodyshell guarantees the water tightness (before and after fatigue/ageing) and is resistant to a vertical force equal to that produced by a pressure of 6000 N/m² applied to the perimeter of the bonded frame. Installation from the outside with the sun roof frame bonded to the bodyshell roof panel. When bonding it is possible to lower the assembly vertically (the bonding by means of the partner remains for a force on the glass perimeter of 250 Kg). Whilst opening, the front glass panel slides horizontally above the rear panel sliding along outer side guides. The colour of the glass used for the panels is grey and the light transmission is TL > 13% and the energy transmission is TE < 10%. The overall weight is 45 kg. SUN ROOF OPERATION Selector The sun roof is operated by activating the controls in the front centre courtesy light, namely the 5 position rotary selector (clockwise for opening and anti-clockwise for closing) for the movement of the glass panel and an impulse type opening/closing button for the blind. When the selector is operated the movement of the roof is only activated when the desired position is maintained for at least 400 ms. There is a corresponding opening of the sun roof for each of the 5 positions; position 1 corresponds to the least opening of the roof until position 5 is reached which is the complete opening of the roof. By pressing it vertically the rotary selector immediately stops the movement of the roof (e.g. in emergencies as described later on). View of 5 position control selector 1 - Selector Roof opening (at key on) From the roof completely closed, rotary selector in position "0", the glass panel opening takes place as described below: - First rotary selector position: translative movement of front panel into tilting position (opening in direction X vehicle 40 mm); - Second rotary selector position: translative movement of front panel (opening in direction X vehicle 180 mm); - Third rotary selector position: translative movement of front panel (opening in direction X vehicle 315 mm) - Fourth rotary selector position: translative movement of front panel (opening in direction X vehicle 453 mm); - Fifth rotary selector position: translative movement of front panel until it is completely open (opening in direction X vehicle 590 mm); By placing the selector in one of the positions, the roof moves automatically until it is in the desired position; therefore to open the roof completely in a single manoeuvre, place the selector in the last (fifth) position. the opening of the electric roof involves the opening of the front blind to prevent the air entering the passenger compartment from tearing the actual blind or producing an undesired noise effect. Roof closing (at key on) The closing of the panel does not affect the position of the blind, for each selector position there is a corresponding closing of the roof with the movement of the moving panel in direct X of the vehicle as described previously. By placing the selector in one of the positions, the roof moves automatically until it is in the desired position; therefore to close the roof completely in a single manoeuvre, place the selector in position "0". BLIND OPERATION Control buttons (one-touch) View of ONE-TOUCH control buttons 1 - Blind opening button 2 - Blind closing button Blind opening/closing (at key on) The opening/closing of the front sun blind takes place after pressing the pulse type button for > 3000ms and the action is interrupted when the button is pressed again. The blind has a One-Touch function for complete closing/opening. During the opening of the roof, in spite of the front blind being secured to the opening, it is not subject to the position of the front glass panel but is is not advisable to drive with the blind closed nd the glass open. The rear sun blind is opened and closed by manual operation. ANTI-CRUSH SAFETY FUNCTION The (HALL effect) anti-crush safety system is activated on the front profile of the glass panel and is managed by the engine electronic control unit (fitted at the rear). It is activated for the entire closing range of the panel therefore guaranteeing the reversal of the direction for a travel of 200mm if an obstacle is encountered. During vertical movements it is activated for openings of h > 14 mm from the level of the rear glass (minimum travel to exclude the contact section for the panel/seal where the maximum load is required to guarantee the water tightness), after meeting an obstacle on the lower rear side of the glass panel. It guarantees the reversal of the direction until the max tilting position is reached. Following the detection of a force of more than a certain level, corresponding to a greater current absorption and drop in rpm the sun roof control unit (CTA) commands the immediate stopping and reversal of movement. At the same time, the anti-crush safety system is activated on the front profile of the blind managed by the Slave electronic control unit (fitted at the rear) and, in particular, it is activated for the entire blind closing range. After it meets and obstacle (e.g. finger, hand, etc.) the slave control unit guarantees the reversal in direction equal to a travel of 200mm. After the activation of the anti-crush safety system, proceed as follows: - turn the rotary selector into another position, the sun roof will move into desired position; - press the rotary selector vertically once: the roof will assume the position indicated by the selector. The sun roof control unit also receives a vehicle speed signal because, depending on the speed, through the change in the force required for closing the roof changes and in certain circumstances this could be perceived as an impediment. The presence of ice or any foreign bodies in the sun roof guides could involve the repeated intervention of the anti-crush safety function. It is therefore necessary to make sure that there are no obstacles. In these cases the device can be inhibited by closing the sun roof (within 5 seconds of the intervention of the device), turning the selector to position "0" and keeping it pressed until the roof is closed. The movement during the closing takes place in stages. The anti-crush safety function can be excluded by using the selector inhibitor position. Following the reversal of the direction caused by the intervention of the anti-crush safety function it can be inhibited by keeping the rotary selector pressed in position "0" within 5 secs; the anti-crush safety function is not activated until the roof reaches the closing position or the selector is released. CONTROL UNIT INITIALIZATION If the sun roof and/or blind control units are replaced or after the battery has been disconnected, an intialization/reset procedure has to be carried out. Roof initialization For the initialization of the roof, carry out the following procedure: - insert the key and turn it to the ON position; - turn the selector fully to the left (anticlockwise, position "0"); - press the selector and keeping it pressed wait until the roof locks mechanically (clearly visible) after which the selector should be released; - within 5 seconds press the selector againn and keep it pressed: the roof should move completing a cycle automatically; in this stage, continue to keep the selector pressed; - when the roof stops, release the selector: the initialization is complete. At this point the selector can be rotated placing the roof in the desired position. Blind initialization For the initialization of the blind, carry out the following procedure: - insert the key and turn it to the ON position; - press the closing button and keep it pressed for long enough to notice the mechanical stop of the geared motor (clearly visible); - release the button; - within 5 seconds press the closing button again and keep it pressed: after the same number of seconds the blind will carry out an automatic cycle; during this stage keep the switch pressed; - when the blind movement cycle is over, the initialization is completed. - release the button. At this point the blind will be in the closed position. EMERGENCY MANOEUVRE The roof motor is housed in the rear part of the roof, at the height of the rear courtesy light. 1 - Emergency activating seat If the electric device for moving the roof fails, the sun roof can be moved manually proceeding as described below: - take the emergency key from the glove compartment; - remove the rear courtesy light applying leverage at the points shown by the arrows (figure A); - introduce the key into the housing (1, figure B) and turn it clockwise to open the roof or anti-clockwise to close it.

SPECIFICATIONS The bodyshell windows, the bonded windscreen and rearscreen and side windows, increase the structural strength of the bodyshell and improve the safety level of the vehicle in addition to greatly reducing aerodynamic noise. WINDSCREEN The windscreen is the heat-proof stratified type with acoustic PVB, comprising two layers of glass with a sheet of acoustic plastic material in between. This conformation prevents the layers of glass from shattering if there is any stone chipping maintaining visibility and, above all, guaranteeing a high degree of protection in the case of a head impact, The windscreen has a perimeter band, in the area that overlaps with the bodyshell, serigraphed in black. The windscreen contains the following: the rain/dusk sensor, stuck near the base of the electro-chromic interior rear view mirror mounting and the solar sensor (on versions with automatic climate control) located at the top of the dashboard at the base of the windscreen. REARSCREEN The rearscreen, made from non stratified tempered glass, is bonded to the tailgate structure. The inner surface of the rearscreen contains a series of defrosting rheophores. The connection of the rheophore to the electrical system takes place by means of two terminals, located on the left and right sides of the actual rearscreen. In the area where it overlaps with the tailgate structure, the rearscreen has a black serigraphed area. FIXED SIDE WINDOWS The fixed side windows, made from heat-proof tempered glass, are bonded to the bodywork. On the side of the windows corresponding to the centre pillar, there is a pressed seal which, with the door closed, prevents turbulence and wind noise. In the area where they are matched with the structure, the side windoes have a black serigraphed area.

SPECIFICATIONS All the vehicle interior trims, designed to satisfy the most stringent international standards governing flammability, are slow burning, do not ignite through accidental contact (for example if a cigarette is dropped), do not develop flames and, in the presence of severe overheating, are subject to combustion that produces strong, dense smoke. The design of the dashboard and the surrounding trims is aimed at producing a high level of comfort and a high degree of passive safety, achieved by eliminating all projections which could be dangerous to the occupants of the vehicle in the case of an impact. On the inside of the driver's sun visor there is a description of the correct usage of the child seat in the front passenger seat. For improved comfort there are two sun visors on the left and right, a courtesy light in the front part of the passenger compartment, a centre rear courtesy light (on versions with a sun roof) or two side rear courtesy lights (basic version) and left and right courtesy lights in the luggage compartment. The puddle lights are housed in the door panels in the lower rear area. The power supply for the vehicle interior courtesy lights follows the battery voltage control logic: the Body Computer acquires the "battery voltage" signal continously comparing it with its own limit value in order to implement the best energy saving strategy. With the ignition OFF or the key extracted (STOP), a 15 minute timer starts when any of the doors or the boot is opened. The lights are deactivated after this time limit. SPECIFICATIONS The structure of the front seats has been designed to assist the protection offered by the occupant protection system. Two metal bars, located at the front and rear under the front seat cushion, maintain the correct support of the occupant in a frontal impact and minimize the distortion of the seat in side impacts. The front pipe and the special shape of the cushion base prevent the occupants from sliding underneath the seat belt providing the so-called anti-submarining effect. The (bilateral type) robust hinging between the backrest and the base has been designed to ensure optimum retention of the occupant in the case of rear impacts at low speed and, in conjunction with suitable lighter areas on the side panels, gradually absorb the impact energy from rear collisions at high speed in a controlled manner. The seats are of vital importance in terms of comfort and safety: they are, in effect, the element that has to absorb the kinetic energy acquired by the body through the effect of stresses when cornering and during acceleration/deceleration. The front seats, in the front part of the seating area, have an excellent structure for anti-submarining, to prevent the body sliding forward under the seat belt in the case of severe frontal impacts. This also contributes in great measure to limiting injury to the abdomen and femur by reducing the body's forward acceleration. The FIAT Croma is equipped with the following devices for achieving and maintaing lasting comfort: 1) to enhance vibrational comfort and especially the absorption of vibrations produced from the road surface (e.g.: tram lines, etc.) the seats on the Croma are equipped, in the area of the gluteus ischium-coccyx, with an efficient spring system with a flexible pack made up of thin steel wires coated in plastic and secured by two clips to the perimeter frame; 2) to improve back support, the CROMA has a modern support system for the lumbar region specially designed to adapt fully to the back and support it tirelessly thanks to its considerable extension and operating range. 3) in addition, the driver's seat on the CROMA is height adjustable with a vertical travel of around 50 mm. The height adjustment is implemented through a ratchet lever with extremely reduced operating loads and is very easy to use. The guides slide lengthwise. They are a slight angle of 4.5° to raise the seat slightly when it is moved forwards. The combination of the seat height adjustment with the height and axial adjustment of the steering wheel makes it possible to produce the optimum driving position for an extremely wide range of drivers. The adjustment of the backrest angle is the continuous type and is regulated by a knob located in the area of the seat towards the outside of the passenger compartment to allow the adjustment of the angle. The adjustment of the lumbar support for the driver and the front passenger is available as an optional extra or is fitted as standard depending on the version; a knob with a lever on the outside of the seat regulates a mechanical that adjusts the lumbar area of the backrest. On versions with a high specification level there is also the possibility, on request, of electric seats that can move the driver's or passenger seat electrically producing height adjustment, tiltin the front and rear of the cushion, sliding the guides and adjusting the angle of the backrest. There is also the possibility for the driver's seat of setting 3 different positions that can be memorized and recalled by pressing the special buttons. Depending on the version, the customer can also request a cushion or backrest heating device for the front seats. This device, which can be activated through heater pads built into the seats, is available in an ON/OFF activation configuration (only on seats with mechanical movement) or with 3 different heating levels (on versions with electrical movement). The foam for the front seats is comfortable thanks to load carrying solutions (a parameter that mesures the capacity of the upholstery to yield under the weight of the body) that are differentiated depending on the area of the seat. The upholstery for the head restraints has been improved in terms of softness and they guarantee pleasant support; the shape of the head restraints has also been designed using the latest ergonomic standards to protect the user from the effects of whiplash. In rear impacts at low speed (< 20 km/h) the most common injury is whiplash. To reduce the risk of this injury to a minimum, the vehicle is fitted with head restraints capable of retaining the head in the case of rear impacts preventing irregular or excessive stresses to the cervical group of the vertebral column. The geometry of the head restraints in relation to the position of the nape of the neck of the occupants and their strength properties are very important in performing this anti-whiplash function. The anti-whiplash function includes devices that reduce the distance between the head and the head restraint. They are based on passive operation that exploits the inertia of the occupant to modify the position of the head restraint: in the case of a rear impact in which the occupant moves backwards significantly, this system uses the thrust of the back against the backrest allowing a movement closer to the seat and to the head restraint. The front head restraints have a height adjustment device that allows a movement of around 40mm, with a fastening to ensure stable and optimum positioning in all intermediate positions. The front seats also have seat belts with pretensioners and a built in seat belt switch plus an SBR presence sensor in the passenger seat only. See descriptions 5580C AIR BAG SYSTEM The front seats have the following specifications: - Distance between the centres of the guides 446 mm; travel 242 mm; - Backrest continuous adjustment device with bilateral joint; - Head restraint with vertical adjustment of around 40mm; - Semi-parallel seat lifting device fitted as standard on driver's and passenger side, travel 47.5 mm; - Rocker (tilt), optional on both front seats, angle +/- 2.5°; - Side bag fitted inside the seat cover; - Adjustable lumbar support. Features: - Seats with electrical movement; - Lumbar support; - Anti-whiplash device.
