Whilst driving, especially on unmade roads, there is knocking coming from the rear suspension. This diagnosis can only be made after See table S015 NOISE WHILST DRIVING . Carry out the latter first. If the problem is only on one side, carry out the checks and any operations on the appropriate side only. Test results 0 PRELIMINARY CHECKS All OK Problems encountered Operation Having carried out the road test, see the Table S15 RUMOROSITA' in condizioni di marcia , there was a knocking noise from the back. Continue depending on the circumstances in which the noise occurs End of diagnosis The noise disappears when the brake pedal is operated. The noise disappears when the handbrake is operated Op. 3380A04 HANDBRAKE - ADJUST TRAVEL The noise is also present in other conditions. Move on to Step 1 1 OIL LEAKS CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Raise the vehicle on a two column lift and check that there are no oil leaks from the shock absorber stem. Slight dampness on the stem is considered normal because there is evaporation during the operation of the shock absorber. If there is a persistent oil leak on the shock absorber stem, make sure that it is not coming from other parts of the vehicle that are lubricated Move on to Step 2 Leaks from other parts that are lubricated Search for the cause of the leak following the appropriate diagnostic procedure Leaks from the shock absorber stem. Replace the shock absorber Op. 4420A30 REAR SUSPENSION SHOCK ABSORBER (ONE), LEFT OR RIGHT - R.R. - CHECK WHEEL GEOMETRY SEPARATELY 2 HANDBRAKE CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Check that the handbrake cables or outer casing do not knock against the fuel tank, heat shields or bodywork during oscillations. Move on to Step 3 Inteference between outer casing or cables and other elements Cover the outer casing with foam rubber tape in the area of the interference or lubricate the cable 3 INTERFERENCE CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Check that the buffer is correctly fitted in its housing. Move on to Step 4 Buffer not correctly fitted. Replace the end of travel buffer Op. 4420A40 L/H OR R/H REAR SUSPENSION COIL SPRING (ONE) - R+R 4 TIGHTENING TORQUE CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Locate the area of the possible noise source: top or bottom. Starting from the area where the knocking was identified, check the tightening torques See Test 4420B on non-shear bolts: - upper shock absorber attachment to the body; - lower shock absorber attachment to the knuckle; - longitudinal arm to the knuckle; - for the brake caliper to steering knuckle; Visually inspect that the yield point type bolts have not loosened, the list is given below: - beam fastening to the body; - fastening of the antiroll bar to the beam; - fastenings of the connection beam to the bar and knuckle; - fastening of the longitudinal arm connection bracket to the body - fastenings of the upper wishbone to the beam and knuckle; - fastenings of the large lower wishbone to the beam and knuckle; - fastenings of the small lower wishbone to the beam and knuckle; - of the knuckle to the bearing. Move on to Step 5 Non-shear bolts not tightened to torque Restore the correct tightness Shear bolts loosened Replace the shear bolts and restore the correct tightness 5 LONGITUDINAL ARM CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Check for damage to the bush securing the longitudinal arm to the body. Move on to Step 6 Damage to the bush fastening the longitudinal arm to the body. Replacement of longitudinal arm Op. 4420C30 L/H OR R/H REAR SUSPENSION TIE ROD (ONE) - R+R 6 UPPER WISHBONE CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Check for clearance in the upper wisbhone attachment to the knuckle and rear frame. Also check the condition of the upper wishbone bushes. Move on to Step 7 There is clearance or the bushes are not intact. Replacement of upper transverse arm Op. 4420B35 REAR SUSPENSION UPPER SWINGING ARM, (ONE) LH OR RH - R R WITH CHECK OF WHEELS ATTITUDE APART 7 LARGE LOWER WISHBONE CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Check for clearance in the large lower wisbhone attachment to the knuckle and rear frame. Also check the condition of the large lower wishbone bushes. Move on to Step 8 There is clearance or the bushes are not intact. Replacing the large lower wishbone Op. 4420B18 REAR SUSPENSION REAR WISHBONE (ONE) - R R checking the camber values are correct Op. 4450A40 REAR WHEEL GEOMETRY - CHECK USING OPTICAL EQUIPMENT, INCLUDES ADJUSTMENT IF NECESSARY 8 SMALL LOWER WISHBONE CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Check for clearance in the small lower wisbhone attachment to the knuckle and rear frame. Also check the condition of the small lower wishbone bushes. Move on to Step 9 There is clearance or the bushes are not intact. Replacing the small lower wishbone Op. 4420B16 REAR SUSPENSION FRONT WISHBONE (ONE)- R R checking the toe-in values are correct Op. 4450A40 REAR WHEEL GEOMETRY - CHECK USING OPTICAL EQUIPMENT, INCLUDES ADJUSTMENT IF NECESSARY 9 ANTI-ROLL BAR CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation After disconnecting the upper ball joint on the connection bar to the knuckle, check that the antiroll bar is resistant to manual movement when symmetrical forces are applied. Move on to Step 10 The antiroll bar is not resistant to manual movement when symmetrical loads are applied. Replace the anti-roll bar Op. 4420C10 REAR SUSPENSION STABILIZER BAR - R+R 10 CHECK ON CORRECT OPERATION All OK Problems encountered Operation Check that the fault is no longer present. End of diagnosis The fault persists The knocking is caused by another system (e.g. the fuel float in the tank). Carry out the appropriate checks to identify the cause of the noise.

During a braking manoeuvre, whistling or squeaking can be heard from the wheel area. Vibrations are also felt in the passenger compartment 1 CHECK THE PAD TYPE AND SURFACE ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check: the condition of the pad braking surfaces; pad type. Move on to Step 2 1. Front braking surfaces vitrified or with traces of grease, oil or water. Pads of non-specified type. 1. Re-clean, check and remove the fault causes. Replace the pads if necessary Op. 3310A60 FRONT BRAKE PADS - REPLACE 2. Rear braking surfaces vitrified or with traces of grease, oil or water. Pads of non-specified type. 2. Re-clean, check and remove the fault causes. Replace the pads if necessary Op. 3310B62 REAR BRAKE PADS - REPLACE 2 CHECK DISCS ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check the condition of the brake discs. End of diagnosis 1. Front discs worn or damaged. Pads of non-specified type. 1. Regrind the discs or, if necessary, replace them Op. 3310A54 FRONT BRAKE DISCS REMOVED - GRIND Op. 3310A48 FRONT BRAKE DISC (ONE), LEFT OR RIGHT - R.R 2. Rear discs worn or damaged. Pads of non-specified type. 2. Regrind the discs or, if necessary, replace them Op. 3310B54 REAR BRAKE DISCS REMOVED - GRIND Op. 3310B48 REAR BRAKE DISC (ONE), LEFT OR RIGHT - R.R.

When the brake pedal is depressed slightly (even with the brakes cold) at average speed, the steering wheel and the brake pedal vibrate. 1 CHECK THE WHEEL STUD TIGHTENING ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check the wheel studs are correctly fastened Move on to Step 2 Incorrect tightness Tighten the wheel studs correctly. 2 CHECK FRONT DISCS ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check the following, in order: condition; changes in thickness; irregular disc wear. Move on to Step 3 Front discs worn irregularly or damaged. Regrind the discs or, if necessary, replace them Op. 3310A54 FRONT BRAKE DISCS REMOVED - GRIND Op. 3310A48 FRONT BRAKE DISC (ONE), LEFT OR RIGHT - R.R 3 CHECK ON PAD SURFACES CONDITION ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check: pad brake surface intactness; that the pads are not worn. End of diagnosis 1. Brake surfaces vitrified or with traces of grease, oil or water 1. Clean again, check and remove the causes of the fault 2. Front pads worn (reduced pad compressibility) 2. Replace the front pads Op. 3310A60 FRONT BRAKE PADS - REPLACE

Whilst the steering is operated there is a noise when it reaches the end of travel position. 0 PRELIMINARY CHECKS ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Visually inspect the power assisted steering fluid in the reservoir. Conduct a test by steering fully to one side and then releasing the steering wheel. Move on to Step 1 1. Fluid level too low. 1. Restore the correct level 2. The noise increases towards the end of travel position and with the engine speed (roar) 2. Move on to Step 1 3. The noise remains constant (hissing whilst steering, puffing on release) 3. No intervention is nececssary: the noise is due to the by-pass valve that discharges the excess pressure 1 CHECK ON POWER ASSISTED STEERING FLUID QUALITY ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Visually inspect the power assisted steering fluid in the reservoir. Make sure that there is no emulsified fluid (fluid that is lighter in colour with bubbles) Move on to Step 2 Emulsified fluid. Remove any air infiltrations from the power steering system pipes or replace the power steering reservoir Op. 4130B25 POWER STEERING PUMP ASSEMBLY R R FOR VERSIONS WITH AIR CONDITIONER 2 POWER ASSISTED STEERING PIPES CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check for constrictions in the flexible and rigid system pipes. Move on to Step 3 Pipes faulty. Replace the damaged parts, replacing all the seals Op. 4130B POWER STEERING HYDRAULIC SYTEM 3 CHECK CORRECT OPERATION OF MPU (Motor Pump Unit) ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check that the MPU is working properly See Test 4110DC ELECTRIC PUMP CHECK End of diagnosis MPU malfunction Replace MPU Op. 4130B25 POWER STEERING PUMP ASSEMBLY R R FOR VERSIONS WITH AIR CONDITIONER

After operating the steering numerous times, a noise is heard when the steering wheel is left still 0 PRELIMINARY CHECKS ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Visually inspect the power assisted steering fluid in the reservoir. Conduct a test by steering fully to one side and then releasing the steering wheel. Move on to Step 1 1. Fluid level too low 1. Restore the correct level 2. The noise heard is a knock/striking noise 2. Move on to Step 1 3. A blowing noise is heard in correspondence with the three steering wheel positions (120° apart) 3. No intervention is nececssary: the noise is due to normal system operation. 1 CHECK STEERING COLUMN BEARINGS ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check for excessive play in the steering column: check the condition and efficiency of the steering column mount bearings. End of diagnosis Bearings worn or damaged Replace the bearings

PRELIMINARY CHECKS ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION 0 Connect the climate control system to the special repressurizing equipment and check the system pressures by carrying out the test: See Test 5040OB CHECK ON OPERATION OF AIR CONDITIONING SYSTEM (PRESSURE) Check the wear condition and correct belt alignment and tensioning. Run the engine at idle speed with the A/C system off and check whether the noise comes from other auxiliary components (engine fan, water pump, alternator). Increase the rpm and check for vibrations. Move on to Step 2 1. Pressure level incorrect 1. Move on to Step 1 2. Belt alignment/tension incorrect or belt worn. 2. Restore correct alignment/tension or replace the belt. 3. The noise is from other auxiliary components (engine cooling fan, coolant pump, alternator). 3. Continue as indicated in the diagnostic test procedure. CHECK PRESSURE VALUES IN HIGH AND LOW PRESSURE CIRCUIT ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION 1 Keep the recharging device connected and check the pressure levels in the system high and low pressure circuit with the compressor on and engine running: pressure values low in high and low pressure circuit; pressure values high in high and low pressure circuit; check that the pressure values (high and low) during compressor operation do not pulse and that the circuit does not equalise slowly when the engine is turned off. End of diagnosis 1. Low circuit pressure values (insufficient coolant in circuit) 1. Flush the system and restore the correct charge of fluid and gas Op. 0010T84 COOLANT FOR AIR CONDITIONING SYSTEM - DEHYDRATE AND REPRESSURIZE 2. High circuit pressure values (too much coolant in circuit) 2. Flush the system and restore the correct charge of fluid and gas Op. 0010T84 COOLANT FOR AIR CONDITIONING SYSTEM - DEHYDRATE AND REPRESSURIZE 3. Pulsing circuit pressure values (compressor discharge valve permanently open) Op. 5040A20 AIR CONDITIONING COMPRESSOR - R+R - INCLUDES FLUID LEVEL CHECK AND TOP UP IF NECESSARY 3. Replace the compressor If the compressor is replaced due to a mechanical problem, remember to clean the entire circuit and change the dehydrating filter. CHECK ON FASTENING OF PIPES AND COMPONENTS ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION 2 Check that the compressor and system pipes and components are correctly fastened. Check the following, in order: bracket fastening to the engine block; fastening of pipes (by bands and spacers) no interference between pipes and other components in the engine compartment condenser cleanlineness or damage (presence of mud, foreign bodies). Also check for cracks in the compressor fastenings to the bracket on the engine block. Move on to Step 3 1. Fastening of components incorrect 1. Retighten fastenings to torque 2. Interference in the engine compartment 2. Restore the correct layout of the pipes 3. Condenser obstructed or damaged. 3. Clean or replace the condenser Op. 5040A40 AIR CONDITIONING CONDENSER - R+R 4. Also check for cracks in the compressor fastenings to the bracket on the engine block. 4. Replace the compressor Op. 5040A20 AIR CONDITIONING COMPRESSOR - R+R - INCLUDES FLUID LEVEL CHECK AND TOP UP IF NECESSARY CHECKS TO CARRIED OUT WITHOUT THE COMPRESSOR ON ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION 3 Checks to be carried out without the compressor on: disconnect the service belt and check for contact between the armature and pulley; with the belt disconnected, check for contact between the pulley and external elements; Check the wear of the pulley bearing off by rotating the moving plate in both directions of rotation. Check whether the compressor magnetic coupling shows signs of overheating. Move on to Step 4 1. Presence of contact between armature and pulley. 1. Replace the compressor electromagnetic coupling with pulley Op. 5040A20 AIR CONDITIONING COMPRESSOR - R+R - INCLUDES FLUID LEVEL CHECK AND TOP UP IF NECESSARY 2. Presence of contact between the pulley and external elements. 2. Remove the contact. 3. Bearing worn 3. Replace the pulley Op. 5040A20 AIR CONDITIONING COMPRESSOR - R+R - INCLUDES FLUID LEVEL CHECK AND TOP UP IF NECESSARY 4. Signs of overheating on the compressor magnetic coupling 4. Replace the pulley Op. 5040A20 AIR CONDITIONING COMPRESSOR - R+R - INCLUDES FLUID LEVEL CHECK AND TOP UP IF NECESSARY If the compressor is replaced due to a mechanical problem, remember to clean the entire circuit and change the dehydrating filter. CHECKS TO CARRIED OUT WITH THE COMPRESSOR ON ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION 4 After restoring the correct connection of the service belt, turn the compressor on and off to check: visually if the compressor magnetic coupling plate slips due to oil or grease on the plate; if slippage takes place between the compressor belt and pulley. Move on to Step 5 1. Oil or grease on the plate. 1. Clean the oil or grease off the plate and find the oil leak. 2. Slippage between compressor belt and pulley. 2. Replace the belt CHECK FOR GAS LEAKS ON THE COMPRESSOR SIDE ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION 5 With the engine started and the climate control system at the maximum speed (compressor button ON), place the temperature adjustment knob/button in the maximum cold position, move the probe of the leak detector near the connector to be analyzed and check for any leaks. If there is a leak, repeat the test to make sure that there really is a leak. Withdraw the pipes from the compressor and ensure that the o-rings on the pipes are correctly positioned. Check the condition of the pipe fastening threads on the compressor. With the engine off and the compressor off, bring the leak detector probe up to the compressor pulley near the shaft stem and rear cylinder head gasket to check for leaks. If there is a leak, repeat the test to make sure that there really is a leak. Also check whether the leak is located in other coolant system components. End of diagnosis 1. Compressor pipe o-rings poorly positioned (pinching). 1. Reposition the compressor pipe o-rings correctly. 2. Pipe fastening threads not intact. 2. Replace the compressor Op. 5040A20 AIR CONDITIONING COMPRESSOR - R+R - INCLUDES FLUID LEVEL CHECK AND TOP UP IF NECESSARY 3. Leak located on shaft stem or compressor rear head. 3. Replace the compressor Op. 5040A20 AIR CONDITIONING COMPRESSOR - R+R - INCLUDES FLUID LEVEL CHECK AND TOP UP IF NECESSARY 4. Leak located in other cooling system components. 4. Remove the leak and restore the circuit to correct operation. If the compressor is replaced due to a mechanical problem, remember to clean the entire circuit and change the drier filter.

Whilst driving there is noise coming from the fan. This diagnosis can only be made after See table S015 VEHICLE RUNNING NOISE Carry out the latter first. The climate control is working normally but there is excessive noise coming from the passenger compartment fan. PRELIMINARY CHECKS ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION 0 Having carried out the road test, during the See table S015 VEHICLE RUNNING NOISE there was a noise from the front identified as a noise coming from the passenger compartment fan. Move on to Step 1 FAN CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION 1 Check the climate control fan. In particular, check: that the fan and spiral is clean, if there are any foreign bodies, deposits of dust on the vanes and/or leaves remove them/blow through moving the fan from the engine support; that there are no breaks or cracks in the fan; there are no vibrations or noise at low speed (check the operation with the fan detached from the assembly but the electrical connection fitted). "The operation for determining vibrations should be carried out with great care wearing protective goggles to avoid fragments of the fan being expelled into the surrounding area" Move on to Step 2 1.Fan dirty 1.Clean the fan casing and all the ducts. 2.Presence of breaks or cracks in the fan. 2.Replace the fan. Op. 5040C30 AIR CONDITIONING FAN - R.R. 3. Electric motor noisy, fan not balanced or blades. 3. Replace the fan. Op. 5040C30 AIR CONDITIONING FAN - R.R. AIR DUCT CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION 2 Check for foreign bodies and damaged components inside the air ducts. Move on to Step 3 Presence of foreign bodies or damaged components inside the air ducts. Eliminate the obstructions from the dashboard ducts. AIR VENT CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION 3 Check that the vents are intact and that there are no foreign bodies that could give rise to noise. Move on to Step 4 Vents obstructed. Restore the operation of the vents. POLLEN FILTER CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION 4 Check that the pollen filter is not blocked and that the recirculation air intake is not blocked with foreign bodies or parts (e.g. wiring) that are not correctly fitted. Move on to Step 5 1. Filter obstructed. 1. Replace the filter element Op. 5010B08 CLIMATE CONTROL OUTSIDE AIR PURIFYING (POLLEN) FILTER - R.R. 2. Air intake blocked by foreign bodies. 2. Eliminate the obstructions and restore correct operation. FAN INTAKE CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION 5 Check that the fan intake in the air intake chamber is not blocked by the presence of foreign bodies. End of diagnosis Presence of foreign bodies in the air intake chamber. Eliminate the obstructions and restore correct operation.

Noise whilst driving 1 CHECK ON MATCHING BETWEEN HEAD RESTRAINT RODS AND PLASTIC BUSHES ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check for clearance between the head restraint rods and plastic bushes Move on to Step 2 Clearance between the head restraint rods and plastic bushes. Replace the bushes Op. 7050B08 GUIDE BUSH FOR HEAD RESTRAINT (ONE) FOR REAR SEAT - R.R 2 CHECK ON MATCHING BETWEEN PLASTIC BUSH AND METAL SEAT ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check for clearance between the plastic bush and the metal seat in the backrest frame Move on to Step 3 Clearance between the metal pipe and plastic bush. Replace the plastic bush (or increase the outer diameter using insulating tape). Op. 7050B08 GUIDE BUSH FOR HEAD RESTRAINT (ONE) FOR REAR SEAT - R.R 3 CHECK ON CORRECT OPERATION ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check that the fault is no longer present. End of diagnosis The fault persists. Replace the left backrest Op. 7045A13 FRONT SEAT WITH SIDE BAG (ONE) LEFT OR RIGHT - R.R. Replace the right backrest Op. 7045A15 R R HANDLE FOR FRONT SEAT FORE AND AFT ADJUSTMENT

0 PRELIMINARY CHECKS ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Raise the windscreen wiper arms off the glass, turn on the panel and select one of the functions using the stalk (e.g. intermittence). Check whether the noise persists. Move on to Step 1 The noise is no longer present. Replace the wiper brushes and/or the arms. Op. 5050B28 WINDSCREEN WIPER BLADE/S - R+R Op. 5050B32 WINDSCREEN WIPER ARM/S - R+R 1 CHECK CORRECT FASTENING OF THE WINDSCREEN WIPER ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Turn off the previously selected function using the stalk and turn off the panel, then remove the brush carrier arms and the plate. Check the wiper is correctly fastened to the body. Op. 5050B32 WINDSCREEN WIPER ARM/S - R+R Move on to Step 2 Incorrect wiper fastening. Restore the correct fastening of the wiper. 2 CHECK THE WIPER LINKAGE ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Turn off the instrument panel and check the linkage moves correctly, in particular: check the linkage does not interfere with the body and is not impeded by foreign bodies present in the wiper housing; check the wiper unit has been correctly assembled. End of diagnosis 1. The linkage interferes with the body. 1. Restore the correct operation of the linkage. 2. Foreign bodies present in the wiper housing. 2. Remove the foreign bodies from the wiper. 3. Incorrect wiper fastening. 3. Replace the wiper unit Op. 5050B38 WINDSCREEN WIPER ASSEMBLY - R+R OR REPAIR

With the vehicle moving, particularly over rough ground or during acceleration or braking, noise can be heard from the dashboard area. 0 PRELIMINARY CHECKS ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Road test the vehicle to check the type of noise See Test 70B ROAD TEST FOR NOISE RECOGNITION Move directly to the relevant step. 1. Squeaking noise cannot be located. 1. Move on to Step 1. 2. Noise from one of the front doors. 2. Proceed as instructed in the See table S062 FRONT DOORS CREAKING 1 CHECK DASHBOARD/WINDSCREEN COUPLING ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check the gap between the lower area of the windscreen and the dashboard is correct: the gap must be sufficiently large for a card to be inserted Move on to Step 2 Faulty dashboard fastening. Renew the felt pads behind the facia in the contact area with the windscreen. 2 CHECK OUTLET FASTENINGS ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check the condition of the air outlet fastening tabs on the dashboard. Move on to Step 3 1. Fault in central outlet fastening. 1. Renew the correct fastening Op. 5010C30 CENTRAL AIR VENT IN DASHBOARD - R.R. 2. Fault in side outlet fastening. 2. Renew the correct fastening Op. 5010C14 TOP OUTLET (ONE) ON FASCIA - R+R 3 CHECK GAUGE FASTENINGS ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check the correct fastening of the three gagues behind the steering wheel: in particular, check for the felt pads in the coupling area with the dashboard. Move on to Step 4 1. Faulty fastening of gauges behind the steering wheel. 1. Restore the correct fastening of the gauges. Replace the felt pads if necessary. See assembly Op. 5560B ANALOGUE CONTROL PANEL 2. Faulty fastening of check gauge behind the steering wheel. 2. Restore the correct fastening of the check gauge. Restore the felt pads if necessary. 4 CHECK STEERING COLUMN TRIM FASTENING ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check the steering column trim is correctly fastened to the dashboard. In particular, check for: insulating material around the cables; felt pads in the mating area with the dashboard; free movement of the steering wheel height adjustment device; fastenings of the steering column cover sections. Move on to Step 5 Faulty fastening. Restore the correct fastening on the facia. Restore the felt pads if necessary Op. 7040A26 STEERING COLUMN TRIM - R+R 5 CHECK THE CENTRAL TRIM FASTENINGS ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check the central console trim is correctly fastened to the dashboard. In particular, check for: insulating material around the cables; felt pads in the mating area with the dashboard. Move on to Step 6 Faulty central console fastening. Renew the correct fastening. Restore the felt pads if necessary Op. 7040A60 UNDERDASHBOARD TRIM - R.R. 6 CHECK THE CLIMATE CONTROL MODULE FASTENING ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check the climate control unit is correctly fastened. Move on to Step 7 Faulty climate control unit fastening. Renew the correct fastening of the control unit Op. 5040D18 AIR CONDITIONING CONTROL UNIT - R.R. 7 CHECK THE GLOVE COMPARTMENT ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check the correct fastening of the dashboard glove compartment and its flap. In particular, check for the presence of the rubber pad used to secure the compartment to the dashboard. End of diagnosis 1. Faulty glove compartment fastening. 1. Restore the correct fastening of the glove compartment on the dashboard. Restore the felt pads if necessary Op. 7040A31 DASHBOARD COMPARTMENT ASSEMBLY - R.R. 2. Faulty flap fastening. 2. Restore the correct fastening of the glove compartment flap on the dashboard. Restore the felt pads if necessary Op. 7040A14 FLAP OF GLOVE COMPARTMENT TRIM ELEMENT (ONE) - ARRANGE 3. Flap will not close correctly. 3. Adjust the striker Op. 7040A14 FLAP OF GLOVE COMPARTMENT TRIM ELEMENT (ONE) - ARRANGE

With the vehicle moving, particularly over rough ground or during acceleration or braking, noise can be heard from the one of the front doors. 1 CHECK DASHBOARD/DOOR PANEL COUPLING ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check that the door panel and dashboard are correctly coupled Move on to Step 2 Faulty dashboard fastening. Restore the correct fastening of the dashboard. Restore the felt pads if necessary 2 CHECK DOOR FASTENINGS ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check the fastening: of the door opening limiter; of the hinges (upper and lower); of the lock. Move on to Step 3 1. Faults in limiter fastening. 1. If necessary, lubricate the limiter and restore the correct fastening Op. 7005A28 FRONT SIDE DOOR LIMITER - R.R. 2. Faults in hinge fastening. 2. If necessary, lubricate the hinge pin and restore the correct fastening Op. 7005A24 FRONT SIDE DOOR HINGES (BOLTED) - R.R. WITH DOOR DETACHED 3. Faults in lock fastening. 3. Restore the correct fastening of the lock Op. 7005N21 FRONT SIDE DOOR LOCK MOTOR/LOCK ASSEMBLEY FOR ONE DOOR, LEFT OR RIGHT - R.R. 4. Faults in striker. 4. Check that the striker fastening is correct Op. 7005B14 FRONT SIDE DOOR LOCK STRIKER - R.R 3 CHECK DOOR PANEL ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Remove the door panel and check for foreign bodies inside the door. Op. 7005E10 FRONT SIDE DOOR INTERIOR PANEL - R.R. Move on to Step 4 Foreign bodies present. Remove the foreign bodies. 4 CHECK DOOR INNER FASTENINGS ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check the fastening: of the window mechanism; of the moving window guides; of the moving window fastening element; of the door opening/closure linkage. End of diagnosis 1. Faults in window fastening. 1. Restore the correct fastening of the window Op. 7005M26 ELECTRIC WINDOW MECHANISM FOR ONE FRONT DOOR LH OR RH - R.R 2. Faults in guide fastening 2. Restore the correct fastening of the guides Op. 7005D14 FRONT SIDE DOOR DESCENDING WINDOW GLASS - R.R. WITH DOOR PANEL (AND SUPPORT FRAME) REMOVED 3. Faults in fastening element 3. Replace the fastening element Op. 7005D18 FRONT SIDE DOOR DESCENDING WINDOW GLASS CHANNEL (ONE), LEFT OR RIGHT - R.R 4. Faults in linkage fastening. 4. Restore the linkage fastening clips, see Assembly Op. 7005C FRONT DOOR LOCK CONTROLS

With the vehicle moving, particularly over rough ground or during acceleration or braking, noise can be heard from the one of the rear doors. 1 CHECK DOOR FASTENINGS ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check the fastening: of the door opening limiter; of the hinges (upper and lower); of the lock. Move on to Step 2 1. Faults in limiter fastening 1. If necessary, lubricate the limiter and restore the correct fastening Op. 7010A28 REAR SIDE DOOR OPENING LIMITER - R.R 2. Faults in hinge fastening. 2. If necessary, lubricate the hinge pin and restore the correct fastening Op. 7010A24 REAR SIDE DOOR HINGES (BOLTED) - REPAIR OR REPLACE WITH DOOR REMOVED 3. Faults in lock fastening 3. Restore the correct fastening of the lock Op. 7010N21 REAR SIDE DOOR LOCK MOTOR/LOCK ASSEMBLY, LEFT OR RIGHT - R.R 4. Faults in striker fastening. 4. Check that the striker fastening is correct Op. 7010B14 REAR SIDE DOOR LOCK STRIKER - R.R 2 CHECK DOOR PANEL ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Remove the door panel and check for foreign bodies inside the door Op. 7010E10 REAR SIDE DOOR INNER PANEL - R.R. OR REPLACE Move on to Step 3 Foreign bodies present. Remove the foreign bodies. 3 CHECK DOOR INNER FASTENINGS ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check the fastening: of the window mechanism; of the moving window guides; of the moving window fastening element; of the door opening/closure linkage. End of diagnosis 1. Window fastening faults. 1. Restore the correct fastening of the window Op. 7010M26 ELECTRIC WINDOW OPENING MECHANISM FOR ONE REAR DOOR LH OR RH - R.R 2. Faults in the fastening of the guides and fastening element 2. Restore the correct fastening of the guides Op. 7010D14 REAR SIDE DOOR DESCENDING WINDOW GLASS (ONE), LEFT OR RIGHT - R.E. The diagnostic equipment signals: Error U1711 (CAN (NCM – NCA)). This error is detected if the control module detects a fault in the automatic transmission system. 0 Preliminary checks ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check that there are no other errors in the engine management and automatic transmission systems using the diagnostic equipment Move on to Step 1 There are also other errors present Continue according to the instructions for the diagnostic equipment for the errors present 1 Error deletion ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Turn the ignition key to the OFF position. Wait for at least 10 secs. Delete the errrors and carry out a road test, trying to reproduce the conditions that caused the error. Check that the error does not occur again End of diagnosis Error U1711 is present Replace the automatic transmission control unit and move on to Step 2 Op. 2135B52 ELECTRONIC AUTOMATIC TRANSMISSION ELECTRIC CIRCUIT -ECU MOUNT R R 2 Correct operation check ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check the fault has disappeared End of diagnosis The fault persists Replace the engine management control unit Op. 1060G80 DIESEL ELECTRONIC INJECTION CONTROL UNIT - .R

The diagnostic equipment signals: Error P0101 (flow meter signal), with detail "general electrical fault" This error is detected if there is a short circuit to earth/positive or break in the circuit connected to Pin 42 of the junction unit. 1 Flow meter operation check ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check that the flow meter is working properly by carrying out the test See Test 1060GG MEASURED AIR MASS CHECK End of diagnosis

The diagnostic equipment signals: Error P0101 (flow meter signal), with detail "beyond the upper limit" This error is detected if there is interference with the signal for the sensor at Pin 42 of the electronic control module. 0 Preliminary checks ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check that the engine oil level is correct Op. 0010T11 ENGINE OIL - CHECK LEVEL AND TOP UP, IF NECESSARY Check that the air intake/vacuum circuit is working properly by carrying out the test See Test 1048OA AIR INTAKE/VACUUM CIRCUIT CHECK Check the condition of the fuel supply circuit and make sure that it is working properly carrying out the test See Test 1040OA FUEL SUPPLY CIRCUIT CHECK Check the operation of the low pressure supply circuit by carrying out the test See Test 1060OB CHECK ON SUPPLY LOW PRESSURE FUEL CIRCUIT Move on to Step 1 Oil level incorrect Restore the correct engine oil level Op. 0010T11 ENGINE OIL - CHECK LEVEL AND TOP UP, IF NECESSARY 1 Battery voltge check ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check the battery voltage carrying out the test See Test 5530BB BATTERY VOLTAGE CHECK Move on to Step 2 2 Flow meter operation check ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check that the flow meter is working properly by carrying out the test See Test 1060GG MEASURED AIR MASS CHECK End of diagnosis

The diagnostic equipment signals: Error P010F (air mass/flow meter inconsistency). This error is detected if the engine speed is below 50 rpm and the difference between the supercharging pressure and the barometric pressure sensor is more than 0.15 bar for at least 10 sec. As a result, the control unit carries out the calculations with a replacement value of 1.013 bar, the maximum power is reduced and the supercharging pressure can no longer be controlled. 1 PRESSURE CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check the value of the atmospheric pressure, by carrying out the See Test 1060GD ATMOSPHERIC PRESSURE CHECK Check the value of the supercharging pressure, by carrying out the See Test 1060GF SUPERCHARGING PRESSURE CHECK End of diagnosis

The diagnostic equipment signals: Error P0111 (flow meter air temp. signal). This error is detected if there is interference with the signal for the sensor at Pin 37 of the electronic control module (detail "general electrical fault") or if there is a short circuit to positive (detail "beyond the upper limit") or to earth (detail "below the lower limit") in the circuit connected to Pin 37 of the control unit. In the case of short circuits, the control unit takes 25 °C as the replacement value. 1 FLOW METER OPERATION CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check that the flow meter is working properly by carrying out the See Test 1060GS CHECK ON FLOW METER OPERATION End of diagnosis

The diagnostic equipment signals: Error P0191 (Fuel pressure signal) This error is detected if there is interference with the signal for the sensor at Pin 43 of the electronic control module. 1 FUEL HIGH PRESSURE SENSOR CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check that the fuel high pressure sensor is working properly, following the instructions in the See Test 1060GH DIESEL FUEL PRESSURE CHECK End of diagnosis

The diagnostic equipment signals: Error P0778 (fuel pressure regulator (high pressure pump outlet or pipe). This error is detected if there is a break in the circuit connected to Pins 4 and 34 of the control unit for at least 0.28 secs. (detail "open circuit"), if there is a short circuit to positive in the circuit connected to Pin 34 of the control unit for at least 0.28 secs (detail "short circuit to +Vbatt"), if there is a short circuit to earth in the circuit connected to Pin 34 of the control unit for at least 0.22 secs. (detail "short circuit to earth") or if the temperature of the electronic control module measured is not within the limits for at least 0.28 secs (detail "excessive temperature"). 1 Check on operation of fuel pressure regulator on the rail ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check that the fuel pressure regulator on the rail is working properly by carrying out the test See Test 1060GR CHECK ON OPERATION OF FUEL PRESSURE SENSOR ON RAIL End of diagnosis

The diagnostic equipment signals: Error P2264 (water in diesel filter). This error is detected if there is water detected in the fuel or if there is a short circuit to earth in the circuit connected to Pin 74 of the junction unit. 0 Preliminary checks ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION In the junction unit under the dashboard See B002 JUNCTION UNIT UNDER DASHBOARD check that fuse F35 has not blown (it is the second one from the right in the top row) Move on to Step 1 Fuse F35 has blown Continue as indicated in the test See Test 1064BE SUPERCHARGING VALVE PROTECTIVE FUSE CHECK 1 Check on operation of water presence sensor ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check that the water presence sensor is working properly See Test 1060GQ CHECK ON OPERATION OF WATER IN DIESEL FILTER SENSOR End of diagnosis

The diagnostic equipment signals: Error P2293 (fuel pressure regulator (high pressure pump inlet or pipe). This error is detected if the control unit recognizes a mechanical malfunction of the pressure regulator on the rail by means of the internal evaluation logic.

Check that the pump supply voltage at the pump connector is 12V Measure the pump absorption current by positioning the ammeter clip for the diagnostic equipment on the pump supply cable (at the fuse box or directly on the pump inlet cable) See E5050 DIESEL ENGINES ELECTRONIC MANAGEMENT The current measured should be between 2 and 10 Amperes.

STEP CHECK TO BE PERFORMED RESOLUTION IF THE CHECK IS NOT OK 1 Turn the ignition key OFF. Disconnect the wiring harness connector from engine control unit connector A Connect a shunt cable with fuse between pin 28 of control unit connector A See M010 ENGINE MANAGEMENT CONTROL UNIT and the battery positive See A001 BATTERY and check that the fuel pump does not activate Replace the engine management control unit Op. 1060G80 DIESEL ELECTRONIC INJECTION CONTROL UNIT - .R 2 In the engine compartment junction unit, remove relay T10 from the base (it is the second from left in the bottom row). Measure the voltage between Pin 86 of the base unit and Earth, ensuring it is greater than 11 V. If faults are found, restore the wiring between the engine management control unit and the engine compartment junction unit See E5050 DIESEL ENGINES ELECTRONIC MANAGEMENT otherwise replace the junction unit Op. 5505A13 ADDITIONAL JUNCTION UNIT IN ENGINE COMPARTMENT - R.R. 3 Measure the voltage between Pins 85 and 86 of the base unit, ensuring it is greater than 11 V. If faults are found, restore the wiring between the engine compartment junction unit and earth See E1020 EARTHS otherwise replace the junction unit Op. 5505A13 ADDITIONAL JUNCTION UNIT IN ENGINE COMPARTMENT - R.R. 4 Disconnect the shunt connection cable and turn the ignition ON. Measure the voltage between Pin 30 of the base unit and Earth, ensuring it is greater than 11 V. Move on to Step 8 Move on to Step 5 5 Turn the ignition key OFF. In the engine compartment junction unit remove fuse F21 from the base unit (it is the third from the left in the bottom row). Turn the ignition key ON. Measure the voltage between the fuse input contact and earth, checking it is less than 11 V Replace the junction unit Op. 5505A13 ADDITIONAL JUNCTION UNIT IN ENGINE COMPARTMENT - R.R. 6 Turn the ignition key OFF. Disconnect the cable loom connector from connector A of the engine compartment junction unit Turn the ignition key ON. Measure the voltage between Pin 16 of control unit connector A See B001 ENGINE COMPARTMENT JUNCTION UNIT and Earth, checking it is less than 11 V Replace the junction unit Op. 5505A13 ADDITIONAL JUNCTION UNIT IN ENGINE COMPARTMENT - R.R. 7 Turn the ignition key OFF. Restore the wiring between the under-dashboard junction unit and the engine compartment junction unit See E5050 DIESEL ENGINES ELECTRONIC MANAGEMENT The test can be considered over 8 Connect the shunt connection lead without a fuse between Pins 30 and 87 of the base unit and check that the fuel pump does not come on Replace the fuel pump relay Op. 1060G88 DIESEL INJECTION SYSTEM RELAYS - R R 9 Disconnect the cable loom connector from the fuel pump Measure the voltage between pump Pin 4 See N040 FUEL PUMP AND LEVEL GAUGE and Earth, checking it is greater than 11 V If faults are found, renew the wiring between the engine compartment junction unit and the fuel pump See E5050 DIESEL ENGINES ELECTRONIC MANAGEMENT otherwise replace the junction unit Op. 5505A13 ADDITIONAL JUNCTION UNIT IN ENGINE COMPARTMENT - R.R. 10 Check the wiring between the fuel pump and earth See E5050 DIESEL ENGINES ELECTRONIC MANAGEMENT and renew if necessary Replace the fuel pump Op. 1040A70 SUBMERGED PUMP ASSEMBLY COMPLETE WITH LEVEL GAUGE CONTROL - R + R

Disconnect the connection from the fuel intake assembly. Connect using an Examiner in Ohmmeter mode to the connection for the fuel intake assembly at pins 5 and 6 Read a resistance proportional to the level of the fuel as illustrated in the table below the tolerance of the measured resistance value is approximately 5% Fuel quantity [litres] Resistance value [ohm] 62 >50 54 73 46 107 38 133 31 159 23 186 15 216 8 (riserve) 248 1 300 The following figure shows the fuel pump assembly

The fuel system is highly sensitive. The work must be carried out with the greatest cleanliness and care. Any air in the system could damage the high pressure fuel pump. The vehicle must therefore never be driven with the fuel tank empty. CHECK TO BE PERFORMED RESOLUTION IF THE CHECK IS NOT OK 1 Check that the tank contains the correct type of fuel Remove the contents and wash the tank 2 The fuel reserve must be greater than 5 litres Make sure there is at least 5 litres of fuel 3 Check for leaks in the fuel circuit. Check the hoses and pipes connected to identify any obstructions, damage etc. Check for breaks/scratches on the fuel supply or injection pipes. Check the fuel pipe fittings (quick-fit). Check that the oil pipes are not leaking. Check the condition of the three-way fastening elements. Check the fittings and seals are correctly fitted (use only Fiat Auto approved sealants). Check for blockages, leaks, air or water in the fuel system. Repair or, if necessary, replace the faulty components Op. 1040 FUEL TANK AND PIPES 4 Check the tightening torques for the capscrews: Restore component tightness to the correct values 5 Check the fuel filter Restore the fuel filter to correct working order or replace if necessary Op. 1044B20 FUEL FILTER FILTERING ELEMENT - REPLACE

CHECK TO BE PERFORMED RESOLUTION IF THE CHECK IS NOT OK 1 Check the vacuum supply system components/functions: in particular, check for leaks or blockages. Check the seal of the secondary air inlet/turborcharging system hoses. Also check for any obstructions or porosity. Check for leaks in the intercooler. Check that the pipe restriction bands in the air intake/inlet system are correctly fitted. Check the hoses and pipes connected to identify any obstructions, damage etc. Check that the flow meter is not contaminated. Check the exhaust gas turbocharger and exhaust system components/functions If possible, renew the pipes. Otherwise replace the faulty components Op. 1048A VACUUM AIR CIRCUIT 2 Check that the air filter is not contaminated Replace the filter element Op. 1048A14 AIR CLEANER FILTER ELEMENT - REPLACE. 3 Check that the air filter is correctly fitted Refit correctly Op. 1048A14 AIR CLEANER FILTER ELEMENT - REPLACE. 4 Turn the ignition key OFF. Disconnect the vacuum hose from the vacuum pump Connect a pressure gauge between the vacuum pump and the hose (see following figure). Start the engine, adjust to idle speed and check that the reading on the pressure gauge is between -0.7 and 1.0 bar Replace the vacuum unit Op. 3330D30 VACUUM PUMP - R+R CHECK TO BE PERFORMED RESOLUTION IF THE CHECK IS NOT OK 5 Turn the ignition key OFF. Reconnect the hose to the vacuum pump. Disconnect the vacuum hose from the turbocharge actuator solenoid (see following figure). Connect the pressure gauge between the solenoid and the hose. Start the engine and adjust to idle speed. Select the following control unit at the diagnostic equipment: EDC16C39 Diesel electronic injection control unit. Carry out the following active diagnosis: Turbo regulator, ensuring that it is successful Replace the solenoid valve Op. 1064B42 SOLENOID CONTROLLING TURBOCHARGER VANE POSITION ACTUATOR - R.R  CHECK TO BE PERFORMED RESOLUTION IF THE CHECK IS NOT OK 6 Check that the vacuum read on the pressure gauge during active diagnosis is between -0.5 and 1.0 bar Check the turbo pressure control solenoid is operating correctly See Test 1064BB CHECK ON OPERATION OF SUPERCHARGING PRESSURE SOLENOID VALVE (PIERBURG) 7 Turn the ignition key OFF. Reconnect the vacuum hose to the turbocharger actuator solenoid. Start the engine and adjust to idle speed. Select the following parameters in the parameter screen: EGR valve opening and measured Air Mass. Set conditions where the EGR valve is open and check that the intake air mass is between 20 and 40 kg/h Check the exhaust gas recovery solenoid is operating correctly See Test 1080CB E.G.R. SOLENOID FUNCTIONAL TEST 8 Then return to idle speed. Set conditions where the EGR valve is closed and in these conditions check that the intake air mass is between 40 and 60 kg/h Replace the flow meter Op. 1060G10 AIR FLOW METER - R.R.

Connect the diagnostic equipment pressure transducer to the return pipe to the tank (1a). Press the START/STOP button. Within 30 seconds check that the pressure reading on the gauge is less than 1 bar. The fuel pump in the tank should switch off after 30 seconds. Make sure that the taps and the adjustment screws at the side of the pressure gauge are open (except the ones on ducts not connected to the system).

Connect the diagnostic equipment pressure transducer between the diesel filter (1a) and the pressure pump (1b) (connect it to the filter outlet). Press the START/STOP button. Within 30 seconds, check that the pressure reading on the gauge is between 2 and 3 bar. The fuel pump in the tank should switch off after 30 seconds. Make sure that the taps and the adjustment screws at the side of the pressure gauge are open (except the ones on ducts not connected to the system).

Disconnect the electrical connections from all the injectors. 1. Disconnect the fuel recirculation pipes from all the injectors. Constrict the pipe so that no fuel comes out during the test. Press the START/STOP and check visually that the quantity of recirculated fuel leaving the injector connections are approximately the same and small in amount

Disconnect the electrical connections from all the injectors. 1. Disconnect the fuel recirculation pipes from all the injectors. Constrict the pipe so that no fuel comes out during the test. Connect the tester. Display the "measured diesel pressure" and "engine rpm" parameters on the "Control Unit Test" parameters screen. Press the START/STOP button and check that the fuel pressure is greater than 300 bar with engine rpm higher than 200 rpm.

Install fitting 1.870.752.000 between the turbocharging sensor and the intake chamber. Connect the pressure transducer to the tool. Position the diagnostic equipment in the passenger compartment and make the connections. Select "pressure gauge" on the diagnostic equipment and prepare for the acquisition of data in "intake pressure" mode with a 2000 mmHg full scale deflection and select a time of 10 seconds. Road test the vehicle (observing the speed limits in force) and perform the following test: - On a motorway route, allow the vehicle to reach 2500 rpm in 4th gear. - Initiate graphic acquistion by pressing start on the diagnostic equipment and 2 seconds later fully depress the accelerator pedal until the engine speed is 3500 rpm. - Once this speed is reached completely release the accelerator pedal. - Display the resulting graph and in the pressure constant section, with the exception of the initial peak, the reading should be 1900 -2080 mbar (1444 -1581 mmHg) corresponding to a supercharging value of 900 -1080 mbar. - On a motorway route with fast-moving traffic, let the vehicle reach 2500 rpm in 3rd gear. - Initiate graphic acquistion by pressing start on the diagnostic equipment and 2 seconds later fully depress the accelerator pedal until the engine speed is 3500 rpm. - Once this speed is reached completely release the accelerator pedal. - Display the resulting graph and in the pressure constant section, with the exception of the initial peak, the reading should be 1900 -2080 mbar (1444 -1581 mmHg) corresponding to a supercharging value of 900 -1080 mbar.

Visually inspect that during start-up, the turbocharger actuator connecting rod (turbine stator vanes adjustment device) moves by around 10 mm in the direction of the actuator. The graphic acquisition of the pressure trend can be carried out by selecting either the 2000 or 4000 mmHg scale.

- Carry out a road test on traffic free roads in safe conditions following the highway code. - Before proceeding with the test, check the inflation pressure of the two vehicles, restoring the values to the correct ones if they are found to be incorrect. - Also check the conditions of the wheel rims making sure they are not distorted or broken, replacing them if any faults are found. - Carry out the test on an uneven road surface, at a speed of 40 km/h to check the capacity of the suspension to absorb the stresses produced by small imperfections (suspension damping) with the consesquent acoustic repercussions inside the passenger compartment. - Check the capacity of the suspension to absorb the stresses produced by large imperfections and the consequent acoustic repercussions inside the passenger compartment, carry out the road test at a speed of 40 km/h over a route that has a series of pot-holes. - Check the rapid damping of any pitching produced by the irregularities in the road surface, carrying out the test at a speed of 50 km/h on a straight road with suitably spaced humps and holes. - This type of test should always be used for comparison with a new vehicle or reference vehicle of the same trim level and engine type, available in the workshop at the time of the test in question. - At the end of the test in question, assess/rate the driving comfort of the vehicle in accordance with the enclosed table. Judgement Vote Poor 3 Mediocre 4 Just acceptable 5,5 Acceptable 6 Good 7 The reference vehicle has a driving comfort default rating of 7.

- Carry out a road test on traffic free roads in safe conditions following the highway code. - Before proceeding with the test, check the inflation pressure of the two vehicles, restoring the values to the correct ones if they are found to be incorrect. - Also check the conditions of the wheel rims making sure they are not distorted or broken, replacing them if any faults are found. - Carry out the test on a route where there are left and right hand bends of different degrees, evaluating the laying down speed of the vehicle round the bends, trying to take the bends at a constant speed, avoiding carrying out pull/release manoeuvres. - Evaluate the stability of the vehicle by simulating a lane change/overtaking and check that violent vehicle reactions do not appear leading to unsafe driving during this manoeuvre. - Then carry out a road test on an unmade road (cobblestones) where there are right/left hand bends of different degrees to evaluate the tendency of the rear of the vehicle to lose grip. - This type of test should always be used for comparison with a new vehicle or reference vehicle of the same trim level and engine type, available in the workshop at the time of the test in question. - At the end of the test in question, assess/rate the behaviour of the vehicle in terms of rolling/pitching in accordance with the enclosed table. Judgement Vote Poor 3 Mediocre 4 Just acceptable 5,5 Acceptable 6 Good 7 The reference vehicle has a rolling/pitching default rating of 7.

Disconnect the electrical connection for the linear sensor. See K120 LINEAR SENSOR FOR FANS Check that Pin 1 is earthed and Pin 2 is at +5V. Connect a linear potentiometer (end of scale 1 KOhm, previously positioned at around 500 ohm between the centre pin andone of the side ones) to the pins of the linear sensor electrical connector. Turn the ignition key to the ON position. Using a multimeter, check that the voltage between pins 1 and 3 is around 2.5V. Switch on the engine and switch on the air conditioning using the special switch located on the climate control system control unit. The climate control system should come on normally in these circumstances. Vary the resistance of the potentiometer, until the voltage reading on the multimeter between pins 1 and 3 is around 0V. In these conditions the air conditioning system should switch off because the engine management node receives low pressure information for the circuit. Alter the potentiometer resistance until the voltage reading on the multimeter between pins 1 and 3 is about 4.6 V. The air conditioning system should switch off in these conditions because the engine management node receives high circuit pressure information.

Disconnect the electrical connector for the passenger compartment air fan maximum speed relay See J041 PASSENGER COMPARTMENT AIR FAN MAXIMUM SPEED RELAY Connect a multimeter in ohmmeter mode between the following pins and measure: Between pins 1 and 4 a resistance of between 272 and 408 mOhm. Between pins 1 and 2 a resistance of between 0.688 and 1.032 Ohm. Between pins 1 and 3 a resistance of between 2 and 3 Ohm.

Disconnect the electrical connector for the climate control system control unit See M70 CLIMATE CONTROL SYSTEM CONTROL UNIT With the ignition ON, turn the temperature knob to the cold position (completely to the left). After about 10 secs. turn the knob to the hot position (completely to the right) checking that the voltage between pins 4 and 5 is between 9.6 and 14.4 V whilst the motor is turning. Repeat the manoeuvre in the opposite direction. Also check that the voltage between pins 29 and 8 is between 4.75 and 5.25 V.

Using a multimeter, check with the ignition key in the ON position between pins 1 and 4 and between pins 3 and 4 of the solar sensor See K90 SOLAR SENSOR that the voltage is proportional to the thermal energy present on the windscreen analyzed by the sensor photodiodes: there should be a signal of less than 5 Volt (between 4.5 V - minimum solar rays - and 0.5 V - maximum solar rays). If there is a problem, using a multimeter and disconnecting the sensor, check the sensor power supply connector, with the ignition key in the ON position between pins 1 and 4 and between pins 3 and 4 See K90 SOLAR SENSOR that there is a voltage of 5 Volt.

Using the Examiner in the voltmeter function, select an end of scale of 20 Volt and basic time of 200 milliseconds. Connect the Examiner black probe to the vehicle earth and the red probe to pin 3 of the air quality sensor output signal. See K064 EXHAUST GAS PRESENCE SENSOR Turn the key to the ON position. Wait about 36 secs for the sensor to warm up. Spray the gas in the canister (part no. 71715571) in less than 60 seconds. Press the START button. The signal shown should be a set of PWM impulses with a frequency of 100 Hz and a Duty Cycle that varies between 15 and 70% as indicated in the table below. PWM% Duty Cycle = T1 / T2 where: T1= duration of impulse T2 = 1/f = 1/100 Hz = Duratation of transmission Pin out: 1. +CH/15 2. earth 3. output signal PWM signal meaning 5% short circuit to earth of signal line 15% non polluted air circulation 30% level 1 pollution 50% level 2 pollution 70% level 3 pollution >90% short circuit +12 signal line

This type of actuator works by reversing the power supply polarity of the motor therefore if it is supplied in one way it turns in one direction and to make it rotate in the other direction the polarity must be reversed. Disconnect the electrical connector for the recirculation actuator See N82 OUTSIDE / RECIRCULATION AIR INTAKE FLAP ACTUATOR and supply it directly with a 12 V battery, connecting the positive battery pole to pin 5 and the negative one to pin 6. Check that with the power supply like that the actuator turns. If this does not happen, reverse the polarity at pins 5 and 6 and check that the actuator turns in one direction. Place the actuator in the end of travel position, then reverse the polarity and place it in the opposite end of travel position. Repeat this test at least twice, checking that the actuator completes the travel in both directions without problems. If there are problems with the travel, check that they are not due to the presence of mechanical impediments or interference. In this case, eliminate them and repeat the test.

There is an open circuit between pins 4 and 2. There is an open circuit between pins 4 and 1. Place the fan speed knob at 1 and check that: There is electrical continuity between pins 4 and 3. This type of actuator works by reversing the power supply polarity of the motor therefore if it is supplied in one way it turns in one direction and to make it rotate in the other direction the polarity must be reversed. Disconnect the electrical connector for the mixture actuator See N080 AIR DISTRIBUTION FLAP ACTUATOR or distribution actuator See N081 MIXED AIR FLAP ACTUATOR (MOTOR) and supply it directly with a 12 V battery, connecting the positive battery pole to pin 5 and the negative one to pin 6. Check that with the power supply like that the actuator turns. If this does not happen, reverse the polarity at pins 5 and 6 and check that the actuator turns in one direction. Place the actuator in the end of travel position, then reverse the polarity and place it in the opposite end of travel position. Repeat this test at least twice, checking that the actuator completes the travel in both directions without problems. If there are problems with the travel, check that they are not due to the presence of mechanical impediments or interference. In this case, eliminate them and repeat the test. Connect the diagnostic equipment in ohmmeter mode between pins 1 and 3 of the actuator and check that the resistance is between 3.76 and 5.64 Ohm. Connect the diagnostic equipment ohmmeter mode between pins 1 and 2 of the actuator and check that the resistance measured varies continuously during the actuator travel.

Turn the wheel on the CRUISE CONTROL stalk towards SET + and release it immediately to store the speed reached. Remove your foot from the accelerator and check the vehicle maintains the set speed. Turn the wheel on the CRUISE CONTROL stalk toward the SET+ position and maintain the position to increase the speed to 70 or 90 km/h (according to maximum speed limit on the road). do not operate the accelerator. The key remote control is supplied by a CR2032 lithium battery (3 V, 220 mAh), remote control operation is ensured between 2.6 and 3.6 V with a maximum current of 15 mA. At least 9000 activations of 1 s duration and 3000 activations of 5 s duration are guaranteed over a period of two years. The battery voltage is monitored to check the charge level: the threshold is set at 2.6±0.06 V. If the remote control receiver detects that the battery is flat, it is still possible to carry out a total of 100 operations. Operating frequency: 433.92 MHz. Check that the voltage exceeds 2.2 Volts. Replace the battery Note that after replacing the battery, the remote control variable code must be re-synchronised: this operation is carried out by pressing the remote control key twice. Note that if the remote control has been activated more than 255 times, variable code synchrony between the sending unit and the receiver will be lost (the receiver will no longer be able to identify a variable code message correctly). Synchrony should therefore be restored by pressing the remote control unit key twice.

Check the operation of the satellite navigation system Check that the map disc is consistent with the vehicle model. In NAV mode, check that the number of satellites in the last line on the right is at least 3 indicating that the satellite reception is correct. If the reading for the number of satellites is less than 3 then the reception is not good enough to locate the vehicle. It is probably a question of insufficient cover. In this case try and move the vehicle to an area where there is good reception or compare the reception with other cars located in the same place. The satellite reception test should be carried out in an open area. In this case, without a comparison it is impossible to say whether or not the navigator is defective. If, on the other hand, the comparison reveals even worse reception, check the connection of the satellite aerial, the electrical continuity, the correct power supply and, if necessary, test with different equipment that is definitely working properly. For the road test: Exit to NAV mode Check that the arrow moves consistently with the vehicle speed, otherwise check the presence of the milometer signal. Check that the arrow changes direction in line with the vehicle. If the arrow does not change direction this means that the gyroscope inside the map reader is broken and the Connect should be replaced. Enter a destination and activate the calculation of the route. Wait for the first instruction and the route on the display and check that it is correct. Irregular instructions: before or after junctions, arrow out of position, they may be due to CD maps that are not up to date: a missing instruction stems from the fact that a road is not on the map because it has not been processed in digital form or the road network has been changed compared with the one on the map. The navigator calculates the position of the vehicle both by means of the satellite signal and using the wheel rpm and the internal gyroscope bush signal. Problems of accuracy may arise when: The odometer speed signal and reversing signal are not received correctly Occasions when the navigation system should be initialised: The vehicle is being transported with the battery disconnected and travelling in a tunnel (the navigator loses the references). Immediately after having changed the tyres (since the wheel rpm/distance conversion factor is not accurate). When replacing the Nit. To initialize the navigator it is necessary to drive about 100 km in optimum satellite reception conditions. If all the tests have not highlighted defects then the problem lies in the Connect which should be replaced.

STEP CHECK TO BE PERFORMED RESOLUTION IF THE CHECK IS NOT OK 1 Check power supply (+15) With the ignition ON, check that the correct battery voltage is present between pins 4 and 8 of the 8-way Connect connector and earth. Check that the connector is correctly inserted in the other part. Try to move it from its seat by making small movements in all directions, grasping the connector body in your fingers and the wiring in your hand. The connector must stay in place Exercise a moderate pulling force. The connector must stay in place check whether the power supply goes off, goes on and/or vice versa (touching/not touching) subject the cable to a pulling force and check cable stability (no shrinkage): exercise repeated pull-push-pull cycles on the lead and ensure its immobility. Apply a solution of soapy water to the entire perimeter of the glass. From inside the passenger compartment, blow through with compressed air along the entire perimeter, moving the trims to the side and the top, if necessary. Visually inspect for any bubbles of air on the outer surface: this makes it possible to locate any areas where the sealant is not sufficient or damaged. If there is a lack of sealant on the vertical pillars, the pillar trim can be moved and rubber type sealant can be injected from the inside. If there is a lack of sealant on the top section, the roof lining can be moved and rubber type sealant can be injected from the inside. If there is a lack of sealant on the bottom section, the trim at the base of the (front) windscreen or the rear parcel shelf (for the rearscreen) can be moved and rubber type sealant can be injected from the inside. If there is insufficient sealant in widespread areas, the overall seal of the window cannot be guaranteed and therefore it has to be removed and the windscreen or the rearscreen must be completely resealed. Op. 7035A18 WINDSCREEN GLASS - R.R INCLUDING CLEANING HOUSING

ATTENTION All the operations should be carried out taking great care to avoid personal injury.The engine compartment contains many moving parts, components at high temperatures and live wires. Follow the warnings given below very carefully when working in the engine compartment: turn off the engine and wait for it to cool down, do not smoke, do not use naked flames and ensure a fire extinguisher is available.The use of special tools is required for certain procedures. The use of these tools is vital for working in safety.Follow the current workshop safety regulations. Where necessary, the Manual contains specific procedures to be followed to prevent dangerous situations from arising.For the use of chemical products, follow the safety instructions on the card from the supplier to the consumer.The electronic ignition system produces voltages of 20,000 V and above which could be very hazardous to people especially if they are suffering from a heart condition. Therefore take great care when working on these systems or in the vicinity of their components. For the 1.8 version only: The injection-ignition system control unit is a component that is sensitive to electrostatic interference. Do not touch the injection-ignition system control unit once the engine is started unless the static electricity has been discharged first by touching the bodyshell. WARNINGS This vehicle is equipped with a starting system known as Smart-Key where there is no longer a traditional ignition key having been replaced with an electronic key "T.E.G." (Transmitter for Entry and go) combined with an electronic key reader and TEG-Reader radio frequency receiver. Access to the vehicle through radiofrequency recognition of the remote control incorporated in the TEG takes place in entirely the same as with the traditional remote control incorporated in the key fob.The vehicle is turned on/started up by inserting the key and turning it in the TEG Reader on the central tunnel.The distribution of the power supply to the vehicle (ignition-controlled INT, INT/A, AVV, etc.) is managed by the steering lock node and takes place in entirely the same way as for models equipped with a conventional key.Before working on the electrical system (connectors, electrical components, wiring etc.), always DISCONNECT THE BATTERY. When the battery is disconnected, the Steering Lock Node remains in the same condition (released or locked) as previously. Whenever it is necessary to turn the steering wheel with the battery disconnected during workshop operations, leave the TEG inserted when disconnecting the battery: the steering will thereby remain unlocked and free to turn. Whenever the battery terminals are reconnected, proceed as follows: - initialise front and rear windows; - initialise the sun roof; - initialise the sun roof blind; - reset the time and date on the instrument panel; - enter the safety code on the radio (if present); - enter the safety code on the navigation system (if present); All the operations should be carried out taking great care to avoid damage to components.To release parts that are sticking, tap gently using an aluminium or lead mallet if iron materials are involved; use a wooden or resin mallet for light alloy parts.When dismantling, check that components that should be marked have the appropriate references.When refitting, lubricate the parts, where necessary, to prevent seizing during the initial operating period. When refitting it is vital to respect the adjustment nut tightening torques.Each time they are refitted, replace gaskets, oil seals, flexible washers, safetly plates, self-locking nuts, pre-treated screws and all parts that have deteriorated.Use adhesive paper or clean cloths to suitably protect those parts of the engine which, if they remain uncovered after dismantling, will allow dust or foreign bodies to enter.Only genuine spare parts should be used to replace units or components that have been removed. this is the only way of ensuring the interchangeability and perfect operation of the various components.

The engine oil level check should be carried out with the vehicle on a flat surface with the engine off a few minutes (5) after the engine has been switched off. 1. Extract the engine oil dipstick, clean it and then fully reinset it, extract it and check that the level is between the MIN and MAX marks on the actual dipstick. 2. If the oil level is close to or actually below the MIN mark, introduce the recommended oil through the filler until it reaches the MAX mark. If, after checking, the engine oil level is above the MAX mark, it must be corrected. After topping up the engine oil, before checking the level, let the engine run for a few seconds and wait for a few minutes after it has been switched off. Only use the recommended coolant checking that the concentration is 50% water and 50% anti-freeze. The anti-freeze not only has the function of protecting the entire cooling system from freezing but it also protects the parts that are in contact with the coolant from corrosion and limescale. Therefore the benefits of anti-freeze should not be underestimated even in tropical climates. In addition to the mixture ratio, the quality of the water also plays an important role. Drinking water normally satisifes these requirements; the quality of regenerated sea water is not good enough. Anti-freeze that is not approved can cause damage to the engine. The air in the hydraulic circuit acts as a pad absorbing a large amount of the pressure exerted by the brake pump and reducing the efficiency of the braking. The air present is felt at the brake pedal making it seem "spongy" and reducing the braking capacity. - Position the vehicle on a lift. - Check that the brake/clutch fluid is between the MIN and MAX levels. The electro-hydraulic power assisted steering hydraulic system bleeds automatically during operation whilst the engine is running. The flow of hydraulic fluid in the system causes the level in the reservoir to go down. After the following procedure has been carried out a small amount of air may remain in the system. This does not have any negative repercussions as the system continues to be bled whilst driving. - Start the engine 3 times and stop each time after 5 seconds with a brief pause between each starting. - Start up the engine, turn the steering wheel from lock to lock 5 times, then switch off the engine. - If necessary, top up the hydraulic system with the recommended fluid. Op. 0010T71 POWER STEERING FLUID CHECK LEVEL AND TOP UP IF NECESSARY

If the instrument panel signals the presence of water in the fuel filter, bleed the system as soon as possible. - Carry out a key on without starting the engine. This operation is designed to pressurize the fuel filter. - Lift up the fuel filter from its housing to gain access to the bleed cap. - Place a suitable container underneath the fuel filter. - Undo the bleed plug. This action should be carried out gradually taking care to check that the amount of fluid expelled is between 75cc and 85cc. - Then close the bleed plug without using excessive force. - Examine the fluid expelled: if there is water and there are no obvious traces of diesel fuel, repeat the bleeding. - If there are traces of diesel fuel, repeating the bleeding will confirm that there is no longer any water in the fuel filter. - Turn the ignition key to the OFF position. - Dry the fuel filter, place it in its housing and check, after having run the engine for about a minute, that there are no leaks in the lower part. If the presence of water in the fuel filer is revealed on the vehicle display, bleed as soon as possible. - Position the vehicle on a lift. - Turn key on without starting the engine. This operation pressurises the fuel filter. Op. 7055B54 UNDER ENGINE PROTECTION/GUARD - R.R. - Disconnect the electrical connection from the water presence sensor on the fuel filter. Fit a pipe of appropriate length to the pipe section on the wate presence sensor on the fuel filter to allow fluid to be drained into a suitable container after bleeding. - Loosen the water presence sensor on the fuel filter. Carry out this action gradually, taking care to check that the amount of fuel expelled is between 75 and 80 cc - Tighten the water sensor on the fuel filter. - Examine the expelled fluid: if it contains water without evident traces of diesel, repeat the bleeding operation. - If traces of diesel appear, repeating the bleeding operation ensures that the fuel filter does not contain any more water. - Turn the ignition key to the OFF position. - Connect the electrical connection to the water presence sensor on the fuel filter. - Check that no more leaks are present in the lower part of the fuel filter after running the engine for one minute. Op. 7055B54 UNDER ENGINE PROTECTION/GUARD - R.R. - Remove the vehicle from the lift.

ATTENTION All the operations should be carried out taking great care to avoid personal injury.The engine compartment contains many moving parts, components at high temperatures and live wires. Follow the warnings given below very carefully when working in the engine compartment: turn off the engine and wait for it to cool down, do not smoke, do not use naked flames and ensure a fire extinguisher is available.The use of special tools is required for certain procedures. The use of these tools is vital for working in safety.Follow the current workshop safety regulations. Where necessary, the Manual contains specific procedures to be followed to prevent dangerous situations from arising.For the use of chemical products, follow the safety instructions on the card from the supplier to the consumer.The electronic ignition system produces voltages of 20,000 V and above which could be very hazardous to people especially if they are suffering from a heart condition. Therefore take great care when working on these systems or in the vicinity of their components. For the 1.8 version only: The injection-ignition system control unit is a component that is sensitive to electrostatic interference. Do not touch the injection-ignition system control unit once the engine is started unless the static electricity has been discharged first by touching the bodyshell. WARNINGS This vehicle is equipped with a starting system known as Smart-Key where there is no longer a traditional ignition key having been replaced with an electronic key "T.E.G." (Transmitter for Entry and go) combined with an electronic key reader and TEG-Reader radio frequency receiver. Access to the vehicle through radiofrequency recognition of the remote control incorporated in the TEG takes place in entirely the same as with the traditional remote control incorporated in the key fob.The vehicle is turned on/started up by inserting the key and turning it in the TEG Reader on the central tunnel.The distribution of the power supply to the vehicle (ignition-controlled INT, INT/A, AVV, etc.) is managed by the steering lock node and takes place in entirely the same way as for models equipped with a conventional key.Before working on the electrical system (connectors, electrical components, wiring etc.), always DISCONNECT THE BATTERY. When the battery is disconnected, the Steering Lock Node remains in the same condition (released or locked) as previously. Whenever it is necessary to turn the steering wheel with the battery disconnected during workshop operations, leave the TEG inserted when disconnecting the battery: the steering will thereby remain unlocked and free to turn. Whenever the battery terminals are reconnected, proceed as follows: - initialise front and rear windows; - initialise the sun roof; - initialise the sun roof blind; - reset the time and date on the instrument panel; - enter the safety code on the radio (if present); - enter the safety code on the navigation system (if present); All the operations should be carried out taking great care to avoid damage to components.To release parts that are sticking, tap gently using an aluminium or lead mallet if iron materials are involved; use a wooden or resin mallet for light alloy parts.When dismantling, check that components that should be marked have the appropriate references.When refitting, lubricate the parts, where necessary, to prevent seizing during the initial operating period. When refitting it is vital to respect the adjustment nut tightening torques.Each time they are refitted, replace gaskets, oil seals, flexible washers, safetly plates, self-locking nuts, pre-treated screws and all parts that have deteriorated.Use adhesive paper or clean cloths to suitably protect those parts of the engine which, if they remain uncovered after dismantling, will allow dust or foreign bodies to enter.Only genuine spare parts should be used to replace units or components that have been removed. this is the only way of ensuring the interchangeability and perfect operation of the various components.
