The front courtesy light includes three lamps with three control switches: - the corresponding spot light can be switched on using external switches; - the centre switch can be used to switch the centre light on or off and the switching on is also subject to a delay timer as described below. The centre rear courtesy light has two bulbs that can be switched on or off by operating the switch or, with a timed delay, as described later on. The front courtesy lighting is managed by the Body Computer, that for the rear lights is managed by the door control units. The timed delay is managed by the Body Computer via the CAN according to the following strategy: - when any of the front or rear doors is opened, a delay timer is activated for the courtesy lights for a time of 3 minutes and is reactivated each time one of the doors is opened; - when all the doors are shut: in key off conditions, the 3 minute delay timer is zeroed and a 10 second one is activated; in the key on condition the courtesy lights are switched off immediately; - when the key is extracted from the ignition, the courtesy lights come on for a timed period of 10 seconds; - when the doors are unlocked (by the remote control, pawl in the driver's and passenger door or by the FIS) the courtesy lights come on for a timed period of 10 seconds, interrupted if the ignition key is turned ON; - during the locking of the doors (by the remote control or the pawl in the driver's or passenger door), all the courtesy lights go out; - when the inertia switch (FIS) is operated, the courtesy lights come on for a period of 15 minutes; if the FIS is reset, the courtesy lights go out. The switching on and off of the courtesy lights should take place simultaneously if more than one of them is involved and the process should be gradual (dimmer) with the cycle lasting 2 seconds. The dimmer time of 2 seconds is always added to the times described previously, for both switching on and switching off. The gradual switching on/off should not be interrupted under any circumstances (not even after another door is opened, a key on, etc.). The activation of the front and rear courtesy lights is also managed by the unstable button on the front courtesy light, in particular: - with the courtesy lights off, both are switched on; - with the courtesy lights on, both are switched off (even with the FIS activated). In the case of the timed activation of the courtesy lights when the door is opened, pressing the button on the front courtesy light causes the interior lights to be switched off and the resetting of the timed delay in progress. With the key in the OFF position or extracted, when all the doors are closed a timed delay of 10 seconds is activated. The timed delay for the courtesy lights with activation by the button on the front courtesy light is 15 minutes with the key in the OFF position or extracted. There is no timed delay with the ignition ON. The front and rear spot lights are activated by a local control and have a timed delay of 15 minutes if they are activated with the ignition OFF, whilst there is no timed delay if they are activated with the ignition ON. The activation/deactivation using the local control does not involve a dimmer. The direct control of the rear spot lights takes precedence over a switching on/off command received on the opening of the door or from the button in the front courtesy light. If the spot lights are switched on indirectly, pressing the local button causes the lamp to be switched off until the next direct or indirect switching on command is received. The power supply for all the courtesy lights follows the battery voltage control logic (SBMT): the Body Computer continuously acquires the battery voltage signal and compares it with its own limit value. With the ignition OFF or the key extracted (STOP), a 15 minute timer starts when any of the doors is opened. The lights are deactivated after this time limit.

The Body Computer M001 receives "door open" input signals at pin 8 of connector D (driver's front door), pin 25 of connector E (passenger front door), pin 16 of connector D (left rear door) and pin 26 of connector E (right rear door). The inertia switch I050 (NA contact) is connected to pin 17 of connector D of M001. Both the front courtesy light G010 and the centre rear courtesy light G020 receive a direct power supply from the battery via the line protected by fuse F39 of the junction unit under the dashboard B002. The front courtesy light G10 is controlled by the Body Computer M001 : the analogue control signal from the three buttons in the actual courtesy light reaches pin 28 of connector E; on the basis of this signal, the Body Computer M001 provides the timed earth signals from pins 21, 30, 37 of connector E respectively for the management of the centre lamp and the left and right spot lights. The centre rear courtesy light G020 comprises two lamps that are controlled by the driver's door M066 and passenger door M067 control units: the control signals from the buttons in the actual courtesy light arrive at pin 12 of connector B, whilst the negative timer and dimmer signals are sent from pin 14 of connector B to the respective lights. The Body Computer M001 - pins 24 and 25 of connector H - is connected, via the CAN line, to the ignition device H003 - pins 1 and 2 - for the timed management of the lights by the remote control (door locking/unlocking) or during the extraction of the key (key off).

When the boot is opened, the two luggage compartment lights come on and go off when the boot is closed. The light in the glove compartment is turned on when the glove compartment is opened and turned off when the compartment is closed. The lights located beneath each of the sun blinds are turned on by a switch on the lights. The power supplies to the boot, glove compartment and sun blind lights follow a batttery voltage control logic (known as SBMT). the Body Computer continuously acquires the battery voltage signal and compares it with its own limit value. With the ignition OFF or key out (STOP), a 15 minute timer starts when any of the doors or the boot is opened. The lights are deactivated after this time limit.

Boot opening switch I011 sends an earth signal with the boot open to pin 36 of connector E of Body Computer M001 and directly to boot courtesy light G040 A (right) and G040 B (left) -. The contact in question indicates boot open status. The switch is equipped with another contact that indicates "boot not completely closed" status, used by the boot lock and alarm functions. See E3045 BOOT AND FUEL FLAP OPENING See E7015 ALARM Boot courtesy lights G040 A and G040 B are supplied from Body Computer M001 from pin 23 of connector E on the basis of the SBMT logic described previously.. Pin 33 of connector E of Body Computer M001 supplies the driver side sun visor light G031 and passenger side sun visor light G032; from pin 16 of connector H, it supplies glove compartment light G030 in similar fashion.

There are two lights for lighting up the ground ("puddle lights") in the front front doors. The two door control units detect the status of the doors, notify the Body Computer and directly control the switching on of the bulb in the door. The function is activated both with the key in the OFF position or extracted and with it in the ON position. The opening of one of the front doors causes the relevant light to come on for a maximum of 3 minutes; when this time has expired the light can only be switched back on again after the door has been reopened. Closing both doors causes the lights to go out immediately.

The Body Computer M001 receives door open input signals at pin 8 of connector D (driver's front door) and 25 of connector E (passenger side door). The puddle lights G051 and G052 are operated by the driver's door control unit M066 and the passenger door control unit M067 connected by the CAN to the Body Computer M001. The control units M066 and M067 receive a direct supply from the battery pin 11 of connector D via the line protected by fuse F32 of the junction unit under the dashboard B002. Pin 7 of connector D of M066 and M067 is earthed. On the basis of the control logic described previously, each control unit supplies the puddle light G051 and G052 with a timed delay from pins 17 and 18 of connector B.

The car is equipped with numerous light sources for optimal lighting of interior instruments and controls. Some of these are light under Key-on conditions (INT), others with the side lights on. Others are dimmable in accordance with a rheostat-controlled adjustment strategy managed by the Body Computer. When the ignition key is turned ON (INT), the following controls are lit: - Hazard warning lights control - Controls on tunnel - Left control panel - Manual air conditioner controls. With the ignition ON (INT) enablement and side light command signals, the Body Computer manages the lighting of: - cigar lighter and rear current socket; - radio wiring; - phone wiring. A "+ light" signal is also sent to the electrochrome interior mirror. See E3032 DOOR MIRROR ADJUSTMENT The Body Computer manages (directly or via the driver and passenger side door control units and the boot compartment control unit), the dimmed lighting of: - the instrument panel and display; - the radio or Connect Nav+ display; - the automatic climate control system display; - the radio controls on the steering wheel (where present); - the control unit on the driver's door - the window switches on the remaining doors. The light intensity can be adjusted to different levels by means of two external keys located in the left control panel. Up to 8 different levels are possible. The brightness level set by pressing the “MODE +” and “MODE -” keys is shown on the instrument panel display. This value is sent via the CAN network so that the information is made available to other nodes. Once set, this value is stored and used again. The light intensity cannot be reduced to zero and the instrument panel indicator/fault warning lights cannot be adjusted or dimmed. The lighting brightness level supplied via the CAN network to the rado or Connect Nav+ and to the automatic climate control system can be used to increase or dim the display backlighting: it can be adjusted from maximum brightness (daytime) to a dimmed setting with the side lights on (night-time) according to the customer's needs.

Supply line INT (key ON) protected by fuse F49 of the under-dashboard control unit B002, sends lighting to tunnel control unit H036, hazard light control H020, left control panel H091 and manual air conditioner M070 - pin 28 -. The front door control lighting H044 and H050 is managed by driver side door control unit M066 and passenger side unit M067, supplied - at pin 11 of connector D - from a line protected by fuseF32 of B002 and connected - pin 15 and 16 of connector B - via the CAN network to Body Computer M001. Similarly, the lightng of the window controls on the left rear door H053 and right rear door H054 is managed by the boot control unit M063, supplied - at pin B8 of connector A - by a line protected by fuse F36 of B002 and connected - pins A7 and B7 of connector B - via the CAN network to Body Computer M001. Body Computer M001 receives the side lights on signal at pin 28 of connector G. See E2010 SIDE LIGHTS / NO. PLATE LIGHTS The side lights on power supply is supplied to Body Computer M001 respectively: - from pin 18 of connector H. to the radio wiring, to phone wiring D099 and to front cigar lighter/power point P050; - from pin 40 of connector E. to electrochromic interior mirror P065 and rear power point P052. The “MODE”, “MODE +” and “MODE -” controls from left control panel H091 send analogue signals to instrument panel E050, pin 16 of connector B and pin 9 of connector A. Instrument panel E050 is supplied by an ignition-operated supply (INT from the steering lock control unit) - pin 1 of connector A - from a line protected by fuse F37 of under-dashboard junction unit B002 and directly from the battery - pin 2 of connector A - via a line from fuse F53 of B002. Pin 7 of connector A is earthed. Via the CAN line, Body Computer M001 is connected to instrument panel E050, from which it receives a brightness adjustment signal that is sent to the radio or Connect Nav+ node P020, automatic climate control unit M070 and steering wheel node M093. See E1050 CAN CONNECTION LINES

The car is equipped with numerous light sources for optimal lighting of interior instruments and controls. Some of these are lit with the ignition device in the ON position (INT from the steering lock control unit), others with the side lights on, others are dimmable in accordance with a rheostat-controlled adjustment strategy managed by the Body Computer. When the key is turned in the ignition device to the ON positin (INT) the following controls are lit up: - hazard warning lights control; - controls on tunnel; - right control panel; - manual air conditioning controls. With the ignition ON (INT) enablement and side light command signals, the Body Computer manages the lighting of: - cigar lighter and rear current socket; - radio preparation; - telephone preparation. A "+lights" signal is also sent to the electrochromic interior mirror. See E3032 DOOR MIRROR ADJUSTMENT The Body Computer manages (directly or via the driver's door and passenger door control units and the boot control unit) the dimmed lighting of: - the instrument panel and display; - the radio or Connect Nav+ display; - the automatic climate control display; - the radio controls on the steering wheel (where fitted); - the controls on the driver's door; - the electric window switches on the remaining doors. The brightness can be adjusted to different levels, by means of two outer buttons on the right control panel. There are up to 8 different settings. The intensity set by pressing the "MODE +" and "MODE -" buttons is shown in the control panel display. This value is transmitted on the CAN in order to make the information available to the other nodes. Once set, this value is stored in the memory and used later on. The brightness cannot be reduced to zero and the instrument panel failure warning lights cannot be adjusted or dimmed. The brightness level supplied via the CAN to the radio or the Connect Nav+ and to the automatic climate control system control unit, makes it possible to increase or decrease the backlighting of the displays. it goes from maximum lighting (daytime) to dimming with the side lights on (nightime) depending on the customer's requirements.

The INT supply line (key turned to ON position) protected by fuse F49 of the junction unit under the dashboard B002, provides the lighting for the controlson the tunnel H036, the hazard warning lights control H020, the right control panel H091 and the manual air conditioning M070 - pin 28. The lighting of the front door controls H044 and H050 is managed by the driver side door control unit M066 and passenger side door control unit M067 , supplied at pin 11 of connector D by a line protected by fuse F32 of the underfacia control unit B002 , and connected- pin 15 and 16 of connector B - via the CAN line to the Body Computer M001 . Similarly, the lighting of the controls for the electric windows in the rear left H053 and right H054 doors is managed by the boot control unit M063 , supplied - at pin B8 of connector A - by a line protected by fuse F36 of the underfacia control unit B002- pin A7 an B7- connected via the CAN line to the Body Computer M001 . The Body Computer M001 receives the side lights on signal at pin 28 of connector G. See E2010 SIDE LIGHTS / NO. PLATE LIGHTS The supply with the side lights on is provided by the Body Computer M001 respectively: - from pin 18 of connector H: at the radio preparation, at the telephone preparation D099 and at the front cigar lighter/current socket P050; - from pin 40 of connector E. to the electrochromic interior mirror P065 and to the rear current socket P052. The "MODE", "MODE +" AND "MODE -" controls in the right control panel H091 send analogue signals to the instrument panel E050 at pin 16 of connector B and pin 9 of connector A. The instrument panel E050 receives an ignition operated supply (INT from steering lock control unit) - pin 1 of connector A - from the line protected by fuse F37 of the junction unit under the dashboard B002 and directly from the battery - pin 2 of connector A - via the line for fuse F53 of B002. Pin 7 of connector A is earthed. The Body Computer M001 is connected via the CAN line to the instrument panel E050 from which it receives the "brightness adjustment" signal which is transmitted to the radio node or Connect Nav+ P020, to the automatic climate control system control unit M060 and to the steering wheel node M093. See E1050 CAN CONNECTION LINES

The vehicle is equipped with a single-tone horn. The horn is operated by pressing the two side areas of the horn cover (around the air bag). The horn circuit is protected by a special fuse and controlled by a special relay located in the engine compartment control unit. For safety reasons, the horn can be operated at any time, even with the key turned OFF in the ignition or removed.

Horn P005 is supplied via relay T3 of engine compartment control unit B001 from a direct line from the battery protected by fuse F10 in unit B001. The coil of the above relay is excited with a general earth signal received following closure of one of the keys on the steering wheel. They are connected to the vehicle wiring via the clock spring D047 (LOW version, steering wheel without controls) or via the Steering Wheel Node M093 and D047 (HIGH version, steering wheel with radio controls). The relay supplies the single-tone horn P005.

The windscreen wash/wipe system is activated by the lever located on the right of the steering wheel, with the following functions: there are several possible positions for the lever, turning it in a clockwise direction, corresponding to: - windscreen wiper off (stationary); - intermittent/automatic operation (according to whether or not the rain sensor is activated); - continuous operation 1st speed (about 45 strokes per minute); - continuous operation 2nd speed (about 65 strokes per minute); - "antipanic" temporary fast operation (unstable position, turning the lever in an anti-clockwise direction). In the intermittent/automatic operation position three different positions can be selected by turning the wheel (off, slow or fast): In the automatic operating position with rain sensor on, the different sensor sensitivity settings are activated: the activation of the rain sensor involves a windscreen wiper arm stroke as feedback to confirm that it has been switched on. The frequency of the windscreen wiper strokes is automatically adjusted depending on the amount of water on the windscreen detected by the sensor: the frequency varies continuously from nil (no stroke - windscreen dry) to wiping at the second continuous speed (heavy rain). The windscreen washer function can be activated by pulling the lever toward the steering wheel: this activates the windscreen washer pump: keeping the lever pulled also switched on the windscreen wiper in accordance with a specific control logic: the rearscreen wiper is activated and then, when the rearscreen washer command ends, an additional stroke is carried out. The control of the functions described above is carried out by an electronic device inside the steering column switch unit which produces the intermittent function and controls the operation of the windscreen wiper motor and the windscreen washer electric pump. The windscreen wash/wipe circuit is protected by a specific fuse and controlled by the ignition-operated exclusion relay located in the junction unit under the dashboard. The windscreen wiper and the windscreen washer can be activated with the key in the ON position (INT/A). If the rain sensor is not working properly, the windscreen wiper operates intermittently, whilst the sensor failure is signalled in the instrument panel display.

The electronic device inside the steering column switch unit H005 and the controls on the right lever receive a power supply at pin 11 of connector A from the line controlled by relay T12 protected by fuse F43, both housed in the junction unit under the dashboard B002. Pin 7 of connector A and 9 of connector C of H005 are earthed. According to the function selected, stalk unit H005 (connector A) sends the following control signals to the wiper motor N015: - from pin 8 for fast operation; - from pin 9 for slow and/or intermittent operation, - pin 6, on the other hand, receives the earth signal coming from the motor end of travel cam which stops operation. The windscreen wiper motor N015 is then earthed. The steering column switch unit H005 windscreen washer switch, once activated, sends two signals from pins 10 and 12 of connector A which operate the windscreen washer pump N022 which turns sending the washer fluid to the windscreen wiper. The rain sensor housed in the mirror P65 receives a supply from the INT line protected by fuse F49 of the junction unit B002 and sends the automatic operating signal to pin 7 of connector D and pin 25 of connector B via the A-BUS serial line of the Body Computer M1 . See E1060 A-BUS SERIAL LINE The Body Computer M001 is connected via the CAN line to the instrument panel E050 to manage the "failure" warning light if there are problems with the rain sensor.

The rearscreen wiper is activated by turning the ring nut on the end of the lever on the right of the steering wheel. The operation of the rearscreen wiper motor is controlled intermittently by the electronic device that also manages the windscreen wash/wipe function. the rear wiper comes on: - in synchrony with the windscreen wiper but at half the rate of the windscreen wiper under all windscreen wiper operating conditions (intermittent/continuous). - continuous mode with rate of 45 beats per minute. Pushing the lever gently towards the steering wheel activates the rearscreen washer function, via the windscreen washer (two way) pump, which rotates in the opposite direction and sends the detergent fluid towards the back following the same control logic: the rearscreen wiper is activated and then, when the rearscreen washer command ends, an additional stroke is carried out. With the windscreen wipers working, if reverse gear is engaged, the rearscreen wiper is automatically activated: this function is managed by the Body Computer which sends the steering column switch unit electronic device this information coming from the reversing lights function control logic See E2022 REVERSING LIGHTS the rearscreen wash/wipe may be activated only with the ignition device ON (INT/A). The windscreen wash/wipe circuit is protected by a specific fuse and controlled by the ignition-operated exclusion relay located in the junction unit under the dashboard.

The electronic device inside the steering column switch unit H005 and the controls on the right lever receive a power supply at pin 11 of connector A from the ignition-controlled line of relay T12 protected by fuse F43, both housed in the junction unit under the dashboard B002. The relay supplies the circuit only when the coil receives the INT/A signal from the steering lock control unit with the ignition ON. The part of the electronic device of stalk unit H005 that manages the rear wiper function is supplied at pin 12 of connector C from the line of relay T12 protected by fuse F52 contained in the under-dashboard control unit B002. Pin 7 of connector A and pin 9 of connector C of H005 are earthed. When the rear wiper function is activated, stalk unit H005 sends a control signal to rear wiper motor N016 from pin 1 of connector B. Pin 2 receives an earth signal from the motor end travel cam that stops its operation. Motor N016 is then earthed. The steering column switch unit H005 windscreen washer switch, once activated, sends two signals from pins 10 and 12 of connector A which operate the windscreen washer pump N022 which turns sending the washer fluid to the windscreen wiper. Pin 3 of connector A receives a signal (positive) from Body Computer M001 - pin 1 of connector A - which activates the automatic operation of the rear wiper with reverse engaged. See E2022 REVERSING LIGHTS

The headlamp washer cleans the headlamp lenses as the windscreen is being cleaned. The headlamp washer function is managed by the Body Computer which automatically activates the headlamp washer, with the dipped headlamps on, when the windscreen washers are activated through the lever on the right of the steering wheel. The headlamp washer consists of a pump that sends detergent to a nozzle located in the bumpers. This in turn sprays a powerful jet on the headlamp. A timer activates the headlamp washer pump by means of a series of pulses lasting about half a second. The headlamp washer circuit is protected by a fuse and regulated by a specific relay in the engine compartment control unit. It may be operated only with the igntion ON (INT/A).

Relay T17 of engine compartment control unit B001 is supplied directly from the battery from the line of fuse F9, also located in engine compartment B001; relay T17 supplies the circuit only when the coil receives an INT/A signal from the steering lock control unit with the ignition turned ON, via a line protected by fuse F31 under-dashboard control unit B002. when an earth signal is received from Body Computer M001 - from pin 14 of connector A - relay T17 operates headlamp washer pumpN025 directly; this command is sent on the basis of a positive windscreen washer request signal from stalk unit H005 - pin 5 of connector A - and with the low beam enablement on (pin 28 of connector G of M001).

In the case of poor visibility it is possible to activate the demisting of the rearscreen, the exterior rear view mirrors and the windscreen jets. The heating resistances for these components absorb a considerable amount of energy and are therefore controlled and, possibly, deactivated after they have been working for a certain length of time: the demisting is subject to a delay timer, managed by the Body Computer, according to the following logic: - key ON (INT/A from steering lock control unit); - engagement signal coming from the special button in the climate control system control panel. Under these circumstances the resistances remain supplied for a maximum of 20 minutes, then the supply is cut off. The supply is cut off in the following conditions: - key OFF or removed; - disengagement signal from the button; - battery voltage below 8.5 V; - after the first 15 minutes of operation if the engine speed is below 960 rpm. With the defrosting on the warning light in the climate control system controls also comes on. The activation timer (20 minutes) is set again each time the button is operated. The climate control system control unit logic also intervenes with the "MAX-DEF" command in accordance with the logic described previously. The "MAX-DEF" function lasts for 3 minutes starting from when the engine temperature exceeds a certain limit. the deactivation of the MAX-DEF control only causes the switching off of the heated rear windscreen if the command to switch it on came from the MAX-DEF button; if, on the other hand, the command was given via the heated rear windscreen button, it remains on) The rearscreen defrosting circuit is controlled by the heated rear windscreen relay and protected by a specific fuse, located in the junction unit under the dashboard. This circuit is controlled by the logic described above directly by the Body Computer. The defrosting circuit for the door mirrors, on the other hand, is protected by another fuse in the junction unit under the dashboard and is controlled by the door control units, in accordance with the logic transmitted by the Body Computer via the CAN.

Heated rear window relay T11, located in underfacia control unit B002, controls the simultaneous activation of the heated rear window demister function P055 - line protected by fuse F40 - and also the demister coils of windscreen washer nozzles O050 and O051 - line protected by fuse F41 -. The coil of relay T11 is supplied with an ignition-operated supply (INT/A from the steering lock control unit) and is excited by an earth signal from Body Computer M001 pin 6 of connector F; this signal is sent via the control logic described previously, and in the presence of an earth signal, to pin 32 of connector G of M001 from the rearscreen activation button pressed or the MAX-DEF function. This signal comes from climate control unit M070 (for versions with a manual climate control system, from pin 14 ofM070; for versions with an automatic climate control system, from pin 4 of connector A), to which as sent a signal to turn on the associated led - from pin 21 of connector H of M001 (only for versions with manual climate control system). Control units M66 and M67 receive a supply - at pin 11 of connector D - from the line protected by fuse F32 of underfacia control unit B002 . On the basis of the complex control logic illustrated previously, the engagement command for the defrosting is sent via the CAN to the two door control units as well which control the resistances located in mirrors P60 and P61 from pins 7 and 9 of connector E of M066 and M067.

The heating resistances for these components absorb a considerable amount of energy and are therefore controlled and, possibly, deactivated after they have been working for a certain length of time: the demisting is subject to a delay timer, managed by the Body Computer, according to the following logic: - key in ON (INT/A from steering lock control unit); - engagement signal coming from the special button in the climate control system control panel. Under these circumstances the resistances remain supplied for a maximum of 20 minutes, then the supply is cut off. The supply is cut off in the following conditions: - key OFF or extracted; - disengagement signal from the button; - battery voltage below 8.5 V; - after the first 15 minutes of operation if the engine speed is below 960 rpm. With the defrosting on the warning light in the climate control system controls also comes on. The activation timer (20 minutes) is set again each time the button is operated. The climate control system control unit logic also intervenes with the "MAX-DEF" command in accordance with the logic described later on. The "MAX-DEF" function lasts for 3 minutes starting from when the engine temperature exceeds a certain limit. the deactivation of the MAX-DEF control only causes the switching off of the heated rear windscreen if the command to switch it on came from the MAX-DEF button; if, on the other hand, the command was given via the heated rear windscreen button, it remains on. The defrosting circuit for the rearscreen and the screen washer jets is controlled by the heated rear windscreen relay and protected by two specific fuses, located in the junction unit under the dashboard. The coil for relay T11 receives an ignition operated power supply (INT/A from the steering lock contro lunit) and is energized by an earth coming from the Body Computer M011 pin 6 of connector F; this signal is sent according to a control logic described previously and, if there is an earth signal at pin 32 of connector G of M001 coming from the heated rear windscreen button or from the MAX-DEF function. This signal comes from the climate control system control unit M070 (for versions with manual climate control from pin 14 of M070; for versions with automatic climate control, from pin 4 of connector A), to which the signal for switching on the LED is sent from pin 21 of connector H of M001 (for versions with manual climate control only). The exterior rear view mirrors are electrically adjusted in two directions (horizontally and vertically) using a joystick; the left or right mirror is chosen using a selector. The driver's front door control unit acquires the adjustment commands and transmits them, via the CAN, to the passenger side and to the driving position control unit. There are three buttons on the driver's front seat controls used for the automatic recall of the positions memorized. See E3076 ELECTRICALLY-ADJUSTABLE SEATS This memory funcion is managed by the driving position control unit, which downloads seat positions directly and also door mirror positions via the CAN network. The control unit stores all the above positions when one of the three buttons is held down for at least three seconds. A buzzer inside the instrument panel goes off when the positions have been stored. The memory recall function is inhibited when the car is travelling faster than 10 km/h, via a signal sent via the CAN network from the Body Computer to the driving position control unit. If command come simultaneously from the joystick and the steering control unit, the former have priority, thereby cancelling the return of the exterior rear view mirrors to the position memorized. The rear view mirrors contain 3 motors: one for movement on the horizontal axis, one for movement on the vertical axis and one used for folding back the actual mirror. The folding function is also managed by the control unit at the driver's door which acquires the command from a button near the joystick. The folding always applies to both mirrors, irrespective of the current position of the selector. The driving position control unit acquires the vehicle speed signal and if it exceeds 10Km/h it inhibits the request to recall a position memorized. If the recall is made when the vehicle speed is above 10 Km/h, the movement is not interrupted but is brought to a conclusion. When reverse gear is engaged and the side lights are on, thanks to the presence of a rain and dusk sensor, the electro-chromic interior rear view mirror is immediately darkened, like the exterior rear view mirrors, allowing improved visibility. All the functions described are enabled with the key inserted and turned to the ON position in the ignition device.

The Body Computer M001 is supplied by ignition controlled (INT) and direct battery lines rrom the junction unit under the dashboard B002. The driver's door M066 and passenger door M067 control units receive a direct supply from the battery via the line protected by F32 of the junction unit under the dashboard at pin 11 of connector D. The driving position control unit M173 only receives a power supply at pin 9 of connector B, from the line protected by fuse F56 of the boot junction unit B045 when the relay T21 is energized directly by the line protected by fuse F52 in junction unit B002. The controls in the driver's door H044 send the following signals to the driver's door control unit M066: - from pin 18 of connector B a door mirror folding signal is sent; - from pin 8 of connector A a driver's/passenger rear view mirror selection command signal is sent; - from pin 6 connector A a shared earth signal is sent for the miror selection; - from pin 9 connector A sends a control signal for the vertical movement of the mirrors deflector; - from pin 7 connector A sends a control signal for the horizontal movement of the mirrors deflector; The driver's door control unit M066 receives the signals described above managing the rear view mirror P060 directly whilst it transmits them to the passenger side control unit M067, via the CAN, where the latter manages the rear view mirror P061. The driving position control unit M173 manages the recall command for the positions memorized by pressing the three buttons. The Body Computer M001 and the control units in the doors M066 and M067 are notified, via the CAN, of the selection made. With the side lights on, the electrochromic interior rear view mirror P065 becomes dark when reverse is engaged. The Body Computer M001 receives the side lights on signal at pin 28 of connector G. The reverse gear engagement signal is received at pin 1 of connector A. See E2022 REVERSING LIGHTS

The simultaneous operation of the door locks takes place via: - the buttons in the control panel on the tunnel; - the remote control; The component for recognizing the door locking system is the T.E.G. (Transmitter for Entry and Go) which acts as a radiofrequency remote control and allows the locking/unlocking of the doors or the release of the boot at a distance. The T.E.G. has three buttons that allow the operation of the central locking system: one button for unlocking the doors, one for locking the doors and one for releasing the boot. The door locking system has a dead lock function which allows the mechanical disconection of the door interior opening handles and the safety knob so that the door cannot be opened from the inside after the glass has been broken (improved theft protection). The dead lock function is switched on using the remote control at the time when the doors are locked by pressing the locking button a second time within one second of the first time it is pressed and this is signalled by two flashes of the direction indicators and the red LED in the door panel for half a second. In general, the door unlocking/locking management strategy is carried out by the NBC, whilst the NPP NPG and NVB nodes activate the motors for the locks in accordance with the commands transmitted via the B-CAN from the NBC. There are two buttons in the control panel on the tunnel that allow the central locking and unlocking of all the doors. If the doors have been locked using the remote control, pressing the unlocking button does not produce any request and the button is disabled. The status of the inertia switch is acquired directly by the NBC therefore it controls the unlocking of the doors in emergencies (accident). In addition, the signal coming from the inertia switch only causes the unlocking of the boot if the boot is subject to the doors: if the boot is set to always locked, this signal does not produce any action. There is a red LED on the vehicle on the driver's door panel which signals the locking of the locks, the engagement of the dead lock and a deterrent function. The deterrence signalling is only activated if a door locking command has been successful. With the vehicle locked, pulling the interior handle produces the mechanical unlocking of the door involved, local to the individual door (not detected by the system). The NBC having detected the transition of the door from closed to open, alters the logic status transmitted on the network and may or may not command the unlocking of the doors. More specifically: - opening via the rear handle: the status of the door involved is aligned; - opening via the driver's handle: according to the vehicle set-up, the unlocking of the doors is commanded; - opening via the passenger handle: the central unlocking is commanded. In the last two cases the boot is also unlocked (if it has not been set in an independent mode). It is possible, using the NQS/NIT set-up menu, to enable or disable the automatic locking of the doors when a pre-set speed is exceeded. If the function is enabled, the NBC compares the vehicle speed with the level of 20 Km/h and requests the locking of the doors when this speed is exceeded. The doors are only locked after all the doors are closed and after the first time the level of 20 Km/h is exceeded. If the doors are locked by this function, the user can unlock the doors using the central unlocking button. If the speed drops below 20 km/h with the doors locked, the doors are not released. If, with the vehicle locked, any one of the doors is opened and then closed (mechanically unlocked), when the speed level is next exceeded, the NBC will request the locking once again. The NQS acquires the door, boot, bonnet (only if the alarm is fitted) status and vehicle speed signals from the B-CAN. After a key on, if the following conditions are verified: - a door or the boot or the bonnet is open; - the speed > 4 Km/h. The NQS emits a cycle of acoustic signals for a period of 5 seconds and (if the display permits) the relevant message is shown (for example, right front door open). The cycle of acoustic signals is only interrupted if at least one of the following conditions takes place: - all the doors, the boot or the bonnet are closed; - the vehicle speed < 4 Km/h.

The front doors locking/unlocking function is produced by the driver's door N066 and passenger door M067 control units, whilst the function for the rear doors is carried out by the boot control unit M063. Alll the control units are managed via the B-CAN line by the Body Computer M001 which receives the opening/closing signals, at pins 24 and 25 (connector H) from the ignition device H003 (T.E.G. Reader). More specifically: - the Body Computer M001 interfaces on the B-CAN line going from pins 28 and 10 of connector D of the junction unit under the dashboard B002; - the driver's front door M066 and passenger side M067 control units communicate at pins 15 and 16 of connector B; - the boot control unit M063, communicates at pins B7 and A7 of connector B. See E1050 CAN CONNECTION LINES Control units M066 and M067 receive a power supply at pin 11 of connector D from the line protected by fuse F32 of the junction unit under the dashboard B002 (pin 11 of connector D). The latter, via pin 13 of connector D, also supplies the control unit M063 at pin B8 of connector A, via the line protected by fuse F36. Control unit M066 and M067 receive, at pin 23 of connector B, the incoming locking signal from the knobs, from pin 6 of connector D a joint power supply is sent to the drives front door N050 and passenger front door N051 lock geared motors, from pin 4 (connector D) the locking/unlocking (B/S) motor is activated and from pin 3 (connector D) the dead lock motor (DL) is activated. Lastly, pin 19 of connector B for both control units is connected to the driver's dashboard earth C015. Control unit M066 still receives, at pins 35 and 34 of connector A, the signals for the locking/unlocking buttons (respectively) located in the control panel on the tunnel H036 and communicates the boot and fuel flap opening commands at pins 12 and 5 of connector E. See E3045 BOOT AND FUEL FLAP OPENING The boot control unit M063 receives the locking signal from the knobs at pin B4 of connectors A and B, from pins A7 of connector A and A2 of connector B the joint supplies for the motors for geared motor for the lock in the driver's rear door N055 and passenger rear door N056 (respectively) is sent, from pins C7 of connector A and C2 of connector B the locking/unlocking (B/S) motors are activated, whilst from pins C6 of connector A and C4 of connector B the dead lock motors (DL) are activated. Lastly, pin C8 of connector A is connected with the driver's side rear earth C030. The intervention of the inertia switch I050 is signalled at pin 17 of connector D of the Body Computer M001 controlling the opening of the doors in emergency situations (accident).

Lastly, pin C8 of connector A is connected with the driver's side rear earth C030. The intervention of the inertia switch I050 is signalled at pin 17 of connector D of the Body Computer M001 controlling the opening of the doors in emergency situations (accident).

The boot opening geared motor (boot "release") is operated via the remote control in two ways. - indepedently of the doors: there is a special button on the remote control that allows the boot only to be "unlocked": the boot is released and lifts up slightly. The operation is indicated by the turn signals flashing twice. in this way the unlocking of the doors leaves the boot locked. - Together and at the same time as the unlocking of the doors: the rear tailgate is to all intents and purposes considered as a fifth door and is subject to the central locking system. For more details on the control logic, See E3040 CENTRAL LOCKING The two modes described above can be selected using a special setup in the instrument panel When the boot is closed, it is aligned to the status of the vehicle (unlocked with doors unlocked, locked with doors locked) by the set up in the NQS: in this case, with the option activated, it returns to locked when it is closed again. The tailgate (after being unlocked) can only be opened from the outside of the vehicle using the opening handle. The boot opening function is disabled (the tailgate does not open) if the speed of the vehicle exceeds 10 km/h (this is to prevent undesired opening whilst driving caused, for example, by vibrations of the exterior handle over very bumpy roads). The boot opening circuit is protected by a specific fuse, located in the junction unit under the dashboard. The remote control receiver aerial is inside the ignition device (TEG Reader). The fuel flap is managed directly by the driver's door control unit and is therefore connected to the locked/unlocked status of the driver's door.

The "boot open" signal is sent by the switch - located in the handle I033 - to pin 35 of connector E of the Body Computer M001. The operation of the boot opening geared motor N057 takes place by means of the remote control signal: in this case, the ignition device H003, receives the signal and transmits it via the CAN to the Body Computer M001 (pins 24 and 25 of connector H). The boot lock geared motor N057 receives the activation signal from pin 11 of connector F of the Body Computer M001. The geared motor N057 receives a power supply until the opening of the boot is detected: the "boot not properly shut" signal is, in effect, sent by switch I011 which is connected to pin 24 of connector E. The contact in question signals the "boot not properly shut" condition; the switch is fitted with another contact that signals the "boot open" condition, a contact used by the boot light function See E2520 GLOVE COMPARTMENT LIGHT - LUGGAGE COMPARTMENT LIGHT - SUN VISOR LIGHT The driver's door control unit M066 receives the door locking/unlocking signals from the controls on the tunnel H036 - pins 34 and 35 of connector A. On the basis of the signal received, the fuel flap lock geared motor N058 is operated by the driver's door control unit M066 via pins 12 and 5 of connector D.

The electric windows for the front doors are operated through the switches on the driver's door (both windows) and the passenger side (passenger side only). The control units in the door control the operation of the driver's and passenger side electric window motors which are operated both manually and automatically. Automatic operation takes place as follows: - if the button is pressed is between 50 and 300 milliseconds (short press), operation is manual. the glass goes up/down only with the key pressed; - if the key is pressed for longer than 300 milliseconds (long press), operation is automatic: even if the button is released, the glass continues to move up/down until the end of travel position is reached or until the intervention of the anti-crush safety system (if fitted); - pressing the button again whilst the window is moving stops it in the position it is in; - if the button is pressed for less than 50 milliseconds, this is ignored (it is treated as an accidental knock). Each control unit in the door also manages the anti-crush safety function: It acquires information of the possible presence of an obstacle whilst the window is closing (upwards movement, two resistive sensors inside the electric window motor which if an obstacle is encountered when the window is closing immediately interrupt the travel and reverse the direction). The anti-crush safety function is activated during both manual and automatic operation. If the control units in the door detect the presence of an obstacle in the "inversion zone" whilst the window is moving upwards, they should: - interrupt the upwards movement and reverse it immediately in a total time of 30ms. - revers the direction of the window which should reach a position corresponding to an opening of at least 200 mm from the upper edge or at least 50 mm higher than the initial starting position of the window. - ignore any type of closing or opening command during the entire reversal time. If the control units in the door detect the presence of an obstacle in the "non inversion zone" they should only interrupt the upwards movement of the window. The correct operation of the anti-crush sensor is controlled by the control unit check function: in the case of a failure this information is sent via the CAN to the instrument panel to light up the general failure warning light and show the information on the display. In addition, if there is a failure the control units should inhibit the upwards movement of the window in automatic mode. The windows are automatically opened or closed through the special prolonged (more than 2 seconds) command sent by the remote control button. The remote control receiver aerial is inside the ignition device (TEG Reader). The circuit is operated according to the door control units control logic with a power supply protected by two special fuses operated by the underdashboard junction unit services relay: The electric window function can only be activated with the ignition ON (INT) except when the windows are closed/opened centrally via remote control and during the timed period with key off. During the starting stage, this relay is temporarily deactivated, whilst with the ignition OFF, the Body Computer keeps the relay activated for 2 minutes, but deactivates it 30 seconds after one of the doors is opened. The driver's door control unit acquires both the commands for the driver's front door and those for the passenger door; it manages the movement of the driver's window directly and transmits the movement commands, via the CAN, for the passenger window to the passenger door control unit which manages the passenger side window directly. The passenger door cotnrol unit only acquires the commands for the front passenger door and controls its own motor directly.

The two control units, driver's door M066 and passenger door M067 receive a direct supply from the batter with the logic described above (and controlled by the Body Computer M001 pin 14 of connector F) via the services relay T13 located in the junction unit under the dashboard B002 via two lines protected by fuses F47 and F48. The supply arrives, for both control units, at pin 8 of connector D. The control units M066 and M067 are connected to one another and to the Body Computer M001 via the CAN line at pins 15 and 16 of connector B. Unit H44 contains the driver and passenger side window controls:: dedicated analogue signals are sent to pins 31 and 33 of connector A of M066 (pin 32 supplies a reference earth). Control unit M066 operates the electric window motor N060 (driver's side) directly - pins 9 and 10 of connector D - and via control unit M067 - pins 9 and 10 of connector D - electric window motor N061 (passenger side). Similarly, the passenger side front door control H050 sends an analogue signal to control unit M067 pin 32 (pin 33 supplies a reference earth), which drives electric window motor N061 . Signals for the anti-crush safety sensors, included in the electric window motors N060 and N061 arrive at pins 2 and 5 of connector C of M066 and M067. The two control units are connected to the instrument panel E)50 via the CAN line to manage the general failure signal if there is a failure in the anti-crush safety sensors. The Body Computer is connected to the ignition device H003 for the central closing of the windows via the CAN line pins 24 and 25 of connector H.

Each control unit in the door also manages the anti-pinch safety function: In other words, it acquires information on the possible presence of an obstacle as the window is closing (as the window rises, two resistive sensors in the window motor immediately stop the window and reverse its direction of travel if an obstacle is encountered during closure. The remote control receiver aerial is inside the ignition device (TEG Reader). The driver's door control unit acquires both the driver's front door and passenger side front door commands; it manages the movement of the driver's window directly and sends the relevant movement commands for the passenger side window via the CAN to the passenger door control unit which manages the passenger side window directly. The electric windows in the rear doors are activated using the switches in the actual doors and the driver's front door. The commands from the driver's front door are transmitted via the CAN from the control unit in the door. The boot control unit controls the operation of the rear electric window motors directly, which are operated eith manually or automatically, in accordance with the following strategy: - if the button is pressed for between 50 and 300 milliseconds (short press), operation is manual: the glass goes up/down only with the key pressed; - if the button is pressed for longer than 300 milliseconds (long press), operation is automatic: even if the button is released, the glass continues to move up/down until the end of travel position is reached or until the intervention of the anti-crush safety system (if fitted); - pressing the button again whilst the window is moving stops it in the position it is in; - if the button is pressed for less than 50 milliseconds, this is ignored (it is treated as an accidental knock). The anti-crush safety function is activated during both manual and automatic operation. If the boot control unit detects the presence of an obstacle in the "inversion zone" whilst the window is moving upwards, it should: - interrupt the upwards movement and reverse it immediately in a total time of 30ms. - revers the direction of the window which should reach a position corresponding to an opening of at least 200 mm from the upper edge or at least 50 mm higher than the initial starting position of the window. - ignore any type of closing or opening command during the entire reversal time. If the boot control unit detects the presence of an obstacle in the "non inversion zone" it should only interrupt the upwards movement of the window. The correct operation of the anti-crush sensor is controlled by the control unit check function: in the case of a failure this information is sent via the CAN to the instrument panel to light up the general failure warning light and show the information on the display. In addition, if there is a failure the control units should inhibit the upwards movement of the window in automatic mode. The windows are automatically opened or closed through the special prolonged (more than 2 seconds) command sent by the remote control button. The circuit is operated according to the luggage compartment junction unit control logic with a power supply protected by two special fuses operated by the underdashboard junction unit services relay: The electric window function can only be activated with the ignition ON (INT) except when the windows are closed/opened centrally via remote control and during the timed period with key off. During the starting stage, this relay is temporarily deactivated, whilst with the ignition OFF, the Body Computer keeps the relay activated for 2 minutes, but deactivates it 30 seconds after one of the doors is opened. The driver's front door control unit also manages the locking of the rear controls (protection) when the special LOCK button is pressed: The locking status is indicated by an LED in the back of the actual button lighting up and the rear control buttons are not lit up. The electric windows cannot be operated using any of the buttons when the lock function is activated. The luggage compartment control unit M063 receives a direct supply from the battery with the logic described above (and controlled by the Body Computer M001 pin 14 of connector F) via the services relay T13, located in the junction unit under the dashboard B002, via the two lines protected by fuses F33 and F34. The supply reaches the control unit at pins A8 of connector A and B8 of connector B. The luggage compartment control unit M063 is connected via the CAN line - pin A7 and B7 of connector B - to the driver's front door control unit M066 - pins 15 and 16 of connector B. The boot control unit M063 controls the electric window motors N065 (left) and N066 (right) from pins C1 and A1 of connector A and from C8 and A8 of connector B. Similarly the controls on the rear doors H053 and H054 send special analogue signals to the control unit M063 to activate the motors N065 (pin B5 connector A) and N066 (pin B5 connector B). The control unit M063 is also connected, via the CAN line, to the Body Computer M001 and to the instrument panel E050 to manage the general failure warning light signal if there is a failure in the anti-crush safety sensors. The roof opening system comprises an extensively glazed area known as the outersliding skydome. The glazed area is divided into two panels: the rear one is fixed and the front one slides on the outside. The latter which is electrically operated, is activated by a switch that can be adjusted using a selector which has 5 positions. There are two sun blinds on the inside of the roof that slide independently towrads the rear of the vehicle. The front sun blind is electrically operated, the rear one can only be controlled manually. The sun roof and electric front blind selectors are located on the front courtesy light cover and, by means of a control unit, they control the activation of the electric motors located on the rear of the roof. The electronic control units are integrated in the electric motor casing: one for the moving glass (master) and one for the blind (slave). The movement of the sun roof takes place by operating the 5 position rrotary selector (clockwise for opening and anti-clockwise for closing), whilst an impulse type opening/closing button controls the front blind. For each of the 5 positions the there is a corresponding roof opening. The roof can be opened completely in one single manoeuvre by switching the selector from position "0" to position "5". Whilst the roof is opening, the system automatically manages the opening of the blind. However, when the roof is fully open, the system allows the independing management of the opening/closing of the blind (one-touch function). It is however not advisble to travel with the sun roof open and the blind closed. The system is equipped with an anti-crush safety function. A HALL effect sensor is located on the front profile of the glass panel and, by means of the sun roof control unit, it halts the movement of the roof if there is an obstacle. In addition, the control unit is capable of recognizing any increased current absorption for the roof moving motors due to any obstacles and it immediately stops the movement and reverses it.

The services relay T13 (pin 87) located in the junction unit under the dashboard B002, supplies, via two lines protected by fuses F45 and F46 respectively the sun roof motor N035 - pin 4 - and the blind operating motor N034 - pin 5. The sun roof blind controls H073 - pin 3 are supplied via the line protected by F49 of the junction unit under the dashboard B002. The relay T13 receives a supply via the line protected by fuse F1 of the engine compartment junction unit B001 and is operated at pin 86 via the Body Compuer M001 - pin 14. The Body Computer M001, via pin 1 of connector D, send a negative remote opening/closing enablement signal for the roof to pin 5 of the sun roof motor N035, whilst from pin 11 of the same connector of M001 it sends a speedometer signal to pin 3 of N035. Pins 6, 5, 3, 2 of the sun roof opening switch H060 are connected to pins 11, 12, 9, 10 of the sun roof motor N035. Pins 1, 2 for the operation of the sun roof blind H073 are connected to pins 7, 8 of N035 which, through its inernal control unit - pin 6 (serial line) manages the blind N034 motor - pin 1. Pin 2 of the motor N035 and pin 9 of motor N034 are connected to the right rear earth C031. Pin 1 of the sun roof switch H060 is connected to the left rear earth C030, whilst pin 4 of the sun roof controls H073 is connected to the passenger side dashboard earth C020.

On the tunnel console, next to the handbrake, there is a standard type current socket which can be used for connecting the diagnostic equipment or equipment working at 12 V. The socket has a ring nut that is lit up when the side lights are on. See E2530 INSTRUMENT LIGHTING There is a second current socket, on the tunnel console, towards the rear seats, similar to the previous one. The sockets are equipped with a thermal protection device: this protection cuts off the power supply if devices that absorb a lot of energy are connected. In order to be able to use the FIX & GO rapid repair kit (a device that needs a high current absorption) a change in the section of the connecting leads to the current sockets on the vehicle is anticipated. The rear current socket (behind the tunnel console) is the only one that should be used when the FIX & GO kit has to be used. The circuit for the two current sockets in the console is protected by two specific fuses and controlled by the ignition-operated exclusion relay located in the junction unit under the dashboard. To prevent the battery from being drained, these sockets only work with the ignition ON (INT/A). For versions equipped with the FIX & GO kit on the other hand, the circuit for the current sockets is protected by a single fuse located in the junction unit under the dashboard. The cigar lighter resistance can be located in the front socket in the console; simply press the knob to operate it: after a few seconds it will come out automatically, ready for use. This resistance is only available on request, in a "smokers kit" comprising, in addition to the cigar lighter, a removable ashtray in the shape of a cup that can be closed to be fitted in the cup holder.

The current socket / cigar lighter P050 receives a direct supply from the battery via the line for relay T12 protected by fuse F52 both housed in the junction unit under the dashboard B002. The rear current socket P052 also receives a supply from the line controlled by relay T12 protected by fuse F44 both housed in the junction unit under the dashboard B002. For versions equipped with the FIX & GO kit on the other hand, both the current socket / cigar lighter P050 and the rear current socket P052 receive a supply from the line protected by fuse F44 of junction unit B002. The lighting for the cigar lighter P050 is supplied by the Body Computer M001 pin 18 of connector H. The lighting for the current socket P052 is supplied by the Body Computer M001 pin 40 of connector E. See E2530 INSTRUMENT LIGHTING

The front seats have a special heating system, consisting of two heater elements (pads) located inthe cushion and in the backrest that allow the seats to be heated when the temperature conditions are very harsh. The seat heating device, which can only be activated if the key is inserted in the igntion device and turned to ON (INT line) can be switched on using the special control in the control panel. The various controls in the switches I065 and I066 adjust the temperature of the seat; an internal temperature sensor, with a feedback function, guarantees that the temperature set is maintained.

The services relay T21, located in the boot junction unit B045, supplies: - via the battery line protected by fuse F57, the driver's front seat heating control unit M170 - pin 5 and the switch for the driver's heated seat I065 - pin 2; - via the line protected by fuse F67, the passenger front seat heating control unit M110 - pin 5 and the switch for the passenger side heated seat I066 - pin 2; Power pin 30 for relay T21 of the boot junction unit B045, receives a power supply from the direct battery line via the junction unit under the dashboard B002 pin A connector B, pin B connector C protected by fise F1 of junction unit B001. The coil for relay T21 is supplied by relay T12 of the junction unit under the dashboard B002; relay T12 is activated by the supply line (INT) when the ignition key is in the ON position. The LEDs inside switches I066 and I065 with a backlighting function, receive a power supply at pin 1 via the line (INT) controlled by the ignition protected by fuse F49 of the junction unit under the dashboard B002. For the driver's seat. The heater pad with the driver's front temperature sensor O046 and the heater pad for the driver's front backrest O048, connected in series, are supplied at pins 3 and 2 of switch I065 - pin 3. Pin 7 of the driver's front seat heating control unit M170 receives the signal from the temperature sensor in the heater pad in the seat cushion whilst pin 6 receives a voltage signal for controlling the system. For the passenger seat. The heater pad with the passenger front temperature sensor O047 and the heater pad for the passenger front backrest O049, connected in series, are supplied at pins 3 and 2 of switch I066 - pin 3. Pin 7 of the passenger front seat heating control unit M110 receives the signal from the temperature sensor in the heater pad in the seat cushion whilst pin 6 receives a voltage signal for controlling the system.

The front driver and passenger side seats are equipped with an adjustment device that ensures the driver and passenger the best possible position and comfort. The driver side electrical adjustment device is fully managed by the driver position control unit: this movement is produced by means of the control unit on the left of the seat, or automatically, by calling up one of possible stored settings. The adjustment of the passenger seat, on the other hand, can only be done using the controls on the right of the seat. The electrical movement of the seats can only be activated with the key ON. When the key is turned OFF again, there is a timed period of around a minute, within which the automatic operation of recalling the position stored in the memory must be automatically completed. The device is excluded temporarily during start-up (INT/A). The seat adjustment control unit includes: - a button to tilt the cushion (forward and back); - a button to slide the seat unit longitudinally; - a button for adjust backrest rake; - a button to raise/lower the seat unit vertically; There are three buttons on the driver's front seat controls used for the automatic recall of the positions memorized. See E3032 DOOR MIRROR ADJUSTMENT This memorizing is managed by the driving position control unit which acquires the positions of the seats and the exterior rear view mirrors directly via the B-CAN. By pressing one of the three buttons for at least three seconds, all the adjustments made to the seat and the mirrors are stored in the control unit memory. The memory recall function is inhibited when the car is travelling faster than 10 km/h, via a signal sent via the B- CAN from the Body Computer to the driving position control unit.

The services relay T21, located in the boot junction unit B045, supplies: - from pin 5 of connector A, via the line protected by fuse F60, the passenger position control unit M175 (pin 9 of connector B); - from pin 3 of connector A, via the line protected by fuse F56, the driving position control unit M173 (pin 9 of connector B); Power pin 30 of relay T21 of the boot junction unit B045 receives a power supply from the direct battery line via the junction unit under the dashboard B002 (pin A connector B) protected by fuse F1 of junction unit B001. The coil for relay T21 receives a power supply from relay T12 of the junction unit under the dashboard B002, via the line protected by fuse F52. Relay T12 is activated by the supply line (INT/A) when the ignition switch is in the ON position. FOR THE DRIVER'S FRONT SEAT The motors inside the component N127 and N132 receive a power supply at pins 1 via pin 2 of connector B of the driving position control unit M173. The motors inside the component N126 and N125 receive a power supply at pins 5 via pin 6 of connector B of the driving position control unit M173. The motors inside the components N125, N126, N127 and N132 receive a power supply at pins 2 from pin 7 of connector of the driving position control unit M173. The motor for adjusting the sliding of the left front seat M127 receives the command at pins 4 and 5 from the driving position control unit M173 (pin 2 of connector A and pin 3 of connector B). The motor for adjusting the height of the left front seat M126 receives the command at pins 1 and 4 from the driving position control unit M173 (pin 10 of connector B and pin 1 of connector A). The motors for adjusting the backrest and the rear height adjustment of the left front seat cushion receive: - the command simultaneously at pins 4 and 1 from pin 4 of connector B of the driving position control unit M173; - the command at pin 5 (N132) from pin 3 of connector A of the driving position control unit M173; - the command at pin 4 (N125) from pin 4 of connector A of the driving position control unit M173. FOR THE PASSENGER FRONT SEAT The motors inside the component N130 and N135 receive a power supply at pins 1 via pin 2 of connector B of the driving position control unit M175. The motors inside the component N129 and N128 receive a power supply at pins 5 via pin 6 of connector B of the driving position control unit M175. The motors inside the components N128, N129, N130 and N135 receive an earth at pins 2 from pin 7 of connector A of the driving position control unit M175. The motor for adjusting the sliding of the right front seat M130 receives the command at pins 4 and 5 from the driving position control unit M175 (pin 2 of connector A and pin 3 of connector B). The motor for adjusting the front height of the right front seat M129receives the command at pins 1 and 4 from the driving position control unit M175(pin 10 of connector B and pin 1 of connector A). The motors for adjusting the backrest (N135) and the rear height (N128) of the right front seat cushion receive: - the command simultaneously at pins 4 and 1 from pin 4 of connector B of the driving position control unit M175; - the command at pin 5 (N135) from pin 3 of connector A of the driving position control unit M175; - the command at pin 4 (N128) from pin 4 of connector A of the driving position control unit M175. The driving position control unit M173 and the passenger one M175 and the door control units M066 and M067 communicate via the B-CAN. The signals for positioning the rear view mirrors are stored in the memories of the control unit M173 and M175 when the request to memorize the position of the seat is made.

The adjustment of the light beam for the headlamps depending on the load is produced using the adjustment device located directly on the headlamps. This device, controlled by a button in the panel to the left of the steering wheel, tilts the headlamp parabola appropriately in order to lower the light beam if the vehicle is particularly laden and raise it when the load conditions decrease. The device is enabled only with the dipped beams on. There are four predefined positions for the headlamp alignment (from 0 to 3). These four positions are produced by adjusting the top part of the headlamp alignment switch to direct the light beam upwards (positions 3, 2, 1, 0) and the bottom part to move it downwards (positions 0, 1, 2, 3); the setting is memorized and shown on the instrument panel display. If there is a fault in the system the headlamps assume a configuration which avoids the oncoming drivers from being dazzled.

The headlamp alignment adjustment is only activated by the system with the main beams on. See E2011 DIPPED HEADLAMPS The steering column switch unit activates the dipped beams on status which is received at pin 2 of connector I of the Body Computer M001. The latter operates the relay 1 of the junction unit under the dashboard B002 with a pin to pin connection (pin 8 and 18). Pin 87of relay T1 supplies the dipped headlamp F010 and F011 at pins 1 via fuses F13 and F12. The switch for the left control unit H091 provides a headlamp alignment adjustment signal, via pin 18 of connector B, at pin 11 of connector B of the instrument panel E050. The latter, going from pins 5 and 6 of connector A, operates the motors in the left headlamp F010 and the right headlamp F011 at pins 7 and 6 respectively moving to the junction unit under the dashboard B002. The motors in the left F010 and right F001 headlamps are earthed via pins 8 to the left front earth C010 and to the right front earth C011 respectively.

The vehicle is fitted with two gas discharge headlamps. The left lamp is the master control unit, whilst the right one performs a slave role. The master lamp acquires the command for the dipped headlamps, the vehicle speed and, for managing the function in question, the signals from two sensors (potentiometers) located on the wheel axles, which measure the geometry at the front and at the back. Depending on the inputs, the control unit controls the adjustment motor located in the headlamps directly and tilts it appropriately on the version with gas discharge headlamps the adjustment of the light beam takes place automatically and there are not the two buttons in the panel on the left hand side. The device is enabled only with the dipped beams on. The relay which controls the engagement of the dipped headlamps also supplies the adjustment motors inside the headlamps; this relay for switching the dipped headlamps on is managed by the Body Computer: relay energizing is activated by enablement signals with key in the ON position and by the steering column switch unit dipped headlamps control. See E2011 DIPPED HEADLAMPS

The dipped headlights activation signal is sent to pin 2 of connector I of the Body Computer M001 from the steering column switch unit. See E2011 DIPPED HEADLAMPS The Body Computer M001, from pin 8 connector F, controls the power supply for the dipped headlamps sending an earth signal to relay T1 inside the junction unit under the dashboard B002 - pin 8 connector E. Pin 87 of relay T1 supplies the dipped headlamps F010 and F011 at pin 1 via fuses F13 and F12. Both electronic systems inside the headlamps F010 and F011 are supplied - pin 9 - from the INT line protected by fuse F37 of junction unit B002. Pins 12 of the control units inside the headlamps F010 and F011 are connected to one another by means of a special serial line, whilst the pin 10 of the control unit located in headlamp F010 receives the speedometer signal from the Body Computer M001 (pin 28 of connector B). The headlamp alignment control unit M073 is incorporated in the headlamp F010 and the two potentiometer sensors that detect the position at the front K001 and at the rear K002 are connected. On the basis of the signals receives, the headlamp electronics automatically adjust the direction of the light beam by means of a special motor. The control units inside the headlamps provide their own diagnostic signal used for the continuous monitoring of the entire device. See E8010 DIAGNOSTIC MULTIPLE CONNECTOR

The parking assistance system provides the driver with information, whilst reversing, on the distance from any objects behind the vehicle which could be out of their range of view. The information of the presence/distance of an obstacle is transmitted to the driver by means of acoustic warnings whose frequency depends on the distance of the vehicle from the obstacle. An electronic control unit activates and controls the operation of the sensors located in the rear bumper, processes the signals received and operates the buzzer in the instrument panel. The system is activated with reverse gear engaged: in these conditions, the control unit energizes the transducers and sends them a signal request, receiving the response signals. The sensors use ultrasound technology and act as intelligent transmitters/receivers with triangulation technology: allowing improved detection in critical situations or in the presence of small obstacles. The impulses emitted are reflected by any obstacles; the transducer receives an echo which is converted into a digital signal and sent to the electronic control unit. The signalling of the distance of the obstacle is achieved through intermittent impulse sound signals: the frequency of this signal increases gradually as the bumper approaches an obstacle: when the distance calculated goes below 30 cm, the sound becomes high pitched and constant; the acoustic signal stops when the distance of the obstacle increases. For more details and information on the operation of the system, See descriptions 5580H PARKING OBSTACLE DETECTION DEVICE The control unit is equipped with an autodiagnostic function: when switched on the control unit carries out an initial test on the sensors which are then continuously subject to fault diagnosis during the operation of the system. A fault in only one sensor inhibits the operation of the entire system: in this case the system excludes itself and sends a fault message, the failure status is signalled to the instrument panel which lights up the special warning light and sends a suitable acoustic signal. The signal that the reversing light has come on See E2022 REVERSING LIGHTS is managed by the Body Computer which forwards this information via the CAN to the parking sensors control unit. If there is a trailer then there is no signalling of rear obstacles. See E2050 TRAILER WIRING The system is supplied by the circuit protected by a specific fuse in the junction unit under the dashboard.

The parking sensor control unit M084 receives a supply at pin 1 of connector A from the ignition-controlled INT line protected by fuse F49 of junction unit B002; pin 8 of connector A is earthed. The control unit is connected, via pins 7 and 4 of connector A and the CAN, to all the other nodes in the same network; in this way it receives, amongst others, the reverse gear engaged signal. It sends the commands for operating the buzzer to the instrument panel via the CAN. A system operation inhibition signal reaches pin 5 if a trailer is connected via coupling D073. See E2050 TRAILER WIRING The four parking sensors K097 are connected to connector B of control unit M084. Pin 1 supplies a reference earth, pin 6 a power supply, pins 5, 3, 2 and 4 are connected to sensors K097E, K097F, K097G and K097H respectively.
