The vehicle is equipped with a radio system comprising: - wiring (speakers and radio); - speakers in the mirror triangle (tweeters); - speakers in the front doors (mid-woofers); - speakers in the rear door (full-range); - AM/FM aerial coaxial cable; - aerial mounting and stem. With the above preparation it is possible to fit a Linea Accessori or After Market radio. The radio leads and speaker leads are grouped together by means of two connectors (both 8-way) located and secured in the rear part of the compartment (1 DIN dimensions) which should be removed when fitting the radio. In this configuration there is no CAN, therefore the customer does not have a series of functions that are available on the radio as the initial system.

The radio preparation couplings receive the ignition-controlled power supply INT at pin 7 of connector A from the steering lock control unit via the line protected by fuse F49 of the dashboard junction unit B002. Pin 6 of connector A receives the signal for the fixed lighting (not dimmed) with the side lights on from the Body Computer M001 - pin 18 of connector H. See E2010 SIDE LIGHTS / NO. PLATE LIGHTS Pin 5 of connector A for the radio preparation is a supplementary electric aerial supply lead. The pin for connector A is earthed. The aerial P025 arrives in the DIN compartment by means of the special coaxial lead. Conector B for the radio preparation is connected to the speakers: - pins 5 and 6 to the driver's side front speakers P035 (mid-woofer) and P045 (tweeter); - pins 3 and 4 to the passenger side front speakers P036 (mid-woofer) and P046 (tweeter); - pins 7 and 8 to the left rear speaker P040, - pins 1 and 2 to the right rear speaker P041.

The vehicle is equipped with a radio system comprising: - radio; - wiring (speakers and radio); - speakers in the mirror triangle (tweeters); - speakers in the front doors (mid-woofers); - speakers in the rear door (full-range); - AM/FM aerial coaxial cable; - aerial mounting and stem. In this configuration the radio is a CAN node through which information is exchanged with the Body Computer and the other electronic units, providing the customer with a series of functions, including: - automatic switching off 20 minutes after the key off to protect the battery; - control of the dimmed lighting in the radio display with the side lights on; - volume control dependent on the vehicle speed (SVC); - controls on the steering wheel (where fitted). The radio, available in two different versions depending on customer requirements, can have a traditional CD player or CD MP3 player (compressed files). The radio has a security system with a four digit identification code on a card that is handed over to the customer when the vehicle is received when there is a factory-fitted radio. The above code should be entered every time the battery is disconnected to prevent it being reused on another vehicle. On request a multipolar cable for connecting the radio with a CD Changer located in the oddments compartment on the passenger side can be fitted. This configuration involves preparation for a mobile phone with hands-free kit. Some versions are equipped with controls on the steering wheel (6 button version): these make it possible to replicate some of the commands which are acquired in the same way by the actual radio. The functions are: - change/preset CD track or radio station (forwards); - change/preset CD track or radio station (backwards); - SCR (switch listening source); - VOL+ (increase volume); - VOL- (decrease volume); - MUTE. For more details, See descriptions 5570 ACCESSORIES

The radio P20 is supplied directly (4 of connector A) from the battery via the line protected by fuse F23 of the engine compartment junction unit B001 . Pins 1 and 3 of connector A are served by the CAN that connects the radio to the Body Computer M001 (pins 24 and 25 of connector H) and to the other system nodes. Pin 8 of connector A is earthed. The radio P020 is connected, via the CAN, to the radio controls on the steering wheel in the steering wheel control unit M093 - pins 1 and 5 - via the clock spring D047 (pins 3 and 4). The aerial P025 is connected to the radio by means of the special coaxial cable. Connector B of P020 is connected to the speakers: - pins 5 and 6 to the driver's front speakers P035 (mid-woofer) and P045 (tweeter); - pins 3 and 4 to the passenger front speakers P036 (mid-woofer) and P046 (tweeter); - pins 7 and 8 to the left rear speaker P040; - pins 1 and 2 to the right rear speaker P041. The cables connected to the CD Changer P075 come out of connector E. The cables connected to the telephone preparation come out of connector D. See E3580 PREPARATION FOR CELLULAR TELEPHONE

The vehicle is equipped with a radio system comprising: - radio; - wiring (radio and speakers); - speakers on the mirror triangle (tweeters); - speakers on the front doors (mid-woofers); - speakers on the rear doors (full-range); - AM/FM aerial coaxial lead; - aerial mount and stem. In this configuration, the radio is a node on the CAN network, via which it exchanges information with the Body Computer and the other electronic units to provide the customer with a set of functions, namely: - automatic deactivation 20 minutes after Key-OFF to safeguard the battery; - control of dimmed radio display lighting with the side lights on; - vehicle speed dependent volume control (SVC); - steering wheel controls (where applicable) The radio is available in two different versions according to customer needs and may be fitted with a conventional CD or a MP3 (compressed file) CD player. The radio is equipped with a safety system with a four-figure identification code on a card given to the customer at the time the vehicle is collected with a radio fitted as part of its original equipment. The above code should be entered whenever the battery is disconnected to prevent its reuse on another vehicle. It is also possible to fit a multi-polar cable connecting the radio to a CD changer located in the glove compartment on the passenger side. This configuration includes wiring for a mobile phone with handsfree kit. Some versions are equipped with radio controls on the steering wheel (6 key version): these make it possible to replicate some of the commands which are acquired as analogue signals by the radio. The following functions are present: - CD track or radio station change/present (forward); - CD track or radio station change/present (back); - SCR (change source); - VOL+ (increase volume); - VOL- (decrease volume); - MUTE. For more details, See descriptions 5570 ACCESSORIES

Radio P020 is supplied directly (pin 4 of connector A) from the battery via the line of fuse F23 of the engine compartment junction unit B001 . Pins 1 and 3 of connector A are served by the CAN network that connects the radio to the Body Computer M001 (pins 24 and 25 of connector H) and to the other system nodes. Pin 8 of connector A is earthed. Radio P020 is connected via the CAN network to the radio controls on the steering wheel integral with steering wheel control unit M093 - pins 1 and 5 - via clock spring junction D047 (pins 3 and 4). The aerial P25 is connected to the radio by means of the special coaxial cable. Connector B of P020 requires connection to the speakers: - pins 3 and 4 to driver side front speakers P035 (mid-woofer) and P045 (tweeter); - pins 5 and 6 to passenger side front speakers P036 (mid-woofer) and P046 (tweeter); - pins 7 and 8 to the left rear speaker P040, - pins 1 and 2 to the right rear speaker P041. The connection lead to CD-Changer P075 leaves connector E. The connection leads to the telephone wirin leave connector D. See E3580 PREPARATION FOR CELLULAR TELEPHONE

The vehicle may be equipped with a radio system with a HI FI acoustic system composed of: - radio; - wiring (speakers and radio); - speakers in the mirror triangle (tweeters); - speakers in the front doors (mid-woofers); - speakers in the rear door panel (tweeters); - speakers in the rear doors (mid-woofers); - audio amplifier with sub-woofer speaker located in the boot on the right hand side; - AM/FM aerial coaxial cable; - aerial mounting and stem. With this acoustic system, the operation of the speakers (tweeter and mid-woofers) is managed directly by the amplifier/sub-woofer system to produce excellent sound in all areas of the passenger compartment. In this configuration the radio is a CAN node through which information is exchanged with the Body Computer and the other electronic units, providing the customer with a series of functions, including: - automatic switching off 20 minutes after the key off to protect the battery; - control of the dimmed lighting in the radio display with the side lights on; - volume control dependent on the vehicle speed (SVC); - controls on the steering wheel (where fitted). The radio, available in two different versions depending on customer requirements, can have a traditional CD player or CD MP3 player (compressed files). The radio has a security system with a four digit identification code on a card that is handed over to the customer when the vehicle is received when there is a factory-fitted radio. The above code should be entered every time the battery is disconnected to prevent it being reused on another vehicle. It is also possible to fit a multi-polar cable connecting the radio to a CD changer located in the oddments pocket on the passenger side. This configuration involves preparation for a mobile phone with hands-free kit. Some versions are equipped with controls on the steering wheel (6 button version): these make it possible to replicate some of the commands which are acquired in the same way by the actual radio. The functions are: - change/preset CD track or radio station (forwards); - change/preset CD track or radio station (backwards); - SCR (switch listening source); - VOL+ (increase volume); - VOL- (decrease volume); - MUTE. For more details, See descriptions 5570 ACCESSORIES

The radio P20 is supplied directly (4 of connector A) from the battery via the line protected by fuse F23 of the engine compartment junction unit B001 . Pins 1 and 3 of connector A are served by the CAN that connects the radio to the Body Computer M001 (pins 24 and 25 of connector H) and to the other system nodes. Pin 8 of connector A is earthed. The radio P020 is connected, via the CAN, to the radio controls on the steering wheel in the steering wheel control unit M093 - pins 1 and 5 - via the clock spring D047 (pins 3 and 4). The aerial P025 is connected to the radio by means of the special coaxial cable. The amplifier P070 is supplied directly by the battery, at pin C8, by the line protected by fuse F54 of the luggage compartment junction unit B045. Pin C1 is earthed. The radio P020 and the amplifier P070 are connected as follows: - from pins 5 and 6 of connector B of P020 to pins C7 and B7 of P070 to manage - pins A6 and A7 - the driver's front speakers P035 (mid-woofers) and P045 (tweeters); - from pins 3 and 4 of connector B of P020 to pins C6 and B6 of P070 to manage - pins A4 and A5 - the passenger side front speakers P036 (mid-woofer) and P046 (tweeter); - from pins 7 and 8 of connector B of P020 to pins C5 and B5 of P070 to manage - pins A2 and A3 - the left rear speakers P040 (mid-woofer) and P047(tweeter); - from pins 1 and 2 of connector B of P020 to pins C4 and B4 of P070 to manage - pins B2 and B3 - the right rear speakers P041 (mid-woofer) and P048(tweeter); - from pin 6 of connector C of P020 to pin C2 of P070 for the enablement signal to switch on the amplifier; - from pin 2 of connector A of P020 to pin C3 of P070 for the signal for the recognition of the actual amplifier; The rear sub-woofer P049 is housed inside the amplifier P070. The connecting cables for the CD-Changer P075 come out of connector E of P020. The connecting cables for the preparation for the telephone come out of connector D. See E3580 PREPARATION FOR CELLULAR TELEPHONE

In the specification with integrated radio-phone-navigation system “Connect Nav+”, the phone (GSM module and SIM-CARD reader) is integral with the unit. The system includes: - GSM module and SIM-CARD reader integrated in the radio-phone-navigation system; - handsfree function via the radio speakers; - microphone located in the front courtesy light; - external aerial. The integated radio-telephone-navigation system is a node in the CAN network, via which it exchanges information with the Body Computer and the other electronic control units. The controls are shown on the integrated radio-telephone-navigation system display. On versions with more accessories, the steering wheel controls are in an "8+3" key configuration: these control the radio and also allow controls to be sent for the telephone function (access the phonebook, make or reject a phone call). A "Voice Recognition" function is also available. this takes the form of a voice recognition module that acquires commands from the microphone and interprets them before sending them to the phone unit. The aerial mount with rod is fitted on the rear of the roof: it includes three cables (triple function aerial). One is for the radio, one is the phone cable and one is for the navigation system. To sum up, the functions included are Radio, GSM, GPS. See E4090 NAVIGATOR For more details on telephone operation, See descriptions 5570 ACCESSORIES

The integrated radio-phone-navigation system P020 is supplied directly- pin 7 of connector A - from the battery via a line protected by fuse F23 of engine compartment junction unit B001. Pin 4 of connector A of the integrated radio-telephone-navigation system P020 receives an ignition-operated supply (INT from the steering lock control unit) via a line protected by fuse F49 of underfacia junction unit B002. Pins 1 and 3 if connector A are linked to the CAN network, which connects the integrated radio-telephone-navigation system P020 to Body Computer M001 (pins 24 and 25 of connector H) and the other system nodes. Pin 8 of connector A and pin 12 of connector F are earthed. Steering wheel node control unit M093 supplies signals relating to the steering wheel controls vai the CAN network through clock spring junction D047 (pins 3 and 4). The GSM aerial is connected to the phone function via a coaxial cable that is not the same as the cable used for the radio function and the navigation system function (GPS). Pins 9 and 18 of connector F are connected to the microphone via handsfree unit P026. Cables leave connector B, pin 2 of connector A and pin 6 of connector C of P020 to connect to the radio HI-FI amplifier P070 that manages the speakers for the handsfree function. See E3510 RADIO

The vehicle is available, on request, with wiring for installing a cell phone. The system includes: - connection for connecting a cell phone with, as an option, hands-free function via the radio speakers; - external GSM aerial. the microphone to complement the hands-free function is not included because it comes with the kit for connecting the telephone and should be positioned freely. The connection for the telephone, located at the base of the centre console, includes all the power supplies and signals needed for the operation of the telephone. As an option, steering wheel controls are available with a 6-key configuration: these are used to send out radio and also phone commands. the aerial mount and rod is fitted on the rear of the roof: it includes two cables (dual-function aerial). One is for the radio aerial, the other is the phone cable. To sum up, the functions provided are Radio and GSM. The radio receives input audio signals from the telephone connection; the telephone sound is always received at a fixed volume which can, however, be adjusted in the radio menu function. The operation of the telephone switches off the radio temporarily (MUTE function). The phone connection has two power supplies: one direct with key turned ON in the ignition. the above two lines are protected by two fuses in the junction unit under the dashboard; there is also a power supply with the side lights on (lights +) to light up the telephone, if fitted.

The radio phone wiring junction D099 receives a direct power supply - pin 9 - from the battery via a line protected by fuse F39 of under-facia control unit B002. The control unit also receives a supply controlled by the ignition (INT from steering lock control unit) at pin 7 via the line protected by fuse F49 of the junction unit under the dashboard B002. Pins 1 and 3 of connector A of P020 are served by the CAN network that connects the radio to the Body Computer M001 (pins 24 and 25 of connector H) and to the other system nodes. Pin 8 of connector A is earthed. Steering wheel node control unit M093 supplies steering wheel control signals, where appropriate, via the CAN network thorough the junction of clock spring D047 (pins 3 and 4). Pin 8 receives the power supply with the side lights on from the Body Computer M1, pin 18 of connector H: the telephone, if fitted, is lit up like the other controls See E2530 INSTRUMENT LIGHTING Pin 10 of junction D099 receives an analogue earth signal from P020 (pin 12 of connector D). Pins 4 and 3 of D099 provide the audio signal (+ and - respectively) for the radio P020 - pins 7 and 8 of connector D, which then controls the speakers. See E3510 RADIO Pin 1 of D099 is also connected to radio P020 - pin 9 of connector D - for the TEL MUTE function.

The panel is installed behind the steering wheel. Its position guarantees maximum visibility/legibility of the information for the driver in all vehicle usage conditions (day/night) without reflections, distortions or double images. The control panel is available in Comfort version and contains: - electronic speedometer - electronic rev counter - coolant temperature gauge with overheating warning light - fuel level gauge with reserve warning light; - warning lights The instrument panel is a CAN node through which information is exchanged with the Body Computer and with the other electronic units. Speedometer: its function allows the vehicle speed to be displayed on the instrument panel. This information is obtained from the ABS control unit via the Body Computer. Rev counter: this function involves the display on the instrument panel of the engine rotation speed by means of the message sent via the CAN from the engine management control unit. Milometer: this function includes the display and storage of the mileometer and trip counter. Mileage information is processed by the Body Computer. A button on the panel zeros the trip counter by means of a counter. Fuel level: the Body Computer receives the signal from the sensor integrated in the pump assembly inside the fuel tank and processes it to guarantee suitable filtering/damping for the panel gauge, also managing the reserve warning light. Engine coolant temperature: this function involves the display of the engine coolant temperature in the instrument panel and the overheating warning light coming on by means of messages sent via the CAN from the engine management control unit. The temperature reading is always guaranteed, even in extreme operating conditions. At every key on the engine coolant overheating warning is checked by a continuous control signal via the dedicated red warning light. Engine oil pressure sensor: this function involves the display on the instrument panel of the engine oil pressure warning light by means of the message sent via the CAN from the engine management control unit. Hanbrake applied: the warning light for the handbrake status is controlled by a specific switch; in addition, if a given speed level is exceeded in conjunction with this signal, a warning signal is activated: Insufficient brake fluid level this function involves the "insufficient brake fluid level" warning light in the instrument panel coming on with the signal sent by the Body Computer via the CAN. The switch is normally closed when brake fluid level is maximum. The ON/OFF switch is monitored only when the key is inserted and turned ON. When brake fluid level is low, the contact closes or opens to send an earth signal to the body computer. General failure signal (check): The Body Computer contains a function that monitors a set of systems and components and turns on a warning light if a fault is detected. The following systems are monitored: - TMPS (system fault and tyre signals) See E7060 TYRE INFLATION PRESSURE CONTROL SYSTEM - Inertia switch operation See E3040 CENTRAL LOCKING See E5030 PETROL ENGINES ELECTRONIC MANAGEMENT See E5050 DIESEL ENGINES ELECTRONIC MANAGEMENT - Engine oil pressure sensor failure See E5030 PETROL ENGINES ELECTRONIC MANAGEMENT See E5050 DIESEL ENGINES ELECTRONIC MANAGEMENT - Rain sensor fault (automatic windscreen wiper mechanism not available) See E3020 WINDSCREEN WASH/WIPE - Dusk sensor failure See E2010 SIDE LIGHTS / NO. PLATE LIGHTS See E2011 DIPPED HEADLAMPS - Parking sensor failure See E3090 PARKING SENSOR - Window antipinch system failure See E3050 ELECTRIC FRONT WINDOWS See E3051 ELECTRIC REAR WINDOWS - Pollution filter blocked signal See E5070 FAP PARTICLE FILTER SYSTEM Light failure signal: The Body Computer contains a function that monitors a set of systems and components and turns on a warning light if a fault is detected. The following systems are monitored: - side light, number plate light, rear fog lamp, direction indicator, brake light faults See E2010 SIDE LIGHTS / NO. PLATE LIGHTS See E2020 DIRECTION INDICATORS / HAZARD WARNING LIGHTS See E2021 BRAKE LIGHTS See E2031 REAR FOG LAMPS - Brake lights fuse failure See E2021 BRAKE LIGHTS For more details, See descriptions 5560 INSTRUMENTS The operation of the warning lights which do not come under any other functions is illustrated below: the other warning lights are described and illustrated in the diagrams for the components to which they refer

The ignition-operated power supply (INT) for the instrument panel E050 reaches pin 1 of connector A via the line for fuse F37 of the junction unit under the dashboard B002; the direct power supply reaches pin 2 of connector A via the fuse line F53 of the junction unit under the dashboard B002; pin 7 of connector A is earthed (earth controlled by the Body Computer M001, pin 36 of connector G). The instrument panel E050 is connected from pins 3 and 4 of connector A with the Body Computer M001 and via the latter to the entire CAN: The signal for the electronic speedometer (from brake system control unit M051) arrives via the CAN network. The same signal is replicated by pin 16 of M051 at pin 7 of connector A of Body Computer M001. The electronic rev counter receives the engine rpm signal received from the engine management control unit M010 via the CAN. The fuel level gauge is controlled by means of signals coming from the level gauge located in the fuel pump assembly N040 - at pins 4 (positive) and 15 (negative) of connector D of the Body Computer M001 and from there via the CAN to the instrument panel E050. The insufficient brake fluid level/handbrake warning light is lit up by a signal from the handbrake switch I040 that reaches pin 14 of connector D of the Body Computer M001 or from the signal from the brake fluid level sensor K025 that reaches pin 18 of connector A of M001. All these signals are transferred via the CAN to the instrument panel E050. Instrument panel E050 also contains electronic modules which control the adjustment of the brightness of the actual panel and the other controls See E2530 INSTRUMENT LIGHTING The TRIP function is illustrated in the relevant diagram See E4080 TRIP COMPUTER Instrument panel E050 also contains electronic modules that control the headlamp alignment adjustment. See E3080 HEADLAMP AGLINMENT CORRECTOR Instrument panel E050 also contains a warning buzzer. One of its functions is to emit parking sensor signals. See E3090 PARKING SENSOR

A road map navigation system reveals the vehicle's position on a map (showing town streets and main roads/motorways) at every moment and pinpoints it on the Connect Nav+ display. In this way the driver is guided to the required destination step by step by means of voice messages and visual information. The system also provides additional information for reaching general services, namely: hotels, carparks, restaurants, chemists, service stations, hospitals, FIAT service outlets, railway stations, airports etc. The navigation system uses GPS (Global Positioning System) satellite localisation technology and is fitted, when ordered, in the integrated radio-phone-navigation system known as CONNECT NAV+ The navigation CD-ROM drive is located in the unit. the navigation system only works with the CD-ROM inserted in the special drive; it is therefore possible to listen to a music CD during navigation. In this case, the navigation function requires the map CD to be inserted whilst carrying out the route calculation procedures. As an option, it is also possible to combine the navigation system with a music audio system by fitting a CD-CHANGER in the glove compartment. The GPS consists of an aerial that allows the vehicle to be GPS satellite-located: The aerial is connected to a receiver located in the integrated unit by means of a special shielded cable. the aerial mount and rod is fitted on the rear of the roof. It includes three cables (triple function aerial): one for the radio function, one for the phone function (GSM) and one for the navigation system (GPS). The position of the vehicle is identified through the analysis of the GPS data and the speedometer and reverse gear signals which come from the vehicle nodes. This position is shown by the display together with the topographical features of the area memorized in the map CD. The navigation system also generates a voice synthesis signal that allows the driver to hear driving instructions through an audio circuit. The radio-phone-navigation unti is a node of the CAN network via which information is exchanged with the Body Computer and the other electronic units (e.g. the navigation system downloads information from the odometer, reverse engagement signal etc.) For more details on the subject, See descriptions 5580 SPECIAL ACCESSORIES

The "CONNECT NAV+" system (integrated radio-phone-navigation system unit) P020 is supplied directly - pin 7 of connector A - from the battery via a line protected by fuse F23 of under-facia junction unit B001. Pin 4 of connector A, integrated radio-phone-navigation system P020 is supplied with an ignition-controlled supply (INT from the steering lock control unit) via a line protected by fuse F49 of underfacia control unit B002. Pins 1 and 3 of connector A are served by the CAN network that connects the integrated radio-phone-navigation system to the Body Computer M001 (pins 24 and 25 of connector H) and to the other system nodes. In this way, the navigation system module in the CONNECT NAV+ receives information used by the function, namely: speedometer, reverse, fuel consumption signal etc. Pin 8 of connector A of P020 is earthed. Steering wheel node control unit M093 supplies steering wheel control signals via the CAN network thorough the junction of clock spring D047 (pins 3 and 4). Connection cables leave connector B, pin 2 of connector A and pin 6 of connector C of P020 for connection to HI-FI radio amplifier P070, which controls the speakers that emit the voice messages. See E3510 RADIO Aerial P025 containing the GPS reception device is connected to the navigation system module by means of a special coaxial cable. It also includes a cable for the radio function and a cable for the phone function (GSM). The Cd Changer module P075 is supplied directly at pin 15 by the integrated radio-telephone-navigation system control unit P020 via which it is also operated. The follow cables lealve P020 connector E: - pin 13: Reception serial line from the Cd changer; - pin 14: Transmission serial line to the Cd changer; - pin 15: Supply (+30) to the Cd changer; - pin 16: Cd changer supply enablement; - pin 17: Gnd for the Cd changer; - pin 18: Cd changer audio reference; - pin 19: Cd changer left audio; - pin 20: Cd changer right audio; The connection cables for the integrated radio telephone function leave connector F of P020. See E3570 INTEGRATED RADIO PHONE

The ignition and recharging circuit comprises the battery, starter motor and alternator. The starter motor consists of a d.c. motor supplied by the battery and an excitation electromagnet. The starting system on this vehicle, unlike classical solutions adopted previously, is distinguished by the use of an ignition device (TEG Reader) combined with the steering lock control unit (NBS). Depending on the position of the key (TEG) inside the starting device, the steering lock control unit determines:f the enablement request for the +15 supply to the Body Computer (ON position), the +50 starting for vehicle (START position) and, if the result is positive, the power distribution to the vehicle and to the various load (INT, INT/A,15/54). The starting system involves that together with the rotation of the key to the START position the clutch pedal (or in recovery conditions, the brake pedal) for versions with a manual gearbox or the brake pedal for versions with automatic transmission, is pressed. On versions with automatic transmission the additional condition of the gear lever in P (PARK) must be observed. Therefore when the steering lock control unit is in the condition to provide the +50 power supply for the starter mtor, the motor windings are suplied, producing the electromagnetic forces that rotate the motor pinion. This simultaneously activates the electromagnet that operates the mechanism that causes the pinion to mesh with the flywheel ring gear and thus turn the crankshaft. The alternator recharges the battery during normal engine rotation. The alternator shaft (rotor) is turned by the crankshaft via a belt. When supplied by an excitation current, the rotor generates a magnetic field that sets up an alternating current in the fixed winding (stator). A diode rectifier bridge allows the alternating current to be transferred into a direct current that is sent to recharge the battery. A voltage governor, also built into the alternator, maintains the power supply at a constant voltage (about 14 V) throughout the load variation and engine speed ranges. For further details, See descriptions 5520 ENGINE STARTING The efficiency of the recharging system is controlled by the Body Computer which measures the D+ signal coming from the alternator with the engine moving (engine revs above 700 rpm). If a fault is detected, the warning light in the instrument panel is lit up. The Body Computer also acquires the battery voltage value in the range 6 - 18 V depending on a control logic known as SBMT. The information, transmitted on the CAN to the door nodes, involves the exclusion of certain services after a timed delay of 15 minutes. For example, See E2520 GLOVE COMPARTMENT LIGHT - LUGGAGE COMPARTMENT LIGHT - SUN VISOR LIGHT

The ignition device H003 receives a supply from the direct battery line protected by fuse F32 of the junction unit under the dashboard B002. The steering lock control unit M089 provides a power supply from the direct battery line protected by fuse F3 of the engine compartment junction unit B001 - pin C1 and, depending on the rotation of the key in the ignition device H003, receives the following signals: - at pin A6, the key inserted signal (TEG_IN); - at pin B5, the key turned to ON signal (TEG_MAR); - at pin C5, the first starting signal with the key turned to START (TEG_Crank1); - at pin C6, the second starting signal with the key turned to START (TEG_Crank2); The ignition device H003 - pins 1 and 2 - communicates, via the CAN, with the Body Computer M001 - pins 24 and 25 of connector H - whether or not the TEG inserted in the reader is recognized. In the same way, control unit M089 - pins A2 and A3 of M089, with the ignition ON, notify the Body Computer of the request to send the system the +15. Once the TEG is recognized (immobilizer function) and allows the distribution of the power lines (INT, INT/A, 15/54) the steering lock control unit M089 is enabled for the starting stage. At pin A5 the steering lock control unit M089 receives the earth signal for the clutch pedal I031 pressure. Turning the key at the same time to START, from pin B8, the steering lock control unit M089 sends the +50 signal to the starter motor A020 solenoid winding (pin 50, connector C). Pin 30 (connector A) of A020, the actual motor, receives a power supply with the voltage coming from the battery A001. On this engine type there is an automatic battery disconnection relay in series to the postive battery terminal located in the maxifuse box on the battery. This relay allows the supply for the starter motor to be interrupted (together with the starting/recharging system) when the inertia switch I050 is activated (pin 2, NA contact) with the earth signal. The continuous current produced by the alternator A010 (pin B+, connector B) is sent to the battery A001, passing through the starter motor A020 (pin 30, connector B). When the alternator A010 is not turning and therefore not recharging the battery, an earth signal is sent from pin D+ (connector A) to the Body Computer M001 - pin 19 of connector A: the latter, connected via the CAN to the instrument panel E050, determines the switching on of the alternator recharging warning light in the panel.

The ignition and recharging circuit comprises the battery, starter motor and alternator. The starter motor consists of a d.c. motor supplied by the battery and an excitation electromagnet. The ignition system adopted for this vehicle differs from the classic products used previously in the application of an ignition device (TEG Reader) combined with the steering lock control unit (NBS). According to the position assumed by the key (TEG) inside the ignition device, the steering lock control unit determines: +15 power supply enablement request to the Body Computer (ON position) and vehicle ignition +50 (START position). If this is successful, it then determines power distribution to the vehicle and the various loads (INT, INT/A, 15/54). During start-up, when the key is turned to START, the clutch pedal must be pressed simultaneously (or the brake pedal in recovery mode) on vehicles with a manual gearbox - or the brake pedal on versions with an automatic transmission. On versions with an automatic transmission, the transmission lever must be in position P (PARK) as an additional requirement. When the steering lock is able to supply a +50 power supply to the starter motor, the motor coils are supplied with power to generate the electromagnetic forces that turn the motor pinion. This simultaneously activates the electromagnet that operates the mechanism that causes the pinion to mesh with the flywheel ring gear and thus turn the crankshaft. The alternator recharges the battery during normal engine rotation. The alternator shaft (rotor) is turned by the crankshaft via a belt. When supplied by an excitation current, the rotor generates a magnetic field that sets up an alternating current in the fixed winding (stator). A rectifying diode bridge on the back of the alternator allows the alternating current to be rectified to a direct current that is sent to recharge the battery. A voltage governor, also built into the alternator, maintains the power supply at a constant voltage (14 V) throughout the load variation and engine speed ranges. For further details, See descriptions 5520 ENGINE STARTING Recharging system efficiency is controlled by the Body Computer, which receives and measures the D+ signal from the alternator with the engine running (engine speed above 700 rpm). If a fault is detected, the warning light in the instrument panel is lit up. The Body Computer also acquires a battery voltage value in the range 6 - 18 V according to a control strategy known as SBMT. The information is sent via the CAN network to the door nodes and cuts out certain services after a time of 15 minutes. For example, See E2520 GLOVE COMPARTMENT LIGHT - LUGGAGE COMPARTMENT LIGHT - SUN VISOR LIGHT

Ignition device H003 is supplied by a direct battery line protected by fuse F32 of underfacia control unit B002. Steering lock control unit M089 supplied by a direct battery line protected by fuse F3 of engine compartment junction unit B001 - pin C1 - receives the following signals according to whether or not the key is turned in ignition H003: - at pin A6, key inserted signal (TEG_IN); - at pin B5, key turned ON (TEG_MAR); - at pin C5, the first ignition signal with key turned to START (TEG_Crank1); - at pin C6, the second ignition signal with key turned to START (TEG_Crank2); Ignition device H003 - pins 1 and 2 - communicates via the CAN network with Body Computer M001 - pins 24 and 25 of H - whether or not the TEG has been recognised when it is inserted in the reader.. In the same way, control unit M089 - pins A2 and A3 - of M089 communicates the request to forward the +15 to the system to Body Computer when the key is ON. Once the TEG is recognised (Immobilizer function) and distribution of the power lines (INT, INT/A, 15/54) is permitted, steering lock control unit M089 is enabled for start-up. The correct transmision lever position signal (PARK) is sent by the solenoid unit on automatic transmission L050 to pin B4 of steering lock control unit M089. The ignition and recharging circuit comprises the battery, starter motor and alternator. The starter motor consists of a d.c. motor supplied by the battery and an excitation electromagnet. The starting system on this vehicle, unlike classical solutions adopted previously, is distinguished by the use of an ignition device (TEG Reader) combined with the steering lock control unit (NBS). Depending on the position of the key (TEG) inside the starting device, the steering lock control unit determines:f the enablement request for the +15 supply to the Body Computer (ON position), the +50 starting for vehicle (START position) and, if the result is positive, the power distribution to the vehicle and to the various load (INT, INT/A,15/54). The starting system involves that together with the rotation of the key to the START position the clutch pedal (or in recovery conditions, the brake pedal) for versions with a manual gearbox or the brake pedal for versions with automatic transmission, is pressed. On versions with automatic transmission the additional condition of the gear lever in P (PARK) must be observed. Therefore when the steering lock control unit is in the condition to provide the +50 power supply for the starter mtor, the motor windings are suplied, producing the electromagnetic forces that rotate the motor pinion. This simultaneously activates the electromagnet that operates the mechanism that causes the pinion to mesh with the flywheel ring gear and thus turn the crankshaft. The alternator recharges the battery during normal engine rotation. The alternator shaft (rotor) is turned by the crankshaft via a belt. When supplied by an excitation current, the rotor generates a magnetic field that sets up an alternating current in the fixed winding (stator). A diode rectifier bridge allows the alternating current to be transferred into a direct current that is sent to recharge the battery. A voltage governor, also built into the alternator, maintains the power supply at a constant voltage (about 14 V) throughout the load variation and engine speed ranges. For further details, See descriptions 5520 ENGINE STARTING The efficiency of the recharging system is controlled by the Body Computer which measures the D+ signal coming from the alternator with the engine moving (engine revs above 700 rpm). If a fault is detected, the warning light in the instrument panel is lit up. The Body Computer also acquires the battery voltage value in the range 6 - 18 V depending on a control logic known as SBMT. The information, transmitted on the CAN to the door nodes, involves the exclusion of certain services after a timed delay of 15 minutes. For example, See E2520 GLOVE COMPARTMENT LIGHT - LUGGAGE COMPARTMENT LIGHT - SUN VISOR LIGHT

The ignition device H003 receives a supply from the direct battery line protected by fuse F32 of the junction unit under the dashboard B002. The engine radiator and air conditioner condenser cooling system consists of a radiator prewired system interfaced with the engine service lead, including relay boxes, resistors and on fan operated at three different speeds according to the engine coolant temperature and air conditioner coolant pressure levels. The temperature sensor on the thermostat and the electrical coil controlled by the engine control unit for advance opening of the thermostat and a temperature sensor on the radiator outlet sleeve are interfaced with the engine prewiring. The engine control unit receives signals managed by sensors (temperature sensor on the thermostat, radiator output temperature sensor and linear sensor), which inform the engine control of the cooling circuit status. Based on internal sensor rules, which are also linked to other parameters, namely: engine rpm, load conditions, gear engaged and outdoor temperature, the engine control excites or deactivates the electrical coil on the thermostat for advance opening of the thermostat and, if necessary, manages fan activation. The supply line for the fan is protected by a special fuse, located in the engine compartment control unit.

Activation of the engine cooling fan integral with radiator prewiring N011 is managed by signals from engine control unit M010: - fan activation level 1 - pin 1 of N011 -, from pin 59 of connector A of M010; - fan activation level 2 - pin 4 of N011 -, from pin 10 of connector A of M010; - fan activation level 3 - pin 7 of N011 -, from pin 61 of connector A of M010; Radiator unit N011 receives a power supply (direct from the battery) via fuse F7 located in engine compartment control unit B001 (pin 5 of N011): Pin 2 of H011 is connected to earth C045. Engine coolant sensor on radiator sleeve K036 receives a reference earth and sends a temperature signal to engine control unit M010, to pins 3 and 28 of connector B respectively. Engine coolant temperature sensor on thermostat K036 receives a reference earth and sends a temperature signal to engine control unit M010, to pins 25 and 60 of connector B respectively. Linear sensor K120 receives a power supply and reference earth from pins 42 and 14 of connector B of M010 respectively and sends a pressure signal to pin 56 of connector A of M010.

An electronic control system supervises and governs all engine parameters to optimise performance and fuel consumption by means of a real-time response to different service conditions. The system is managed by a single control unit which MULTIPOINT phased sequential injection. Depending on the signals received from numerous sensors, the control unit controls the injectors connected to it managing the following systems: - fuel supply; - air supply; - accelerator pedal; - engine cooling; - control of combustion - Lambda sensors; - control of exhaust with catalytic silencer. - fuel vapour recirculation. The motorised drive by wire throttle body is also controlled electrically by the control unit: throttle opening is calculated in accordance with specific software mapped inside the engine control unit. This system does away with the need for a mechanical link between accelerator pedal and throttle body. Engine ignition is managed by the engine control unit, but the function is implemented by the ignition module (DIS). The electronic management system described above ensures that this engine meets the very latest EOBD (European On Board Diagnogis) system emission control and monitoring requirements. This system allows continous diagnosis of emission-related car components and notifies the driver if any of the components should deteriorate by turning on a warning light in the instrument panel. For more details, See descriptions 1056 PETROL INJECTION SYSTEM The system is also controlled by dedicated relays in the engine bay control unit. Lines supplying the control unit and various system components (sensors and actuators) are protected by dedicated fuses that are also located inside the engine bay.

Engine management control unit M010 controls and governs the entire electronic ignition and injection system. The control unit M10 is supplied directly by the battery at pin 20 of connector A via a line protected by fuse F18 of the engine compartment junction unit B001 he ignition-operated power supply (15/54 from the steering lock control unit) is received from a line protected by fuse F16 of B001 at pin 19 of connector A. Main injection relay T9 of B001 controls the entire system: t is energized by an earth signal from pin 1 of connector A of engine control unit M010 and then forwards a power supply: - to injectors N070 and ignition module A031 - pin A - with interference filter P087 - through a line protected by fuse F22 of B001; - to vapour recovery solenoid L010, to the lambda sensors on the catalyic converter K017 and K018 and to the air flow meter K041, via a line protected by fuse F11 of B001; - to pins 48, 64 of connector A of control unit M010, via the line protected by fuse F17 of B001; Fuel pump relay T10 of B001 is supplied by the line of fuse F21 of B001. It is energized by a control signal coming from pin 51 of connector A of control unit M010 and provides the power supply for the electric fuel pump N040 which is earthed via the inertia switch I50 which interrupts the circuit in the case of an impact and stops the dangerous outflow of fuel. The NO contact of I050 is connected to the maxifuse control unit on the battery B099 to cut off the vehicle electrical supply in the event of impact. See E5010 STARTING AND RECHARING Control unit M010 receives signals from the various sensors in order to control all engine service parameters. Engine coolant sensor/sender unit K036 receives a reference earth from pin 38 of connector B of control unit M010 and sends a signal proportional to engine coolant temperature to pin 8 of connector B of the control unit. The detonation sensor K050 provides information, by means of frequency signals, concerning the onset of detonation in the combustion chamber: it receives a reference earth from pin 4 of connector B of M010 and sends the respective signal to pin 37 of control unit connector B. These signals are shielded. Engine rpm sensor K046 supplies information on engine speed and crankshaft angular position via a frequency signal sent to pins 23 (negative) and 26 (positive) of connector B: these two signals are very low intensity and are thus appropriately shielded. Absolute pressure sensor K048 erceives a positive and negative signal from pins 32 and 42 of connector B of control unit M010 and sends the corresponding signal to pin 12 of connector B of M010. The control unit M10 receives - at pin 15 of connector B - a signal from the minimum engine oil pressure sensor K30. Pin 54 of connector A of control unit M010 receives a signal from engine oil level sensor K032. Air flow meter (debimeter) K041 sends pin 29 of connector B a signal proportional to the air flow. K041 also contains an air temperature sensor: a reference earth is provided by pin 58 of connector B of M010, while pin 10 of connector B receives an air temperature signal. The Lambda sensor upstream of the catalyzer K017 and the one downstream K018 provide the control unit M010 with information concerning the correct composition of the air/fuel mixture. The sensor on the preconverter K017 sends a signal to pin 5 of connector B of M010, while pin 6 provides a reference earth. The sensor is heated by a coil to ensure correct operation even when cold, via an earth signal from pin 57 of connector B of M010. The sensor on the preconverter K018 sends a signal to pin 7 of connector B of M010, while pin 19 provides a reference earth. The sensor is heated by a coil to ensure correct operation even when cold, via an earth signal from pin 62 of connector B of M010. Fuel vapour recovery solenoid L010 allows fuel vapours to flow through toward the engine intake, where they join the mixture that is entering the combustion chamber. Valve L010 is opened by the control unit when the motor is loaded via an earth signal from pin 17 of connector B of M010. Accelerator pedal K055 is equipped with two built-in potentiometers: a main potentiometer and a stand-by potentiometer. The former receives power and earth signals from pins 29 and 34 of connector A and sends a correspondong signal to pin 12 of the same connector of M010. The latter receives power and earth signals from pins 50 and 44 of connector A of M010 and sends a corresponding signal to pin 13 of the same connector. According to the signal from accelerator pedal K055, control unit M010 controls the throttle opening by means of a motor built into throttle body N075. Pins 47 and 64 of connector B of M010 control closure of the motorised throttle while pins 46 and 63 of the same connector control closure. Throttle body actuator N075 is equipped with two integral potentiometers: a main potentiometer and a stand-by potentiometer. The former receives power and earth signals from pins 30 and 34 of connector B and sends a correspondong signal to pin 28 of the same connector of M010. The latter receives power and earth signals from pins 31 and 35 of connector B of M010 and sends a corresponding signal to pin 25 of the same connector. Ignition module A031 - pin F - sends pin 18 of connector B of control unit M010 engine timing information to replace the typical timing sensor function. Engine management unit M010 controls the opening of individual injectors N070, via appropriate signals (duty-cycle type) sent from pins 33 (cyl.1), 49 (cyl.2), 51 (cyl.3), 50 (cyl.4) of connector B. Injectors N070 receive a supply to enable excitation of main relay T9 of B001. Ignition module A031 contains 2 coils that supply cylinders 1-4 and 2-3 respectively via command signals received - pins B and G - from pins 27 and 13 of connector B of M010. Pin E is earthed. Pin 38 of connector A of control unit M010 receives an NO signal from the switch on brake pedal I030, supplied by an ignition-controlled supply (INT from the steering lock control unit) via a line protected by fuse F37 of junction unit B002. Pin 27 of connector A of control unit M010 receives an NC signal from the switch on brake pedal I030, also supplied by an ignition-controlled supply (INT from the steering lock control unit) via a line protected by fuse F35 of junction unit B002. Pin 22 of connector A of M010 receives a signal (earth) from clutch pedal switch I031. Control unit M010 then connects via the CAN network - pins 5, 6 and 37, 39 - to Body Computer M001 - pins 36 and 37 of connector B - and to the other network nodes. Via this connection, it sends information on: - coolant temperature, which is sent to instrument panel E50 that controls the gauge and warning light; - engine rpm, that is sent to the rev counter on instrument panel E50; - minimum engine oil pressure, which is sent to instrument panel E50 that controls the warning light. Control unit M010 receives a speedometer signal generated by the ESP control unit M051 via the CAN network. The control unit self-diagnostic system M10 also generates a negative signal that leaves pin 24 of connector A - that is connected directly to the EOBD warning light located in instrument panel E050 . The check function within instrument panel E050 monitors the operation of the inertia switch and checks for faults in the oil pressure sensor: If faults are detected, the general failure warning light is turned on and the information is shown simultaneously on the display. The control unit autodiagnostic data can be read by connecting to connector C of M001, pin 7: it receives signals from pin 59 of connector A of M051 via the special diagnostic K line.

An electronic control system supervises and governs all engine parameters to optimise performance and fuel consumption by means of a real-time response to different service conditions. The system is managed by a single control unit which controls the phased, sequential MULTIPOINT injection. Depending on the signals received from numerous sensors, the control unit controls the injectors connected to it managing the following systems: - fuel supply; - air supply; - accelerator pedal; - engine cooling; - control of combustion - Lambda sensors; - control of exhaust with catalytic converter. - fuel vapour recirculation. The motorised Drive By Wire throttle body is also controlled electronically by the control unit: throttle opening is calculated in accordance with specific software mapped inside the engine control unit. This system does away with the need for a mechanical link between accelerator pedal and throttle body. Engine ignition is managed by the engine control unit, but the function is implemented by the ignition module (DIS). The electronic management system described above ensures that this engine meets the very latest EOBD (European On Board Diagnogis) system emission control and monitoring requirements. This system allows continous diagnosis of emission-related car components and notifies the driver if any of the components should deteriorate by turning on a warning light in the instrument panel. For more details, See descriptions 1056 PETROL INJECTION SYSTEM The system is also controlled by dedicated relays in the engine bay control unit. Lines supplying the control unit and various system components (sensors and actuators) are protected by dedicated fuses that are also located inside the engine bay.

Engine management control unit M10 controls and governs the entire electronic ignition and injection system. The control unit M10 is supplied directly by the battery at pin 20 of connector A via a line protected by fuse F18 of the engine compartment junction unit B001 The ignition-operated power supply (15/54 from the steering lock control unit) is received from a line protected by fuse F16 of B001 at pin 19 of connector A. Main injection relay T9 of B001 controls the entire system: t is energized by an earth signal from pin 1 of connector A of engine control unit M010 and then forwards a power supply: - to injectors N070 and ignition module A031 - pin A - with interference filter P087 - through a line protected by fuse F22 of B001; - to vapour recovery solenoid L010, to the lambda sensors on the catalyic converter K017 and K018 and to the air flow meter K041, via a line protected by fuse F11 of B001; - to pins 48 and 64 of connector A of control unit M010 via a line protected by fuse F17 of B001; Fuel pump relay T10 of B001 is supplied by the line protected by fuse F21 of B001. This is excited by a command signal (earth) from pin 51 of connector A of control unit M10 and supplies power to fuel pump N40 , which is earthed via inertia switch I50 , that cuts off the circuit in the case of impact and thus prevents dangerous outflows of fuel. The NO contact of I050 is connected to the maxifuse control unit on the battery B099 to cut off the vehicle electrical supply in the event of impact. See E5010 STARTING AND RECHARING Control unit M010 receives signals from the various sensors in order to control all engine service parameters. Engine coolant sensor/sender unit K036 receives a reference earth from pin 38 of connector B of control unit M010 and sends a signal proportional to engine coolant temperature to pin 8 of connector B of the control unit. The detonation sensor K050 provides information, by means of frequency signals, concerning the onset of detonation in the combustion chamber: it receives a reference earth from pin 4 of connector B of M010 and sends the respective signal to pin 37 of control unit connector B. These signals are shielded. Engine rpm sensor K046 supplies information on engine speed and crankshaft angular position via a frequency signal sent to pins 23 (negative) and 26 (positive) of connector B: these two signals are very low intensity and are thus appropriately shielded. Absolute pressure sensor K048 erceives a positive and negative signal from pins 32 and 42 of connector B of control unit M010 and sends the corresponding signal to pin 12 of connector B of M010. The control unit M10 receives - at pin 15 of connector B - a signal from the minimum engine oil pressure sensor K30. Pin 54 of connector A of control unit M010 receives a signal from engine oil level sensor K032. Air flow meter (debimeter) K041 sends pin 29 of connector B a signal proportional to the air flow. K041 also contains an air temperature sensor: a reference earth is provided by pin 58 of connector B of M010, while pin 10 of connector B receives an air temperature signal. The Lambda sensor upstream of the catalyzer K017 and the one downstream K018 provide the control unit M010 with information concerning the correct composition of the air/fuel mixture. The sensor on the preconverter K017 sends a signal to pin 5 of connector B of M010, while pin 6 provides a reference earth. The sensor is heated by a coil to ensure correct operation even when cold, via an earth signal from pin 57 of connector B of M010. The sensor on the preconverter K018 sends a signal to pin 7 of connector B of M010, while pin 19 provides a reference earth. The sensor is heated by a coil to ensure correct operation even when cold, via an earth signal from pin 62 of connector B of M010. Fuel vapour recovery solenoid L010 allows fuel vapours to flow through toward the engine intake, where they join the mixture that is entering the combustion chamber. Valve L010 is opened by the control unit when the motor is loaded via an earth signal from pin 17 of connector B of M010. Accelerator pedal K055 is equipped with two built-in potentiometers: a main potentiometer and a stand-by potentiometer. The former receives power and earth signals from pins 29 and 34 of connector A and sends a correspondong signal to pin 12 of the same connector of M010. The latter receives power and earth signals from pins 50 and 44 of connector A of M010 and sends a corresponding signal to pin 13 of the same connector. According to the signal from accelerator pedal K055, control unit M010 controls the throttle opening by means of a motor built into throttle body N075. Pins 47 and 64 of connector B of M010 control closure of the motorised throttle while pins 46 and 63 of the same connector control closure. Throttle body actuator N075 is equipped with two integral potentiometers: a main potentiometer and a stand-by potentiometer. The former receives power and earth signals from pins 30 and 34 of connector B and sends a correspondong signal to pin 28 of the same connector of M010. The latter receives power and earth signals from pins 31 and 35 of connector B of M010 and sends a corresponding signal to pin 25 of the same connector. Ignition module A031 - pin F - sends pin 18 of connector B of control unit M010 engine timing information to replace the typical timing sensor function. Engine management unit M010 controls the opening of individual injectors N070, via appropriate signals (duty-cycle type) sent from pins 33 (cyl.1), 49 (cyl.2), 51 (cyl.3), 50 (cyl.4) of connector B. Injectors N070 receive a supply to enable excitation of main relay T9 of B001. Ignition module A031 contains 2 coils that supply cylinders 1-4 and 2-3 respectively via command signals received - pins B and G - from pins 27 and 13 of connector B of M010. Pin E is earthed. Pin 38 of connector A of control unit M010 receives an NO signal from the switch on brake pedal I030, supplied by an ignition-controlled supply (INT from the steering lock control unit) via a line protected by fuse F37 of junction unit B002. Pin 27 of connector A of control unit M010 receives an NC signal from the switch on brake pedal I030, also supplied by an ignition-controlled supply (INT from the steering lock control unit) via a line protected by fuse F35 of junction unit B002. Control unit M010 then connects via the CAN network - pins 5, 6 and 37, 39 - to Body Computer M001 - pins 36 and 37 of connector B - and to the other network nodes. Via this connection, it sends information on: - coolant temperature, which is sent to instrument panel E50 that controls the gauge and warning light; - engine rpm, that is sent to the rev counter on instrument panel E50; - minimum engine oil pressure, which is sent to instrument panel E50 that controls the warning light. Control unit M010 receives a speedometer signal generated by the ESP control unit M051 via the CAN network. The control unit self-diagnostic system M10 also generates a negative signal that leaves pin 24 of connector A - that is connected directly to the EOBD warning light located in instrument panel E050 . The check function within instrument panel E050 monitors the operation of the inertia switch and checks for faults in the oil pressure sensor: If faults are detected, the general failure warning light is turned on and the information is shown simultaneously on the display. The control unit autodiagnostic data can be read by connecting to connector C of M001, pin 7: it receives signals from pin 59 of connector A of M051 via the special diagnostic K line.

An electronic control system supervises and governs all engine parameters to optimise performance and fuel consumption by means of a real-time response to different service conditions. The system is managed by a single SIMTEC 75.9 control unit which controls both the ignition and the sequential, phased injection. Depending on the signals received from numerous sensors, the control unit controls the injectors connected to it managing the following systems: - fuel supply; - air supply; - accelerator pedal; - engine cooling; - control of combustion - Lambda sensors; - control of exhaust with catalytic converter. - fuel vapour recirculation. The motorised Drive By Wire throttle body is also controlled electronically by the control unit: throttle opening is calculated in accordance with specific software mapped inside the engine control unit. This system does away with the need for a mechanical link between accelerator pedal and throttle body. The intake air is then directed to a modular intake manifold controlled by the engine management control unit by means of an electropneumatic valve. The control unit controls the engine phasing by means of a pair of phase transformers, one on the inlet shaft and one on the exhaust shaft; this solution allows optimum phasing, managing the inlet and exhaust separately, if necessary. Two timing sensors allow the solution set to be continuously monitored. The engine ignition is managed by the engine management control unit and there is a single coil for each spark plug with a built-in power stage. The electronic management system described above ensures that this engine meets the very latest EOBD (European On Board Diagnogis) system emission control and monitoring requirements (EURO 4). This system allows continous diagnosis of emission-related car components and notifies the driver if any of the components should deteriorate by turning on a warning light in the instrument panel. For more details, See descriptions 1056 PETROL INJECTION SYSTEM The system is also controlled by dedicated relays in the engine compartment junction control unit. Lines supplying the control unit and various system components (sensors and actuators) are protected by dedicated fuses that are also located inside the engine compartment junction unit.

The engine management control unit M10 controls and governs the entire electronic injection system. The control unit M10 is supplied directly by the battery at pin 32 of connector A via a line protected by fuse F18 of the engine compartment junction unit B001 The ignition-operated power supply (15/54 from the steering lock control unit) is received from a line protected by fuse F16 of B001 at pin 64 of connector A. The main injection relay T9 of B001 controls the entire system: it is energized by an earth signal from pin 62 of connector A of the control unit M010 and then forwards a power supply: - to the injectors N070 and the ignition module A031 - pin 2 - through the line protected by fuse F22 of B001; - to the vapour recovery solenoid valve L010, to the Lambda sensors on the catalyzer K017 and K018, to the electronic thermostat N086, to the intake variable geometry solenoid valve L015, to the intake side N092 and exhaust side N093 phase transformer solenoid valve and to the air flow meter K041, via the line protected by fuse F11 of B001; - to pins 31 and 47 of connector A of control unit M010 via a line protected by fuse F17 of B001; The fuel pump relay T10 of B001 is supplied by the line protected by fuse F21 of B001. This is energized by a (positive) command signal from pin 49 of connector A of control unit M10 and supplies power to the fuel pump N40 , which is earthed via the inertia switch I50 , that cuts off the circuit in the case of impact and thus prevents dangerous flows of fuel. The engine management control unit M010 receives signals from the various sensors in order to control all engine service parameters. The engine coolant temperature sensor on the radiator hose K036 receives a reference earth and sends a temperature signal to engine management control unit M010, to pins 3 and 28 of connector A respectively. The engine coolant temperature sensor on the thermostat K036 receives a reference earth and sends a temperature signal to the engine management control unit M010, to pins 25 and 60 of connector B respectively. The detonation sensor K050 provides information, by means of frequency signals, concerning the onset of detonation in the combustion chamber: it receives a reference earth from pin 27 of connector B of M010 and sends the respective signal to pin 10 of control unit connector B. An earth signal is sent, from pin 44 of connector B of M010, to the screening for the cables connecting the detonation sensor K050 with the engine management control unit. The engine prm sensor K046, located at the rear of the crankshaft, receives a positive signal and a reference earth respectively from pins 42 and 39 of connector B of the engine management control unit M010 and provides information concerning the engine speed by means of a signal sent to pin 35 of connector B of the control unit. The control unit M10 receives - at pin 5 of connector B - a signal from the minimum engine oil pressure sensor K30. A negative reference signal is sent by the engine management control unit M010, from pin 42 of connector A, to the engine oil level sensor K032 and the signal is received at pin 36 of connector B. The air flow meter K041 sends pin 59 of connector B a signal proportional to the air flow rate. K041 also contains an air temperature sensor: the reference earth is provided by pin 28 of connector B of M010, while pin 12 of connector B receives the air temperature signal. The Lambda sensor upstream of the catalyzer K017 and the one downstream K018 provide the control unit M010 with information concerning the correct composition of the air/fuel mixture. The Lambda sensor K017 sends a signal to pin 53 of connector B of M010, while pin 23 provides a reference earth. An earth signal is sent, from pin 6 of connector B of M010, to the screening for the cables connecting the sensor inside the Lambda sensor K017 with the engine management control unit. The sensor is heated by a coil to ensure correct operation even when cold, via an earth signal from pin 58 of connector B of M010. The Lambda sensor K018 sends a signal to pin 54 of connector B of M010, while pin 29 provides a reference earth. An earth signal is sent, from pin 11 of connector B of M010, to the screening for the cables connecting the sensor inside the Lambda sensor K018 with the engine management control unit. The sensor is heated by a coil to ensure correct operation even when cold, via an earth signal from pin 19 of connector B of M010. The fuel vapour recovery solenoid L010 allows fuel vapours to flow through toward the engine intake, where they join the mixture that is entering the combustion chamber. The valve L010 is opened by the control unit when the motor is loaded via an earth signal from pin 46 of connector B of M010. The variable geometry control solenoid L015 is controlled by means of an earth signal from pin 3 of connector B of the engine control unit. The intake side timing sensor K106 receives a power supply form pin 42 of connector B of control unit M010 and a reference earth from pin 26 of connector B and sends a frequency signal corresponding to the timing to pin 21 of connector B of the actual control unit. The exhaust side timing sensor K107 receives a power supply form pin 42 of connector B of control unit M010 and a reference earth from pin 7 of connector B and sends a frequency signal corresponding to the timing to pin 56 of connector B of the actual control unit. The inlet side phase transformer N092 mechanically controls the timing advance at the intake: it is controlled by pin 56 of connector B of the control unit M010. The exhaust side phase transformer N093 mechanically controls the timing advance at the exhaust: it is controlled by pin 55 of connector B of the control unit M010. The accelerator pedal K055 is equipped with two built-in potentiometers: a main one and one safety one. The former receives power and earth signals from pins 24 and 26 of connector A and sends a corresponding signal to pin 54 of the same connector of M010. The latter receives power and earth signals from pins 25 and 27 of connector A of M010 and sends a corresponding signal to pin 53 of the same connector. According to the signal from accelerator pedal K055, control unit M010 controls the throttle opening by means of a motor built into throttle body N075. Pins 31-32 (positive) of connector B of M010 control the closure of the motorised throttle, while pins 47-48 (negative) of the same connector control the opening. The throttle body actuator N075 is equipped with two integral potentiometers: a main one and one safety one. The former receives power and earth signals from pins 41 and 40 of connector B and sends a corresponding signal to pin 9 of the same connector of M010. The latter also receives power and earth signals from pins 41 and 40 of connector B of M010 and sends a corresponding signal to pin 8 of the same connector. The engine management control unit M010 controls the opening of the individual injectors N070, via appropriate (duty-cycle type) signals sent from pins 64 (cyl.1), 61 (cyl.2), 62 (cyl.3), 63 (cyl.4) of connector B. The injectors N070 receive a power supply to enable the energizing of the main relay T9 of B001. The ignition module A031 contains 4 coils (one per cylinder). The engine management control unit M010 controls the main windings by means of the signals sent from pins 1-2 (cyl.1), 17-18 (cyl.2), 33-34 (cyl.3), 49-50 (cyl.4) of connector B, whilst the secondary windings send the impulse to the spark plugs. Pin 1 of A031 is connected to the earth on the engine C040. Pin 57 of connector A of control unit M010 receives an NA signal from the switch on brake pedal I030, supplied by an ignition-controlled supply (INT from the steering lock control unit) via a line protected by fuse F37 of junction unit B002. Pin 45 of connector A of control unit M010 receives an NC signal from the switch on brake pedal I030, also supplied by an ignition-controlled supply (INT from the steering lock control unit) via a line protected by fuse F35 of junction unit B002. Pin 16 of connector A of M010 receives an earth signal from clutch pedal switch I031. The control unit M010 then connects via the CAN - pins 6, 38 and 37, 21 - to the Body Computer M001 - pins 36 and 37 of connector B - and to the other network nodes. Via this connection, it sends information on: - engine coolant temperature, which is sent to instrument panel E50 that controls the gauge and warning light; - engine rpm, that is sent to the rev counter in the instrument panel E50; - minimum engine oil pressure, which is sent to the instrument panel E50 that controls the warning light. The control unit M010 receives the speedometer signal produced by the ABS/ESP control unit M051 via the CAN. The control unit self-diagnostic system M010 also generates a negative signal that leaves pin 1 of connector A - that is connected directly to the EOBD warning light located in instrument panel E050 . The check function within the instrument panel E050 monitors the operation of the inertia switch and checks for faults in the oil pressure sensor: if faults are detected, the general failure warning light is turned on and the information is shown simultaneously on the display.
