The EHPS (Electrical Hydraulic Power Steering) is a power assisted steering device designed to reduce the effort required for steering the vehicle by using the torque from an electric motor. The power assisted steering is the electrohydraulic type and its intervention varies according to the speed of the vehicle and the steering angle. The power assisted steering is programmed so that its effects decrease as the speed of the vehicle increases. In this way it is possible to turn the steering wheel with great ease whilst parking and maintain safe contact with the road whilst driving at high speed. In practice, the system varies the hydraulic assistance (pump rpm) according to the rotation speed of the steering and the speed of the vehicle thereby being able to produce greater assistance when parking and extremely low hydraulic assistance at speed. An electronic control unit, an integral part of the CAN, manages and controls the system: processing the input information and using the internal operating logic, the control unit determines the direction of rotation and the supply current for the electric motor producing the desired servo-assistance effect. The system is available in two versions: - on all versions where ESP is not fitted as standard, the steering angle signal is supplied by a sensor connected directly to the steering column; - on all versions where ESP is fitted as standard, the steering angle system is supplied, via the CAN, by the steering angle node located on the vehicle steering wheel. The control unit is equipped with an autodiagnostic function: when an error is detected in the Electric Steering function, the electric steering failure warning light in the instrument panel is lit up. The presence of serious errors in the function activates an emergency (recovery) condition. For more details, See descriptions 4110 STEERING CONTROL AND LINKAGE The battery power supply line for the control unit is protected by a specific maxifuse in the engine compartment; the ignition-controlled power supply (INT from the steering lock control unit) is protected by a fuse in the junction unit under the dashboard.

The electrohydraulic power assisted steering control unit M086 controls and regulates the electrically operated steering system. The direct power supply for the control unit arrives from the battery via the line protected by the electric steering control unit B053 maxifuse at pin 1 of connector A of M086. Pin 2 of connector A of M086 is earthed. The ignition-controlled power supply (INT from steering lock control unit) arrives from the line protected by fuse F51 of the junction unit under the dashboard B002, at pin 1 of connector B of M086. The control unit M086 is connected via the CAN (pins 2-3 and 4-5 of connector B) with the other nodes, in particular the Body Computer M001, the steering angle sensor M092 and the instrument panel E050 to which it sends signals for switching on the electric steering failure warning light. The autodiagnostic data can be read by connecting to connector C of the Body Computer M001 (pin 12): it receives signals from pin 2 of connector C of control unit M086 via the special diagnostic K line. See E8010 DIAGNOSTIC MULTIPLE CONNECTOR

The presence of serious errors in the function activates an emergency (recovery) condition. For more details, See descriptions 4110 STEERING CONTROL AND LINKAGE The battery power supply line for the control unit is protected by a specific maxifuse in the battery control unit; the ignition-controlled power supply (INT from the steering lock control unit) is protected by a fuse in the junction unit under the dashboard.

The electrohydraulic power assisted steering control unit M086 controls and regulates the electrically operated steering system. The direct power supply for the control unit arrives from the battery via the line protected by maxifuse F73 of the battery control unit B099 at pin 1 of connector A of M086. Pin 2 of connector A of M086 is earthed. See E1010 POWER SUPPLY The ignition-controlled power supply (INT from steering lock control unit) arrives from the line protected by fuse F51 of the junction unit under the dashboard B002, at pin 1 of connector B of M086. The control unit M086 is connected via the CAN (pins 2-3 and 4-5 of connector B) with the other nodes, in particular the Body Computer M001, the steering angle sensor M092 and the instrument panel E050 to which it sends signals for switching on the electric steering failure warning light. The autodiagnostic data can be read by connecting to connector C of the Body Computer M001 (pin 12): it receives signals from pin 2 of connector C of control unit M086 via the special diagnostic K line. See E8010 DIAGNOSTIC MULTIPLE CONNECTOR

The vehicle is equipped with automatic transmission which regulates and controls the automatic engagement of the gears. An electronic control unit manages a complex operating logic that allows the use of the gearbox in both sequential conditions, in which the driver manages the engagement of the gears using the lever and, in automatic mode, where the management of the gear changes is delegated to the electronic system. The presence of the transmission control unit makes available the following set of operating modes and specific operational functions: - basic operating mode; - ability to adapt to operating conditions; - functions designed to improve comfort and fuel consumption. In manual operating mode, the driver may select the gears by pressing the gear lever to the left. At this point the lever may be pushed up (towards +) to shift up or pushed down (towards -) to shift down a gear. Its ability to adapt to operational condtions allows the vehicle to adapt to the driver's driving conditions and/or road conditions. The most important are as follows: - up & down slope: this function allows the vehicle to recognise road slopes (upward and downward) and modify gear shift points to achieve the best possible compromise at all times between the driver's needs, the road conditions and the vehicle situation (speed and engine speed). - Fast off: automatic transmissions normally shift from one gear to the next when the driver raises his foot from the accelerator. This function inhibits this gear shift when the foot is raised quicklyl from the accelerator, limiting the number of gear shifts and increasing driver comfort. - Cornering: this function inhibits gear shifts when the vehicle is cornering in order not to jeopardise vehicle safety. The functions designed to improve comfort and fuel consumption allow vibrations and pulses felt by the driver to be reduced: - Neutral control: after the vehicle has been parked with the gear shift lever in position D for a few seconds (e.g. waiting at a green traffic light), this function is activated. It releases the hydraulic clutch inside the transmission to reduce the resistant torque in the torque converter and thus save fuel while reducing the vehicle's vibration level when idling. - Self-learning to minimise the pulses perceptible to the driver during gear selector operation with the car parked (i.e. shifts from N-R and N-D), it is possible to apply the self-learning procedrue to set the band and clutch activation pressures to ensure smoother operation; The control unit has its own diagnostic signal used for the continuous monitoring of the entire device. See E8010 DIAGNOSTIC MULTIPLE CONNECTOR

The automatic transmission control unit M055 controls and regulates the entire gearbox management system. The direct power supply (+30) reaches, via a line protected by fuse F18, engine compartment control unit B001, at pin 33 of connector A of automatic transmission control unit M055 and pin 9 of gear selector control unit M053. An ignition-operated power supply (15/54) from the steering lock control unit reaches pins 22 and 31 of connector A of M055, at pin 22 of automatic transmission solenoid unit L050 and pin 1 of speed selector control unit M053 via a line protected by fuse F24 of engine compartment control unit B001. The passenger side dashboard earth C020 is connected to pin 2 of speed selector control unit M053. Left front earth C010 is connected at pins 23 and 32 of connector A of transmission control unit M055 and pin 21 of automatic transmission control unit L050. Gear selector control unit M053, via pins 4 – 6, 7 – 5 and automatic transmission control unit M055, via pins 25 – 26, 35 – 36, communicate via the C-CAN network and interface with pins 36, 37 of the Body Computer control unit. See E1050 CAN CONNECTION LINES The Body Computer also transmits, via pins 6 and 5, signals related to the operating status of the transmission to the display on instrument panel E050, via the B-CAN network. P/N (Parking/Neutral) position sensor on the automatic transmission solenoid unit L050 is connected via pin 1 to pin B4 of steering lock control unit M089. Its function is to inhibit vehicle start-up. The pins of connector B of automatic transmission control unit M055 are directly connected to the pins of the automatic transmission solenoid unit L050. More specifically: - pins 6, 16, 7, 17 are connected to pins 23, 24, 25, 26 of the automatic transmission solenoid unit L050 and receive the speed selector configuration; - pins 32 and 22 are connected via pins 17 and 18 of automatic transmission solenoid unit L050 to vehicle speed sensor;3 - pins 33 and 23 are connected via pins 19 and 20 of automatic transmission solenoid unit L050 to Revolution sensor C1; - pins 25 and 12 are connected via pins 11 and 12 of automatic transmission solenoid unit L050 to the linear lock-up solenoid; - pins 35 and 15 are connected via pins 7 and 8 of automatic transmission solenoid unit L050 to the linear throttle solenoid; - pins 26 and 36 are connected via pins 13 and 14 of automatic transmission solenoid unit L050 to the clutch control pressure linear solenoid solenoid; - pins 31 and 21 are connected via pins 16 and 15 of automatic transmission solenoid unit L050 to the fluid temperature sensor; - pins 34, 24, 8, 14, 13 are connected via pins 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 of automatic transmission solenoid unit L050 to the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th and 5th speed selection solenoids respectively. A reverse engagement solenodi is present at pins 10 and 30 of automatic transmission solenoid unit L050. See E2022 REVERSING LIGHTS Self-diagnosis of control unit M055 may be performed by connecting to connector C – pin 7 - of Body Computer M001: it receives signals from pin 16 of connector A of control unit M055 via the special diagnostic line (K LINE). See E8010 DIAGNOSTIC MULTIPLE CONNECTOR

The vehicle is equipped with automatic transmission which regulates and controls the automatic engagement of the gears. The 6 speed gearbox, in addition to being compact and light, features a control unit integrated with the transmission and has been designed with special attention paid to limiting consumption. An electronic control unit manages a complex operating logic that allows the use of the gearbox in both sequential conditions, in which the driver manages the engagement of the gears using the lever and, in automatic mode, where the management of the gear changes is delegated to the electronic system. The presence of the gearbox control unit makes the following series of operating modes and specific functions available: - standard operating mode; - capacity to adapt to operating conditions; - operation aimed at improving comfort and consumption. In manual operating mode, the driver can select the gears by pushing the gear lever on the right; at this point a impulse upwards (towards "+") makes it possible to shift to a higher gear whilst an impulse downwards (towards "-") produces a shift to the previous gear. The ability to adapt to the operating conditions allows the vehicle to adjust to the driving styles and/or road conditions. The most important include: - up & down slope: this function allows the vehicle to recognize a slope (upwards or downwards) modifying the gear change points appropriately to produce the best compromise between the requirements of the driver, the road conditions and the situation of the vehicle (speed and engine revs). - Fast off: automatic transmissions shift from one gear to a higher one when the driver takes their foot of the accelerator. This function inhibits this gear change when the driver's foot is taken off the accelerator quickly, limiting the number of gear changes and increasing driver comfort. - Cornering: in order not to adversely affect the stability of the vehicle, this function prevents gear changes when the vehicle is cornering. - Neutral control: a few seconds after the vehicle has stopped with the gear lever in position D (for example, waiting at traffic lights) this function is activated and releases the hydraulic clutches inside the transmission with the effect of reducing the resistant torque in the torque converter and thereby saving fuel and reducing the level of vibrations during idling. - Self-learning: in order to reduce the impulses felt by the driver especially during the activation of the gear selector with the vehicle stationary (i.e. shifts N-R, N-D) it is possible to apply the self-learning procedure which allows the implementation pressures for the bands and clutches to be set so that they operate smoothly; - Braking assist: this function is activated when the driver brakes and is designed to increase the deceleration of the vehicle by downshifting; - Poor grip: in order to prevent the wheels slipping, during take off in poor grip condtions the gear changes automatically from first to a higher gear. The control unit has its own diagnostic signal used for the continuous monitoring of the entire device. See E8010 DIAGNOSTIC MULTIPLE CONNECTOR

The automatic transmission control unit M055 controls and regulates the entire gearbox management system. The direct power supply (+30) arrives via the line protected by fuse F18 of the engine compartment junction unit B001, at pin 11 of connector A of the automatic transmission control unit M055 and at pin 9 of the gear selector control unit M053. The ignition controlled supply (15/54) for the steering lock control unit reaches pin 1 of connector A of M055 and pin 1 of the gear selector control unit M053 via the line protected by fuse F24 of the engine compartment junction unit B001. The passenger side dashboard earth C020 is connected at pin 2 of the gear selector control unit M053. The gear selector control unit M053, via pins 4-6, 7-5 and the automatic transmission control unit M055, via pins 8-14, 7-6, communicates via the C-CAN interfacing at pins 36, 37 of the Body Computer control unit. See E1050 CAN CONNECTION LINES The Body Computer also transmits, via pins 6 and 5, the signals for the operating state of the gearbox to the instrument panel display E050, via the B-CAN. The reversing sensor is present at pin 13 of connector A of the automatic transmission control unit M055. See E2022 REVERSING LIGHTS Pin 5 of connector A of the automatic transmission control unit M055 is connected directly to pin B4 of the steering lock control unit M089. Its function is to inhibit the starting of the vehicle. The pins for connector B of the automatic transmission control unit M055 have a pin-to-pin connection at the pins for the automatic transmission solenoid valve unit L050. The autodiagnostic system for control unit M055 is achieved by onnecting to connector C of the Body Computer M001 (pin 7): it receives signals from pin 4 of connector A of control unit M055 via the special diagnostic line (K LINE). See E8010 DIAGNOSTIC MULTIPLE CONNECTOR

The tyre pressure monitoring system consists of: - 4 RF pressure sensors located inside the tyre on the wheel rim; - 4 sensors fitted on each wheel arch; - 1 RF management and reception electronic control unit in the passenger compartment. The pressure sensors continuously monitor the correct inflation of the tyres: if a fault or a loss in pressure is detected, the sensor transmits a message via RF to the receiver control unit. The control unit sends the Body Computer, via the serial line, the information relating to the pressure and the monitoring of the system; the Body Computer, in turn, forwards these signal via the CAN allowing the display in the instrument panel of signals relating to: general failure warning light and signalling system failures and insufficient tyre pressure in the display. The control unit supply lines are protected by fuses in the junction unit under the dashboard.

The tyre inflation pressure control unit M047 is supplied directly by the battery at pin 1 of connector A via the line protected by fuse F39 of the junction unit under the dashboard B002. The ignition-controlled power supply (INT from steering lock control unit) arrives at pin 16 of connector B of M047 from the line protected by fuse F51 of the junction unit under the dashboard B002. Pin 10 of connector A is earthed. The control unit M047 provides a positive signal, from pin 2 of connector A, for the tyre inflation pressure sensors P012 and four reference earth signals from pin 15 (left front sensor), pin 14 (right front sensor), pin 12 (left rear sensor) and pin 13 (right rear sensor) of connector B. The sensors send the corresponding signals to the control unit M047, respectively: - pin 4 of connector A, from the left front sensor (P012B); - pin 5 of connector A, from the right front sensor (P012 A); - pin 3 of connector A, from the left rear sensor (P012 D); - pin 6 of connector A, from the right rear sensor (P012 C). The control unit M047 is connected, from pin 18 of connector A, via the serial line, to the Body Computer M001 - pin 25 of connector B. See E1060 A-BUS SERIAL LINE The autodiagnostic data can be read by connecting to connector C of the Body Computer M001 (pin 13): it receives the signals from pin 17 of connector A of M047. See E8010 DIAGNOSTIC MULTIPLE CONNECTOR

The steering lock allows a particular management of the vehicle protection system and engine starting. The system is managed by the steering lock control unit which controls and regulates the entire steering column locking/unlocking system electrically controlled by means of special actuators. The steering lock control unit, an integral node of the CAN, is the power distributor for the vehicle providing the ignition-controlled power supplies INT, INT/A, 15/54 and 50. See E1010 POWER SUPPLY Depending on the position of the key (TEG) inside the starting device, the steering lock control unit determines:f the enablement request for the +15 supply to the Body Computer (ON position), the +50 starting for vehicle (START position) and, if the result is positive, the power distribution to the vehicle and to the various load (INT, INT/A,15/54). The starting system involves that together with the rotation of the key to the START position the clutch pedal (or in recovery conditions, the brake pedal) for versions with a manual gearbox or the brake pedal for versions with automatic transmission, is pressed. On versions with automatic transmission the additional condition of the gear lever in P (PARK) must be observed. For further details, See E5010 STARTING AND RECHARING The release of the steering is activated when the TEG is inserted in the ignition device and is recognized. The locking of the steering takes place with the TEG in the OFF position as long as the safety condition that involves the continuity of the steering release when the vehicle speed is above 4 km/h is respected. In this case the user is advised by means of a signal in the NQS: "The steering will not be locked".

The steering lock control unit M089 controls and regulates the entire electrically controlled steering column locking system. The direct power supply for the control unit M089 - pin C1 - arrives from the battery via the line protected by fuse F3 of the engine compartment junction unit B001. Pin A4 of M089 is earthed. The steering lock control unit M089, depending on the rotation of the key in the ignition device H003, receives the following signals: - at pin A6, the key inserted signal (TEG_IN); - at pin B5, the key turned to ON signal (TEG_MAR); - at pin C5, the first starting signal with the key turned to START (TEG_Crank1); - at pin C6, the second starting signal with the key turned to START (TEG_Crank2); The ignition device H003 - pins 1 and 2 - communicates, via the CAN, with the steering lock control unit M089 - pins A2 and A3 - for the enablement of the steering release after recognizing the TEG inserted in the reader. At pin A5 the steering lock control unit M089 receives the earth signal for the clutch pedal I031 pressure. In recovery conditions, the control unit M089 - pin C4 - uses the NA contact signal for the switch on the brake pedal I030. See E5030 PETROL ENGINES ELECTRONIC MANAGEMENT See E5050 DIESEL ENGINES ELECTRONIC MANAGEMENT The steering lock control unit M089, depending on the position of the key in the ignition device H003, provides the following power supplies: - INT, from pin A1 to the junction unit under the dashboard B002 - pin 11 of connector H -; - INT/A, from pin C8 to the junction unit under the dashboard B002 - pin 1 of connector H -; - 15/54, from pin B1 to the engine compartment junction unit B001 - pin 30 of connector A - ; - +50, from pin B8 to the starter motor A020. For further details, See E1010 POWER SUPPLY See E5010 STARTING AND RECHARING

The steering lock device allows the vehicle protection and engine start-up system to be managed in a specific way. The system is managed by the steering lock control unit that controls and governs the entire steering column lock/release system electrically via special actuators. The steering lock control unit node, part of the CAN network, distributes vehicle power to supply ignition-operated power supplies INT, INT/A, 15/54 and 50. See E1010 POWER SUPPLY Accordig to the position of the key (TEG) inside the ignition device, the steering lock control unit determines: the +15 power supply enablement request to the Body Computer (ON position), vehicle start-up +50 (START position) and, if this is successful, the distribution of power to the vehicle and the associated loads (INT, INT/A, 15/54). During the start-up stage, as the key is turned to the START position, the clutch pedal (or the brake pedal during recovery) is pressed simultaneously for versions with a manual gearbox while the brake pedal is pressed on versions with an automatic transmission. On versions with an automatic transmission, the gearlever must be in position P (PARK) as an additional condition. For further details, See E5010 STARTING AND RECHARING The steering release is activated when the TEG is inserted in the ignition device with the associated recognition. The steering is locked with the TEG in OFF position, unless the safety condition that requires continuity of steering release at a vehicle speed higher than 4 km/h is not respected. In this case, the user is notified by a signal via the NQS. "The steering will not be locked".

Steering lock control unit M089 controls and governs the entire electrically-controlled steering column lock system. A direct power supply from control unit M089 - pin C1 - reaches the battery via a line protected by fuse F3 of engine compartment junction unit B001. Pin A4 of M089 is earthed. According to the rotation of the key in ignition H003, steering lock control unit M089 receives the following signals: - at pin A6, a key inserted signal (TEG_IN); - at pin B5, a signal to indicate the key is turned ON (TEG_MAR); - at pin C5, an initial start-up signal with the key is turned to START (TEG_Crank1); - at pin C6, the second start-up signal with the key is turned to START (TEG_Crank2); Ignition device H003 - pins 1 and 2 - communicates via the CAN network with steering lock control unit M089 - pins A2 and A3 - to enable steering release after recognising the TEG up on its insertion in the reader. Steering lock control unit M089 receives signal from the NC and NO contacts on brake pedal I030 at pins C4 and C7 respectively. See E5030 PETROL ENGINES ELECTRONIC MANAGEMENT See E5050 DIESEL ENGINES ELECTRONIC MANAGEMENT The signal indicating the correct position of the gear lever (PARK) is sent to the solenoid unit on automatic transmission L050 at pin B4 of steering lock control uint M089. The signal indicating the correct positon of the gear lever (PARK) is sent from automatic transmission control unit M055 (pin 5 of connector A) to pin B4 of steering lock control unit M089. According to the position of the key in ignition H003, steering lock control unit M089 receives the following signals: - INT, from pin A1 of underfacia junction unit B002 - pin 11 of connector H; - INT/A, from pin C8 of underfacia junction unit B002 - pin 1 of connector H; - 15/54, from pin B1 of engine compartment junction unit B001 - pin 30 of connector A -; - +50, from pin B8 to starter motor A020. The steering lock allows a particular management of the vehicle protection system and engine starting. The system is managed by the steering lock control unit which controls and regulates the entire steering column locking/unlocking system electrically controlled by means of special actuators. The steering lock control unit, an integral node of the CAN, is the power distributor for the vehicle providing the ignition-controlled power supplies INT, INT/A, 15/54 and 50. See E1010 POWER SUPPLY Depending on the position of the key (TEG) inside the starting device, the steering lock control unit determines:f the enablement request for the +15 supply to the Body Computer (ON position), the +50 starting for vehicle (START position) and, if the result is positive, the power distribution to the vehicle and to the various load (INT, INT/A,15/54). The starting system involves that together with the rotation of the key to the START position the clutch pedal (or in recovery conditions, the brake pedal) for versions with a manual gearbox or the brake pedal for versions with automatic transmission, is pressed. On versions with automatic transmission the additional condition of the gear lever in P (PARK) must be observed. For further details, See E5010 STARTING AND RECHARING The release of the steering is activated when the TEG is inserted in the ignition device and is recognized. The locking of the steering takes place with the TEG in the OFF position as long as the safety condition that involves the continuity of the steering release when the vehicle speed is above 4 km/h is respected. In this case the user is advised by means of a signal in the NQS: "The steering will not be locked".

The steering lock control unit M089 controls and regulates the entire electrically controlled steering column locking system. The direct power supply for the control unit M089 - pin C1 - arrives from the battery via the line protected by fuse F3 of the engine compartment junction unit B001. Pin A4 of M089 is earthed. The steering lock control unit M089, depending on the rotation of the key in the ignition device H003, receives the following signals: - at pin A6, the key inserted signal (TEG_IN); - at pin B5, the key turned to ON signal (TEG_MAR); - at pin C5, the first starting signal with the key turned to START (TEG_Crank1); - at pin C6, the second starting signal with the key turned to START (TEG_Crank2); The ignition device H003 - pins 1 and 2 - communicates, via the CAN, with the steering lock control unit M089 - pins A2 and A3 - for the enablement of the steering release after recognizing the TEG inserted in the reader. The steering lock control unit M089 receives signals from the NC and NA contacts for the switch on the brake pedal I030 at pins C4 and C7 respectively. See E5050 DIESEL ENGINES ELECTRONIC MANAGEMENT The signal for the correct position of the gear lever (PARK) is sent by the automatic transmission control unti M055 (pin 5 of connector A) to pin B4 of the steering lock control unit M089. The steering lock control unit M089, depending on the position of the key in the ignition device H003, provides the following power supplies: - INT, from pin A1 to the junction unit under the dashboard B002 - pin 11 of connector H -; - INT/A, from pin C8 to the junction unit under the dashboard B002 - pin 1 of connector H -; - 15/54, from pin B1 to the engine compartment junction unit B001 - pin 30 of connector A - ; - +50, from pin B8 to the starter motor A020. For further details, See E1010 POWER SUPPLY See E5010 STARTING AND RECHARING

The car is fitted with numerous electronic control units that perform a self-diagnostic function. When a diagnostic tester (Examiner or other device) is connected to these control units, self-diagnosis data can be read (parameters, errors) or the available active diagnostic tests can be carried out. As set out in the CEE EURO 3 regulations (in accordance with Directive 98/69/CE - ISO standard J1962 -) and CEE EURO 4 (in force since 01-01-2005) in addition to becoming more stringent about emissions, it is compulsory to install the EOBD (European On Board Diagnosis) in the vehicle in the Body Computer (connector C).) The same connector is responsible for connecting nodes (control units) connected to the low transmission speed B-CAN network, while control units, while control units connected to the C-CAN network are tested by means of a specific K line. The following are checked via the B-CAN line: - junction unit under the dashboard; - instrument panel; - door control units; - radio controls on the steering wheel; - built-in radio-telephone-navigator unit; - boot comparment control unit; - seat position control unit; - (automatic) climate control sytem control unit; - Air Bag control unit; - parking sensor control unit; - steering lock control unit; - T.E.G. Reader. For more details, See E1050 CAN CONNECTION LINES The following are monitored via individual diagnostic K lines: - engine management control unit (and automatic transmission control unit, if present) - ABS/ESP control unit; - electric steering control unit; - tyre pressure control unit; - headlamps electronic control unit (xenon gas discharge headlamps version); - additional heater control unit (JTD versions).

The EOBD central diagnostic socket is built into Body Computer M001 connector C. It is supplied directly by the battery at pin 16 of the line protected by fuse F39 of underfacia control unit B002 ; pins 4 and 5 are earthed. Pin 1 is connected to the K line at the ABS/ESP control unit M051 (pin 6) See E7023 ESP Pin 7 is connected via the K line to the engine management control unit M010 (pin 59 of connector A) and, on versions with automatic transmission, to the automatic transmission control unit M055 (pin 16 of connector A). See E5030 PETROL ENGINES ELECTRONIC MANAGEMENT See E7050 AUTOMATIC TRANSMISSION Pin 13 is connected to the tyre inflation pressure control unit M047 (pin 17 of connector B). See E7060 TYRE INFLATION PRESSURE CONTROL SYSTEM The gas discharge headlamp control units F010 (left) and F011 (right) and the electric steering control unit M086 (pin 2 of connector C) are connected at pin 12. See E2011 DIPPED HEADLAMPS See E7045 ELECTRIC STEERING Pins 6 and 14 are connected to the B-CAN; the following are controlled and "diagnosed" via this network: the junction unit under the dashboard B002, the instrument panel E050, the driver's door control unit M066, the passenger door control unit M067 and the luggage compartment control unit M063, the steering lock control unit M089, the radio (or built-in radio-telephone-navigator) P020, the climate control system control unit M070, the parking sensor control unit M084, the radio controls on the steering wheel control unit M093, the Air Bag control unit M060, the left seat position control unit M173, the right seat position control unit M175 and the T.E.G. Reader H003.
